### Reading and authority contract

This document establishes a proposed unified product and engineering contract, rather than a new development track. Part I defines shared requirements, canonical ownership, integrated workflow and interface rules, reconciled decisions, release sequence and evidence. Part II maps all incorporated source sections and explicit addendum requirements to those rules and preserves the full original review documents in Annexes A–L. Part III records immutable repository source identities. The exact repository text of v1.2, ADRs, domain designs and other repository-only sources is incorporated by normative reference to the pinned commit, not represented as a verbatim embedded copy in this review edition. The companion read-only materialization utility can append every pinned repository source from a local authenticated clone and verify each Git blob, producing a fully self-contained archival edition. This is an explicit completeness limitation of the delivered review edition, not a relaxation of requirements. Do not approve it as a source-complete replacement until the repository-only payloads and any open reconciliation questions are reviewed. The twelve original review annexes are byte-preserved; the TDS and PAC original review editions are longer than their integrated repository editions and must not be mistaken for identical authoritative files.

**Normative terminology:** MUST denotes mandatory product or integrity requirements; SHOULD denotes a preferred design with a documented, authorized exception; MAY denotes an optional supported capability. A planning target is not an achieved SLA; a logical entity is not a migration; a proposed route or permission code is not an implemented API. Current SQL, OpenAPI, runtime and accepted ADRs remain authoritative for engineering behavior until reviewed changes are implemented. “Approved scope” means the twelve approved addenda, not approval of every proposed low-level engineering choice or completion of their features. No historical text is overwritten by this document. If a source contains an older status or roadmap, the dated integration notes and current roadmap govern sequencing; the original statement is retained as provenance. Do not resolve material contradictions by silently selecting the less restrictive rule. Where implementation or product requirements conflict, block the affected slice pending review, preserve the more protective runtime constraint, and record a successor decision if required. Source incorporation includes every clause, acceptance condition, exception, data model, proposed API, and operational limit in the identified immutable revisions; the consolidated rules below compose them, not erase them.

# Part I — Unified normative product and engineering specification

<a id="b13-product"></a>
## B13-PRODUCT — Product mission, scope and governing invariants

Eventor is a self-hostable Event Operations and Guest Logistics Platform. It supports the complete venue-provider and event-organizer lifecycle from inquiry to preparation, event operation and handover. It is not simply a seating tool, invitation sender, booking calendar or form builder. A simple meeting needs only the features relevant to it; a large institutional ceremony can enable production planning, registration, delegated hospitality, precise allocation, admission stations and live operations. All levels use the same model and authorization. GHB is the reference organization and venue portfolio, never an application branch or a reason to hardcode facts.

1. Maintain one canonical record per owning domain, with authorized projections and immutable historical revisions. Distinguish operational state, presentation state and evidence. Person, participation, invitation, invitation link, response, registration, eligibility, allocation, admission credential, attendance, service arrangement, delivery evidence and booking are separate facts. No derived metric, task, printed artifact, provider receipt or form submission changes them except through the exact owning authorized command.
2. Hierarchical venue objects, allocatable resources, display labels, approved operational capacities and spatial features are distinct. An allocation can point to a precise chair/floor position, row, zone or capacity pool; a table or a visible source-plan cell is not inherently a seat. The system must support banquet, theatre, standing and carpet/prayer layouts without fabricated furniture or positions. No resource conflict, overlapping allocation, illegal capacity or unauthorized record is permitted.
3. Automation provides proposals, suggestions, validated defaults and deterministic diagnostics. Human review and domain-specific approval remain mandatory where specified; setup, workflow configuration, solver proposals and integrations must not relax those constraints. Every material decision records actual actor, context, source revision, reason where required, timestamp and resulting receipt.
4. Deployment supports private intranet and opt-in internet access, local operation without mandatory cloud or paid provider, native Linux and Docker Compose packaging of the same build. Independent optional capabilities must fail independently. Guest-facing publication is deliberately enabled and restricted; never expose an unrestricted staff application, database or file store merely because public HTTPS exists.
5. Do not turn Eventor into a payment processor, full accounting system, ticket marketplace, hotel/property management, restaurant POS, transportation dispatcher, medical records system, unrestricted workflow engine, general-purpose BI/SQL tool, general project management suite, or emergency-response/security command system. External prerequisites are coordination only. Future enterprise identity, integrations, expanded finance and isolated training are separate reviewed scope beyond the explicit existing requirements; MFA and safe synthetic preview/training already required by the sources remain in scope. AI or automation cannot infer guest status, precedence, protected traits, financial authority or business decisions.

<a id="b13-operating"></a>
## B13-OPERATING — Parties, optional capabilities and organizational responsibility

Venue provider owns facilities, its service catalogue, booking availability and commercial terms; requester may differ from contracting party/payer; organizer owns its operational event and participant records; operator/vendor performs assigned duties under explicit grants. These identities may coincide but must never be merged conceptually. A booking-only provider must operate with no event record, guest directory, seating, station, solver or external communication subscription. A hybrid tenant can separately own bookings and events. Operating profiles are configurable defaults, not rigid tiers. Preserve provider-side facility obligations even where the organizer delegates operational work. An event can use external or unresolved location as a draft only where the owning lifecycle permits; never manufacture a venue reservation.

The effective capability is the intersection of deployed support, platform policy, tenant enablement, event applicability, current configuration readiness, lifecycle, exact role/field/grant authority and task/device scope. Activation does not grant access; navigation does not grant access; a configured feature can be unavailable or blocked; a permitted feature need not be activated. Dependency graph must be explicit, acyclic and minimal. Invitations require eligible participation and a permitted distribution path, which may be manual. RSVP does not require email. Seating requires appropriate approved resources/capacities; simple allocation does not require advanced solver. Admission requires its own eligible subject and separate credential or permitted manual procedure; it does not require every optional guest-service feature. Registration can exist without seat assignment; venue booking can exist without registration. No unrelated prerequisite may block a simple meeting or independent booking.

Collaboration is an explicit lifecycle: grantor proposes scope/action/projection/validity; recipient reviews stable meaning and accepts; each downstream command checks the accepted grant and exact subject/action. Revocation, expiry or suspension stops new protected actions and protected delivery. Already intentionally shared immutable history is retained as allowed by owning policy; no future broad access. Do not infer access from a booking/event link, supplier relationship, guest group, organization membership or task label. Keep provider internal commercial/operational facts and organizer Registry/guest data private by default. Task delegation gives only the minimal task/action projection. Preserve separate owners, resource authority and authentic actor attribution. ADRs 0004, 0005, 0006, 0021–0024 govern implemented commands.

<a id="b13-governance"></a>
## B13-GOVERNANCE — PAC, OAC, identity and delegated administration

### B13-GOV-01 Control plane and trust domains

PAC is the installation/platform control plane: owner authority, delegated Superadmin and constrained operators, tenant lifecycle, global account and access directory, typed module/configuration policy, default platform identity, governance, health/jobs/communications, backup/recovery/release metadata, scoped support and emergency intervention. The application cannot execute arbitrary shell, SQL, root/Docker socket operations, edit service units or obtain host credentials. Protected host CLI/installer is a separate operator boundary. Host operations use the real database principal/session_user and reason; do not invent a tenant member for host action. Distinguish control-plane oversight from data-plane tenant authority. No automatic restricted guest, private commercial, prerequisite or correspondence access merely by holding a technical role. Read-only safe health/counts do not authorize drilling into private records. Any support inspection, administration or emergency data access must be purpose-limited, approved where required, expiring, auditable, revocable and explicitly attributed. Emergency access cannot override integrity, conceal actions, or serve as a routine bypass. Single-owner host recovery uses local protected confirmation; it does not create blanket confidential-data self-approval.

### B13-GOV-02 Current account and future authority compatibility

Keep ADR 0015 email-first authentication; verify password and rate limit before exposing eligible workspace names. A single eligible workspace opens; multiple choices use credentials only in memory until selection. Rotate session/CSRF on switching under existing lock ordering, revoke old session atomically, preserve original expiry and actual actor, clear former workspace UI/caches/streams/jobs as applicable. Selected-tenant principal is determined by server session, not client role or tenant claims. OAC managers cannot assign platform flags or manage unrelated accounts. The host-only platform flag and managed memberships currently reconcile all non-platform grants in active tenants under ADR 0015; do not silently rewrite or broaden this model. PAC's future narrow control/data authority requires M0 audit and reviewed successor ADR/migration before changing those grants, with tests for existing memberships, revocation, recovery and explicit support scopes. Existing broad permissions are a review item, not proof of a verified leak. Retain active administrator guard, per-membership suspension revoking that tenant's sessions, restoration preserving grants without restoring sessions or affecting other memberships. Preserve local account operation even if OIDC/LDAP/AD later offered. Enforce modern password hashing, MFA for sensitive/admin functions as required, secure session lifecycle, recovery with separate authorization and least privilege. Host new-account bootstrap and host existing-membership provisioning stay separate: no upsert/reset/reactivation, no implicit roles/platform flag/email proof, atomic audited create, sanitized output and password via hidden stdin only (ADR 0017, 0020). Do not convert current host tools into unguarded HTTP operations.

### B13-GOV-03 OAC independent organization self-service

A properly provisioned tenant can run daily administration without routine platform-owner or SQL intervention. OAC owns first-login handoff and adaptive readiness, tenant identity/profile, brand/preferences, configurable roles/access, member enrollment, venue portfolio, owned resource/service catalogue, bookings, organizer portfolio and Registry, TDS/FRS/CID/RAI, supplier coordination, audit/privacy and controlled support. Tenant owner governs policy and appointments, administrators act within delegated ceilings. Global identity and membership are independent; invite, accept, suspend, restore and revoke follow their own lifecycle. Separate rights to configure, prepare, approve, publish, send, reconcile, export, read sensitive fields, manage budget and grant access. Readiness state `not_applicable`, `not_started`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `ready` is not permission; expose reasons and next safe action with observed revision/time. A retired or suspended configuration blocks new use but retains historical records and legitimate retained obligations. Tenant offboarding has reviewed impact preview, legal hold, retention/purge/portability, drain or refusal, explicit archive/restoration policy, no implicit booking/event cancellation, auto refund, guest deletion or credential issuance. Organization export is scope-limited logical portability, not physical backup.

### B13-GOV-04 Branding and communication service governance

One versioned branding hierarchy: event override > venue override > organization > platform default; supported surface/purpose decides applicable levels. Personal interface theme/locale is independent. Pinned brand/assets/templates/locales are reproducible for historical artifacts; rebrand never changes issued content. PAC may optionally offer explicitly granted shared communication services; OAC can independently configure tenant-owned providers. Shared account secrets, sender identities, rate/usage/budget policies and tenant grants are isolated. No tenant sees another tenant's correspondence or credentials. Disable/restore fences jobs and reconciles uncertain sends before resumption. See TDS/PAC/OAC/CID full annexes and pinned repository editions.

<a id="b13-ux"></a>
## B13-UX — Shared adaptive experience, localization and accessible setup

### B13-UX-01 One shell, three presentation modes

Staff application uses a thin composition root and feature-oriented modules. PAC, organization home/OAC, event workspace/EOC, vendor/staff task, guest portal, public booking/registration, station and passive display are role-specific surfaces, not independent copies of the source data. Provide Quick Start (essential information and safe defaults), Guided Setup (adaptive steps), Advanced (full specialist controls), with preference and per-workflow switching. Switching mode preserves event identity, draft state, authorization, revision, history and enabled capabilities. A user can create a minimal event draft with name, schedule/timezone and ownership per existing domain command, decide other details later, and extend it without migration. Minimal mode cannot hide blockers, unresolved dependencies or mandatory review. Simple forms use approved presets and concise validated inputs; advanced designer remains available. The mode is not a capability switch or permission, and is not a subscription tier.

### B13-UX-02 Setup orchestration and safe presets

Use typed preset identities and revisions with suggested values, provenance, explicit field copy allowlists, capability dependencies and validation. Inherit organization defaults, apply event-specific choices only when allowed; preview effective values and changed/omitted/blocked fields, including override reasons. Presets and template clones must never copy real persons, contact values, credentials, approvals, completed facts, audit history, sent messages, reserved capacity or external commitments by default. An actual copy of a permitted source list/record must use a separate explicit reviewed owning operation. Setup draft is resumable, revision-checked, scoped to the authorized context, bounded by expiry/retention; save/back/retry does not create an event twice. Preview does not mutate; final apply binds actor, exact inputs, relevant revisions, capability graph and readiness; stale review yields conflict and re-review. Execute atomic core command where possible; separate consequential effects into explicitly approved domain steps and show per-step receipt, retry/compensation, not falsely atomic cross-provider operation. No automatic publication, confirmed booking, issue/send, role assignment or station pairing as a side effect of creating a draft. Capability disable requires impact review; drain/block unsafe removal, preserve historical facts and active obligations.

### B13-UX-03 Navigation and operational UX

Role- and context-filtered landing, menus, counts, search, notifications and drill-down; empty states differentiate no data, no permission, feature disabled, pending and stale/degraded. Unauthorized objects must not leak via counts, autocomplete, errors, pagination or hidden tabs. Context switch cancels stale reads and clears sensitive UI; server reauthorizes every command. Native accessible dialogs and keyboard alternatives to drag/drop, fieldset/labels, logical focus and announcements, status not color alone, reduced motion, contrast, zoom/mobile, readable print. Use shared date/number/currency formatting; bs-BA and en initial locale, valid canonical BCP 47, user preference > selected organization > en for staff; explicit validated interaction language > purpose-available customer preference > owner default > en for public/customer. UI catalogues are version-controlled, stable domain codes never translated identifiers. Authored translated content revisioned and pinned. Missing required locale is visible and blocks or permits only approved fallback. Store instants with timezone-aware semantics and IANA schedule timezone; reject nonexistent local times, explicit ambiguity handling, preserve exact unchanged deadline. Render bs-BA/en dates/diacritics and locale-appropriate currency without changing stored facts.

### B13-UX-04 Quick paths throughout

Quick venue: basic capacity and room only; detailed geometry optional until required. Quick allocation: explicit manual table/zone move respecting all invariants. Quick guest: reviewed import or manually create/link; no automatic identity merge. Quick invitations: approved template and eligible route, explicit send. Quick production: checklist and owners. Quick hospitality: aggregate counts without sensitive guest attributes. Quick forms: approved versioned preset. Quick reports: standard authorized projections. Guided native/Compose installer uses same validation/protected host commands as advanced; dry-run no writes. Safe synthetic previews/training use fictional records and local capture, no production clone or actual external sends. Usability target AES-AC-27: median ≤120 seconds, ≤4 required steps over 30 representative trained-operator trials; report p95, errors and task success. It is a proposed measurement, not an achieved benchmark.

<a id="b13-booking"></a>
## B13-BOOKING — Venue catalogue, commercial lifecycle and disruption

### B13-BOOK-01 Catalogue and reservations

Provider owns sites, rooms, resource/equipment/service types, quantities/units, calendars/closures, setup/teardown/rehearsal buffers, maintenance, capacity and permitted inventory policies. Distinguish physical inventory, count-based reusable resources, staff/personnel availability, consumables and commercial service products. A proposal/availability preview is not a hold or confirmed reservation. Holds are time-bounded, expire/explicitly release through owning commands; booking confirmation converts exactly eligible holds in one transaction after current capacity/conflict check. For discrete resources enforce overlap exclusion; for pooled quantities lock appropriate stable parent and calculate active overlap using authoritative UTC times; reject race where sum would exceed approved capacity. Use stable IDs, tenant-qualified FKs, effective-dated/revisioned configuration and durable reservation history. Do not release unrelated reservation or confirm from EPW task/form/booking link. Existing reservation commands and migration integrity remain authoritative.

### B13-BOOK-02 Booking intake and review

Localized published booking form revision pins field schema, allowed field types, stable IDs, answers, customer locale, required/optional validation and privacy notice. Public inquiry submits a bounded request without staff account where enabled; abuse protection, idempotency and safe receipt. It does not reserve space or create an event/confirmed booking. Staff assigned inquiry queue: inspect, request clarification, add authorized notes/history, record source, convert reviewed inquiry to draft or use explicit manual/direct draft. Keep requester, contracting/paying party, provider, organizer and operator distinct. Draft revisions support date/space/resource alternatives, service lines, quantities, approved price/tax/discount policy, validity and commercial snapshots. Revision changes require stale-offer guard; prior issued offers historical, explicitly withdraw/supersede rather than rewrite. Offer approval, issue/delivery, customer acceptance/rejection and booking confirmation independent. Public `offer_accept` capability is high-entropy opaque, purpose/revision/contact scoped, expiring and consumed atomically only by explicit decision. GET/preview bot never consumes. Customer decision requires active issued revision and valid eligibility; concurrent accept/reject at most one authoritative decision. Delivery failure does not rewrite issued offer or customer decision.

### B13-BOOK-03 Commercial policy and confirmation

Versioned price list and immutable published revisions, effective date/venue/service applicability, no silent rate replacement. Organization tax profiles and jurisdiction-neutral calculation rules: explicit inclusive/exclusive treatment, currency/decimal/minor-unit rules and rounding; line and adjustment allocations use pinned recorded policy, validated totals; do not guess actual GHB rates or fiscal treatment. Authorization separates catalogue author, publisher, offer issuer, approver and confirmer; policy-defined thresholds and required approval, no unauthorized self-approval. Effective confirmation locks eligible draft/offer/customer decision/approval/holds, validates latest/pinned facts and capacity, writes confirmed booking, party snapshots, commercial/price/tax/cancellation policy, reservation and status/audit/outbox atomically. Failure leaves no partial effects. New price/tax/form/cancellation revision cannot reinterpret confirmed commercial history. Recorded charges/payment evidence/manual settlements are separate from offered or contracted amounts; no payment processing/refund implied. Booking-only workflow has independent readiness and scope.

### B13-BOOK-04 Cancellation, amendments and disruption

Versioned policy supports eligible confirmed booking, request-only, approval-required or allowed self-service modes with pinned terms; preview explicit reservation and commercial consequences without mutation, reason and current authority. External booking-action capabilities high-entropy hashed, revocable/expiry/purpose/booking/contact scoped. Request submission uses bounded action and idempotency; status capability separately read-only. Staff review, return for changes, approve/reject/withdraw, execution require lifecycle and authority. Approval is not effective cancellation; execution atomically releases eligible reservations exactly once, appends immutable effects/commercial consequences and follow-up obligations, and does not execute money movement. Amendment/postponement revalidate replacement availability and preserve old revisions/terms; no silent release before reviewed decision. Organizer-owned event change requests, approved event decisions, affected session outcomes and publication independent from venue booking decision. Provider append-only notice may inform linked event only via explicit allowed projection; recording a notice does not send, acknowledge or cancel anything. Public summary and affected times may be shared, operational/private commercial details remain restricted. Event-owned receipt acknowledgment is first attributed receipt only, not resolution, consent or business approval. Source grant revocation blocks new projection, retains historical intentionally shared receipt under event authority. CID uses separately reviewed notice intent and evidence; EPW issue board proposes action only.

<a id="b13-events"></a>
## B13-EVENTS — Event and session lifecycle, production planning and readiness

### B13-EVT-01 Event/session aggregate

Use existing event, schedule revision, session and capability revision/override aggregates. Bilingual titles/codes, owner, timezone, schedule, venue reference/snapshot, event configuration, optional modules and status. Draft/planning, approval, publication, start, completion/close, archive and cancel/postpone/reschedule use owning lifecycle commands; enforce valid transition, actor/reason/time, expected revision and required policy, no Draft→Closed shortcut. Session-specific lifecycle and timing separate; event decision records affected sessions. A live event may change only through approved new revision/operational change record; prior plans remain intact. Association to a local booking requires exact event and booking management; cross-party requires accepted exact booking link grant. An identical active association returns original ID after current authority recheck; changed meaning, ended or revoked association requires correction, not reactivation. Association never reserves resources or implies disclosure. End is attributed with immutable provenance; event-owned metadata remains visible to authorized event managers after source grant revocation.

### B13-EVT-02 EPW planning, tasks, schedule and resources

EPW provides per-event production plan revisions, milestones and responsibility/task references, checklist, timeline/Gantt, run-of-show cues, staffing/shifts and preparation/equipment/service readiness. Reuse existing responsibility/delegated task and reservation authorities; no parallel task or booking source. Task status, scheduled vs actual timestamps, owner/assignee, due date, evidence, escalation, blocking reason, handover and corrections are separate facts. Dependency edges typed and bounded, no cycle, calculate critical path/slack from declared durations/working calendar and time zone; explain blocked and unresolved prerequisites without auto-closing tasks. Validate graph/revision on edit, handle concurrent cycle creation under lock, compute asynchronously for large models with pinned inputs; no holding transaction during calculation. Schedule changes show downstream impact and require explicit review of affected resource/time conflicts, especially overlapping staff shifts, buffers and dependencies. Planned shift is not attendance/payroll. Programme/run-of-show planned vs actual cues, skip/delay/complete and versioned changes; guest-visible published programme separate from internal production and restricted tasks. Disruption may trigger reviewed alternatives, not automatic rescheduling/booking changes.

### B13-EVT-03 Constrained approvals, reusable templates and recurrence

Approval designer uses typed allowlisted owning-domain adapters and immutable policy revisions (scope, reviewers, sequential/parallel steps, threshold/quorum, separation of duty, required evidence, deadlines, escalation/substitution). Cannot relax a mandatory commercial, allocation, event, privacy or access guard; no arbitrary script, SQL or approval-generated authority. Review digest binds exact subject, current actor, configuration and source revisions; stale/incomplete/expired approval blocks execution, no automatic approval on timeout or reassignment. One decision per authorized step/idempotency key; actual execution remains explicit owning command. Preserve existing accepted domain policy semantics and audit. Templates clone only explicitly safe configuration (capabilities, checklists, categories, layouts/constraints by approved ref, published content/roles by valid preset), not private data or prior decisions. Bounded recurring series preview occurrence IDs, IANA timezone/DST, exceptions, conflict and intended scope; each occurrence distinct event/draft or booking with its own review/reservation, no unlimited generation, no silent copy of confirmed holds/credentials/guests. Series edits preserve past occurrences and review affected future instances; concurrent creation idempotent.

### B13-EVT-04 CDI and ordinary operational issues

External prerequisite coordination only: requirement type/authority, responsible party/coordinator, request/submission date and optional reference, scheduled/due date, state/history, authorized completion receipt, restricted optional references/attachments, readiness gate according to configured policy. External authority performs any inspection; no internal CDI inspection workflow, police personnel allocation, procedures, findings, tactical material or claims of official clearance. Ordinary operational issue board links affected areas/tasks/plans/services and limited context; assign, acknowledge, escalate, resolve or close with history. Material changes record initiator, reason/category, affected IDs, before/after plan references, proposed/accepted actor, output impact and raised/assessing/proposed/approved/applied/rejected/closed status. Sensitive reasons restricted; show only action needed to operational staff. EOC reflects readiness and authorized alerts, never fabricates completion. Handover and retrospective preserve open obligations, accountable follow-up and lesson records; close does not silently mark tasks complete or erase data.

<a id="b13-registry"></a>
## B13-REGISTRY — Persistent identity, event participation and import/export

### B13-REG-01 Data separation and roster

Organization Person owns reusable name/title/salutation/organization/delegation, preferred names, language, permitted contact methods/address, identifiers/source references and provenance, internal labels and relationships with classification/retention. Event participation links Person to event and pins event-specific identity/name, category/subcategory, status, groups/tags/roles, allocation preferences and rules, optional custom fields, restricted notes/service needs, invitation, RSVP, eligibility, allocation, credential and attendance projections. One person may participate in many events without duplicate identity; master update never rewrites approved/historical event snapshot; explicit event override separate. Archived/merged/anonymized lifecycle with authorized correction, retention/hold, no uncontrolled cascade. Registry access and event-only access separate. Sensitive attributes optional, purpose-limited and field-authorized, never necessary for ordinary participation unless genuine approved operational need. Internal Registry labels stable IDs and retired assignments retained; event categories and restricted tags separate; no label leak to guest/venue. Mutual/directed relationships preserve kind/direction, no self/duplicate active tuple; group hierarchy and allocation relation/role preferences distinct. Person profile cannot imply grant or authorization.

### B13-REG-02 Import, match and bulk actions

Native CRUD/search/filter/sort/group/saved views and history; imported rows remain editable as native records. CSV/XLSX upload, bounded size/worksheet/header selection, mapped fields/locale validation, preview row-level errors, normalized name or exact permitted source-reference match, separate Registry candidate vs existing event participation; explicit create/reuse/link/update/distinct person choice, no silent match/merge. Never compare or expose fields outside authority. Reviewed commit binds batch, current revisions, source refs and selected resolution; idempotent, atomic defined batch/row scope and receipts, downloadable diagnostics. Bulk category/status/tag/group/archive changes permissioned, revision-checked, all-or-nothing where current command specifies, explicit preview and result. Formula-safe CSV/XLSX export uses applied filters before pagination, separate export and sensitive field authority, bounded private job/artifact, audited. Registry and event reports use event snapshot vs master semantics, no implicit data mixing.

### B13-REG-03 Supervised merge/restoration and encryption identity

ADR 0009, 0012, 0013, 0018, 0019 define exact supported merge resolution. Review actor-bound source/destination active identities and versions, current contacts/reference/label/relationship sets, explicit transfer permissions and separate choices. Preserve source row marked merged, original IDs and snapshots; closed non-overlapping events retained; unsupported overlap/open-event histories, incoming merge chains, conflicting primary/duplicate contacts, unsupported identifiers, duplicate/self-link relationships, overlapping labels or excessive assignments block pending separately reviewed correction. Contact IDs, encrypted values, consent, primary flags and verification preserved; organization/kind binding unchanged on same-tenant ownership transfer. Source references preserve `encryption_person_id` (original encryption identity), same-org FK; ciphertext replacement sets current identity; ownership-only move does not change binding. Private transfer journals store versioned canonical hashes and references, not private copied values; timestamp epoch and hex bytes stable, no reconstructing removed records. Label transfer preserves original author/time/ID and retirement, no silent union; active relationship transfer preserves ID, kind/direction, original time/author, canonical mutual UUID ordering, ended history remains. Parent locks stable UUID order plus definition/current row locks; relationship end can change evidence without parent revision, so current fingerprint mandatory. Recheck authority even cached replay. Restore unchanged records using existing command; changed/removed contact/reference use actor-bound reviewed current-state restoration, explicitly choose return/keep/acknowledge removed; revalidate exact current state and required permissions, removed remains absent, atomically reactivate source and restore selected unchanged/current data, separate correction history. Changed transferred labels/relationships remain blocked where no reviewed correction exists; do not invent fallback or resurrect removed data. No rewrite of event snapshots/invitations/RSVP. Full ADR constraints are normative, not this paragraph alone.

<a id="b13-spatial"></a>
## B13-SPATIAL — Venue geometry, source artifacts and capacities

### B13-SPA-01 Generalized model and editor

Reusable versioned venue/site/building/level/room/space hierarchy, optional levels for simple rooms, separate booking resource identity and spatial resource geometry. Layout types banquet with tables and positions, theatre/cinema fixed rows, standing/count zones, prayer/floor rows, mixed and custom. Normalize plan-space coordinates independent of screen resolution, calibrate scale, source dimensions/transforms, units/rotation/viewport, layers and labels. SVG-native editor supports import background PDF/image/SVG/workbook, draw polygons/rooms/zones, tables, seats, rows/segments, positions, features, move/resize/rotate/label/duplicate/snap/align, undo-safe edits and keyboard-accessible equivalents. Stable resource IDs, parent-scoped visible labels and composed locator; repeated display numbers permitted across different scopes, no ambiguous exports. Allocatable resource distinct from container, wall/pillar/passage/entrance/stairs/lift/footwear/service/special reserved area/lectern/minber, blocked/unavailable/restricted/staff-only features. Visibility separate public/staff/private source layers. A simple space can use capacity-only workflow without drawing.

### B13-SPA-02 Capacity and source onboarding

Maintain physical maximum, operational maximum, approved event limit, assignable count, reserved capacity and blocked/unavailable resources, provenance and confirming authorized venue representative. No summing overlapping area annotations or treating source number as approved capacity; validate hierarchy, count/capacity consistency, occupancy and allowed resource sets. Source original immutable private artifact with hash, media/worksheet metadata, rendered comparison and reviewer; create native traced objects with source cell/range/region/extraction method/reviewer where feasible. No blind auto-conversion from spreadsheet cells/merged regions/colors/numbers into chairs, live allocations or capacities. Review source-render alignment, labels, repeated numbers, special/non-allocatable features, capacities and safe layers before publish. Revision pin/copy into event; later master template change cannot change approved event automatically. Preserve source references and native revision history, new source artifact for new version, sanitized guest projection independent.

GHB reference portfolio: large/medium/small halls and separately modelled mosque/prayer space; exact hierarchy and ownership/capacity not inferred. The original workbook references red 74, green 150, blue 140, Mahfil Donji 14, Mahfil Gornji 10, Maksura Lijeva 10, Maksura Desna 10 as unconfirmed source annotations, not approved total or limits. Confirm overlap, function, accessible paths and actual operational limit. Retain minber, pillars, entrance, passage and footwear as typed features; optional row and numbered floor position with scope, no forced chair model. Use synthetic examples in code/tests; keep actual private source artifacts outside Git. The workbook is not included here; the historical blueprint source preserves its observations and required validation.

<a id="b13-allocation"></a>
## B13-ALLOCATION — Manual, rules-based and advisory optimization

### B13-ALLOC-01 Resource and assignment invariants

Allocation links event/session/guest or group, resource or capacity pool, plan revision, effective period, status, method, lock/reason, rule/run ref, actor/time. Model individual seat/floor position, row/segment/block, table container/open-seat scope, zone/standing/capacity pool and reserved/accessible capacity. No double-booked precise resource; no conflicting active allocation for participant or overlap across sessions except explicitly modeled legitimate multi-participant/staff cases; capacity never exceeded; inactive/blocked/unavailable not assigned; correct event/room/resource/revision and tenant. Lock and validate all affected resources/pools in stable order; concurrent assignments cannot exceed count cap. Zone-only does not invent precise seat. Manual move fast path uses same authority/validation and atomic revisioned history.

### B13-ALLOC-02 Constraint model and solver

Modes fully manual, rules/category-driven, automatic proposal, with locks, hybrid adjustment and targeted reflow. Non-overrideable invariants above; configurable hard constraints: permitted/excluded building/level/room/zone/resource set, together/avoid group scope, separation, accessibility, reserved pools, protected locks. Explicit rule subject and target person/group/category query, scope same resource/table/row/zone/room/level/site or calibrated distance, effective period/session, direction/symmetry, strength, weight/priority and restricted reason. Group separation can require distinct resource count, not arbitrary unseen pairwise expansion. Soft preferences weighted/explainable: family/delegation proximity, preferred areas, category distribution, legitimate authorized composition, protocol placement, accessible/distance and balance/fill/minimum moves. Do not infer sensitive characteristics or precedence. Priority: system invariants, active hard rules, locks/protected assignments, weighted soft objectives, deterministic tie breaks. Infeasible returns meaningful conflict report, no silent downgrades. Human may revise configurable rule/unlock/add approved capacity with reason; never override invariant. For fixed model version, seed, limits and reproducibility configuration record solver metadata, feasibility/objective breakdown and diagnostic. OR-Tools CP-SAT C++ isolated controlled worker behind validated versioned JSON contract; no mandatory Python daemon or solver-driven DB writes. Distinguish OPTIMAL, FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE, UNKNOWN/TIMEOUT and INVALID; timeout is not infeasibility. Async proposal input captures all revisions/locks/resources/rules; validate output independently, compare before/after moved/unchanged/unassigned/conflicts and reject stale model. Authorized explicit human commit only (ADR 0003); proposal cannot become active on job completion.

### B13-ALLOC-03 Plan revisions, publication and reflow

Working/proposed/submitted/approved/published/superseded immutable revision lifecycle; approved plan pins exact event/venue/resource/rules/assignments and source facts, actor/time/revision ID. Publish atomically current revision and supersede previous, outbox event committed with domain facts; staff viewer lists alphabetically, by table/row/zone/room, unassigned/conflict/capacity status and map/print version. Guest-safe map/locator separately generated. New arrival/cancellation, VIP/delegation/constraint change, blocked resource, capacity/room disruption or ordinary incident triggers targeted reflow against current revision; lock unaffected by default, identify impact, diagnostics, review moves and approval, commit new revision, update authorized views and configured notice task. Old outputs marked superseded where possible; do not automatically reissue invitation/admission credential merely because seat changes; re-render/refresh/reprint vs explicit replacement separate under AGIS/TDS/CID. Current lookup uses current approved destination, print identifies revision; no publishing draft solver output. Operational change history/audit and privacy-safe reason codes.

<a id="b13-forms"></a>
## B13-FORMS — FRS typed forms, registration, accreditation and submissions

### B13-FRS-01 Schema, authoring and publication

FRS provides a purpose registry for booking inquiry, public or invitation-only registration, accreditation, RSVP questionnaire, staff/vendor application/evidence, hospitality and internal requests, feedback and other reviewed purposes. Reuse booking form revision/authoring/runtime contract and existing RSVP policies. Common UI/schema validation/rendering does not make all submissions one unrestricted aggregate or universal write API. Each purpose declares owning handler, permitted subject/actor, input types/fields, data classification, limits, workflow, capability mode, allowed mapping and result projection. Stable field UUID/code, locale label/help/error and option IDs, typed text/number/date/time/choice/multiple-choice/contact/consent/file and reviewed structured values, required/default/range/length/format constraints, bounded multi-step and conditional visibility/requiredness. Conditional expressions must be deterministic, typed, acyclic, bounded, side-effect-free; no arbitrary JavaScript, SQL, URL fetch or external widget code. Server re-evaluates applicability and validation; hidden/inapplicable values cannot silently override owning policy. Existing form definitions/revisions retain semantics; migration compatibility, purpose mapping and legacy runtime audit precede generalized authoring. Safe preset library and visual component/ordering designer, keyboard alternative, synthetic preview, publish authorized immutable revision, explicit retire/replacement and grace policy. TDS governs appearance/brand assets, not validation or field mapping. FRS author cannot automatically publish or view submissions.

### B13-FRS-02 Intake, capacity and review

Public routes explicitly enabled and purpose-scoped, stable form/revision resolution or distinct high-entropy capability for invitation/subject; no user identity assumption from contact value. Staff-assisted paper/phone/in-person capture records source, actual actor, received and recording time; no-email participation supported. Draft/resumable submission if configured, bounded expiry and private storage; validation on submit, review exact published revision, consent notice/version, idempotency key bound to input and actor/capability. Confirm receipt only after durable commit, non-mutating resolution; receipt/status capability read-only and minimal. Invalid/stale/retired forms return safe error or approved grace policy; no reinterpreting answers under changed schema. Protect public abuse with rate/size/concurrency budgets, abuse controls and safe retry, not account/guest enumeration. Uploads stage quarantined private objects with size/count/type and content checks, malware handling and approved sanitization, immutable content hash; authorize before upload, review, download and commit; do not expose unscanned file or fetch arbitrary URL. Expire orphan files safely; legal hold and retention reviewed. Never attach real identity/credential in synthetic preview.

Submission received, under review, returned, accepted/rejected/withdrawn and applied/result are distinct state dimensions with immutable review/decision history. Review inbox assigned with exact scope, approve/return/reject, reason, revisions, evidence and current authority; apply purpose-specific domain command only with explicit reviewed mapping and idempotent receipt. Match Registry using permitted evidence; no automatic duplicate merge. Registration approval/waitlist/eligibility separate from participation/RSVP, invitation, accreditation, admission QR and attendance. Capacity reservation for registration/waitlist is a specifically scoped authoritative eligibility rule, not seating allocation or venue booking. Lock event/session registration pool and review current counts, atomically commit approval/eligible reservation if required; competing approvals cannot exceed cap. Waitlist ordered by explicit configured policy, visible to authorized staff; promotion reviewed and rechecked for current eligibility/capacity/time, no automatic invite/QR. Accreditation decision records allowed purpose, category, approved access scope/expiry and separate revision; never creates platform/staff privilege. Feedback may be anonymous only with verified non-linkability policy; do not claim anonymous where identifying data/logs retained. Vendor/staff applications or submissions do not grant roles or mark deliverable complete merely on receipt. HPG service requests remain requests. CID sends approved receipt/decision/reminder using purpose-limited contact and current consent; failed/uncertain delivery does not alter submission state. RAI report counts distinguish received, reviewed, approved, applied, waitlisted and actual attendance. FRS annex contains detailed field limits, schema/API, failure semantics and 32 acceptance cases.

<a id="b13-invitation"></a>
## B13-INVITATION — Invitation, RSVP and guest portal lifecycle

Maintain invitation identity/revision and policy reference, invitation capability state, distribution attempts/evidence, RSVP response history and event participation eligibility independently. Event policy version includes response choices (accepted/declined/tentative nonempty allowed subset), absolute deadline in effective IANA timezone, response change policy, late staff override, approved template/channels, reminder schedule/quiet hours, optional verification/questions. Existing publication (ADR 0016) locks event, verifies event lifecycle/expected policy/zone, inserts immutable next revision, retains current issued policy and response history; no implicit module activation, link, send or reminder. Preserve existing deadlines as instants across other settings and DST, reject nonexistent times. Current invitation issuance validates participant eligibility, effective approved schedule, policy, allowed content and authority. Remove universal email requirement in scheduled CID work: issue valid invitation without electronic destination, then separate explicit permitted delivery/share/print/phone action. Maintain stable invitation/response identity; resend/distribution does not revoke/reissue token or reset RSVP. Replacement explicit revoke/reissue reason and historical proof. Existing email issue routes remain compatible until reviewed successor.

Invitation capability random high entropy (at least 256 bits per existing design), opaque bearer scoped to one event participation and purpose; hashed lookup at rest, encrypted transient secret only where existing controlled delivery/render workflow needs it, no plaintext logs/db, no third-party analytics/referrer. Distinct from admission QR and guest portal credential/session. Link transport via URL fragment where existing public flow, TLS, remove from browser history, no reusable token in ordinary history, no external shortener. Resolution non-mutating (including preview/bot/GET); resolve POST when token transport needs it, scoped session/explicit response confirmation. Validity/expiry/revocation separate from response deadline. Verify current policy/link/eligibility, rate-limit and prevent enumeration; append RSVP history with actual receipt and recording time, source and actor, current projection; changes only per pinned policy, late staff override authorized and reasoned. Staff may record phone, in-person, email, written, representative, staff entry or other permitted channel independently of email/token, explicit corrections append not overwrite. Do not consume link or infer attendance on read. Guest Portal optional per event, window/purpose/locale/brand/allowed content policy. Own event/session information, current approved personal destination (venue/building/level/room/zone/row/place as applicable), sanitized map/text/accessible directions and approved contact/updates, no public guest directory. Dedicated portal access scope, distinct from QR, no automatic profile edits; device/session expiry, capability revocation and stale revision handling. Guest can receive configured seat change notice only after approved publication; no disclosure of other guest or sensitive reason. Portal may work with no individual allocation and provides honest zone-only/general directions. Intranet or public policy as enabled; staff workflow not dependent on public route. Info Pult is separate supervised/verified station projection; AGIS below.

<a id="b13-hospitality"></a>
## B13-HOSPITALITY — HPG optional hospitality, protocol and guest services

HPG coordinates optional service taxonomy, estimates/headcounts, requests, reviewed arrangements, capacity, assignments and actual fulfillment. Use event/session participation and approved group/delegation references; no duplicate identity aggregate. Aggregate refreshments/headcount can work without guest list. Categorize requested, estimated, confirmed, allocated, fulfilled, cancelled, unmet and unknown with explicit source and unit; no false fulfillment from approval or task completion. Catering menu/service type, meal/service period, confirmed quantities, special dietary requirements collected only where operationally needed, allergen/dietary flags verified by responsible supplier rather than inferred or medical judgment; guest-facing information truthful and no guarantee of safety from platform. Supplier receives aggregate quantities and minimum actionable specific instructions only when necessary and authorized, not ordinary access to private guest notes or entire Registry. Accessibility assistance requested and reviewed, verified available route/resource/escort, separate assistance and seating preferences; unknown/not verified visibly distinct; never infer disability or diagnose. Store sensitive reason under field-level protection, optional minimum actionable instruction; guests can choose assisted/manual channel. No public kiosk/passive display or supplier unrestricted diagnosis, dietary or profile data.

Delegation/party leads, representatives and companions with explicit authority and event participation; not every companion automatically eligible; avoid duplicate attendance/guest links. Protocol precedence/placement rules are tenant-approved versioned data, never inferred from nationality, religion, gender, title or VIP label; soft/hard scope passed to allocation only after authorized review with feasibility/integrity constraints, restricted reason omitted in general projection. Hosts/escorts and assigned reception tasks use EPW ownership and explicit scoped staff access. Transport arrival/departure, vehicle or pickup references and accommodation rooming references optional, external arrangements recorded with authority/limited retention; no dispatch, booking/payment or tracking system. Guest/staff/vendor service requests through FRS or manual, stage review, availability/capacity verification, assign responsible provider/task, confirm or decline, record delivery/fulfillment evidence separately. Lock resource/quantity scope, validate concurrent capacity and existing owning reservation; cancellation/changes require reviewed impact and authorized release, no duplicate allocation or automatic financial consequence. Reconcile actual count vs planned, unmet service and exception; notify guest/staff only through CID with approved minimal content. TDS prints private approved service artifacts, RAI publishes privacy-safe aggregates including small-cell/inference controls. Audit protected reads and changes, export authority and expiration, legal hold/retention. Close/disable requires handover or block unresolved obligation; corrections append history. See HPG full annex for all 16 requirements, 31 cases and quality envelope.

<a id="b13-admission"></a>
## B13-ADMISSION — AGIS stations, QR admission, information and print

### B13-AGIS-01 Station taxonomy and device authority

Six supported station modes: entrance/gate scanner, self-service Info Pult, staffed Info Pult, seating assistance, printing station and passive information display. OAC owns tenant device/profile/layout/pairing and permitted hardware, staff roles; EOC event/session assignments, station health/status, anchor/location, operating window, allowed actions and fallback policy; PAC governs deployment/service/support. Constrained Station Designer uses typed allowlisted widgets/brand assets, guest-safe projection per mode, approved profiles/revisions; no arbitrary script, unrestricted URL or public directory. Staff actor/session and device credential are separate and both scope-checked where applicable; passive display/device cannot gain staff privilege. Enroll through reviewed short-lived single-use pairing, exact organization/event/session/station/device mode, credential rotation/revocation and expiry, heartbeat/status, context clearing and assignment conflict handling. No host access by device. Device key storage, offline capability and secure clock policy reviewed; scoped browser/PWA camera permission and HID scanner/manual fallback, supported printers/browser print, optional reviewed scoped bridge only, no arbitrary device command. UI locale/keyboard/touch/zoom, visible degraded state and safe failure.

### B13-AGIS-02 Credentials, scan and attendance

Separate admission credential with opaque cryptographically random token/lookup ref, scoped to event/participation and intended session policy, no readable PII/name/seat/category/notes. Store hash/keyed digest and minimum issuance/revoke/expiry facts, one current valid credential per defined scope; replacement explicit revoke/issue with reason/authority and preserved history. Bearer possession is not verified identity; where configured, independently verify minimal required information through authorized procedure. Check-in command validates actual actor/device/station assignment, current event/session eligibility, credential scope/expiry/revoke and existing attendance under locks, request idempotency and unique station attempt identity. Valid initial arrival records authoritative fact exactly once despite duplicate scans, lost responses or concurrent gates. Return duplicate/invalid/revoked/expired/wrong event/blocked/manual review outcomes without disclosing other guest. Current attendance projected from append-only arrival/departure/manual arrival/correction history as configured, separate RSVP/registration. Manual lookup permissioned, minimal search and correction; lookup alone no check-in; explicit manual admission/correction requires reason and authority, records actor/time/prior state and idempotent receipt. Exceptions and supervisor review preserve safety, no bypass of non-overrideable capacity/eligibility policy. Realtime multiple gates synchronized and stale indicators, no false duplicate or count inflation. Scan displays current allowed destination not old QR content, no sensitive reasons.

### B13-AGIS-03 Info Pult, wayfinding and controlled print

Self-service kiosk verifies appropriate separate purpose-bound capability or pass plus independent minimal verification per policy, only own current permitted event details/destination and guest-safe sanitized map, not unrestricted portal or attendance mutation. Idle timeout/auto privacy reset and cleared history/session/cache; no public search across guests. Staffed info/seating assistance verifies operator scope and purpose, approved minimal fields and authorized referrals. Station physical anchor defines route start; use sanitized navigable public geometry entrances/corridors/stairs/lifts/accessibility edge metadata, reviewed path/text instructions or approved static fallback, no indoor tracking or fabricated precise seat; unavailable/unverified routes clearly marked, accessible alternative where verified. Guest portal phone credential separate. Passive displays publish only approved programme/welcome/session/general direction/status, no personal list, restricted prerequisites, internal alerts, credential or guest-specific data. Printing uses TDS approved template/content/brand revision; print queue receipt distinguishes render, generated, submitted, physical handover/unknown. Reprint exact historical artifact, refresh/re-render current approved content and explicit credential replacement are distinct; no automatic issue/revoke/send/attendance or blind retry after uncertain print. Controlled private artifact, disposal/expiry and operator audit; printer outage leaves core workflow functional.

### B13-AGIS-04 Online-first, degraded and bounded offline

Online authoritative mode primary; policy can allow encrypted bounded deferred capture (provisional, not confirmed) or time-limited local validation package per Blueprint §13.4 and AGIS. Offline package minimal necessary scoped dataset, signed/versioned/encrypted, valid device/assignment, expiry/time validity, no unrestricted Registry. Queue unique attempt IDs, bounded storage/retention, local receipt and visible provisional/unknown state. Online revocation immediate for server; offline cannot promise instantaneous revocation — lease/expiry/reconnect policy limits risk, disallow offline where required; device revocation stops new online actions and cached package expires, reconcile all queued attempts on reconnect in authoritative transaction, duplicate/conflict/invalid review, no double arrival, no automatic override. Synchronize current published allocation/revocation snapshot before fresh authoritative operation, no hidden offline success. Reconnect stale/limited warning, privacy reset, delete expired local data per policy. Gate, Info Pult, printing and display failure policies distinct; no mandatory external provider to run local gates. AGIS §17 detailed mode matrix and all 40 cases preserved in annex.

<a id="b13-content"></a>
## B13-CONTENT — TDS template library, brand and rendering

One template/revision library and purpose/output assignments: rich-text WYSIWYG for structured content, visual responsive block email, precision graphical card/invitation/print designer, reusable assets/components and starter templates. User selects Quick Start approved preset or full editor; purpose restrictions not arbitrary executable document code. Support localized subject/body, safe plain text, responsive HTML with text fallback, graphical dimensions/units/pages, positions/layers/grid/alignment/rotation/print margins/bleed as applicable, fonts/graphics/logos, typed dynamic variables and purpose-specific QR placeholders; preview realistic long names/diacritics/empty/overflow/locale, approved sample values no real credentials. Field binding allowlist by purpose and field classification; required variables, allowed formatting/defaults and validation; never arbitrary SQL, property path into confidential data, script/iframe/external tracking asset. Output types explicit, no silent conversion/fallback to legacy content on render error. Use event > venue > org > platform brand and immutable assets/revisions. Shared assets private by default, sanitized MIME/size/SVG/fonts/license/metadata, protected fetch no SSRF; versioned upload, retirement no historical deletion. Templates draft/edit/review/publish/retire, revision optimistic concurrency, role separation between designer/publisher/recipient-reader/sender. Publication or rendering alone never sends or issues invitation/QR. Independent jobs for preview/render/batch/print/send; immutable input manifest (purpose, source data/snapshot, template/brand/asset revisions, locale, renderer version, page geometry, digest). Server authoritative deterministic rendering and bounded job/CPU/memory/time, no browser-only trusted result; safe HTML sanitization, restricted renderer process, no unrestricted network/file access, private encrypted storage and scoped short-lived download authority rechecked. Preview/test separate from live send; synthetic verified test recipient and non-live marker/link, audit/rate limits. Actual send reviewed fixed audience and current eligibility/authority, CID route and cost; no silent rerender or stale content after approval. Retain exact historical issued artifact manifest/bytes per policy. Printed outputs identify revisions and current/superseded state; use separate station print/reissue rules. Shared TDS with FRS presentation (not field schema), RAI PDF appearance (not query), AGIS station/display widgets, EPW schedule/HPG artifacts and CID channel content. Source annex and current repository version carry 16 requirements and 25 cases; full review-only details subject to reconciliation decision below.

<a id="b13-communications"></a>
## B13-COMMUNICATIONS — CID unified intent, routing, distribution and evidence

### B13-CID-01 Purpose, provider and channel independence

Separate domain intent/trigger, audience, reviewed content and policy, route, attempt, provider result, verified delivery and recipient action. Applies to booking inquiry/offer/confirmation/amendment/cancellation, commercial notices, event invitations/RSVP, schedule/reconfirmation/disruption, guest portal/seat/pass/arrival, staff/vendor tasks/approvals, collaboration, forms/service receipts, report schedules, platform/organization/security/service alerts and post-event feedback. Each purpose declares owner, allowed recipient projection, required consent/legal policy, allowed templates/channels, capability and lifecycle, not generic send privilege. Reuse current event notification, booking offer and invitation delivery queues, IDs, commands, encryption, leases, attempt history and signed Resend evidence; initial shared read projection and adapter wrap, not parallel engines or duplicate sends. Audit all three populated queues/states/permissions before any convergence migration; old APIs and delivery identities compatible. Existing SMTP plaintext/password or no auth and Resend callbacks are actual foundation, not evidence of HTTP/OAuth/messaging support.

Adapter registry typed capabilities per provider/account (channel, auth, send format/size/segment, idempotency window, delivery/read evidence, webhook/poll, quotas/regions, test, failure semantics). Required email SMTP with TLS/verified cert, STARTTLS/implicit and authorized relay; rich multipart HTML/text/attachments only approved; HTTP email API and OAuth-supported providers with real account approval, token expiry/refresh, scope and state/PKCE as applicable, secrets encrypted write-only. SMS gateway official API and segmentation/cost, phone normalization, eligibility and opt-in. WhatsApp official business platform with approved account/templates and service window policies; Viber official business messages vs subscribed bot distinctly; optional Telegram only after recipient starts/binds bot, no arbitrary phone targeting. Web push opt-in subscription/device/browser permission, secure endpoint/key handling, expiry/revoke, privacy-safe payload, provider acceptance not read. In-app scoped authorized inbox distinct delivery evidence. Manual secure personalized link/file sharing, PDF/image/printed invitation/card, postal/courier/handover, telephone/staff-recorded outcomes. Guest without any electronic contact supported; manual distribution is recorded evidence, no provider verification claim. No mandatory paid provider or external service for core workflows; local capture/manual and intranet work. Provider restrictions/registration, pricing, regional/account availability, auth and legal policy must be verified at actual adapter implementation, not inferred from research.

### B13-CID-02 Provider configuration, consent and campaign review

OAC manages multiple organization-owned provider profiles/revisions/sender identities, allowed purpose/channel, readiness/test/disable, write-only credential rotation, callback keys and quotas; PAC optionally grants shared service to explicit tenants, allowed purpose/sender/account, budgets and suspension. Account/secret isolation and safe egress/SSRF controls, no arbitrary provider endpoint or cross-tenant credentials. Store contact points with authorized verification, purpose/channel preferences, event override, consent/legal basis/provenance/withdrawal/suppression and verified representative authority. A phone/email value alone does not authorize messaging; preference not consent, respect purpose restrictions, quiet hours and opt-out. Use minimal recipient audience from approved participation/domain projection, not entire Registry. Campaign Designer fixed candidate set/rules, eligible/excluded counts/reasons, template/revision/locale/route and current contact/policy/sender/provider snapshot, scheduled/relative reminder window/timezone, estimated worst-case permitted cost including fallback, quota and budget. Test-send isolated synthetic approved destination, no live credential, separate from bulk. Preview digest binds actor, recipients, route strategy, content revisions, source facts, timing and cost, explicit approval (separation-of-duty per policy). Changed eligibility, contact, consent, source revision/content/provider policy or material price invalidates relevant approval or blocks affected delivery, never silent audience growth. Recheck current authority and eligibility at queue claim/dispatch; suppress on revoke/withdrawal. Allow explicit immediate/scheduled or relative to approved event/RSVP deadlines; UTC instants with IANA timezone/DST, quiet hours and cutoff, reminder count and dedupe, rescheduling invalidates stale planned send. Domain trigger cannot secretly send on publication; reviewed configured policy and authorization required. Cancellation prevents pending work but cannot retract already submitted external effects.

### B13-CID-03 Routing, retry, reconciliation and accounting

Preferred eligible channel, explicit multi-channel, approved fallback chain, manual review. Separate definite failure/nonacceptance from accepted but unknown delivery. Verified delivered/read stops ordinary fallback; no automatic fallback/retry on uncertain submission (provider may already have accepted), no opt-out circumvented by provider/channel switching. Only confirmed failure triggers approved alternate route after current consent, permission, cost and eligibility recheck. One logical intent per reviewed recipient/route/trigger/dedup key, canonical request hash and stable provider idempotency key/message ID where supported; explicit retry policy bounded, jitter/backoff, rate limit/Retry-After, lease claim and generation fence, safe handling timeout/crash/restore. Before network send persist attempt/correlation/reservation and check fence; no open transaction across network. Provider-specific idempotency guarantee verified, do not promise exactly once external send. Normalize queue/render/sending/submitted/provider accepted/delivered/bounced/failed/suppressed/uncertain/read (only verified) and manual printed/handed over/phone recorded states; attempts and evidence append-only, current projection respects valid transitions and contradictory event evidence. Authenticated callback (signature, replay/timestamp, body limits, account/attempt/message correlation, stable event ID/digest unique); never trust sender from payload alone, raw secrets/PII omitted from logs. Out-of-order/replayed/contradictory evidence preserved with safe reconciliation, unknown correlation quarantine; poll only allowed provider scope. Preserve signed Resend callback and stable pre-submission Message-ID uncertain resolution; operator reconciliation/explicit retry with reason, current authority and no false delivery status. Reserve cost/quota atomically with submission and allowed fallback maxima, integer minor units/decimal currency, per channel/provider/account/tenant/campaign window, rate/segment/attachment/print estimates vs actual provider verified charges; uncertain costs reserved pending review, release only evidence permits. Distinguish projected, reserved, submitted estimate, reconciled actual; no fictional cost or auto billing/payment. Queue recovery fences all uncertain work and reconciles before replay; independent core unaffected by provider outage. Role-scoped delivery history, cost/health/exclusion reports and audit; no ordinary history bearing capability URL or private body/recipient data. Detailed adapters, route/state matrices, schemas/APIs/limits, 48 cases in CID annex.

<a id="b13-cockpit"></a>
## B13-COCKPIT — Live EOC, authorized projections and interventions

Event cockpit is active operational workspace, not a passive unrestricted dashboard: current event/session, plan revision/status/freshness, capacity/allocated/unassigned/conflicts, RSVP and admission/attendance, arrival rate by entrance, task/readiness, station/device health, published map and affected areas, alerts/exception queue, activity timeline, restricted prerequisite status. Counts/drill-down consistent with approved metric definitions, distinguish operational real-time freshness from historical/estimated, no forbidden counts. Role workspaces for reception, gate, seating, floor/zone, provider, coordinator, guest services, production, management, vendor and prerequisite; all use same owning commands and permission rechecks; actionable minimal data, no inference of permissions from layout. Alert lifecycle raised/acknowledged/assigned/escalated/resolved/closed, severity/category/time/owner, references to source and authorized explanation, history; acknowledgment not resolution or audit deletion. Explicit interventions preview expected revision, impact, relevant constraints and reason, authorized commit, subsequent notification and output supersession; no bypass via cockpit. Timeline operational projection separate from append-only audit/security evidence. Real-time updates via transactional outbox with monotonic sequence/cursor scoped to tenant/event/authorized stream, small invalidation events not raw sensitive payload; authorize subscription and reconnection, expire/revoke stream access, gap detection/resnapshot, dedupe/version ordering; show stale/degraded/sync time and reload current authorized snapshot after reconnect. Avoid cache leak across role/context, no public internal streams; guest portal own projection only. Manual critical functions survive solver/provider/render outage. Use EPW for production tasks, HPG for service exceptions, AGIS for stations, RAI for metric definitions and CID for approved communications; not duplicate status stores.

<a id="b13-reporting"></a>
## B13-REPORTING — RAI reporting, analytics and intelligence

RAI offers standard reports, permissioned graphical report/dashboard designer, saved/versioned definitions, filters/grouping/sort/approved typed measures/calculations, chart/table accessibility, comparisons, private CSV/XLSX/PDF/print and scheduled distribution. Use typed dataset registry with owning read function, tenant/event/task scope, fields/classification, allowed join keys/cardinality, aggregation/suppression, units/currency/time basis, source freshness/snapshot, semantic version, allowed operations and required rights. No unrestricted SQL, arbitrary executable formula, external data join or autonomous predictive scoring/surveillance. Query compiler allowlist validates typed parameters, bounds rows/time/memory/cardinality/export and pagination, safe prepared queries/RLS; separate query/design/read/field/aggregate/export/schedule/download permissions, even preset metrics. Standard Quick Start report uses same pipeline, no bypass. Context-safe cache keyed by exact tenant/authorization/scope/filter/source revision/metric version; never reuse stale data after revocation; privacy-safe invalidation. Dashboard widget does not confer dataset rights; all counts/unknown values and drill-downs rechecked. Use privacy-safe small-cell suppression and complementary/differencing controls, protect restricted fields even aggregate across events, no bypass through filter or exports. No universal PAC guest or staff-performance ranking. Explicit retention, legal hold and audited artifact lifecycle; formula-injection-safe spreadsheets; TDS render pinned brand/template/locale and immutable report input/result manifest; authorized private artifact download expiry and reauthorization, no ordinary public URL. Scheduled report binds owner/approved service intent, scope/dataset/filters/locale/schedule/recipient/route and permission review at generation and delivery; CID evidence/uncertainty/budget applies, no blind replay after restore; recipient authorization for restricted artifact is independent of delivery, never automatically attach private exports to external message.

Metric catalogue must distinguish event-snapshot vs current Registry facts, current vs as-of/period/snapshot, timezone/cohort and denominator, unknown/suppressed/not applicable/zero; exact currency/unit and definition, source revision/observed time, provisional vs authoritative. Do not sum different currency without approved explicit conversion policy. Venue utilization numerator/denominator use defined approved availability windows and resource capacity; booking inquiry/draft/offer/confirmed/cancelled and price/tax/charges/payment evidence separate. Guest unique persons vs participation, submitted applications vs approved registration, RSVP vs confirmed admission, issued vs delivered and read only verified; allocation precise/zone/unassigned and conflicts based on current approved plan, not solver draft; authoritative arrival excludes duplicate/invalid/provisional scans; current present vs cumulative arrival explicit. Production planned/actual task status, overdue vs blocked, readiness denominator; HPG estimated/requested/confirmed/fulfilled counts and unit; CID estimated/reserved/reconciled costs, submission vs verified delivered and uncertain; event change/notice receipt vs business decision; privacy-safe support and job/health metrics. Report historical facts and definitions reproducible from pinned source snapshots; refresh creates new run rather than mutating past output. RAI standard reports include all Blueprint §26 families (guest by category/organization/delegation/tag, roster/duplicate review/cross-event history, RSVP, allocation by guest/table/row/seat/zone/capacity/unallocated/conflicts, card issue/reissue, check-in by time/entrance/no-shows/exceptions, revision/change, staff assignments/area/prerequisites/readiness, portal access and delivery, alert volume/timeline). Full RAI annex defines metric catalogue, jobs, API/data model, schedule, 35 cases.

<a id="b13-data"></a>
## B13-DATA — Unified logical data ownership, integrity and migration contract

The following registry names logical aggregates, not unapproved DDL. Audit existing migrations, `eogp` schema, SQL functions and constraints before extending; reuse, do not create duplicate identity/queue/template/task/booking/report engines. Current schema design v0.3, integrity design, test matrix and migration conventions are incorporated in full by pinned reference. Existing migrations and accepted ADRs take precedence over illustrative v1.2/addendum table/field names. Tenant foreign keys include owner organization and object identity; event-specific references include event where necessary. Separate shared explicit grant/projection from owner data. Use stable UUID canonical hexadecimal 8-4-4-4-12 text, including valid persisted non-v4 variant/version bits (ADR 0011); canonical normalize before fingerprint/key derivation; no generic rejection of old valid identifiers. Stable human-readable labels not IDs. Store UTC instants plus IANA schedule context, canonical BCP 47, monetary decimal/minor units/currency, typed enum state codes independent of display locale. No invented policy defaults for GHB.

| Owning boundary | Canonical existing foundation / future logical extension | Important invariants and references |
|---|---|---|
| Identity / tenancy / PAC-OAC | organizations, users, organization_memberships, scoped role/permission grants, sessions, collaboration grants/revisions/audit, platform routing/host audit; future control-plane service grant, support case, policy/readiness profile | User distinct from membership, host authority distinct, no cross-tenant raw select, active admin guard, current grant/actor scope |
| AES / UX | existing event capability sets/revisions/overrides, org settings; setup preset/revision, resumable setup session/draft, reviewed apply receipt, view preference | Presentation mode independent of capability/permission, no duplicate event, reviewed idempotent apply |
| Provider / booking | owned venues/resources, booking forms/inquiries/drafts/revisions/offers/decisions/approvals, price/tax/cancellation policies, holds/reservations, confirmed booking/snapshots, request/effect/notice | Exact effective revision, locks and no double/over capacity, issue/delivery/decision/confirm independent |
| Organizer / EPW | events/schedules/sessions/capability policies, booking-event links, event decisions/status, responsibility/delegated tasks, prerequisite records, production plan/revision, milestone/cue/shift/dependency, template/series, typed approval instance/decision, issue/handover | Separate canonical lifecycle and task status, cycle detection, actor-bound approval, recurrence per-occurrence idempotency |
