| Registry | persons, contacts, identifiers/source refs, labels/relationships, merge/restoration/transfer journals, participation identity snapshot, guest categories/tags/groups/custom fields, imports/reports/views | Same tenant, encrypted context, stable transfer evidence, no historical snapshot rewrite, authorized matching |
| FRS | booking form revisions and submissions; typed purpose schema/revision/mapping, submission/answer/review, registration/waitlist capacity/eligibility and accreditation decision, private attachments | Submission vs applied owning domain, capacity under lock, immutable form revision and receipt, no auto merge or pass |
| Spatial | venue hierarchy/template, source-plan asset, calibration/geometry/zone/row/feature/resource, capacity confirmation, published native/map projection, anchor/route edge | Internal IDs vs labels, no source assumption, publication immutable, sanitize public graph |
| Allocation | allocation revisions/runs/assignments/locks, constraints/group rules, plan approval/publication, change history | No overlapping unique resource/guest or count overflow, solver advisory, atomic revision |
| Invitations / RSVP | invitation policy/revision, invitation/revision, invitation links/deliveries, response history/current projection, portal scope/session | Purpose token hashed, explicit issuance/response, no automatic attendance or credential reuse |
| HPG | service taxonomy/revision, demand/request/review, arrangement/reservation ref, service assignment/fulfillment/correction, group/protocol/assistance refs | Request not confirmed/fulfilled, sensitive minimum projection, no duplicate identity/resource authority |
| AGIS | admission_credentials, checkin_stations, checkin_attempts, attendance_records, operational_alerts; station profile/revision/device enrollment/assignment, offline package/provisional receipt, print job refs | Revocation/expiry/actor/station scope, attempt unique, authoritative attendance once, no lookup mutation |
| TDS / private storage | brand profile/revision/asset, template/revision/typed assignments and render manifest/job/artifact, source attachments | Immutable content and source refs, protected artifact access, render not issue/send |
| CID | organization_delivery_config_revisions/heads, event_notification_campaigns/recipients/exclusions/attempts/provider events, booking_offer_email_deliveries, invitation_deliveries/attempts, existing tenant queues; adapter profile/sender/grant, intent/route, consent/preference/suppression, campaign review, distribution task, budget reservation/ledger | Preserve existing identity/history; one logical submission intent, current authority, no blind uncertain retry, distinct external evidence |
| RAI | existing roster exports and campaign reports; approved dataset/metric definitions, report/dashboard/schedule definitions/revisions, query/run/result manifest, protected artifact | Read projections only, exact semantic versions, no arbitrary query, scope/cost/privacy at run/download/delivery |
| Shared infrastructure | append-only actual actor audit, idempotency receipts, transactional outbox, typed job leases/fences, revisioned configuration, encrypted storage/retention/hold | Narrow authorized command boundary, durable receipts, no cross-tenant leakage, bounded external recovery |

### Transaction, authorization and failure rules

- Every command begins with active principal/context/scope and action authorization before subject lookup or private projection; non-enumerating unauthorized vs not found behavior per existing contracts. Runtime/auth/worker have least privileges, no broad direct access; FORCE RLS tenant policies, composite keys, narrow `SECURITY DEFINER` functions with pinned search_path and explicitly revoked PUBLIC execute, authentic actor and exact tenant context. No tenant context switching to bypass RLS. Host migration owner distinct; narrowly bounded owner backfill, restore FORCE RLS before commit. Validate global identity access and worker tenant discovery separately. Foreign references only via explicit relationship/grant and minimum projection. Do not assume schema presence means runtime/UI complete.
- Optimistic revision for routine edits; stable lock order on parent/event/booking/role/subject and affected child/resource rows; use unique/exclusion constraints and count-capacity locks, transaction serialization or advisory locks only where justified. Recheck current state under lock. Review digest canonical fields/version, UTC epoch, normalized IDs and relevant ciphertext/hash, binding actor/scope/subject/configuration and permitted action. Stale state blocks apply; preview never mutates; signed digest is not authorization. Approval/command receipt returns actual outcome; cache replay rechecks current authority, meaning, lifecycle and actor where required. Distinguish request idempotency key and semantic dedup uniqueness; mismatch same key different body conflict, no duplicate audit/history. Preserve deterministic request canonicalization and existing compatibility overloads.
- Commit domain state + audit + durable outbox/queue intent atomically. Never hold SQL transaction open for render, solver, provider network, upload or large reporting; pin immutable input, process bounded job with lease generation/fence, recheck before apply/output. Exactly-once authoritative domain effect within database where invariant permits; external submissions uncertain require evidence, not exactly-once promise. Define crash before commit, after commit/before response, during external call, lease expiry, duplicate callbacks and restore; retries must not duplicate business effect. Jobs bounded progress, failure code, retry/dead letter/manual review, cancellation and scoped status; no raw secrets or private payload in errors.
- Append-only historical facts/decisions/evidence; correction is new attributed event. Versioned published settings/templates/plans/forms/policies and financial snapshots immutable; retirement affects new use, not history. Cryptographic digests canonical algorithm/version recorded. Private assets use immutable object identity/hash, protected metadata, tenant-safe path, auth at creation, execution and download, expiration, quarantine and retention/hold. Secret envelope encryption context binds tenant/purpose/kind/identity per existing contracts; key versions and backup/recovery, no plaintext secret logging. Do not rewrite old migration files, v0.2 snapshots or accepted ADR text; additive forward migration, populated upgrade and old/new runtime compatibility review, explicit blocker on invalid legacy facts, no silent destructive cleanup. Apply migrations under runner transactional rules and reviewed lock budget, schema/contract tests incl fresh/upgrade/RLS/restore and rollback or forward fix as documented.

<a id="b13-api"></a>
## B13-API — Interface contract, principal types and service boundaries

API-first Fastify TypeScript; existing OpenAPI v0.3 contract and actual runtime endpoints govern implemented shape. Versioned route families below are intended logical surfaces, not a mandate to rename existing paths or add a duplicate API. Each new vertical slice updates OpenAPI, shared types, UI/client and SQL/worker command tests together. Existing public capability transport is purpose-specific; use TLS, secure HttpOnly/SameSite session cookies and CSRF/origin for staff mutations, explicit cookie vs bearer separation, no credential in query/logs, non-mutating resolution. Staff session, host-only CLI, platform operator scoped session, assigned worker service principal, partner staff grant, guest/public purpose token, station/device credential and signed provider callback are distinct principal classes; never authorize one based on an identifier supplied by another. Strict JSON/schema validation, bounded inputs/pagination/uploads, normalized UUID/time/locale, revision preconditions, idempotency for retryable commands, machine-readable sanitized Problem Details/validation conflict codes and correlation ID. Return authorized minimal projection, no ciphertext, raw provider secrets, cross-tenant records or unauthorized metadata. POST for explicit consequential commands/jobs; GET/preview must not submit/approve/consume/issue/confirm, PATCH for permitted revision-checked editing, DELETE only explicit authorized retirement/deletion under policy. Public unknown/token invalid/expired responses non-enumerating, rate limits independent of business decision. SSE/WebSocket or reviewed supported transport carries small authorized invalidations and cursor, never raw private object broadcast. No direct browser DB. Exact paths, methods and role codes in existing API design and all addenda remain incorporated; M0 review reconciles old/new proposals without breaking clients.

| Logical route family | Read / prepare examples | Explicit commands and authority |
|---|---|---|
| PAC / host / OAC | `/me`, workspaces, organization readiness/profile, effective role/source, platform health/tenant directory | login/switch/suspend/restore, enroll/assign, typed config/review, scoped support request; privileged bootstrap/recovery host only |
| AES setup | presets/revision, setup draft, capability/readiness/impact preview | save/resume, reviewed apply minimal draft, explicit enable/disable review, safe separate domain steps |
| Booking | forms/inquiry/draft/catalogue/availability/offer/status/booking/policy | submit, convert, revise, issue, customer decision, approve, confirm, request/review/execute cancellation; provider notice explicit |
| Event / EPW | event/session/plan/checklist/dependency/series/approval/readiness preview | create/update/schedule/approve/publish/start/close/cancel, link/end, assign task/shift, reviewed plan/series/approval decision, owning action |
| Registry / participation | authorized directory/profile/contact/ref/roster/import/merge review/export | create/link/update/archive, verify contact, reviewed import/bulk/merge/restore, role-specific field grant |
| FRS | form schema/revision/preview, public form/receipt, submission inbox/review | draft/publish, submit/upload, return/approve/reject, reviewed apply, waitlist promotion/accreditation, owning mapping |
| Venue / spatial / allocation | venue hierarchy, source artifact/geometry/calibration, plan/resource/rule/reflow preview | create/revise/import trace, confirm capacity, allocate/move/lock, solver job/accept explicit, approve/publish revision |
| Guest invitation / portal | non-mutating token resolve, own current invitation/status/destination/map | issue/revoke/reissue, explicit RSVP submission/correction, portal access/renew/revoke, separate CID send |
| HPG | authorized service demand/requests/arrangement/assignment | request/review/confirm/allocate/fulfill/correct/release/close with minimal scopes |
| AGIS | station/profile/device health, scoped lookup, current approved destination | enroll/assign/revoke, issue/revoke credential, scan/manual/correct, offline reconcile, print/reprint/replace explicit |
| EOC / realtime | scoped current snapshot/counts/map/alert/timeline | acknowledge/assign/escalate/resolve, explicit owning interventions, authorized subscription/reconnect |
| TDS / CID | library/preview/render status, provider readiness, audience/route/cost/exclusion/attempt history | create/revise/publish, test/render/export, connect/rotate/disable, review/schedule/confirm/cancel send, reconcile/manual distribution, signed callback |
| RAI | dataset definitions, safe standard/custom query preview, dashboard/run/artifact metadata | review/save definition, bounded run/export, schedule, cancel/expire, scoped download/delivery |
| Collaboration | grant review/shared configuration, own task/booking link/event receipt | grant proposal/recipient accept/grantor revoke, exact partner command, publish and acknowledge explicit receipt |

### Authorization matrix (minimum boundaries, not automatic grants)

| Actor / permission group | Allowed scope by explicit grant | Must not imply |
|---|---|---|
| Host owner | protected provisioning, release, backup/recovery, platform designation | routine staff impersonation or public host execution |
| PAC delegated admin/support | typed scoped platform operations; separately reviewed data support | universal tenant/private guest, commercial or secret access |
| Organization owner/admin | owned tenant policy, role delegation within ceiling, tenant lifecycle requests | platform designation, all restricted fields, other tenants |
| Booking manager / commercial approver | exact owned booking/catalogue/offer decision | organizer Registry or unrestricted cancellation/refund; own approval where forbidden |
| Event manager / plan approver | exact event/session/planning/approved plan lifecycle | source Registry cross-event access, solver auto commit or provider bookings without grant |
| Registry manager / field grants | tenant person/merge plus independent contact/ref/relationship/export rights | event-only user gets same access, unrestricted historical export |
| Forms author / reviewer / mapper | typed purpose and exact submission scope; separate publish/apply | public intake becomes role, identity merge or admission |
| Hospitality coordinator / supplier | request/arrangement and minimum assigned service projection | medical details/general guest list, automatic booking/payment |
| Station operator / device | assigned event/session/station/mode and permitted actions | attendance mutation via lookup, cross-event use, unrelated portal or admin |
| Template designer / publisher | authorized typed content/brand/artifact purpose | recipient read, issue, send or report dataset access |
| Delivery configurator / campaign preparer / approver / worker / reconciler | exact provider/purpose/account/audience and approved budget, separate secret/read | recipient unrestricted, auto business approval or other tenant credentials |
| Report designer / reader / exporter / scheduler | allowlisted dataset, scope, field and aggregate rights separately | SQL access, report shares grant recipient data authority |
| Partner vendor / assigned staff | accepted current grant/assignment and minimal projection | tenant membership, entire event or commercial directory |
| Guest / public requester | one purpose, own approved projection and bounded commands | staff privilege, others' identity, other-purpose credentials |

<a id="b13-security"></a>
## B13-SECURITY — Security, privacy, abuse and compliance engineering

Threat model includes cross-tenant enumeration/IDOR, scope escalation through roles/managed platform memberships, stale approval/grant replay, cache/stream leakage, invitation/QR/portal token replay or purpose confusion, public upload/render SSRF/XSS, CSV formula injection, compromised device/provider, ambiguous external delivery, race overbooking/duplicate attendance, stale offline and backup replay, sensitive inference in reports, insider misuse, destructive maintenance. Enforce default deny, authorization before lookup, scope recheck after locks/on queued job/export/download/replay/subscription; no direct application roles to private tables, tenant-qualified FK/RLS, bounded public capability resolution and high-entropy hashed tokens, least privilege with separate key/secret storage. Password Argon2id, existing rate controls, MFA for administrative/sensitive functions, secure cookie flags and rotation/revoke, session expiry, origin/CSRF and TLS, strong external access (VPN/identity-aware proxy or MFA according to policy); no local browser password/token storage, no anonymous staff endpoints. Keep host recovery separate. Secrets encrypted with version/context, service account credentials limited to allowed purpose, rotation/revocation, protected backup and restore keys. Never commit real credentials, tokens, guest info or private plans; redact errors/logs/audit/provider payload; actual actor/correlation IDs, immutable mutation and sensitive read receipts, least-data audit not raw secrets/medical/restricted private content. Explicit privacy class and purpose/lawful basis/notice/consent policy; data minimization, field-level read/write/export, restricted reasons and minimum actionable supplier projection, guest own map/destination only; CDI coordination only and no police findings. Retention reviewed per tenant/event/purpose, legal hold before deletion, anonymization/correction/purge reviewed with historical references and export manifest; no promise to erase all backups. Audit protected downloads and support, not covert impersonation. Incident response/recovery procedures preserve evidence, scoped emergency access and revocation; no application privileged shell. Rate/size/time/budget/quotas, bounded recurrence/query/solver/render/upload and webhook replay; sanitized asset rendering no arbitrary JS/SQL/file/URL access, network deny by default except reviewed adapters, safe spreadsheet export. Intranet/public segmentation, separate route policy and optionally hostname, no database/storage publicly exposed. Validate supported security libraries/provider contracts/retention/legal requirements at implementation and actual deployment; no claim of regulatory certification from blueprint.

<a id="b13-deployment"></a>
## B13-DEPLOYMENT — Self-hosted delivery, installer, operations and recovery

API-first modular monolith per ADR 0001: Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite frontends, Fastify + TypeScript API/background workers, PostgreSQL authoritative data (current CI PostgreSQL 18.6), SVG-native spatial model and controlled OR-Tools CP-SAT C++ worker. Existing incremental frontend modularization per ADR 0008. Independent frontends/worker processes permitted, no microservice or mandatory Redis/Valkey/cloud dependencies (ADR 0002). Transactional outbox and PostgreSQL-backed queues, private artifact storage and shared schemas/client contracts. Native Linux and Docker Compose first-class equivalent modes; same versioned application builds, migrations, configuration and security defaults, not separate products. Native: supported distro/prerequisite detection, dedicated service identities and filesystem permissions, DB roles/migrations, systemd services API/worker/solver, frontend/reverse proxy and TLS, protected initial admin/bootstrap, health/log/backup/restore/upgrade/rollback. Compose: production topology, non-root containers, persistent volumes, secrets not baked images, readiness/dependency/migration/bootstrap, equivalent reverse proxy/external proxy option, backup/restore/update/rollback, no arbitrary Docker socket in API. Deployment-independent network: local DNS and TLS where feasible, intranet no external services, optional public DNS/HTTPS, explicitly enabled public guest/booking/form/callback endpoint families, staff access controlled, external SMTP or HTTP provider optional. Home ISP limitations only local test, not product design. Local email capture/manual distribution available. Installer Quick Start or advanced selects mode, checks prerequisites/ports/DB/TLS/storage/keys/network and validates config before mutating, dry-run no writes, reviewed protected host apply, idempotent rerun and fail-safe recovery; no guessed passwords/tenant policies. Document supported Linux, sizing, networking, DNS/TLS, proxy, egress/callback, OAuth/SMTP/push/provider account requirements, health/startup order and recovery. Existing deployment runbook governs current commands; do not assume Compose application packaging complete merely from database-only dev Compose.

Health/liveness vs readiness for API/db/worker/queue/solver/storage/provider, job age and error codes, station/device/portal/realtime freshness, scoped PAC/OAC diagnostics with safe correlation IDs and no secrets, metrics latency/rate/solver/backup capacity. Keep solver/render/provider failure from blocking unrelated manual functions; internet outage retains intranet; DB unavailable must not falsely confirm business/attendance, local network loss explicit offline limitations; stale plan/read model visible. Automatic PostgreSQL backup/PITR where feasible, consistent private artifact/source/brand/template/report and encryption-key manifests, encrypted off-host copy, access control, retention and restore drills. Include Registry, all event/booking/reservation/credential/attendance/production/forms/HPG/CID/RAI/outbox/audit data; preserve foreign keys and private file references. Validate backup not merely success status: restore isolated, verify schema/data/digest/key decryption/reference consistency, no external side effects until reviewed fence/reconcile uncertain jobs/callbacks/print/notifications; stale credentials/role revoked correctly; test RPO/RTO per deployment. Upgrade reviewed migration compatibility, backup before change, maintenance/drain, verify same release in both modes, rollback only supported safe path or forward fix without silently losing new data. Final host acceptance VM in Phase 9 only; synthetic CI throughout, no early VM reliance.

<a id="b13-quality"></a>
## B13-QUALITY — Non-functional service targets and measurable evidence

All targets provisional until agreed fixture/hardware/network, data size and peak load tested. Use documented actual environment, clocks, workload, p50/p95, error rate, exact expected vs actual results, limits/defects, not unverified claims. Preserve all stricter purpose-specific targets in addenda (not replace by broad averages). Support initial bs-BA/en, UTF-8, Firefox/Chromium and Safari where practical, target camera/mobile/printer hardware; accessibility keyboard/assistive technology, contrast, 200% zoom and 360/768/1280/1920 representative widths, text alternative for map/chart/drag, print overflow. Cross-domain counts and database invariants exact; zero unauthorized data disclosure or duplicate authoritative commits in tested concurrency. Measure performance without real guest data. Blueprint NFR-01–12 and §38.5 preserved:

| ID | Initial target / evidence |

| NFR-01 | Typical filter/search of 10,000 guests under 2 s on agreed adequately sized local server; simple Registry/event search p95 <500 ms target LAN (excluding large export/fuzzy job) |

| NFR-06 | Document/test DB/files/key restore, RPO/RTO set per deployment; prove safe recovery and no external replay |
| NFR-07 | Material mutation and sensitive access traceable; authorized receipt and retention tests |
| NFR-08 | Keyboard, readable contrast/scalable text, assistive technology and drag alternative across surfaces |
| NFR-09 | Supported Firefox/Chromium and Safari where practical, representative camera/PWA/device testing |
| NFR-10 | UTF-8, bs-BA/en localization, date/time/currency and diacritics, pinned localized outputs |

| BP38-EOC | Incremental update p95 visible within 2 s of commit on healthy LAN; reconnect fresh snapshot within 5 s after stable reconnection |

## B13-DECISIONS — Reconciliation and accepted ADR register

No accepted ADR is changed by this proposed blueprint. The following decisions are operational rules for consolidation; details and exceptions in the pinned ADR files are part of the contract. “Review” means a material implementation design choice remains unresolved, not approval to alter code now.

| Topic / sources | Consolidated resolution | Status |
|---|---|---|
| v1.2 initial single-organization GHB vs later multi-tenant collaboration/PAC/OAC | Tenant-aware architecture and explicit independent organizations remain required; one tenant deployment allowed, no SaaS requirement or hardcoded GHB. | Reconciled |
| v1.2 phase sequences vs current roadmap | Preserve all requirements and use current roadmap's Phase 0–9 and #104/#112 → #105–107 → #110/#111/#108. Historic phases not erased; map to current ownership. | Reconciled |
| ADR 0002 optional Docker vs #108 dual installers | Native remains first-class; Compose is required packaging deliverable, never mandatory runtime dependency. | Reconciled |
| ADR 0015 managed non-platform permissions vs PAC least-privilege | Existing implemented behavior preserved; audit grant catalogue and propose successor ADR with migration/authority tests when scheduled. Do not claim privilege redesign already done or infer vulnerability without test. | Open engineering decision |
| v1.2 portal-only public surface vs public booking, FRS, offer/RSVP/cancellation/callbacks | Explicit opt-in purpose-specific public route families, no implied exposure by hostname. Guest portal is only guest information surface by default; public booking/forms are separately authorized. | Reconciled |
| Invitation email readiness vs CID no-email | Current email issue path remains; extend channel-independent eligibility/issue in CID M3 through owning invitation commands. No breaking migration or automatic credential reissue. | Scheduled |
| Hash-only capability language vs existing encrypted delivery capability envelope | Hash lookup and no plaintext; preserve existing limited authenticated encrypted envelope for required worker/share/render secret recovery with explicit scope/retention; audit and review exact lifetime. Never general plaintext recoverable history. | Review retention/binding |
| v1.2 card reissue on seating change vs AGIS | Guest portal bound to person, QR to admission credential; change approved destination, notify per policy; print same artifact or re-render current; replacement only explicit revoke/reissue. | Reconciled |
| v1.2 offline later vs AGIS offline modes | Online-first; bounded provisional/deferred or leased local validation only by policy, no instant offline revocation claim; final integration evidence required. | Reconciled; engineering review |
| TDS visual form/report design vs FRS/RAI | TDS owns content appearance/renderer, FRS schema/validation/intake, RAI dataset/metric/query/result. Reuse assets/revisions and private artifacts. | Reconciled |
| EPW approvals vs domain policies | Constrained typed adapters, domain guards cannot be weakened; approval is not execution. | Reconciled |
| Registry labels/relationships vs HPG protocol and allocation | Internal classification distinct, explicit event policy/approved constraint; no inferred guest precedence or relationship privilege. | Reconciled |
| Booking financial vs RAI/HPG/CID costs | Estimates/service demand, offered/contracted amounts, actual recorded charges/payment evidence separate; no payments/refunds/repricing on task/notice. | Reconciled |
| CID fallback and restore vs delivery resilience | Retry confirmed nonacceptance only per reviewed policy; uncertain external state fenced pending reconciliation. | Reconciled |
| RAI cross-event analytics vs privacy | Field and aggregate authorization, small-cell/differencing controls, artifact authority independent of recipient; no directory via reports. | Reconciled |
| Full original TDS/PAC review editions vs shorter integrated versions | Preserve both in source manifest/annex. Current integrated repository text/accepted ADRs govern; full original review wording retained as candidate detail. Require owner review of any extra/differing low-level requirements before declaring source-complete v1.3 authoritative. | Open content reconciliation |
| Exact APIs, table names, role codes and numeric limits in addenda | Proposals, audit live contracts and schema first; use reviewed successor, preserve existing compatibility. Do not conflate mock/schema/design with completion. | Scheduled M0 review |

## B13-ROADMAP — Dependency-safe implementation and Codex continuity

The verified `main` commit above includes documentation integration of PR #237 and all required CI passes on first attempt. This proves the merged source and covered existing checks, not that new approved features are implemented. The current development handoff `PROJECT_STATE.md` is preserved and its dated implementation receipt remains historical; inspect latest Codex checkout/PR/main and existing tests before next slice, do not reset/rebase unfinished work. Gap analysis describes partial/foundation/missing vs implemented runtime; not a numeric completion percentage. Keep issue #104/#112 closure and existing development sequence; no blanket task switch or new duplicate issue queue because v1.3 prepared. Individual milestones in twelve annexes remain mapped work packages, not independent phases. Every slice audits existing schema/API/UI/permissions, adds reviewed compatible migrations/contracts/tests/docs together; maintain exact-head CI then post-merge CI. <a id="b13-acceptance"></a>
## B13-ACCEPTANCE — Integrated verification and release gates

All source acceptance conditions remain cumulative; no acceptance case is replaced by the following integrated gates. Source-specific AC IDs retain their original meaning and exact evidence definitions in Annexes and Part III. CI proves existing covered behavior, not product readiness; optional external probes skipped are not passes, mocked HTTP/browser tests and schema presence not actual provider/device/full workflow evidence. Each requirement tracks expected and observed result, commit, build/config/schema/environment/fixture, evidence links, time, actor/reviewer, limitations and defects; state `not_run`, `pass`, `fail`, `blocked`, or explicitly owner-reviewed `not_applicable`. Waiver is not pass; never waive tenant isolation, integrity, auth/credential security. Independent reviewers where feasible; single owner recovery separately documented. Use reserved example.invalid and synthetic GHB/A/B/C tenants, staff roles and event/booking fixtures, no real private data or credentials committed. Use fixed timezone/DST cases and deterministic fixture clock, isolate runs and do not trigger live sends; final supported real-provider sandbox only with approved accounts. Evidence levels: unit/schema/contract, real API/PG integration and populated upgrades, real browser and device, cross-module/failure/load/accessibility, actual native and Compose host acceptance and approved provider sandbox. Negative and concurrent tests required, not just happy path.

| Gate | Required evidence and owning requirements |
|---|---|
| G1 — Integration and contracts | Exact-head required OpenAPI, PostgreSQL migrations/RLS/concurrency, staff web type-check/build, systemd, secret history all pass; post-merge same checks on exact merged commit; diff/source/migration compatibility, no code/config from docs-only integration. |
| G2 — Independent tenant operation | PAC provision and secure admin first login, OAC guided setup, provider-only booking independent, organizer simple event Quick Start/advanced expansion same identity, real staff role management/booking/full workflows, no routine host SQL. |
| G3 — Isolation, security and governance | Distinct tenant/party/role/task/device/principal, no unauthorized data/count/stream/artifact/secret, revocation at every step, last admin and host recovery, public capabilities distinct, merge/restoration/approval races and safe audit, retention/legal hold, restricted supplier and aggregate privacy. |
| G4 — Content, intake, communication and print | TDS localized typed render and exact historic manifest, FRS versioned form/review/waitlist/attachments and no auto business effect, CID approved no-email/manual and required provider paths, consent/quiet hours/budget/fallback/uncertain/reconciliation, AGIS controlled print distinct from handover/attendance. |
| G5 — Full event and provider journey | Booking inquiry→offer→decision→approval→confirm→disruption/cancellation; organizer event/session→Registry/import→registration/RSVP→approved geometry/allocation→QR/portal/wayfinding→gate/realtime/Info Pult→reflow/published notice→HPG/EPW service/task→handover/close→authorized reports. Provider/organizer collaboration explicit, no inappropriate disclosure. |
| G6 — Quality and resilience | Locale, accessibility, supported browsers/devices, peak load/latency, solver status/constraints, version/cache/reconnect, provider/worker/storage/network failure, offline provisional reconciliation, queue/lease/retry/idempotency, no duplicate authoritative records or false verified status. |
| G7 — Installation and recovery | Native and Compose same build/migrations/security, clean install/upgrade, dry-run/rerun, protected host bootstrap, consistent backup/PITR/off-host/key and artifact restore, scope/revoke checks, no uncertain replay. |
| G8 — Actual external evidence | Approved external SMTP and public HTTPS/security headers, actual advertised HTTP/OAuth/SMS/WhatsApp/Viber/push/other supported adapters with eligible accounts and verified policy/evidence, camera/print/degraded scenarios on target environment; optional Telegram only explicit disabled N/A, if advertised tested. No mandatory external provider to run core. |
| G9 — Traceability and exit decision | All original v1.2 criteria, NFR, 12 addenda, ADR/domain/schema and issue gates accounted; exact applicable cases pass or explicitly approved non-applicable, open defects/limitations recorded, owner reviews and release candidate frozen; no missing source hidden by summary or score. |

<a id="part-ii"></a>
# Part II — Source-to-consolidated requirement traceability and original annexes

## Traceability interpretation

Every mapped requirement retains its exact source text. A B13-<source ID> alias points to the original clause; the B13 family column gives the integrated ownership/implementation contract. Mapping to a family is not a declaration that the source clause has been reimplemented or independently tested. The original matrices linking each requirement to its acceptance cases are preserved in the annexes. For older unnumbered sources, the stable alias is the source ID and inclusive line span at the pinned commit. These ranges partition each source (including examples, historical context, and trailing logical empty line if present); exact external text is normative by reference until materialized. This is exhaustive source-range coverage and explicit-ID traceability, not a certified sentence-by-sentence equivalence proof for the older sources. A requirement is not removed merely because it is repeated or not repeated in the core. The consolidated owner/engineering review must resolve conflicts before adopting a new authoritative baseline. A blank line or contextual paragraph is not itself a new mandatory requirement.

<a id="part-iii"></a>
# Part III — Immutable repository source manifest and materialization

The exact pinned source texts below remain incorporated, including technical schema/API details, examples, alternatives, limitations and acceptance conditions. Links target the immutable Git commit and require authorized repository access. Current Git blob SHA-1 identities are those returned by the non-truncated tree at the verified commit. The manifest includes all 24 ADRs, current versions of the twelve addenda, v1.2, all seven v0.3 domain designs, the design index, architecture, operating model, roadmap, gap analysis, handoff, API/database design/integrity/test/migration docs, roles/MVP/form schema and deployment/acceptance runbooks. Historical v0.2 snapshots remain unchanged and are linked from those sources; they are not made a competing normative runtime contract. Source lines use `split("\n")` semantics, including final empty logical line if present. Original review annexes retain their original relative links, which were written for their proposed repository paths, not this combined file. Do not rewrite original bytes to fix standalone relative links: use the pinned manifest/line links here or materialize the source tree alongside the document. The exact-source materialization utility reads from an existing local Git clone (`git cat-file`/`git show` only), checks each byte length, line count and blob hash, and appends the exact 61 repository documents; it does not write to Git or contact external providers. It also validates the embedded original annex digests. This is a reproducible way to eliminate the local source-transfer limitation without modifying any repository branch.
