| Device or staff crosses event/tenant | Composite scope constraints, current grants and RLS, no source directory; negative IDs/roles and streams. |
| Duplicate or replayed admission | Subject lock/current-state guard + idempotency fingerprint + append history; parallel gates and retry tests. |
| Revocation during scan/reissue/print | Consistent locks/order and recheck; no stale cached authorization; preserve committed history. |
| Kiosk prior guest or late response | Reset/expiry, generation guard, no-store/bfcache handling, browser back/restart and offline timer tests. |
| Malicious station layout, QR, SVG or notice | Typed schema/purpose allowlist, CSP, no arbitrary JS/URL/network, safe geometry/asset projection, input validation. |
| Lost device/offline manipulation | Bounded lease, encrypted queue, no plaintext, server reconciliation under current auth, quarantine; local cutoff. |
| Public display leaks names/private layers | Separate public projection, no personalized endpoint/device grant, cache partition and tests across formats. |
| Unauthorized print or uncertain print retry | Explicit purpose, private artifacts, current eligibility, copy limits, reason and review, no blind reprint. |
| Recovery resurrects revoked access | Protected PAC restore review, invalidate device/guest leases, reconcile credential revocations and queues before reopening. |

Audit records include actual actor kind/ID (membership or device/guest-session/service/host where applicable), acting organization, exact event/session/station/device context, action/purpose, target opaque ID, server time, policy/layout/plan revision, result/reason code, correlation/idempotency, approval/review link and offline capture provenance where relevant; redact values. Read access audit proportionate to privacy, personal kiosk lifecycle with minimal identifiers, no movement analytics inferred. Security-denied attempts may use separate safe audit with actor type/unknown, do not force fake checkin record to satisfy existing non-null actor. Write audit and domain mutation atomically; protected audit access and append-only, no editing historical log; archive/purge only through approved retention/hold with evidence, preserve necessary business history and references. Station audit views authorized scoped, logs never tokens. Export aggregate/authorized attendance and station performance data with time window, definitions, source revision, omissions and current download auth, CSV injection protection. No default export of personal kiosk access events to broad operator. Platform support under PAC actual actor, reason and bounded scope; emergency access never substitutes for required admission eligibility, cannot directly edit DB or audit. PAC health safe, OAC data governance/retention policies and staff membership access remain authoritative.

## 20. AGIS-18 — Technical architecture, logical data model and migration

### 20.1 Components and trust zones

```text
PAC deployment policy / safe technical oversight
    |       (protected scoped support; no routine access)
OAC tenant settings, device inventory, station profiles, permissions
    |       EOC event/session station assignment and operational dashboard
    +---------------------- existing staff session -------------------+
    |                                                              |
    v                                                              v
Vue feature workspaces: gate | assisted info | seating | print | management
Separate restricted surfaces: kiosk verification/view | passive display | phone portal
    | HTTPS, mode-specific session/device auth; bounded requests/projections
Fastify modular API: station authority + credential/attendance command + info projection
    |            |                      |                 |
existing auth   event/Registry      spatial/allocation  TDS render/print orchestration
                eligibility         published snapshots  (isolated renderer)
    +----------------------- PostgreSQL authoritative ---------------------+
     RLS / scoped commands / append-only audit / idempotency / transactional outbox
                                  |
                scoped snapshot/realtime invalidation + bounded workers
                                  |
                       EOC / staff / kiosk / display refresh
```

Vue components follow ADR 0008; maintain thin composition root and isolated feature state. Proposed modules `stations`, `admission`, `guest-information`, `station-designer`, `station-print` and existing `event-operations` feature when implemented; share scanner adapter, projection renderer, localized status and design tokens. Names illustrative, not actual paths or instruction to create all now. Keep transport types/validation in shared contracts/API client, domain logic server-side, test adapters for camera/HID without bypassing server auth. Guest portal is existing planned domain; no second guest identity store. API uses explicit contexts and safe read models; restricted kiosk/portal/display ingress separates scopes from staff, protected PAC ingress. Data and locks authoritative PostgreSQL, transactional outbox for live invalidation, worker for bounded render/print/reconciliation where needed. Do not grant runtime role DB owner access, host shell, Docker socket, arbitrary print command or broad key material. Static web assets locally served, no external CDN required. Service workers cache shell and approved public assets only with explicit cache partition/version/expiry; deny authenticated and personal API responses and raw token material; clear on context change/logout, test upgrades. Isolated TDS worker accepts immutable sanitized input and returns private artifacts, not a mutating domain agent.

### 20.2 Logical model (proposed additions/extensions, not DDL)

| Entity / ownership | Key fields, relationships and invariants |
|---|---|
| Existing admission_credentials | Reuse org/event/participation, digest/kind/status/validity/issuer. Reviewed policy/session scope, optional replacement lineage and issue receipt. Exactly one active pass under current index semantics until successor reviewed; expiry enforced at read. No plaintext. |
| Admission policy revision | Reuse/extend event/session capability configuration: eligible subject kinds/states, allowed sessions/window, arrival/re-entry/departure/manual/correction/reissue/offline rules, minimum verification, revision/effective time. Pin issuance/commands as policy dictates, current safety/revocation rechecked; no inconsistent duplicate policy stores. |
| Existing checkin_stations | Extend/reuse event/session station identity, code, label, status; anchor/projection and mode assignment via compatible fields/sidecar. Preserve historical attempts and non-null session semantics. Non-admission modes may need generalized station profile/binding with optional session; no weakening historical checkin FK to support display. |
| Tenant station profile / mode preset | Org, name/code, kind, allowed modes, defaults, locale, device class constraints, policy/brand reference, revision/state. Reusable across events; no guests or live credentials. |
| Station layout revision | Org/allowed purpose, immutable typed component schema + digest/version, locale variants, approved assets/brand refs, validation/approval actor/time/state. Active assignment pins revision. |
| Station event assignment | Org/event/session as applicable, logical station/profile, physical anchor, allowed/active mode, time window, revision, operator/task scope, layout/brand reference, readiness. Gate must use exact non-null session. Prevent mismatched event/venue references. |
| Device installation | Org, nonsecret ID/label, credential verifier/key ref, allowed mode/approved device class, enrollment status, created/revoked actor/time. No staff password or broad API token; secret storage separate. |
| Device enrollment challenge | Org/intent/scope, digest, expiry, attempt limit, approval/consumption state, issuer/reviewer, current context. Single use, no plaintext code in DB/log. |
| Device binding / station lease | Device, org/event/session/station/mode, assignment/policy revision, actual operator session if required, allowed actions, issued/expiry/revoked, key/session verifier. One active context per device; current authorization rechecked. |
| Device health sample / summary | Last seen server time, safe client version, mode/layout, bounded reported capabilities/queue count/errors, source/as-of and expiry. Time-limited telemetry, not proof of authority. |
| Kiosk verification challenge/session | Restricted device/station/mode/event/participation purpose, digest/nonce, verification method/result, attempt/idle/absolute expiry, invalidation. No general portal token; no raw pass persistence. |
| Guest-visible venue projection / route anchor | Reuse #105 snapshots/classification/publication, public nodes/instructions/geometry, accessibility/closure revision and safe locale labels. Own marker is authorized overlay, not public roster. |
| Existing event_allocation_revisions / allocations | Reuse #106 current published plan and assignment; consistent projection pointer, destination typed union and source revisions. No copies of seat truth in station/device or credential. |
| Existing checkin_attempts | Preserve org/event/session/station/credential, outcome, key, actor, attempted_at, safe_result; extend device/binding/policy/source/receipt/fingerprint metadata as needed. Real actor provenance, correct session composite checks, bounded safe errors. |
| Existing attendance_records + effective projection | Append-only transitions/corrections and target reference, server time/actor/reason, authoritative lock/version per org/event/session/participation; unique effective-state invariant via reviewed command. No duplicate attendance store. |
| Offline capture lease/intent/receipt | Scope/device/original actor/policy/time/count limits, intent ID/digest/envelope version, observed untrusted time/counter, server received time, outcome/linked attempt/correction, reviewed quarantine/discard evidence. No raw token in durable receipt. |
| Information access audit/session outcome | Minimal event/station/device/actor/purpose, guest subject only if necessary, verification/outcome/time/revision, no raw fields; separate from attendance attempts. Reuse existing audit where suitable. |
| Print request / artifact / receipt | Reuse TDS render jobs/manifests; station-purpose/printer profile/copies/idempotency, exact template/plan/brand/credential revision, approved private artifact, submit/ack/uncertain/reconcile history. No duplicate render subsystem. |
| Published display assignment | Org/event/venue/session where applicable, public projection content/revision, layout/brand schedule, device binding, valid window and safe expiry. No PII by default. |
| Existing operational_alerts, audit and outbox | Extend safe station/admission/print alert taxonomy, scoped links/dedup, actual actor and append-only transition/evidence. No duplicate EOC ledger. |

Invariants: all tenant-scoped IDs use composite organization keys and event/session constraints; event/provider ownership never inferred from booking link; station lease exact mode/scope/action; kiosk session exact challenge and subject; invalidation cascades logically, not destructive SQL deleting history; retired configuration revisions immutable. Station/event/profile/device references not cross-tenant unless explicit approved share of safe projection. Time windows server authoritative, normalized UTC with event timezone presentation; finite timestamps as current code patterns. Unique scoped station codes, device pairing consumption, command idempotency keys, active binding and effective attendance state. Enforce policy/type compatibility at command and DB constraints where feasible; default deny on unknown purpose/enum/version. No service impersonation of membership; extend actor model only after review of current schema and tests. Data classification and retention per field: public content separate, personal lookup transient, credential digests/private keys restricted, audit minimum, offline encrypted and bounded, print private encrypted artifact. Sensitive data encrypted per existing key policy where stored; no new incompatible key system without review.

### 20.3 Migration strategy

M0 inspect current migrations/commands/RLS/role grants/foreign keys and existing seeded historical rows (including nullable actors, existing credential kinds, one-active index, station session association and status semantics). Decide generalized station registry vs compatible sidecar with existing checkin_stations as admission-specific authoritative record; avoid double sources of truth. Do not infer a kiosk is a gate or backfill fabricated station mode/location/actor/policy from legacy facts. Mark unknown where needed, review and map existing stations. Add backward-compatible columns/relations, scoped commands and indexes in successor migration, preserve old IDs and append-only records. Verify populated upgrade/fresh install, rollback compatibility and forward-fix/recovery; no destructive downgrade. Existing historical v0.2 SQL/OpenAPI/Blueprint untouched; update current API contract and tests together only when owning implementation scheduled. Lock ordering with revocation/session cancellation/reissue/allocation review documented and concurrency verified with actual runtime role (not owner bypass). Review permissions and remove unnecessary direct table access safely only in scheduled implementation, test independent grants and RLS. Rollout: read-only inventory then strict online station slice, limited verification/print, optional offline after threat review; migration feature flags/default disabled where appropriate. Legacy invitation and booking-only behavior remains unchanged. No environment config republish now.

## 21. AGIS-19 — API design and authorization contract

The following are conceptual endpoint families (not an approved OpenAPI change). Align paths, naming, error envelope, version fields and permission codes with current OpenAPI v0.3 and accepted commands during M0. Staff paths under selected tenant/event; station paths use restricted binding context derived from authenticated lease, not an arbitrary organization/event/station ID in the payload. Portal paths reuse planned §36.5 purpose-specific routes; no generic guest search. Use bounded typed requests, canonical UUIDs (ADR 0011 compatibility), finite ISO timestamps normalized to UTC, stable enumerations, expected revision, request ID and idempotency key for consequential mutations. Every endpoint requires current scope, not just authenticated session. All GET/read commands are non-destructive; no credentials consumed by preview bots or read-only pages. Credential-bearing requests use POST body and never URI query/path; no-cache/no-store headers and redacted diagnostics. Canonicalized request fingerprint includes operation, actor/lease/context and semantically significant payload; do not retain raw token in fingerprint material/log, use secure digest with reviewed keying where appropriate. Duplicate key different request returns conflict. Error shape follows existing privacy-safe problem details; no raw SQL/secret/stack trace; wrong event/unknown pass indistinguishable outside authorized minimal scope. Idempotency caches never bypass current authorization.

| Method / conceptual resource | Principal and contract |
|---|---|
| GET/POST `/organizations/{org}/station-profiles` | Tenant scoped list/create presets, safe metadata, bounded pagination; revisioned commands for changes. |
| GET/POST `/organizations/{org}/station-layouts`; POST `/{id}/revisions`, `/{id}/preview`, `/{id}/publish` | Authorized designer/reviewer, typed schema, synthetic preview, publish pinned revision/digest, no side effects on admission or send. |
| GET/POST `/events/{event}/stations`; GET `/{station}/readiness`; POST `/{station}/activate`, `/disable`, `/retire`, `/change-assignment` | Exact organizer/event management, current revision/impact/reason; validate session/mode/anchor/approved layout/operator/device/policy, revoke affected leases atomically. |
| GET `/organizations/{org}/station-devices`; POST `/device-enrollments`; POST `/device-enrollments/{id}/approve` | Tenant inventory and explicit one-time enrollment intent, reviewed pairing, expiry/attempts and appropriate recent auth. |
| POST `/station-device/enroll`, `/station-device/lease`, `/station-device/renew`, `/station-device/end` | Narrow device principal, verified challenge/credential, exact assignment/mode/current actor where required; revocable scoped lease, not staff session. |
| POST `/organizations/{org}/station-devices/{id}/revoke`, `/rotate`, `/lock` | Tenant/event authorized management, current revision/reason, invalidation and review pending queue; server denial, no OS remote control. |
| POST `/station/heartbeat`; GET `/station/configuration` | Current device binding, minimal status/version/readiness and safe layout/brand/config; no guest records. |
| GET `/events/{event}/admission-policy`; POST `/events/{event}/admission-policy/revisions` | Scoped event policy view/authoring, explicit review/publication, reuse owning capability/policy patterns. |
| POST `/events/{event}/admission-credentials/issue`, `/{credential}/revoke`, `/{credential}/replace` | Issuer with exact participation/event grant, policy, explicit target scope/reason and idempotency; atomic replacement, restricted one-time output or authorized artifact reference, no new attendance. |
| POST `/station/gate/scans` | Active gate binding + operator + admission action, opaque pass in body; authoritative transaction and receipt, bounded outcome/destination. |
| POST `/station/gate/manual-lookup`, `/manual-arrivals`, `/departures` | Gate-specific lookup and separate authorized attendance actions with reason/subject/current state; departure/reentry only policy-enabled. |
| GET `/station/receipts/{receipt}` | Exact original action scope, reauthorized status read; no stale private response, no side effects. |
| POST `/events/{event}/attendance/{record}/corrections` | Explicit correction authority, reviewed target/current revision/reason; append only, same subject lock. |
| POST `/station/info/verification-start`, `/verification-complete`; GET `/station/info/personal-view`; POST `/station/info/end` | Restricted kiosk device and scoped challenge/view session; separate verification, no attendance mutation, minimal fields, server session expiry, reset. |
| POST `/station/info/assisted-lookup` | Staffed information binding + current minimal lookup authority and verification; no gate command, no reusable portal credential. |
| GET `/station/info/public-content`; GET `/station/display/content` | Explicit allowed audience, published sanitized programme/map/instructions, revision/as-of/expiry; display cannot fetch personal view. |
| GET `/station/info/route` (using current verified session) | Authorized own destination with approved origin/route mode, revision pair and textual fallback; no arbitrary participation/guest ID. |
| POST `/station/print-requests`; GET `/station/print-requests/{id}`; POST `/{id}/acknowledge`, `/reconcile`, `/cancel` | Approved purpose, authorized subject or safe guest directions session, pinned TDS artifact, printer/copies bounds; actual evidence/uncertain distinction; no implicit issue. |
| POST `/station/offline-leases`; POST `/station/offline-reconcile` | Optional policy, exact original device/actor scope and current submitter, bounded encrypted items, per-intent receipt/quarantine, authoritative online command reuse. |
| GET `/events/{event}/cockpit/stations`, `/attendance-summary`, `/station-alerts` | Authorized scoped projections with definition, snapshot revision/as-of and freshness; safe filtered counts. |
| GET `/events/{event}/station-audit`; POST `/events/{event}/station-report-exports` | Explicit audit/export permission, bounded filters, safe receipts, private authorized download. |
| Scoped realtime subscription / snapshot | Purpose-specific authenticated connection, authorized scope/cursor, invalidation only; reconnect snapshot, revalidate on revocation. |

Illustrative gate command body (all IDs, pass values and results here synthetic):

```json
{"requestId":"synthetic-intent-001","credential":"TEST_NON_LIVE_VALUE","action":"arrive","expectedStationRevision":3}
```

`action` is a closed enum checked against fixed gate operation and policy, not a free capability selector. The actual TEST value must never be accepted for live admission. Example *successful synthetic fixture response shape*, not response to the non-live value:

```json
{
  "receiptId":"synthetic-receipt-001",
  "outcome":"accepted",
  "recordedAt":"2026-12-05T17:02:31Z",
  "attendance":{"state":"present","transition":"arrived"},
  "destination":{"kind":"position","roomLabel":"Example hall","tableLabel":"07","seatLabel":"04","allocationRevision":12,"asOf":"2026-12-05T17:02:31Z"},
  "nextAction":"next_guest"
}
```

Outcome `accepted` means commit succeeded; duplicate/rejected/invalid/disabled/cancelled/assistance outcomes need distinct safe response fields, no leaked unauthorized destination. `pending`/`unknown` are client or reconciliation states, not accepted DB scan outcomes; don't introduce unreviewed enum values into existing table. Distinguish HTTP authentication/authorization error from valid domain decision response. Idempotency conflict/stale expected revision yields 409 or existing equivalent, rate limiting 429, malformed bounded request appropriate validation error, transient failure retry advice only when safe. Do not expose whether a specific external guest exists. Retry lookup after credential revoke returns denial/limited historical receipt as currently authorized, never fresh acceptance. No direct API endpoints for unrestricted SQL, shell, printer address, raw token retrieval, full kiosk guest search or changing station mode via client-only payload.

Example personal-view response shape: `{ "destination": {"kind":"capacity_pool","areaLabel":"Example foyer","entryLabel":"Entrance B"}, "publishedRevision":12,"mapRevision":5,"route":{"kind":"text","instructions":["Follow approved foyer signs."]},"expiresAt":"...","asOf":"..." }`. No seat label for a capacity pool; actual route values must be approved, not synthesized. Include programme/locale/help and optional authorized display name only when allowed. All results schema validated; data-minimized projections tested at HTTP, SQL and cache boundaries. API and browser contract tests must use real runtime roles and synthetic fixtures; mocked scanner/renderer adapters are supplementary and not proof of actual hardware acceptance.

## 22. AGIS-20 — Operational quality, localization, accessibility and lifecycle

Inherit existing UX and OAC requirements. Default locale bs-BA/en, preserve diacritics, UTF-8, locale-specific date/time and separate event timezone/DST. Human readable station code/location independent of language; do not translate enum/IDs. Guest can switch language without reissuing token or altering staff preference, personal session still bounded. Fallback language explicit if a permitted authored translation missing, mandatory publication policy for critical instructions. Brand precedence event → authorized venue → organization → platform per TDS/PAC; station-specific presentation overrides only approved tokens within inherited policy, personal staff theme not published brand. High contrast mode, visible focus, readable typography, large touch controls (candidate 44 CSS px target), keyboard-only equivalents, screen-reader status/live regions (no unnecessary spoken personal data), text alternatives to color/map/audio, manual camera fallback, accessible route choices. Target WCAG 2.2 AA for web surfaces; require manual assistive-tech evidence, no conformance claim from automated tool alone. Representative viewports 360/768/1280/1920 CSS px, portrait/landscape, 200% zoom and selected kiosks. Do not require horizontal scroll for critical actions, avoid obscured focus/scan status. WCAG references/design measurements candidate acceptance until reviewed; no actual devices measured.

### 22.1 Provisional service targets and reference test envelope

These are proposed initial engineering targets, subject to Blueprint/PAC/OAC baseline reconciliation and measured environment. Specify actual server CPU/RAM/storage, topology, software build, network RTT/bandwidth, browser/device and dataset, not an unqualified SLA. Initial synthetic reference: 1 tenant/event, 2,000 participations, 3 sessions, 10 gate devices, 4 information stations, 2 passive displays, 1 print station, 20 concurrent staff clients; 10 scan commands/s sustained 5 minutes and 25/s 10-second burst (including duplicate/invalid attempts). Use 4 vCPU/8 GiB reference only as candidate benchmark, measure and adjust; hardware not specified by owner. Separate server latency from human scan/decoder/physical printer time and queue processing. Candidate successful scan API p95 ≤ 500 ms on trusted LAN with healthy DB excluding camera decode, p99 ≤ 1.5 s; authorized duplicate/reject measured separately; UI result ≤ 1 s p95 after valid decode under test RTT ≤ 50 ms; kiosk verified personal projection p95 ≤ 1 s excluding factor delivery and map asset download; no false successful response, no duplicate attendance under concurrent test. EOC material committed change visible p95 ≤ 2 s under healthy connection; show stale status after defined threshold and resync within 5 s p95 after successful reconnect/snapshot at test load. Heartbeat 15/45/90 s proposed as above; measure browser background throttling separately. Print/render queue target reported by artifact complexity and device, no unsupported physical print SLA; one render failure cannot block gate commands. Rate limiting must preserve normal throughput; test invalid flood without exposing personal records. Optional offline caps as §17, security invariants zero tolerance. Record p50/p95/p99, throughput/error rate, queue age, DB locks, memory/CPU, network and sample count; define how timeout/rejected requests counted. If target not met, document gap and reviewer decision, not silent adjustment or pass. Do not let advanced graph routing/rendering block initial static directions/check-in reliability.

### 22.2 Monitoring, recovery and closing event operations

Safe operational logs/metrics: scan outcome counts, processing duration, idempotent retries/conflicts, queue age and reconciliation outcomes, device heartbeat age, lease expiry, publication freshness, print state and worker failure; redact token, guest fields, raw scanned content and sensitive IDs from broad labels. Avoid high cardinality and personal tracking. Correlation IDs support permissioned drilldown; safe PAC technical status not tenant guest info. Alarm thresholds configurable and deduplicated; alert acknowledges receipt, resolution requires actual remediation. Health endpoints separate liveness/readiness, DB/outbox/render status; show dependencies accurately (render failure doesn't imply gate down). Backups include existing database, brand/assets, published revisions, private artifact store and protected encryption keys under PAC; device lease/cache not a substitute. Restore isolated with delivery/printing disabled, validate migration/key consistency and append-only audit, revoke/reissue potentially stale credentials/leases and reconcile revocations that occurred since backup, uncertain attendance and pending jobs before reopen. No automatic replay of old scans/print or resurrected access. Include safe host recovery, both native/Compose installers, LAN certificate trust, least-privilege runtime and maintenance drain. No application host shell/Docker access. Final deployment acceptance remains Phase 9; testing incremental in CI/synthetic env.

Event/session closure: review actual confirmed arrival/present/exception counts, unresolved offline captures, outstanding print jobs, current station bindings, public display publication end, retention/hold policy. Stop accepting new scans according to owning event/session policy; explicitly close/disable/expire devices and guest views, preserve historical receipts and current approved snapshots, no destructive clearing of authoritative records. Unresolved offline/uncertain work needs authorized reconciliation/discard with reason; no fake attendance or automatic settlement. Close station before redeploy; purge transient personal cache/print files under policy, not audit history; show safe post-event help/public content only within validity. Reports clearly label event/session and definitions, time, source revision and filters, authorized export only. On tenant suspension, preserve facts and revoke current scopes as PAC/OAC; restoring access requires explicit readiness/new lease, no resurrection of previous guest sessions. Retention periods, legal requirements, device custody, guest verification policy and venue procedures require actual organization validation. No claim of legal compliance or production readiness solely from spec.

## 23. Implementation milestones, issue ownership and dependencies

Preserve current Codex #104/#112 foundation closure, then #105 spatial editor, #106 allocation and #107 admission/Cockpit, with #110/#111 and #108 in existing roadmap order. AGIS work packages refine those issues, not a new competing project. M0 when owning work scheduled; no wholesale authentication rewrite, no early VM testing, no branch reset or environment republication. All criteria below are **not run**. Each test uses synthetic data, actual authorized identities and exact candidate commit, recorded fixture, preconditions, expected/observed results, counts/queries, evidence links and unresolved limitations. # Eventor Communication, Invitation Distribution and Multi-Channel Delivery (CID)
## Technical specification v1.0

**Status:** Proposed for product-owner review. Not an authorization to integrate or implement.  
**Date:** 2026-11-27. **Inspected main:** `a5cfcf0ad9d86dbf06ebb7599cc97e2070f64b01` (PR #234). AGIS approved scope inspected at PR #235 head `86ab2e5827cc363cc91cde8be4a8bb9f4bcbe92f`; PR was open and unmerged at inspection.  
**Proposed repository destination:** `docs/implementation-design/v0.3/COMMUNICATION_INVITATION_DISTRIBUTION_AND_MULTI_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESIGN_v1.0.md`. Relative links below target that location.  
**Document control:** CID-01–24; CID-M0–M7; CID-AC-01–48. All future interfaces, limits and entity names are proposals unless described as existing. Acceptance cases not run. CID here means communication and invitation distribution; it is not the CDI external prerequisite/coordination module.  
**Primary owning issue:** #111. Dependencies and integration: #104, #107, #108, #110, #112; #105/#106 for published maps/allocations. No new development track or issue requested.

## 1. Executive objective and product rules

Deliver a unified, configurable Communication and Delivery Center for Eventor organizations. A venue provider can communicate with booking customers without an operational event; an organizer can invite participants, collect RSVP, distribute passes and send approved updates; a hybrid organization can independently do both. Authorized operators can choose electronic or physical distribution methods according to purpose, recipient eligibility, organization policy, provider capabilities and actual cost. Eventor must support persons who have no email address, telephone, messaging account, smartphone or internet connection. Sending a message is an operational action, not a mandatory dependency of every business workflow.

Separate domain intent, approved content, audience, transport, delivery evidence and recipient action. Invitation, RSVP, eligibility, admission credential, physical attendance, booking offer/acceptance, payment and event lifecycle remain independent facts. A sent invitation is not an accepted RSVP. A delivered offer is not a booking confirmation. A read notice is not acceptance of a cancellation, a task or a collaboration grant. A print job does not confirm handover, admission or payment. No delivery adapter may alter any of those business facts. Domain owners initiate and authorize their own commands; CID transports or records distribution and exposes purpose-limited evidence. Where a recipient acts, the authoritative domain endpoint verifies the exact capability and explicit action.

A shared delivery service does not imply a global recipient directory, shared credential, shared provider account or cross-tenant access. The normal organization context, explicit event/booking/task scopes, field-level restrictions, active grants, purpose and recipient authority apply. Platform-level service administration is a separate bounded context, not inherited access to guest or customer communications. A provider-only booking need not create event/guest records. Cross-party notices contain the deliberately shared projection, not an organization's underlying booking, guest, commercial or security data.

**Deployment independence:** native Linux and Docker Compose remain first-class. Local/intranet-only operation, local capture and manual distribution must work without paid services. Public guest links require reachable approved origin and TLS; external provider access, DNS, mail domains and callbacks depend on site networking. Home ISP limitations are a test environment characteristic, not product architecture. Do not require incoming SMTP, a hosted SaaS control plane, a specific port, commercial gateway or cloud dependency for core operation. No mandatory public webhook for offline/manual operation; supported polling/manual reconciliation when callbacks cannot be configured, with honest limitations.

**Out of scope:** general-purpose marketing automation/CRM, bulk contact harvesting, social network, private inbox scraping, arbitrary provider scripts, public mail relay, spam tools, unofficial personal-account browser automation, call recording/transcription, unrestricted chatbot conversations, payment processing or platform invoice issuance. Recipient contact consent is not inferred from appearance in the Registry. Do not use the system for unsolicited mass messaging. No guaranteed message delivery, read or provider-side deletion. Optional future channels need reviewed adapters, not arbitrary custom code in the UI.

| AGIS v1.0 ([approved PR #235 revision](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/blob/86ab2e5827cc363cc91cde8be4a8bb9f4bcbe92f/docs/implementation-design/v0.3/ADMISSION_GUEST_INFORMATION_AND_STATION_MANAGEMENT_DESIGN_v1.0.md)) | Admission, Info Pult and printing boundaries; current published seat, distinct credentials and reprint/refresh/replace operations. No personal data on passive displays. Integrate cross-reference after AGIS lands; no assumption its PR has merged. |
| [Organization Lifecycle Acceptance](ORGANIZATION_LIFECYCLE_ACCEPTANCE_SCENARIOS_v1.0.md) | OLA-01–15, G1–G9 and underlying PAC/TDS/OAC/UX tests remain; extend journeys and evidence, no waiver. |
| [Operating model](../../OPERATING_MODEL.md), [architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md), [role model](../../product/USER_ROLES_AND_PERMISSIONS_v0.1.md) | Independent provider/organizer ownership, modular monolith, permissions separate from navigation, deployment-neutral. |
| ADR [0004](../../decisions/0004-optional-event-operations-scope.md), [0005](../../decisions/0005-separate-invitations-rsvp-attendance.md), [0006](../../decisions/0006-cross-organization-collaboration.md), [0007](../../decisions/0007-internationalization.md), [0008](../../decisions/0008-modular-staff-frontend.md) | Optional capabilities, separate lifecycle states, explicit collaboration, bs-BA/en, incremental Vue feature modules. |

Preserve all other accepted ADRs and original history. |

### 2.1 Runtime foundations (read-only inspection, not a new application test)

- `apps/api/src/smtp-transport.ts`: Nodemailer SMTP factory, STARTTLS required or implicit TLS, certificate validation, password or no authentication, sender and reply-to; current send interface is subject + plain text, not HTML/attachment or OAuth sending. No generic HTTP provider or SMS/messaging runtime inferred.
- `apps/staff-web/src/features/email-delivery/EmailDeliveryView.vue`: tenant delivery settings, write-only credential fields, test before enabling config revision, Resend callback configuration for Resend SMTP. `GuestInvitationManagementView.vue`: issue/reissue gated by eligible participation, email readiness and schedule/RSVP revision; staff outside-channel RSVP recording. No general no-email issue/manual sharing path implied by this view.
- `database/migrations/000013_event_changes_notifications.sql`: existing `notification_templates`, `notification_template_revisions`, `event_notification_campaigns`, fixed recipients/exclusions and delivery attempts. Campaign is bound to event decision and specific purposes; do not simply remove constraints to make a generic sender. 000031–000039 extend worker discovery, review/confirmation, configuration, cancellation, report, reconciliation and signed provider events.
- 000033 `organization_delivery_config_revisions` and `organization_delivery_config_heads` are tenant-scoped, versioned, with encrypted EDC1 credential envelope and restricted read/write functions; channel constraint includes email/sms but SMS schema presence is not SMS delivery. Existing one-head-per-channel is not yet multi-provider routing. Preserve existing `organization.delivery.manage` permission semantics.
- 000034–000039: SMTP queue, leases, immutable attempt events, `event.notifications.delivery.manage` reconciliation, provider-neutral normalized events, verified Resend delivered/bounced callbacks and pre-submission stable Message-ID for supported correlation. Callback support inspected for existing notification flow, not proof of identical coverage for every delivery aggregate. Resend SMTP is not Resend HTTP API. Preserve uncertain outcome semantics and no automatic blind retry.
- 000058–000059, 000074: `booking_offer_email_deliveries` and tenant queue, encrypted recipient and capability, pinned offer/config revision, explicit issue and queue, retry/reconcile. Booking offer acceptance is separate.
- 000012, 000075–000089, 000099–000105, 000111: invitation/RSVP identity, encrypted worker envelope, `invitation_deliveries`, `invitation_delivery_attempts`, tenant queue, claim/lease, request-bound idempotency, authorization locks, revocation/eligibility and non-enumerating history. 000078 preserves attempt number and actual result. 000076 guards legacy sending rows as uncertain. Historical design wording about hash-only token means no plaintext durable bearer secret; current authenticated encrypted worker envelopes are a deliberately restricted boundary, not an excuse to persist raw URLs.
- `apps/api/src/notification-worker.ts` currently claims separate domain queues and uses SMTP factory. Contact/credential encryption in `delivery-credentials-crypto.ts` and domain contact routines. Reuse existing tenant discovery, RLS, narrow functions and actual send-authorization locks. Audit newer migrations and route registrations before changing them; no claim of exhaustive runtime coverage.

This design adds shared adapters and a unified **read projection** first, not a wholesale replacement of these domain tables/queues. Preserve IDs, foreign keys, actor attribution, queue state, existing API payloads and browser behavior. No historical status inferred from schema or migrated to stronger evidence. Do not count passing existing CI as CID implementation acceptance. [Project handoff](../../PROJECT_STATE.md) remains authoritative for active work.

## 3. CID-01 — Communication purpose catalogue and owning domains

Purpose is a stable, versioned allowlist, not free-form strings used for authorization. Each purpose specifies owner command, permitted recipient subject types, allowed content bindings, action-capability type, sensitivity, mandatory or optional policy, eligible channels, approval, expiry, retention, and whether automated scheduling/fallback is permissible. Extend catalogue via reviewed migration/contract; no user-created arbitrary SQL recipient selection or action code. One event may enable invitations without admission, or RSVP without portal; a channel can be disabled without deleting existing history or cancelling event.

| Purpose family | Owner and audience | Examples / restrictions |
|---|---|---|
| Organization enrollment, security and support | PAC/OAC identity/membership services; verified intended account or authorized admin | Enrollment, password/security alerts, account recovery and support receipts; use dedicated identity capability, not guest token; offline protected host bootstrap/recovery remains. Generic notification worker cannot reset credentials. Never send passwords or MFA seeds. |
| Booking inquiry and offer | Booking domain; requester/contracting party/contact explicitly authorized | Acknowledgement, clarification, revised offer, expiry reminder, customer decision, confirmation and instructions. Public links scoped to exact offer/action; no implicit event participation. Prices/policies only from pinned permitted snapshot; never disclose unrelated customers. |
| Cancellation, amendment and disruption | Booking provider or organizer per distinct decision/grant | Customer request receipt, authorized decision/effective cancellation, linked organizer notice, replacement date/reconfirmation. Public reason only; delivery cannot execute decision, cancel event, refund or change reservation. |
| Guest invitation / RSVP | Event participation and invitation domain | Issue, distribute, reminder, resend, explicit reissue, response confirmation, reconfirmation; guest-specific purpose/expiry. No response is not declined; delivery does not reset answer. |
| Admission / guest portal / seating | Admission, portal and allocation domain (#105–107/AGIS) | Separate pass distribution, guest-safe destination, programme and published seat change; no other guest positions or internal reason; no attendance on lookup/send. |
| Event programme, operational announcement | Event/session owner | Arrival instructions, approved public schedule/venue notices, accessibility directions, reminders, closing notice; select private vs public projection. A passive display is a publication surface, not recipient delivery evidence. |
| Staff and vendor coordination | Task owner and authorized recipient role/grant | Assignment, due date, request, revision, acknowledgement, escalation, readiness. No broad Registry disclosure or restricted external-prerequisite evidence; coordination not official inspection/certification. |
| Partner collaboration | Grantor/recipient party scoped to grant lifecycle | Proposal/review prompt, acceptance/revocation notification, explicit permitted booking/event link or disruption notice. Message cannot grant access or accept proposal. |
| Post-event correspondence | Event owner; permitted audience | Thank-you, approved feedback form, certificate/document notice; purpose and preference check; no implied marketing authorization. |
| System operation | PAC/OAC operational owner | Queue health, quota/credential expiry, backup incident and readiness; sanitize no secret/content, distinguish staff inbox from external send. |

Some security/contract notices may have a separately lawful necessity, not blanket consent bypass. Default deny unsupported purposes; organization policy cannot bypass law/provider limits. Critical business decision always remains recorded and visible even when no channel eligible; show contact/notification obligation and safe follow-up. Staff must be able to complete non-communication business work independently.

## 4. CID-02 — Channel and provider capability registry

Distinguish channel (email, SMS, WhatsApp, Viber, Telegram, web_push, in_app, manual_share, print, postal, handover, telephone) from provider (SMTP relay, email API, official messaging platform, local renderer, operator) and endpoint/account/sender identity. Multiple providers may serve same channel. A provider transport selection cannot change a recipient's contact or legal eligibility. Define typed capability metadata: supports plain text, HTML, multipart, attachments/media and size/type limits; structured template and approval, localization, sender kinds, destination kinds, opt-in prerequisites, message-window rules, batch behavior, idempotency support/window, callback signature and status types, polling, cancellation, rate limits, cost units/currency, region/registration restrictions, link length and content rules. Each capability version pinned to routing/validation evidence. Unknown is unsupported, not permissive. Official docs and actual account evidence required at scheduling; provider policy/version changes trigger readiness revalidation.

| Channel | Candidate adapter pattern | Evidence / limitations |
|---|---|---|
| Email SMTP | Existing Nodemailer factory; TLS, approved credentials, local relay | SMTP acceptance only; DSN/provider callbacks only when verified. No read/open inference. |
| Email HTTP | Versioned first-class API adapters e.g. Resend initially; other candidates Brevo, Mailgun, SendGrid, SES, Gmail API, Microsoft Graph | Per-account authentication, permissions, verified sender, provider idempotency semantics and callbacks; no blanket compatibility claim. |
| SMS | Official gateway API, e.g. Twilio or regional provider | E.164 or approved regional routing, registration, Unicode and segment cost, status receipts if supported; no read confirmation. |
| WhatsApp | Official Business Platform or approved BSP | Registered business sender, recipient opt-in, approved templates/categories/windows as required by account/provider, media/link constraints. No consumer session automation. |
| Viber | Official Business Messages provider or official subscribed-bot adapter | Business route and bot subscription IDs are different; phone contact alone not bot enrollment. Delivery/read only supported evidence. |
| Telegram (optional) | Official Bot API | Guest initiates/binds bot conversation; no unsolicited lookup by phone; use verified chat reference; no read receipt assumption. |
| Web push | Standards-based push service with VAPID, encrypted payload and subscription | Browser permission + verified subscription; no forced prompt; push-service acceptance not human read; notification text minimal. |
| In-app | Existing scoped realtime/inbox projection | Only active entitled account/session or guest portal with valid capability; no external delivery claim. |
| Manual digital share | Explicit secure copy/download/handoff | Operator evidence only; no automated WhatsApp/Viber delivery claim from opening share sheet. |
| Print / handover / postal | Existing TDS and AGIS print/document paths + manual record | Rendered/printed/dispatched/handed-over separate; carrier tracking when verified. |
| Telephone | Operator task and structured outcome | Not dialer or call recording; actor records contacted/left message/no answer and separate domain response if authorized. |

The minimum supported product includes independent manual, print, in-app and configurable SMTP even without external account. CID proposes official HTTP email, OAuth-capable email, SMS, WhatsApp and Viber adapter coverage for the complete scope, with web push supported as opt-in; Telegram remains optional extension. For each advertised supported provider, require actual provider/account sandbox evidence as applicable. An event/tenant may choose none or subset. Release-wide omission of a required channel needs explicit scope decision, not fake “supported” toggle. Provider examples are candidates, not promises of accounts/free plans/current prices. No provider-specific mandatory dependency.

## 5. CID-03 — Organization-managed providers and readiness

OAC → Administration → Communication and Delivery → Providers shows channel, provider/account, sender, config revision, readiness, last verified time, supported features, health, usage and callback capability without plaintext secrets. An authorized tenant administrator may add named profile(s), choose channel/adapter, configure approved endpoints, verify sender identity, supply write-only credentials, authorize OAuth, test and publish an immutable revision. Choose primary/default profile per purpose and channel within tenant policy; optional alternative profile not auto-selected unless reviewed route plan. Support disabled/draft/verified/active/draining/retired state with distinct credential and health dimensions. “Verified” is a test of a specific revision/account/sender/capability, not promise of eventual delivery. Changed host, sender, account, key or permissions invalidates applicable test. Test sends limited to separately verified operator-controlled destinations, synthetic text and non-live links, no real guest audience. Credential validation can be read-only where provider supports, then actual test send when enabling. No save/preview/test triggers live invitation.

Store settings non-secret allowlisted projection; never return password, API token, refresh token, webhook secret, encrypted blob or unmasked recipient in ordinary list. Credential revision/secret version and access controls separate; rotate/revoke without altering historic provider reference. If a pinned job uses a disabled/revoked credential or provider, block before submission; replan or reapprove route, never silently use unrelated sender. In-flight submissions may already have escaped; mark honest uncertain/accepted and reconcile. Provider removal/drain reviews queued jobs, scheduled campaigns, pending callbacks, suppression and active leases; do not delete evidence. Expired OAuth access or temporary rate-limit is not same as revoked provider access. Readiness includes domain verification, provider account status, credentials, permission scope, test, reachable endpoints, callback state and appropriate data processing review. Missing callback may allow accepted-only send if policy explicitly permits; never invent delivered. Health checks do not send unsolicited messages.

## 6. CID-04 — Platform-managed delivery services

PAC may optionally offer a shared provider service (for example operator-paid SMTP or email API) to explicitly assigned organizations. Organization-owned profiles remain independent. Platform service = service identity, allowed purpose/channel, provider and sender policy, revision, secret scope, quotas, cost/usage allocation, support/recovery policy. Tenant assignment = explicit active service grant with own routing profile, tenant-specific verified sender/domain or disclosed shared sender, allowed purpose/limits, start/end, billing/usage attribution, audit. Separate activation and assignment from tenant choosing to use it. No implicit entitlement via admin flag, hosting plan or OAC login. OAC sees own assignment/readiness/remaining quota only, not global credential/account ID that can route another tenant or other tenants' volume/content/destinations.

Prefer provider subaccounts/scoped keys and tenant-specific callback routing whenever supported; if shared account cannot reliably isolate callbacks, senders, suppressions, recipient evidence and quotas, do not support that deployment mode. Shared account provider event IDs may collide across provider accounts; use service/account namespace and exact correlation; ambiguous mapping quarantined with no disclosure. PAC can rotate/disable service or change limits with impact preview; active tenant grants revocation prevents new sends and discloses in-flight uncertainty. Only narrow broker/worker can retrieve permitted secret after validating tenant assignment, purpose, sender, destination policy and live lease. No cross-tenant secret reads from staff or general runtime. Platform operator's support diagnostics are aggregate/redacted, and sensitive tenant inspection requires explicit approved support under PAC policy and actual actor, expiry, audit; never silent impersonation. Cross-tenant abuse/bounce complaints investigated within authorized bounds. Shared suppression constraints handled without revealing other tenants' contacts (deny generic reason; service scope not public directory). Tenant cannot override provider/global abuse stop. Platform quotas not customer invoices; optional settlement separately designed, no charge execution.

## 7. CID-05 — Email SMTP and modern HTTP API

Preserve compatible SMTP with explicit TLS mode and server certificate verification; prefer authenticated submission or approved local relay. Password/app credential supported only when provider policy permits; no promise that consumer Gmail or Microsoft 365 password auth works. OAuth may authenticate SMTP (SASL XOAUTH2 where supported) or HTTP API; authentication and transport are separate settings. Add TDS text + sanitized HTML multipart, optional approved private generated PDF/ICS/inline approved asset where provider supports; always useful plaintext alternative. Do not send bearer credentials in headers, subject, attachment names or tracking data. One intended recipient per personalization, no bulk CC leaking guests; BCC operational generic notices only after reviewed policy, default one recipient. Avoid list headers disclosing recipient selection. Reply-to approved per organization/purpose; non-spoofable verified sender; domain SPF/DKIM/DMARC readiness documented and checked as applicable without exposing DNS changes as automatically made. Include provider-supported unsubscribe options for relevant consent-bound content, separate purpose policy and mandatory transactional notices. No tracking pixel default; open rates not read evidence. Bounce/complaint suppression scoped and audited.

HTTP adapters send a deterministic immutable request or approved provider template reference, validated envelope, recipient and content hashes, stable attempt/request reference; if provider supports idempotency, persist key before call and use only within documented validity and exact payload. Never retry an ambiguous acceptance after idempotency expiry on assumption safe. Provider receipt ID not global; accepted does not mean delivered. Retry only on definite rejection before acceptance, with bounded policies. HTTP timeouts, network reset after write, unknown response, partial batch outcome and worker crash after transmission are uncertain unless proven otherwise. Disable automatic POST retry/redirects by SDK unless reviewed. HTTP API key scope least privilege, webhook reconciliation per adapter. First reference HTTP adapter proposed Resend due to existing correlation knowledge; actual choice at M0, no mandate to use Resend commercially. Provider-specific callbacks reviewed rather than applying SMTP Resend webhook semantics globally.

## 8. CID-06 — OAuth account linking and secret lifecycle

Provide approved named OAuth integrations (not arbitrary token endpoint input). Use confidential server-side client, Authorization Code + PKCE where provider supports, exact redirect origins, cryptographically random single-use state bound to tenant, actor/session, provider, requested scope and expiry; validate issuer/tenant/account, redirect and token claims as applicable. OAuth callback must not switch Eventor workspace or expose another organization's account. Store refresh/access token only in authenticated encrypted secret boundary; short-lived access token in memory when possible; never browser storage, URLs/logs or editable settings. Scope send-only where available, no mailbox read or broad directory unless specifically approved and necessary. Service/client-credentials flow only where supported with explicit provider admin consent and allowed mailbox/resource grant; avoid blanket delegated access. Disconnect/revoke locally immediately; best-effort provider-side revocation separately reported. No OAuth as substitute for Eventor user session, no password reset or global membership created.

Serialize refresh per provider credential version with lease/CAS to avoid losing rotating refresh token; on invalid_grant or expired consent stop sends, show reauthorization required. Retry on definite pre-send auth expiry only after renewed same-account credentials and current permissions; never switch account or payload automatically. Token encryption key separation/rotation under existing key policy, no secret access via backup report. Restore must not resurrect revoked provider or old consent; reconcile credential epoch/revocations with operator before opening queues. Provider admin approval/account ownership changes require re-review. Audit link/refresh outcome/revoke with safe actor/account ref/scope and no secret. OAuth discovery endpoints fixed/allowlisted TLS, no arbitrary IdP URL. Test CSRF, stale state, account mix-up, replay, concurrent refresh, wrong tenant callback and revoked consent.

## 9. CID-07 — SMS delivery

Use official gateway adapters supporting target countries and sender registration. Normalize phone numbers with country context, preserve original encrypted value and explicit verification; do not guess country when ambiguous, do not treat phone identity as proven. Prefer per-recipient single message intent, provider segment calculation/limits and cost preview. GSM-7 extension table and Unicode/UCS-2 behavior must be tested against provider algorithm; Bosnian diacritics, long links, emoji and multi-segment messages may affect cost. Never silently transliterate a guest's name or split a secure URL. No sensitive details in SMS/lock screen; short approved personal link and minimal context. First-party token URL may be compact using opaque capability; never third-party public shortener with tracking or enumerable reference. Sender ID/short code/number and reply support country/provider specific; only approved registered sender. STOP/opt-out or provider suppression normalized and applied to correct contact/purpose scope, authenticated inbound callback; no free-form reply as RSVP unless separate reviewed verification/domain command. Receipts may be delayed, unavailable or partial; no read status. Cost cap by actual estimated segments and country; policy blocks uncertain/unpriced paid route unless bounded approved quote. No rerouting around carrier blocks or suppression.

## 10. CID-08 — WhatsApp official business messaging

Use official Business Platform or approved provider service only. Tenant-owned business identity/number and explicit verified sender assignment, account readiness, region/recipient eligibility, opt-in proof and approved template/category/language mapping where required. Provider rules and any conversation/time-window eligibility validated at review and send, not hardcoded timeless assumptions. Approved provider template version must match TDS mapped fields/locale and allowed purpose; template rejection/paused status stops send, not auto-switch to arbitrary text. Map text/media/button/URL parameters from typed purpose projection; approved attachment via private bounded provider upload or dedicated revocable short-lived link as supported. No shared public guest file URL. Do not transmit private floor plans, internal notes or unrelated contacts. No unofficial WhatsApp Web scraping, consumer personal session/token import, bulk phone probing or bypass of provider policy.

Inbound event scope: verified status events, opt-out, structured replies routed to minimal staff follow-up or approved domain verification. A WhatsApp number/chat receipt alone is not RSVP/booking acceptance; explicit verified Eventor capability and separate authoritative action required. Read receipt only if verifiable and allowed, never as legal acceptance. Provider fees/quality/quotas/template categories may change; readiness tracks current policy/estimate. Manual sharing via user-selected app remains separate from official business API send, no fabricated delivery tracking.

## 11. CID-09 — Viber and optional Telegram

Viber has distinct official Business Messages (where approved service can address eligible phone contacts) and bot interfaces (subscriber identifier and prior subscription). Maintain explicit adapter variants and destination kinds. Do not assume a phone number identifies a bot subscriber or that a business sender works in all countries. Register sender, verify service/contract requirements, capture opt-in, map approved message/template formats and callback semantics; normalize delivery/read only if supported. Validate rich media/URL constraints, country pricing and provider status before activation. No personal account automation or unofficial Viber desktop integration. Staff may record manual handoff without claiming Viber delivered/read.

Telegram optional Bot API: tenant-managed or explicitly granted bot identity, guest initiates conversation and binds verified chat via a one-time, purpose-limited enrollment challenge from authenticated portal/staff-assisted flow. Do not include live RSVP/admission token in bot enrollment URL; separate nonce bound to tenant/event/intended contact and expiry, explicit confirmation prevents wrong-chat linking. Store encrypted chat identifier scoped to bot/tenant/contact, user can disconnect, respect blocked/deleted chat. Never scan usernames, phone numbers or group members; private chat for personal content, group broadcast only approved public projection. Verify webhooks via supported secret mechanism or authenticated polling with durable update cursor; no arbitrary command execution. Bot send acceptance not proof of read. Optional extension can remain disabled with no effect on core workflow.

## 12. CID-10 — Web push and in-app delivery

Browser/PWA subscription only after contextual explanation and user permission; no coercive prompt on login, no requirement to accept for RSVP/booking. Bind subscription to authorized account or event-scoped verified guest context, browser/service worker/origin and purpose; explicitly confirm selection and support revoke/unsubscribe, expiry and rotation. Encrypt endpoint and key material, validate endpoint through approved push-service/egress policy, prevent SSRF from attacker-controlled subscriptions. VAPID key per deployment or isolated scope as reviewed; use standard payload encryption, key rotation and bounded TTL. Push message default generic (“Event information updated”), no name, private seat, credential, price or restricted details on lock screen. Clicking opens approved origin and revalidates current authority; not a raw token in notification body. Push provider acceptance, service-worker receipt (if specifically implemented) and human action are distinct; no read claim. Multiple device subscriptions and shared device removal; clear sensitive state on workspace switch, logout, guest expiry or kiosk reset. No guest push subscription on shared Info Pult by default.

In-app notification is an authorized projection of event/task/booking/communication state and separate personal read/ack marker. Use existing outbox/realtime cursor rules, no global data broadcast, revalidate on reconnect and revoke. A read marker is not approval or acceptance. Public programme signage is publication through AGIS/TDS, not a push subscription or personal delivery. Offline local operation may show current reachable-server notices even if external push fails; no dependency on browser vendor service for core.

## 13. CID-11 — Channel-independent invitation and capability distribution

Refactor only the owning invitation command boundary when scheduled. Separate issuance of one invitation revision and one appropriate purpose-bound access capability from preparation of zero or more distribution jobs/tasks. Preserve current explicit issue-and-email command/API behavior through an adapter; add explicit issue-without-email and reviewed distribution choices. A person with no electronic contact can receive a printed invitation or a staff-recorded invitation and answer by phone or in person. Issuance policy must check eligible participation, event/schedule/RSVP revisions, actual permission, optional capability, expiry and explicit delivery/handover intent; lack of email is a channel eligibility problem, not invitation eligibility. Do not convert all current invitations into a new state or assume that every guest must have an RSVP token. If RSVP disabled or not applicable, issue only approved invitation/card semantics; never invent consent or attendance. Preserve invitation history, current response and eligibility. Separate issue, resend same valid credential, repeat distribution of same version, and explicit replacement/reissue that revokes old link. A changed seating plan alone does not necessarily replace invitation/admission/portal credential. A revoked/expired capability cannot be distributed again through cached artifact/job; show blocked and require authorized review.

| Operator action | Required authoritative effect |
|---|---|
| Prepare invitation draft/preview | No credential issuance, delivery, response or attendance. Synthetic link/QR in preview. |
| Issue invitation without email | Explicit invitation revision, optional active purpose-limited capability and distribution plan; no false sent status. |
| Send existing active invitation on another permitted channel | New reviewed delivery intent linked to same invitation/revision, same valid credential; no RSVP reset. |
| Reissue expired/compromised invitation | Existing domain lifecycle revokes/replaces atomically, old pending jobs/artifacts blocked, history retained; new distribution reviewed. |
| Distribute admission pass or portal access | Separate authorized domain-issued capability, typed TDS binding, no invitation token reused as admission/portal. |
| Record telephone/written response | Existing authorized staff response command with source/respondent/time/reason, not a transport callback or delivery state. |

Use high-entropy opaque tokens, hashed server lookup and purpose-bound revocation. Follow existing fragment-based secure link resolution and no-referrer/no analytics policy. Encrypt necessary delivery-only bearer material with existing authenticated envelope binding to tenant, purpose and exact subject/revision; only issuing/rendering/delivery services get narrowly scoped access. Durable plaintext URLs prohibited in logs, reports, queue metadata, idempotency receipts, templates, metrics and provider correlation. Delivery content can necessarily contain the intended live capability; minimize provider retention and disclose third-party processing, avoid unnecessary bearer attachment, and do not promise message recall. The first-party portal links must not contain guest personal data, nor trigger domain mutation on GET or automated preview. Public link resolution must not depend on staff cookie, and must preserve rate limits, non-enumeration and locale. When possible warn against forwarding, allow secondary verification for sensitive purposes, expire and revoke leaked links. All new channels must use these same domain constraints, not a general link generator.

## 14. CID-12 — Manual digital sharing, physical distribution and telephone workflow

An operator with explicit `share/export` authority for the exact domain record may reveal/copy an active personalized link or obtain a private approved document, after reviewing recipient, purpose, current revision, channel policy, expiry and confidentiality. A one-time reveal response is no-store, redacted from traces and not retained in local/browser history; audit actor, intended recipient, reason, action and digest (not token). Prefer server-rendered private document through TDS; actual PDF may contain live QR and must be encrypted/authorized at rest and served only through a short-lived controlled download, not public object URL. Clipboard and external app cannot be reliably cleared or controlled by Eventor: explicitly warn, avoid on unattended kiosk; support staff-managed safe alternative. No public batch export of live links or address lists by default; any high-risk batch handover needs separate scope, approval, access expiry, recipient-specific packet manifest, audit, storage/retention and explicit opt-in policy. A manual handoff cannot be auto-verified; “link prepared/copied” or “file downloaded” is not “sent/delivered”. Opening a user-selected share sheet/email draft is not evidence of delivery. Do not launch unsolicited sends or automate personal messenger accounts.

Printing: use AGIS/TDS approved document jobs for individual cards, multi-up PDF, envelopes/address labels, direction slips and distribution packs. Verify physical dimensions, localized names/diacritics, QR decode, and revision manifest. A printed invitation may include distinct RSVP link/QR and admission QR only if authorized; use labels and validation to prevent confusion. Reprint same artifact if retained and still authorized; render current revision if reviewed; replace credential only via explicit issuing command. Prevent repeated job submission after ambiguous print; print spool acceptance is not paper success or handover. No event attendee list on unattended shared printer or public display. Track printer output pickup/disposal in tenant procedure. Printed access credential may still work until expiry/revocation even after policy changes; warn when old seating/document stale, verify current data at gate/Info Pult. Do not imply all old paper can be recalled.

Physical dispatch task: intended recipient (domain subject, not loose arbitrary contact), delivery method handover/post/courier, approved address snapshot only if permitted, packet/document refs and version, assigned operator, due time, status and evidence, restricted reference if carrier tracking allowed. States prepared, ready, dispatched, handover_claimed, carrier_confirmed (if verified), returned, cancelled, lost, unknown; separate events with actual actor/source and observed vs recorded time. Optional receipt signature is minimized and retention-governed, not mandatory identity document collection. No upload of identity documents by default; restricted evidence only with defined necessity. Correct erroneous handover by append-only correction, not deleting history. If recipient declines to accept packet, record refusal of handover, not RSVP declined unless independently recorded. Postage/handling estimate and actual cost separately; no automatic buying or carrier integration required.

Telephone task: approved contact with masked number until authorized reveal, script/template pinned to language and purpose, operator confirms intended person under event policy, record attempted/no answer/left message/contacted/wrong number/declined contact, safe notes and follow-up date; no confidential information left in voicemail or passed to unverified third party. Optional representative allowed only by existing invitation/response policy. Record RSVP separately via outside-channel command, never interpret call outcome as acceptance. Phone contact preference and do-not-contact apply. No autodial/recording/transcription; staff calls through own authorized means. If guest has no usable contact, permit assigned in-person invitation or manual follow-up queue. Booking customers, vendors and staff use analogous purpose-bound manual tasks, not guest-only records. All distribution modes searchable by authorized subject and history, with evidence level and status provenance.

## 15. CID-13 — Recipient identity, contact points, preferences and consent

Reuse existing Guest Registry encrypted contact points, verification/source references and event participation; do not clone all guest contacts into campaign records. Booking customer/contact, organization staff account/membership, delegated task contact and collaboration party have distinct identity boundaries. Communication targets are typed domain subject references; resolution uses exact owning context, not universal cross-tenant matching. Model phone/email/postal/verified chat/subscription/contact kind, normalized encrypted value, keyed tenant-scoped blind index where existing search policy permits, purpose/owner and verification evidence. Do not use unsalted hashes of phone/email for public dedup; low entropy contacts can be enumerated. Chat IDs and push endpoints treated as sensitive. A contact may be shared by relatives/assistants; same address does not prove same person or authority, and dedup must not suppress different personalized invitation subjects silently. Prompt operator review for shared contact and require policy-permitted delivery and representative evidence. Normalize phone with actual country, validate syntax not proof, do not probe contacts without permission. Preserve old snapshots and merge/restoration rules; verified contact does not imply consent. Guest Registry update never silently rewrites pinned recipient contact or previously issued content.

Preferences: tenant + subject + contact + purpose family + channel (and explicit event override where appropriate), ordered preferred routes, allowed fallback, language, contact hours/timezone, accessibility/print assistance and representative rules. Unknown preference means apply reviewed policy or manual follow-up, not every channel. Organization default may suggest, not override a restriction. A preference is not consent, verification or legal basis. Record channel eligibility facts separately: purpose/legal basis category, source, collection notice/version, scope, consent status and time, expiry/withdrawal, evidence ref, verified subject/contact, operator or provider event. Do not label legitimate operational necessity as consent when not obtained; actual lawful basis, data processing terms, transfers and retention require local legal review. Consent not inferred from importing a contact, a past RSVP, contact verification, a prior message or provider acceptance. Default deny when required proof unknown. Provide recipient-controlled preference/opt-out link/token distinct from RSVP and admission; no account required if scoped secure link; token GET non-mutating, explicit confirmation POST. Provider opt-out verified and reconciled; opt-in only affirmative appropriate proof, not reset by contact edits, merge, importing CSV or provider switch. Revocation wins over stale snapshots.

Suppression hierarchy: legal/security/abuse and provider block; tenant/channel/purpose-specific consent or verified opt-out; hard bounce/wrong address/unreachable/subscription revoked; purpose and event policy; preference; verified route readiness. A lower-level override never bypasses a hard block. Transactional/necessary notices require separately approved lawful basis and provider permission; avoid treating event cancellation as promotional consent, do not circumvent provider STOP, use another separately permitted route or authorized manual task. Record exclusions by safe reason and scope. Do not reveal other organizations' suppressions or raw contact data in logs/metrics. Global provider suppression may be enforced without disclosing which tenant or person caused it. Scoped correction of mistaken suppression requires proof, actor/reason/audit and actual provider clearance where applicable.

Merge and deletion: retain immutable delivery attribution to historic event subject/contact version; current opt-out must propagate to still-effective matching contact within same allowed subject/policy scope; avoid accidental consent transfer on merge or restoration. Re-resolve current authority before submission, but do not retarget silently; changed address/version requires reviewed recipient/plan or explicit domain policy with fresh evidence. Retention/legal hold and lawful purge apply to contact/callback/attachment evidence; preserve non-identifying required integrity/audit facts when content lawfully purged. No shared marketing data, guest directory export or vendor use without explicit grant. Contact consent/preferences are not public listing API.

## 16. CID-14 — Campaign Designer, authoring, audience and review

OAC Communication and Delivery Center and EOC Communications tab are views over same authorized domain services. Canonical workflow: Choose purpose/domain subject → audience → communication policy → select TDS variants → route/eligibility preview → schedule and cost estimate → review → explicit approval/confirm → queue/schedule → monitor/reconcile → close/cancel remaining. Booking-specific send action may open a prefiltered single-recipient flow, with same gates; no need to enter event context for booking. Operator sees only accessible purposes, audience rows/fields/counts, masked contact and readiness. Search and saved filters server-scoped; no broad Registry export to browser or provider. Audience sources: selected event participants with statuses/groups/authorized tags, previously invited/accepted/tentative, session allocation, booking contacts for exact booking, permitted vendor task recipients, explicit partner party, active staff members, approved public bulletin. Exclude hidden restricted tags from unauthorized segmentation; do not leak restricted cohorts via counts, search or exclusions. OAC broad access still requires relevant domain action permission. No arbitrary pasted destination list for transactional purpose or using platform account as generic relay. Legitimate custom audience requires explicit eligible domain subjects, not untrusted raw addresses. Import contacts through existing reviewed Registry/booking contact lifecycle first.

TDS supplies versioned templates, language variants, rich text/block email/graphical canvas, approved assets and typed fields. CID owns campaign/route/schedule/estimate configuration, not content editor. Add channel-specific bounded short text/message template mapping in same TDS catalogue with approved provider template ID/version/status; validate locale, variable names/count/order, media constraints, URL action semantics and safe rendering. Explicitly link representations of same communication intent; no assumption that HTML can be converted losslessly to SMS or WhatsApp template. Locale resolution uses recipient preference > purpose/event policy > organization default > safe supported fallback; explicit missing variant warning/exclusion or approved fallback, not accidental wrong-language send. Preserve bs-BA/en and diacritics, local date/time format and timezone. Sensitive template variables allowlisted by purpose and current field authority; preview uses synthetic fixture by default. Privileged real-recipient preview requires exact permission and audit, no live token, never sends or issues. Test send uses separate safe verified target with TEST marker and non-live token. No hidden tracker, arbitrary script or remote resource fetch in renderer. HTML, attachment and image size/content validated. Message lock includes exact resolved brand/asset/template/locale/renderer/projection revisions and digest.

Review snapshot: purpose/domain revision and current relevant capabilities; audience identities, contact versions and exclusions; selected channels/ordered routes and provider/config/sender revisions; eligibility policy revision, consent/preference evidence versions, template/brand/locale mapping, rendered sample/diagnostics, estimated billable units/currency/max reservation, schedule/timezone/cutoff, approval expiry and fallbacks; canonical sorted digest of all material meaning. Distinguish draft audience preview from reviewed fixed audience.
