# ADR 0012 — Source-reference encryption identity during profile merges

- Status is accepted.
- Date is 2026-11-24.
- Related: [ADR 0009](0009-guest-registry-merge.md), [#104](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/104).

## Context

Source-reference keys already include organization, person ID and source system. Reassigning an identifier's logical owner without preserving its encryption identity makes the existing ciphertext unreadable. Reference fingerprints used for exact import matching are organization/source/value scoped and must remain stable.

## Decision

Keep the existing key derivation and encrypted contents. `person_identifiers.encryption_person_id` records the identity used for encryption, with a same-organization person foreign key. A trigger sets it to the current person on insertion or explicit ciphertext replacement. An ownership-only merge/restoration leaves it unchanged. The authorized service projection supplies this private binding to the API for decryption; the HTTP response continues to expose only reference ID, source and value.

Migration 000183 backfills the binding from existing ownership without changing ciphertext. The migration runner holds an atomic transaction and table lock. Owner-only RLS bypass is limited to that backfill, and forced RLS is restored before commit. A populated two-tenant upgrade rehearsal verifies both bindings, unchanged values, tenant isolation and the same-organization foreign key.

A reviewer with Registry merge and source-reference management authority may explicitly transfer supported external source references. Contact transfer requires its own authority and confirmation when contacts are also present. The review binds both reference sets; stable parent locks serialize changes. Both profiles' revision semantics continue to invalidate stale reference editors. Older merge signatures cannot bypass the new resolution requirement.

The append-only `person_merge_reference_transfers` journal stores only references and canonical v1 SHA-256 state evidence. Its hash uses explicit fields, hexadecimal bytes and epoch time, so session timezone and bytea formatting cannot change the result. The journal intentionally has no foreign key to the current identifier: an authorized later reference removal remains possible. Removed encrypted values are not copied into the journal or recreated during restoration.

Restoration returns unchanged references with their original IDs, values and encryption bindings. An edited or missing reference produces `MERGE_REFERENCES_CHANGED` before profiles or contacts partially restore. A separate correction review is required for that case; see [ADR 0013](0013-reviewed-merge-restoration.md). Unsupported identifier kinds, active relationships and open/overlapping event history retain their existing blockers. This decision does not complete the broader conflict/correction workflow under #104.

## Verification

Tests cover exact import matching before/after transfer and restoration, reference-only authority, combined contact/reference choices, older-signature refusal, stale reviews, revoked permissions on retries, canonical state hashing, changed/removed reference guards and private helper/journal access. API regression tests decrypt a transferred value with its original person binding, reject an incorrect binding and ensure ciphertext/binding metadata never appears in the HTTP projection.

# ADR 0013 — Reviewed restoration using current Registry records

- Status is accepted.
- Date is 2026-11-24.
- Related: [ADR 0009](0009-guest-registry-merge.md), [ADR 0012](0012-reference-encryption-identity.md), [#104](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/104).

## Decision

Keep the existing unchanged-record restoration command. Add a separate reviewed correction path for an active merge whose transferred contacts or source references were subsequently edited or removed.

The authorized reviewer sees current source/destination identities and the transferred records, with changed/removed indicators. Each existing contact/reference can explicitly return to the source or remain at the destination. Current consent, primary flags, verification evidence, reference values and encryption identity are preserved. Removed references cannot be selected for return and require explicit acknowledgement that they remain removed. No original private values are copied into correction evidence or recreated from transfer journals.

Review and application require Registry merge authority plus the contact/reference management grants required by the original transfer journals, even when the reviewer keeps records at the destination. A review is bound to the actor, merge, both current profile revisions and current transferred-record state. The apply command locks the merge, both parents in stable order and current transferred rows, then revalidates that evidence and the selected subsets. Changed state requires a new review. A source identity changed outside the supported merge lifecycle or records moved to an unexpected owner remain blocked.

Application reactivates the original source and returns only selected records. Kept records stay at the destination. Removed references stay absent. Source revision advances once; destination reference editors are invalidated when references return. All steps, the existing restoration audit and a private append-only correction record commit atomically. Replayed API commands recheck current authority. The UI retains its idempotency key for retries of unchanged choices.

Correction evidence contains actor/review/merge references and returned/kept/removed record IDs, without copying contact values, consent snapshots or reference ciphertext. Merge history distinguishes reviewed correction from unchanged-record restoration. Event participation IDs, event identity snapshots, invitations and responses are not rewritten.

## API and UI boundary

A POST restoration preview returns a review ID, both profile projections, contact IDs/current revisions/changed flags, and reference IDs/changed/removed flags. The client obtains current values through the existing separately authorized contact/reference APIs.

A separate idempotent restore-reviewed command requires the review ID, explicit arrays of contact/reference IDs to return, removed-reference acknowledgement and the constant resolution `return_selected_current_records`. Unknown, duplicate or removed selected IDs are rejected. Unselected existing records remain at the destination. The UI requires a review acknowledgement and a count-based confirmation before applying the choices.

# ADR 0014 — Internal labels on persistent Registry profiles

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-24.
- Related: #104 and the product owner's preview feedback requesting VIP and similar classifications.

Organizations can define reusable named Registry labels and assign several to an active persistent profile. Labels have stable UUIDs; users do not invent technical codes. Labels are internal Registry data, governed by Registry read/manage permissions. They appear in authorized Registry directory/profile reads and are not added to event or public guest projections. Event-specific guest categories remain separate.

Labels can be retired without deleting existing assignments or repurposing their identity. Retired labels cannot be newly assigned. Assignment changes require the current person revision and preserve an audit trail of label IDs. Runtime callers have no direct table access; tenant RLS, actor context and server authorization protect the command boundary.

The initial implementation blocked merging a source profile with labels. Staff must separately review its classifications; a merge must never silently hide, discard or combine these linked facts. Destination classifications are preserved. The reviewed, non-overlapping transfer extension is defined in [ADR 0018](0018-reviewed-registry-label-merges.md); overlapping and subsequently changed assignments retain explicit guards.

## Classification filters — 2026-11-25

Registry readers can list their organization's active and retired classification options, then filter the directory by one stable label ID. The filter intersects with the existing name and active/archived profile filters before pagination. Unknown or foreign label IDs return no matches without disclosing another organization's definitions. Retired assignments remain searchable.

CSV/XLSX exports use the applied directory filters and retain their separate export permission and row limit. Filtered reads/exports record the selected ID in internal audit evidence; contact details and unrelated private fields remain excluded. This does not assign classifications, change merge rules, add event categories or change public guest projections. Migration 193 adds a label-first assignment index and compatibility overloads for existing SQL callers.

# ADR 0015 — Email-first sign-in, workspace switching and platform administration

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-24.
- Related: owner preview feedback and #104. Organizations and venues retain their separate domain meanings.

## Authentication and workspace selection

Ordinary users enter email and password. Password verification and the existing atomic login throttling precede disclosure of workspace names. One active membership opens directly. Multiple memberships return named choices without issuing session cookies; the selected organization ID is submitted with the credentials held only in the current form's memory. Slug selectors remain optional API compatibility inputs. No password, session token or selection credential is stored in browser storage.

Signed-in users can switch among their active memberships through a workspace menu. The command revalidates and locks the target account/membership and current session, issues new opaque session/CSRF credentials, revokes the old session and records the actual user's switch audit in one transaction. It preserves the original expiry. Target locks are acquired before the session lock; switching does not rewrite password-authentication timestamps. The browser replaces the page to clear prior workspace state. Every data command still checks the selected tenant and its scoped permissions.

## Explicit platform administrator

Existing users default to `is_platform_admin=false`. Only a privileged host-owner operation can change this flag; application authentication and runtime roles cannot update it. `scripts/admin/platform-admin.sh` grants/revokes it for an existing account and records the database principal, reason and time. An organization manager is not automatically a platform administrator.

An active platform administrator receives tracked, managed memberships and immutable-identity system role/grant references for active organizations. The managed organization role includes current non-platform permissions. Access is reconciled at login/session-profile refresh, including newly created organizations and permissions. The normal selected-tenant runtime remains in use; the flag never bypasses tenant RLS on application data.

Global provisioning uses private organization-ID, managed-access and append-only audit tables, following the existing private global routing-index boundary. Ordinary runtime, authentication and worker roles have no direct table access. A locked, transactional migration seeds the organization-ID index and restores FORCE RLS before commit; organizations themselves retain forced tenant RLS. Auth receives only narrow SECURITY DEFINER provisioning, target-membership lock and switch-audit routines with pinned search paths. This avoids granting auth UPDATE on tenant memberships just to lock them.

Tenant membership commands cannot suspend a platform-managed administrator while the global role is active. Host revocation removes its managed grants, revokes affected sessions and restores prior membership status where it was not active. Independently held ordinary memberships and grants remain. Provisioning audit identifies the host database principal, rather than falsely attributing it to the affected staff user. Workspace switching separately records the authenticated user's target membership as actor.

Inactive-organization recovery and global account provisioning remain host operations; this does not claim a complete global account-management console. All normal memberships, organization/venue boundaries, guest privacy and existing command authorization continue to apply.

## Tenant directory controls — 2026-11-25

The authorized member directory exposes a `hostManaged` boolean for each membership in the selected organization. It does not expose global account lists, emails or other memberships. Both searched and unfiltered directory paths use the same projection. The staff UI identifies host-managed access and omits tenant suspension/restoration controls for those members. The existing database membership guard remains authoritative; hiding a control grants no authority and does not replace server checks. Independent event-role assignments remain ordinary tenant-managed facts.

# ADR 0016 — Staff publication of event RSVP settings

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104, ADR 0004/0005, RSVP and invitation design v0.3.

## Decision

Expose read/publication commands for the existing event RSVP policy tables to staff with `event.manage` for the selected event. Staff explicitly choose a nonempty subset of accepted/declined/tentative, an optional absolute response deadline entered in the effective event schedule's IANA time zone, and whether guests can change their answer. The first form uses the existing schema defaults; publishing requires explicit confirmation. No modules, guest records, links, messages or reminder jobs are created by this command.

Each publication inserts an immutable published revision. A new event receives a stable policy identity and an internal generated reference; subsequent publications reuse the current published policy's identity. A retired current policy is rejected rather than silently reactivated. Revision numbers advance above all existing event policy revisions, including legacy multiple-policy data, so existing invitation and uninvited staff-response selectors choose the newly published revision unambiguously. Existing revisions and issued invitation/response references remain untouched. Existing late-change and reminder settings are preserved, rather than introducing new reminder/override behavior through this form.

The command locks the event, checks an open lifecycle (not completed/cancelled/archived), the expected published revision ID (null for first publication), and the expected effective time-zone name. A stale policy or changed time zone requires reloading. Absolute deadlines are not silently shifted or constrained by an invented venue policy. Permission is checked both on command execution and idempotent replay. An audit records the actual membership, event and new/previous revision IDs. Runtime direct policy-table writes are revoked; publication remains a narrow SECURITY DEFINER boundary with tenant context and pinned search path.

The staff UI includes permission errors, stale-edit recovery through refresh, fieldset/checkbox labels and confirmation. Closed events remain readable without publication controls. Reuse the event scheduler's local-date conversion and reject nonexistent local times. Preserve an unchanged deadline's exact instant when editing other settings, including DST ambiguity and sub-minute precision. Settings publication is separate from invitation reissuance and does not reinterpret existing guest answers.

## Limits

This slice does not add reminder scheduling, policy retirement, invitation template authoring, bulk reissuance, attendee admission, or a full capability-management console. Those require their own workflows. Existing guest self-service and explicit staff deadline-override enforcement remain authoritative.

# ADR 0017 — Host-only initial staff account provisioning

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104 and ADR 0015; later installer bootstrap under #108.

## Decision

Provide an explicit host-owner command for a new staff account before broader invitation/account administration is implemented. It accepts an email, display name, an operator reason and an optional active organization ID. The initial password comes only from hidden terminal entry or stdin, never a command argument or exported password variable. The built API's existing Argon2id dependency hashes it before storage. This tool requires a nonblank password of 12–1024 UTF-8 bytes; this is a host-bootstrap input boundary, not a change to existing account authentication.

A privileged migration connection selects `eventor_owner`. One transaction inserts the active account, optionally an active membership and an append-only host provisioning receipt. Existing case-insensitive email identities are refused; no upsert, password reset, account reactivation or privilege repair is attempted. An unavailable/inactive organization or audit failure rolls back the operation. The new account explicitly has no platform-admin flag, no email-verification assertion and no role grants. A membership alone does not authorize application data. Organization administrators assign permitted roles separately; platform authority requires the distinct host-admin grant command from ADR 0015.

Reuse the private `platform_admin_audit` host control-plane journal with action `staff_account_provisioned`, the affected account, optional selected organization, operator reason and the real `session_user` database principal. Do not fabricate a membership actor for a host operation. This journal already covers host provisioning of accounts' platform access and remains inaccessible to runtime/auth/worker table queries. No tenant API, new table, authorization grant or OpenAPI route is introduced.

The CLI prints only created identifiers and explicit false role/platform flags. Errors are sanitized so password hashes, database connection details and SQL parameter values are not emitted. Tests use synthetic disposable data. Operators must communicate initial credentials securely; the command does not send email or prove mailbox ownership.

## Limits

This is an initial host bootstrap and recovery-environment prerequisite, not a tenant invitation, password-change/reset, email-verification or full global account-management workflow. A global account without memberships cannot enter an ordinary workspace until explicitly provisioned. Existing users must be handled through separate reviewed administration; rerunning this command never overwrites them.

# ADR 0018 — Reviewed Registry classification transfer

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104, ADR 0009/0013/0014.

## Decision

Extend the existing supervised identity merge to carry non-overlapping Registry label assignments from source to destination, only after a separate explicit `move_to_destination` choice. Registry merge authority already requires Registry management, which is also the label-management boundary. Contact/reference transfers retain their separate field permissions and acknowledgements. Older merge overloads delegate to the new boundary with no label choice and therefore cannot silently move classifications.

The review shows both profiles' labels, including retirement state. The source assignments move unchanged: stable label IDs, original author membership and original assignment time are preserved. A retired assignment is historical classification evidence being reassigned with the duplicate identity, rather than a new classification selected through the ordinary editor. Existing destination assignments remain untouched. Overlapping labels and a combined total above the existing 100-assignment profile limit remain blocked; no automatic union, deletion or classification priority is invented.

Stable parent locks serialize assignment edits. Definition locks prevent concurrent retirement from changing the reviewed configuration during commit. The actor-bound review includes a hash of both assignment sets and definition-retirement timestamps; profile revisions and all existing contact/reference/history review checks still apply. The canonical v1 hash uses explicit fields and epoch timestamps, independent of session time-zone formatting; future formats must not reinterpret existing journal evidence. Destination revisions invalidate stale label editors. Existing event identity snapshots and public guest projections are unchanged.

An append-only, tenant-RLS transfer journal records merge/label references and the transferred assignment-state hash, without copying label names or reconstructable deleted assignments. The merge record identifies the actual operator and its resolution. The journal deliberately does not reference a current assignment row, so later authorized removal remains possible. Runtime/auth/worker cannot query or mutate this journal directly; private implementation helpers are not executable by application roles.

## Restoration

Both ordinary unchanged-record restoration and the reviewed current-contact/reference correction path first validate the transferred labels. Unchanged assignments return to the reactivated source with their original metadata; unrelated destination labels stay in place. The correction preview lists the returning classifications read-only, separately from selectable contacts/references. Confirmation explains this automatic return. Contact/reference edits can be reviewed through ADR 0013 while the labels remain unchanged.

An edited, removed or removed-and-re-added transferred assignment produces `MERGE_LABELS_CHANGED` before any profile/contact/reference state is restored. A later label-definition retirement alone does not discard historical assignments or prevent their return. A separate label correction workflow is required for changed assignments; no journal rewrite, metadata reset or ghost assignment recreation is allowed. All permission checks precede private-state disclosure, including idempotent replay.

## Migration and limits

Migration 191 adds the private journal and composes the existing merge/restoration implementations through guarded wrappers. It adds no backfill and changes no existing classifications or completed merge records. Existing merges without label transfers continue through their previous restoration semantics. Every compatibility overload has explicit grants; renamed implementation helpers are private. This does not complete active relationships, unsupported identifiers, overlapping event history or overlapping/edited classification correction under #104.

# ADR 0019 — Reviewed Registry relationship transfer

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104, ADR 0009/0013/0018, Blueprint v1.2 §33.4.

## Decision

Extend supervised duplicate-profile merging to transfer non-conflicting active Registry relationships after an explicit `relationshipResolution=move_to_destination` acknowledgement. The operator needs the existing Registry merge and relationship-management permissions. Contact/reference/label choices retain their independent boundaries. No permission is implied by a relationship or by an event participation.

The comparison lists active source and destination links only when the operator has relationship-management authority and there are source links to transfer. A permission blocker exposes no relationship rows or source count. It shows related names, relationship kind and direction. Commit preserves each relationship ID, kind, directionality, creation time and original author. Directed incoming and outgoing endpoints retain their meaning; mutual endpoints are reordered to satisfy the existing canonical UUID invariant. Ended links remain attached to their original profiles as historical facts. Unrelated destination links are untouched.

A source-to-destination link would become a self-link and remains blocked. A transfer that would duplicate an existing active destination tuple is also blocked. Neither case silently ends, combines or prioritizes links; separate reviewed correction is required. Unsupported identifiers, incoming merge chains and open/overlapping event history keep their existing guards.

## Review, concurrency and audit

The actor-bound review fingerprints the active links of both profiles, including their IDs, endpoints, kind, direction and creation/end attribution, using a versioned epoch-based hash. Ending a link does not increment the profile revision, so parent revision checks alone are insufficient. Even ending the last source link invalidates a new review. A pre-migration review can still merge profiles without active source links; it cannot authorize their transfer.

Commit locks both profiles in stable UUID order and the affected active relationship rows in stable UUID order before recomputing evidence. Existing relationship creation locks its parents, while ending a link locks its row. The boundary therefore serializes against both operations. A stale review or new conflict refuses the whole statement. Concurrent multi-profile graph operations may require retry after PostgreSQL deadlock detection; no partial transfer may commit.

Migration 192 adds a private, forced-tenant-RLS, append-only transfer journal with original endpoint IDs and the expected transferred-state hash. It deliberately has no FK to a current relationship row, so missing rows are detected rather than reconstructed. The existing merge record retains the acting operator and the explicit relationship resolution. No public guest projection, event relationship, historical event snapshot or sensitive contact value changes. Renamed helpers are private and every compatibility overload has explicit ACLs.

## Restoration and limitations

Both strict and current-contact/reference restoration first require current relationship-management authority for journalled transfers. They lock and verify the transferred rows before any profile or linked-record restoration. Unchanged relationships return with their exact original endpoints and attribution. The correction preview shows them read-only; contact/reference selection does not discard them. Unrelated destination links stay in place.

A changed, ended or missing transferred link returns `MERGE_RELATIONSHIPS_CHANGED` before partial effects. Restoration never reopens a later ended link, overwrites changed relationship facts or recreates a removed row. A separate relationship-correction workflow is required for those cases. Cached API retries also recheck current relationship authority. Existing merges without relationship transfers retain their prior behavior. This extension does not complete the full linked-record conflict workflow or #104.

# ADR 0020 — Host provisioning of an existing account's new membership

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104, ADR 0015/0017; installer bootstrap under #108.

## Decision

Provide a separate privileged host command to add an existing active staff account to an active organization. This completes the missing counterpart to initial account bootstrap without creating another identity or replacing credentials. The host operator specifies email, organization UUID and a reason. Email lookup is case-insensitive. The command creates exactly one active membership, with no role grants or platform authority. It is deliberately separate from an invitation or proof of mailbox ownership.

One owner-role transaction locks the active organization and account, refuses any existing organization/account membership, inserts the new membership and records `staff_membership_provisioned` in the existing private append-only host audit. The journal identifies the account, selected organization, operator reason and real `session_user`; the organization/account unique constraint identifies the membership. No tenant member is fabricated as the host actor. Concurrent attempts serialize on the account and can produce only one membership/audit receipt. Audit failure rolls back the insert.

Existing active, invited, suspended and revoked memberships are all refused. The command does not restore access, replace identity, change email/password/verification/platform flags, assign roles, revoke sessions or change other workspaces. Existing membership correction remains a separate authorized workflow. Normal authentication discovers the new named workspace; selected-tenant permissions still control every operation. A membership alone grants no Registry or event-data permission.

## Boundary and limitations

The built API exports the host implementation for the command and tests, not an HTTP route. The shell/Node entry points require a privileged migration connection that can select `eventor_owner`; runtime cannot execute the host operation. CLI output contains identifiers and explicit unchanged-account/no-role-grant flags. Errors omit raw SQL, connection strings and private database details. No password input is accepted.

No migration, new table, API contract or mandatory dependency is needed. Non-active accounts or organizations are refused rather than repaired. Existing accounts without usable credentials still need a separate credential workflow. This is a host onboarding tool, not self-registration, tenant invitations, password reset or a complete global account console.

# ADR 0021 — Authorized booking/event association commands

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104/#112, ADR 0004/0006, Cross-Organization Collaboration v0.3.

## Decision

Expose the existing `booking_event_links` aggregate through explicit create/list commands. The event organization owns the association. An active actor needs `event.manage` for that exact event. A same-organization association additionally requires `booking.manage` for the booking and carries no collaboration grant. A cross-organization association requires an active, accepted, unexpired booking-scoped grant from the booking owner to the event owner with `booking.event.link` and the exact booking ID. Existing grant/creator/audit triggers remain authoritative.

An association records a relationship between existing booking and event identities. It reserves no capacity and changes no booking/event status, commercial terms, guest data or snapshots. Existing record statuses are not reinterpreted as availability. The API accepts a null/omitted grant for same-organization links, reconciling the historical external-only request schema with the existing relational model.

An identical active association returns its original ID. Different relationship kinds/grants and ended/revoked associations require separate correction; create never silently repurposes or reactivates them. The event row serializes duplicate creation before the existing audited BEFORE INSERT trigger. This avoids phantom duplicate audit entries from an INSERT/ON CONFLICT path. Current event, booking or collaboration authority is checked again before an idempotent cached response is returned.

## Projection and boundary

Event managers can page their own event's association metadata, including terminal records, after a source grant is revoked. This preserves event-owned provenance, not future provider access. The allowlisted projection contains IDs, relationship kind, association status and creation time; provider commercial data, contact details and organizer guest records are excluded. It does not enumerate the provider's other bookings or the organizer's other events. Read access is audited in the event owner's tenant.

Migration 194 revokes direct application-role access to the association table and grants runtime execution only on the scoped commands. It introduces no parallel aggregate, backfill or new permissions. Existing owner-level maintenance and append-only attribution remain. No tenant context is switched to bypass RLS. Invalid/stale authority or conflicting association meaning refuses the whole command.

## Delivery scope

This is an API/command foundation with explicit OpenAPI/shared client types. The staff booking/event selector, association correction/lifecycle UI, disruption delivery, acknowledgement and event resolution remain separate work under #112. Creating an association sends no message and grants no guest-directory access. This does not complete collaboration or production acceptance.


## Staff selector and display extension — migration 195

The staff Events panel explicitly confirms selection from the selected organization's permitted booking references. Users never supply organization identifiers in this flow. The existing booking metadata lookup is exposed through a generic reference-search alias, retaining its server scope filtering. Same-organization reference labels require current booking management; external/restricted links remain generic. Membership in a second tenant does not grant cross-tenant reference access. The event-history projection index changes no lifecycle facts.

The selector supports existing relationship kinds and paginated read-only history. It does not add partner discovery, association correction/reactivation, notice publication or event resolution. Failed authority clears private panel results; a multi-request reload publishes results only when both requests succeed. English/Bosnian controls, explicit confirmation, labeled inputs, keyboard-scrollable history and browser checks cover the user-visible boundary.

## Attributed ending extension — migration 197

An exact event manager may explicitly end the event-owned association, including a restricted local reference or a partner link whose source grant has since been revoked. Ending changes only the link's one-way status/actor fields under the existing audit trigger. It does not require source booking authority because it mutates no provider record or collaboration grant. The fixed `event_manager_ended` audit reason identifies the chosen command; it does not invent an operational/business explanation or require a user to type a code.

Ended links retain their original actor/reason and audit on retries. Revoked links cannot be relabelled, and create never reactivates either terminal status. Event-row locking follows creation/publication lock order: a concurrent notice publication commits wholly before ending or is rejected after ending. Previously published event receipts remain readable/acknowledgeable under their own event authority. API cached replies recheck exact event scope.

The bilingual staff action requires confirmation explaining the retained history and separate booking/event decisions. Booking status, reservations, event modules, grants, snapshots and prior notices remain unchanged. This supplies retirement only; changing relationship meaning, reactivation and partner setup remain separate work.

## Accepted partner booking selector — migration 200

Exact event managers can page booking scopes already shared with their selected organization through accepted, currently effective `booking.event.link` grants. The chooser returns only grant/booking/provider identities, the captured provider name and shared purpose; it never reads provider booking records, directories, commercial data, guest data or raw grant configuration. Collaboration administration or local booking management is not required to use an already accepted linking capability.

Existing associations of every status are excluded before pagination, preventing duplicate or terminal links from being offered as new choices. The existing create command independently rechecks event/grant authority and preserves one original association. Source revocation between selection and confirmation refuses creation. The bilingual picker needs no typed organization/booking identifiers and uses explicit confirmation. Names/purposes identify choices without granting provider-record access; acceptance or association does not establish availability or change booking/event decisions. New grant proposals/discovery and partner notice delivery remain separate work.

# ADR 0022 — Explicit event disruption publication and acknowledgement

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #112, ADR 0004/0006/0021, Cancellation and Event Disruption Design v0.3.

## Context

Provider notices are append-only source facts. Recording one neither informs a linked event manager nor authorizes disclosure of internal booking data. An event-owned receipt aggregate already exists, but its original mandatory collaboration grant excluded same-organization operations. Treating a booking link as broad read permission would cross field and role boundaries.

## Decision

Reuse `event_disruption_resolutions` for explicitly published receipts. The initial command supports same-organization source bookings only. A sender needs current exact `event.manage` and `booking.manage`, an active local booking/event association, and a source notice belonging to that booking. The sender deliberately publishes an allowlisted version-1 snapshot: notice code, reason category, public summary, affected times and issuance time. No operational summary, commercial/booking reference, contact, guest data or resolution notes enter the projection. This is explicit internal inbox publication, not email delivery or automatic fan-out.

The event manager can subsequently read and acknowledge the event-owned public snapshot without booking management. Losing source authority blocks new publication and cached publication retries; it does not erase an intentionally published historical receipt. Losing event authority blocks reads, acknowledgements and cached acknowledgement replies. Tenant context is never switched. Cross-organization publication is deferred until accepted grant capabilities and partner controls are implemented; cross-organization historical receipt provenance remains supported.

One event/source/provider tuple identifies a receipt. Event-row locking serializes publication before insertion/audit. A duplicate returns the original receipt; no duplicate publication audit is emitted. Acknowledgement locks that receipt, changes only `received` to `acknowledged`, and preserves the first actor/time. Retrying against an advanced resolution state returns it unchanged. `noticeId` in the acknowledgement API identifies the event receipt, not the provider's source notice.

Migration 196 allows local null-grant receipts while retaining mandatory matching provider grants for external receipts. It adds uniqueness and immutable provenance/first-acknowledgement guards, revokes direct application-role access, and grants only scoped command execution. Existing duplicate or incompatible legacy rows stop migration for explicit reconciliation; no history is silently consolidated or deleted. Legacy snapshots of unsupported versions project no source payload; resolution ciphertext is never projected.

## Consequences and limits

Publication and acknowledgement are audited and leave booking/event status, schedules, reservations, guest modules, invitations and RSVP unchanged. Acknowledgement means receipt was seen; it is neither resolution nor acceptance of a booking amendment. No cancellation, postponement, relocation, notification campaign, outbox delivery or commercial decision is inferred. Those commands and partner delivery remain subsequent #112 slices. The API foundation does not by itself expose staff action controls.

SQL/API tests cover scope, revocation, safe snapshots, immutable provenance, unchanged aggregates, pagination and retry identity. Real PostgreSQL concurrent publication and acknowledgement tests require one receipt, one audit per transition and the original acknowledgement timestamp. Live SMTP/HTTPS and production installation acceptance are separate.


## Staff controls extension

The Events inbox uses server-filtered local association references and existing source-notice reads. Staff preview the public notice before native confirmation; repeated publication retains the original receipt. Event-only managers see published safe snapshots and may acknowledge, while source controls remain unavailable without booking authority. Role enforcement remains in the commands. Bilingual text separates receipt from resolution and inbox publication from email/partner delivery. Keyboard heading focus, escaped summaries, contained mobile layout and authorization cleanup are covered in Chromium/Firefox.

# ADR 0023 — Permissioned collaboration grant review and lifecycle

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104/#112, ADR 0006/0021/0022, Cross-Organization Collaboration Design v0.3.

## Context

The existing proposal/acceptance/revocation commands already enforce organization-scoped collaboration management. Runtime routes and permission-filtered review were missing, while the runtime database role retained raw SELECT access to grants. The original constraint also contradicted the revoke command by requiring acceptance facts when an unaccepted proposal was withdrawn.

## Decision

Expose selected-party list/detail and acceptance/revocation commands over the existing grant aggregate. Every operation requires active organization-scoped `collaboration.manage` in the selected tenant. General organization administration or membership alone is insufficient. List/detail access is audited. The list allowlists party/scope identifiers, purpose, allowed action codes, status, validity and lifecycle timestamps; it excludes actor identities, source records, private revisions and raw projection configuration. Detailed review also returns the deliberately shared projection configuration. It does not query the provider's underlying booking, venue, guest or commercial records, and it enumerates no organization directory.

Only the recipient can accept; only the grantor can revoke. Existing functions and audit attribution remain authoritative. New wrapper commands lock the grant and revalidate party, action, state and acceptance window before executing. An already-active acceptance belongs to its original accepting actor. Cached acceptance replies recheck current role, grant state/window and accepting actor; source revocation/expiry cannot return a stale cached active response. Cached revocation replies recheck grantor authority and retain the first revocation timestamp/audit. Revocation reasons are bounded, validated and stored only through the existing grantor audit; they are omitted from shared projections.

Migration 198 revokes direct application-role table access and grants only scoped wrapper execution. It also permits a revoked proposal to retain null acceptance actor/time, matching the existing command. Active/expired grants still require genuine acceptance; acceptance actor/time and revoked-status/time pairing remain required. No acceptance is manufactured and no historical facts are backfilled. Concurrent acceptance and revocation serialize: acceptance first retains authentic acceptance under subsequent revocation; revocation first prevents acceptance.

## Limits and follow-up

This is a runtime review/lifecycle foundation. Staff controls, new proposal creation/discovery, scoped partner booking selection and cross-organization notice publication remain follow-ups. Accepting a grant changes neither booking/event status nor guest access; each downstream operation must enforce the exact capability and projection separately. Revocation blocks future protected use while retaining prior association/snapshot/audit provenance. It does not cancel provider bookings, organizer events or published receipts.

SQL/API tests cover party/context/permission boundaries, shared projections, validity, never-accepted revocation, retained accepted history, retry sanitization and authority rechecks. Real runtime-role concurrent transactions and PostgreSQL-backed API retries verify both transition orders and role/grant revocation. No live SMTP/HTTPS or deployed installation acceptance is implied.

## Managed booking proposal extension — migration 201

A dedicated HTTP command proposes only `booking.event.link` for one booking, with an empty shared data projection. It requires organization-scoped collaboration management and organization/exact-booking management; neither permission alone can share a booking. Recipient identity, purpose and validity are explicit. Null expiry is an explicit caller choice, not a policy default. No arbitrary actions, scope or configuration payload is accepted.

The command reuses existing proposal/revision/audit/name-capture behavior. It creates an unaccepted proposal, never grants immediate booking/event access, changes no booking facts and leaves recipient review/acceptance separate. Cached creation returns the original receipt after rechecking both source authorities; consumers read grant detail for current lifecycle state. UUIDs, purpose and equivalent timestamp representations normalize for retries. Concurrent HTTP retries produce one original proposal/revision/audit. New staff proposal controls and recipient discovery remain follow-ups; no directory or organization-role delegation policy is inferred.

# ADR 0024 — Shared party names and reviewed grant acceptance

- Status: accepted.
- Date: 2026-11-25.
- Related: #104/#112, ADR 0006/0023.

## Context

Partner-access controls need recognizable party names and a complete grant review. Looking up another tenant's organization row to display a name would widen the tenant boundary. A user must also avoid accepting a different scope/configuration after its review changes.

## Decision

Each party publishes its own existing organization name through the grant lifecycle. Proposal captures the grantor's name in the grantor context; valid acceptance captures the recipient's name in its context. Names remain immutable on the grant despite later organization renames or revocation. Migration 199 leaves historical unknown names null without backfill or invented original names. No organization directory policy, cross-tenant context switch or source-record permission is added. Legacy/unaccepted counterparts use a reference fallback.

Detailed review returns a SHA-256 fingerprint of party identities, scope, purpose, allowed actions, shared configuration and validity. Lifecycle/actor/timestamp metadata is excluded so genuine acceptance retries remain stable. Timestamp inputs use epoch values to avoid session-time-zone differences. Interactive acceptance supplies that fingerprint. The server locks/rechecks the grant, compares current meaning and accepts atomically; stale reviews are refused, including cached replies. The fingerprint is concurrency evidence, not a credential or authorization grant. Existing programmatic acceptance without a fingerprint and its original idempotency representation remain compatible.

`/me/workspaces` includes an organization-scoped collaboration-management navigation hint. Settings displays Partner access only with that hint. Grant metadata supplies current party/state/window action hints; each command independently rechecks authority. Staff review scope, configured actions and deliberately shared configuration before native confirmation. Revocation requires a bounded reason and confirmation. Conflicts clear the stale review and require a fresh read; authorization failure clears private list/detail state. Dates use the selected language, and grant names describe the names shared at proposal/acceptance rather than an unverified current directory entry.

## Consequences and limits

This adds no provider booking, event, guest or commercial data to shared access. Accepting a grant does not create broad tenant membership or perform downstream booking/event decisions. New proposal creation/discovery and partner booking/notice workflows remain separate. Host maintenance can still correct source configuration; interactive retries will not silently approve changed meaning. Any future runtime grant-revision workflow must preserve explicit versioned meaning and downstream authority.

Populated 198-to-199 rehearsal verifies unchanged legacy grant facts and null uncaptured names. SQL/API and real PostgreSQL tests cover immutable names, unchanged directory isolation, stale/renewed reviews, cached retries and timezone-independent fingerprints. Chromium/Firefox cover names, escaped configuration, cancelled/confirmed actions, stale-review recovery, unaccepted revocation, source-data denial, Bosnian dates, mobile containment and permission cleanup. Live SMTP/HTTPS and production installation acceptance remain separate.

# Eventor — Template Design Studio technical specification v1.0

**Status:** Product-owner-approved scope (2026-11-27); detailed engineering design and library choices remain subject to implementation review and ADRs.
**Baseline:** main at e69d1c9cf86e8c4e55c4ee03f7c291830383bb2c.
**Tracking:** [#111](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/111), Roadmap Phase 7.
**Document control:** Repository integration edition of the approved 2026-11-27 specification. Consolidates its requirements, TDS-01–16, M0–M6 and AC-01–25. No historical blueprint, accepted ADR, runtime contract or implementation status is silently superseded.

## 1. Purpose, scope and non-goals

Deliver a unified, reusable, self-hosted Template Design Studio, not merely a subject field and HTML textarea. Authorized nontechnical operators can design formal bilingual personalized invitations with branding, text, images, RSVP CTA and optional print layout; preview synthetic or authorized recipient examples; publish reviewed revisions; then explicitly issue/send through existing domain commands.

Three distinct authoring modes share the library, components, assets, branding, typed bindings, review/revisions, rendering, localization, permissions and audit. A template is not an invitation, booking offer, audience, credential, send command or attendance record.

| Purpose | Modes/outputs | Authoritative data |
|---|---|---|
| Invitations and RSVP reminders | Rich text, block email, graphical; text/HTML/PDF/print packs | Organizer; invitation and RSVP policy |
| Booking correspondence, offers and cancellations | Rich text and block email; optional letter PDF | Booking owner; pinned commercial/policy facts |
| Admission passes, badges, seating/place cards | Graphical; PDF/sheets | Organizer; distinct admission credential, published allocation when enabled |
| Welcome signage, wayfinding, announcements | Graphical; PDF/image, safe display content | Authorized event/venue owner; public projection |
| Staff/vendor correspondence | Rich text/block email | Explicitly responsible party; scoped task projection |
| Certificates, letters, summaries | Rich text/graphical; PDF/email as appropriate | Purpose-specific authorized projection |
| Reports/maps | Graphical layout and approved components | Report/published plan projection; existing CSV/XLSX exports unaffected |

Allowlist purpose/mode/output combinations. Booking-only deployments work without organizer event or guest modules; optional capabilities gate dependent variables and navigation. SMS uses bounded plain text if enabled. Multi-channel outputs are explicit linked assignments, not forced lossless conversion. Existing #111 requirements for forms, reminders, reports, displays and communication reconciliation remain separately required. No unrestricted report designer, public directory, arbitrary executable content, mandatory SaaS, automatic mass send or pixel-perfect email client parity.

## 2. Reconciliation and current implementation baseline

| Source | Alignment |
|---|---|
| [Blueprint v1.2](../../blueprint/v1.2/Event_Operations_Platform_Technical_Blueprint_v1.2.md) §§11.1–11.3 | Brand-aware templates, dimensions, typography, fields, QR placement, print packs and immutable outputs |
| Blueprint §§10,12,21,26,34,41,46 | Published allocation only; portal privacy, reports/audit, property-level inheritance, language variants, conditional blocks and preview |
| [Implementation Design v0.2](../v0.2/Event_Operations_Implementation_Design_v0.2.md) | Template designer, brand tokens/data fields, single/batch preview, print sheets, output history |
| [RSVP Design v0.3](RSVP_AND_INVITATION_DESIGN_v0.3.md) | Template and policy revisions; domain owns issue/reissue/revoke, RSVP, audience review |
| [ADR 0004](../../decisions/0004-optional-event-operations-scope.md), [0005](../../decisions/0005-separate-invitations-rsvp-attendance.md), [0006](../../decisions/0006-cross-organization-collaboration.md) | Optional modules, distinct credentials and attendance, explicit collaboration grants |
| [ADR 0007](../../decisions/0007-internationalization.md), [0008](../../decisions/0008-modular-staff-frontend.md) | BCP 47 locales, authored translations; modular staff UI |
| [Architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) | API-first modular monolith; isolated asynchronous rendering |
| [Gap analysis](../../BLUEPRINT_TO_REPOSITORY_GAP_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md) / [Roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md) / [#111](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/111) | Explicit rich text, block email and precision canvas; preserve original communications, branding, forms/reports/displays and acceptance scope |

Migration [000013](../../../database/migrations/000013_event_changes_notifications.sql) defines notification_templates (owner/code/purpose/status) and notification_template_revisions (locale/subject/body/revision/state), referenced by invitation revisions and event notification campaigns through tenant-composite FKs. [000032](../../../database/migrations/000032_notification_campaign_review_confirmation.sql) adds campaign review/confirmation and snapshot guards. [Notification worker](../../../apps/api/src/notification-worker.ts) renders subject and text using renderNotificationTemplate. [Campaign workspace](../../../apps/staff-web/src/features/campaigns/CampaignWorkspaceView.vue) reviews those fields, not authors them. None of the three editors is delivered at the audit baseline. Existing form definitions are separate business aggregates.

Audit actual RLS, privileges, guards, queued message semantics, invitation/booking paths and shared contracts before implementation. Reuse and extend existing notification identities/revisions; historical conceptual document_templates is not authority for a competing email aggregate. Forward migrations only. Preserve existing IDs, queued behavior and history. Do not rewrite historical v0.2 SQL/API snapshots.

## 3. Authority, lifecycle and common workspace

### TDS-01 — Permissions and lifecycle

Proposed permission families (reconcile with existing catalogue): template.read, template.edit, template.review, template.publish, template.preview.recipient, template.test_send, template.asset.manage, brand.manage, brand.publish, template.export. No template privilege implies guest data, real issuance, campaign approval or delivery. Existing exact organization/event/booking management, field permissions, membership and grant checks remain authoritative. Parent organization templates/brands are editable only with parent authority. Provider access to organizer guests never follows from booking linkage or brand use. Cross-owner shared assets require explicit effective scoped grant and approved read-only reference/copy. Enforce non-enumeration, actor binding, RLS and separate least-privilege worker roles.

Lifecycle: draft → in_review → approved → published → superseded/retired; review may return/reject. Approval pins digest of source, variant, dependencies, schema/catalogue and validation. Edits invalidate approval; published payload immutable; retirement prevents new use per policy without rewriting history. Unsafe/revoked asset blocks new use, not automatic recall of distributed bytes. Authorized single-operator publishing may be configured; separation of duties required where policy specifies. Audit all transitions.

Draft autosave with status, manual save, undo/redo, duplicate/restore from prior version, compare and discard. Optimistic revision preconditions; conflicts offer compare/reload/copy changes, not last-write-wins. No sensitive preview/token browser-local persistence. Real-time collaborative editing not initially required.

### TDS-02 — Template library and common UX

Settings → Templates & Branding; event → Communications → Templates; booking → Correspondence, subject to permissions/capability. Search/filter by name, code, purpose, scope, mode, locale completeness, state and update time. Create blank/from approved starter, clone, retire, view dependencies, assignments and revision history. Show owner, author/reviewer, approval state, validation issues and inherited selection. Choose purpose, locale, output and mode. Workspace has canvas/content, properties, variable/asset/component pickers, preview, diagnostics and save/review/publish controls. Keyboard navigation, focus/zoom, labels and non-drag alternatives for every critical action. Staff UI locale independent of authored document locale.

## 4. Three authoring modes and shared components

### TDS-03 — Rich-text WYSIWYG

- Word-like formatted paragraphs/headings, bold/italic/underline/strike, allowed fonts/sizes/colors/highlight, alignment/spacing, lists/indent, quotes/rules, links, images with alt text, bounded tables, typed merge fields and conditional sections.
- Toolbar/keyboard shortcuts, undo/redo, normalized office paste with explicit notice of significant formatting loss. Separate single-line subject/preheader (reject CR/LF); editable plain-text alternative with explicit regenerate/compare. Unicode including Bosnian diacritics; test long and missing values.
- Safe HTML authoring/import in allowed contexts through parser and allowlist; rejected constructs reported before save. Structured canonical document, not executable raw HTML. No silent unsupported conversion. Render HTML/text for email or page-flow PDF for letters. Clone explicitly when changing mode.

### TDS-04 — Responsive drag-and-drop email

- Sections/rows, 1–3 columns, headings/rich text, logo/image, spacer/divider, CTA button, RSVP link, event summary, conditional blocks, footer/contact/help. Drag/drop or keyboard insert/move/reorder, properties, duplicate/delete and save reusable components.
- Responsive stacking, content width/padding, approved typography/link/button styling, desktop/mobile preview, overflow warnings, preheader and plain text. Conservative email markup/tables and inline CSS, no arbitrary JS, forms, iframe, remote CSS, tracking pixel or user-specified remote image fetch.
- Brand tokens/approved overrides; assets with alt/decorative flag, bounded size; explicitly public nonpersonal hosted assets if enabled or approved inline attachments/fallback. Never private URL or recipient token in asset fetch.
- Actual MIME test via provider adapter with text/plain and text/html multipart alternative; image-blocked content remains useful. Representative client compatibility and dark-mode checks where feasible; report limitations, no false pixel parity.

### TDS-05 — Graphical invitation and card designer

- A4/A5/common card and badge presets, bounded custom width/height, portrait/landscape, front/back and bounded multipage. Exact physical coordinates (mm/scaled integer/decimal), trim/bleed/safe margins/crop marks, deterministic conversion to PDF points; screen zoom does not change design.
- Rulers/grid/snap, select/multiselect, move/resize/rotate, align/distribute, layers/z-order, group/ungroup, lock/hide, duplicate/delete; numeric properties and keyboard nudging/alternatives. Text, vector shapes/lines/frame, logo, image/background, typed QR, variable, approved map/report components. Nondestructive crop/fit, aspect ratio default; no arbitrary active SVG.
- Text wrapping/alignment/line height, rich formatting, overflow error or controlled shrink/wrap with minimum readable size. Server measures actual fonts; never silently clip required name/legal text/QR. Semantic reading order and decorative elements explicit.
- QR typed RSVP or admission; use corresponding domain service. Preserve quiet zone, contrast, module readability, no stretch/crop/overlap; decode at final size. Synthetic marked non-live sample only in preview. RSVP never doubles as admission.
- Single personalized PDF, ordered bulk pack, A4 multi-up imposition, rows/columns/gutters/margins/cut marks, fit check, optional bounded DPI PNG. No invented seat label; safe published allocation/map projection only. Professional CMYK/PDF-X not promised without later validation.

### TDS-06 — Assets, reusable components and starters

Neutral synthetic starter designs (formal invitation, email, reminder, booking letter, A5 invitation, badge/pass where enabled), no real GHB brand or personal data. Reusable headers/footers/CTA/sections with immutable component revisions pinned by templates. No component cycles, bounded nesting/count. Clone and sanitized import/export versioned packages with dependency manifest, remap/revalidate bindings and permissions on import; imported source is new draft. Tenant-scoped content hashes; no cross-tenant existence oracle. Asset metadata (owner, type, dimensions, alt, license, allowed use); approved immutable binaries, quarantine and revoke. Prevent destructive deletion of retained dependencies; revoked asset blocks future use. Licensed fonts and embedding rights; no unlicensed assets or font files shipped.

## 5. TDS-07 — Typed personalization

Use a versioned purpose-specific variable catalogue, not arbitrary interpolation or generic person objects. Each definition supplies stable key, resolver, type/nullability, sensitivity, allowed purpose/channel, permission, formatting and synthetic sample. Variable nodes are structured; double-brace notation only presentation. No arbitrary traversal, SQL/JS, reflection, custom function or loops; bounded presence/enum predicates and approved bounded list components. Required missing or forbidden binding fails closed; optional permitted absence has explicit fallback/hide rule, not a forbidden-field presence oracle. Validate at preview/publish/render/issue. Escape by output context; typed validated URL/asset/QR slots, never string interpolation into arbitrary attributes/styles.

| Example proposed key | Permitted projection |
|---|---|
| guest.display_name, guest.salutation, guest.reference | Recipient's approved event identity |
| event.title, event.start_at, event.timezone | Published/approved schedule |
| venue.name, venue.public_address, venue.arrival_instructions | Public-safe venue projection |
| rsvp.deadline, rsvp.url | Invitation policy and capability |
| admission.qr | Separate admission credential |
| allocation.public_label | Own published assignment only |
| booking.reference, booking.offer_total, booking.action_url | Authorized customer/commercial snapshot and purpose-bound action |
| brand.logo, brand.primary_color | Resolved brand asset/color |
| task.public_due_at, task.public_summary | Explicit task/collaborator grant |

These names are illustrative, not existing API promises. No internal notes, restricted tags, private security/CDI data, other recipients, contact list, raw stored credentials, internal identifiers or arbitrary custom fields in external templates. Staff-only report requires distinct authorized projection. Resolve from server-owned record/snapshot, not user-submitted arbitrary data. Synthetic preview default and watermark; real preview exact recipient permission, audited, non-live placeholders; already issued artifacts through existing domain access only. Batch preview tests representative recipients/locales/missing fields/long names/no seat with scoped diagnostics. Real issue/send confirmation pins template/brand, recipient set, policy/plan and preview digest; stale inputs require review. Live link creation only through domain-authorized issue transaction/handoff. Rendering cannot create invitation/credential/attendance or change RSVP.

## 6. TDS-08/09 — Branding and localization

Revisioned logos, palette/semantic roles, typography, spacing/style, legal footer/contact and email/print defaults. Per-property precedence event → authorized venue → organization → platform default; absent inherits, explicit removal is a validated value; preserve mandatory footer policy. Venue and organizer owners distinct: explicit approved cross-owner asset/brand reference and authority, no implicit data access. Booking-only path has no event requirement. Validate preview/contrast/assets on publication and audit. Persist exact resolved values, revision IDs and assets in manifest; rebrand affects only explicitly reviewed new output, never previously issued materials.

Support bs-BA and en, BCP 47, UTF-8, licensed Unicode fonts, locale-specific authored variants under stable identity; no automatic translation. Follow ADR 0007: explicit validated interaction/communication choice → collected recipient preference → owner default → deployment en, subject to published variants and fallback policy. Show missing variant/actual language before issue; required legal/commercial text blocks send unless an approved alternative is explicitly selected consistently with policy. No inferred language from identity; staff preference not recipient locale. Persist locale and explicit IANA event/booking timezone. Locale-aware date/time/currency formatting without changing business facts. Test Č Ć Ž Š Đ and lowercase, long content, DST, numbers; accommodate future bidi/RTL shaping with full language acceptance later.

## 7. Architecture and rendering

Vue staff feature (proposed apps/staff-web/src/features/template-studio) → Fastify authorized template/brand/asset/preview/publish commands → PostgreSQL revisions/RLS/audit/outbox; scoped domain projection resolvers → render jobs → isolated render worker → private storage. Existing invitation/booking/campaign commands → existing notification worker/provider adapter for delivery only. Modular monolith, no mandatory cloud/Redis/microservice. Keep contracts explicit and avoid putting all logic in server route file. Reuse queue/outbox patterns; CPU-heavy PDF/image process separate bounded identity with no general DB credentials/network. Orchestration resolves authorized inputs; renderer receives only immutable sanitized source and approved assets and cannot mutate domain records.

### TDS-10 — Canonical source and adapters

Versioned discriminated JSON source: schemaVersion, purpose, mode, output, locale, source tree, component/asset/brand revision refs, catalogue version and validation digest. Rich document AST, responsive email block tree, fixed-layout scene graph with stable node IDs and z-order. Legacy text remains immutable legacy_text_v1 adapter, not silently parsed as new AST. HTML authoring/import normalized by parser/allowlist to supported representation; report rejected/ambiguous constructs; quarantine diagnostics only with short retention. No arbitrary CSS/scripts/includes. Explicit source transformations create drafts; published revisions remain compatible or retain original artifacts. No forced lossless round-trip between modes.

Illustrative typed email button node: {"type":"button","label":"Potvrdite dolazak","target":{"variable":"rsvp.url"}}. Example canvas QR: {"id":"n7","type":"qr","binding":"admission.qr","xMm":12,"yMm":48,"widthMm":26,"heightMm":26,"rotationDeg":0}; example size is not a validated minimum.

M0 evaluates maintained permissively licensed Vue-compatible rich text, constrained block editor, SVG/canvas scene editor, email compiler and PDF renderer (vector or sandboxed headless). Evaluate accessibility, paste sanitation, email client fixtures, source portability, fonts/metrics, determinism, licenses, security maintenance, offline native/Compose deployment, bundle size, no telemetry/remote dependency. Record decision and pinned versions in ADR; no library chosen now. Never disable sandbox for deployment convenience.

### TDS-11 — Server-authoritative rendering and private artifacts

Compile validated source + typed data + immutable brand/assets/components + locale/timezone + versioned adapter. Validate layout, overflow, dimensions/QR, digest and manifest before separate delivery/export/issue command. Browser preview may approximate, server is authoritative. PDF embeds licensed fonts, selectable text where feasible, vector shapes/QR, physical page boxes, DPI and imposition checks; print/decode evidence. Accessible reading order/alternatives; tagged PDF/PDF-UA only if actually verified. Do not promise byte-identical rerender after engine upgrades; preserve exact allowed artifact or canonical rendered payload and digest, engine/version. Explicit audited rerender; normalize volatile metadata if byte equivalence required.

Manifest: tenant/scope, template/revision/locale and source digest, brand resolution/revisions, component/asset hashes, projection type and source revisions, locale/timezone, renderer/schema/catalogue version, output/dimensions/page count/hash/size, actor/job/correlation/status/time/retention and private object ref. Private deployment-local filesystem/volume or approved store; authorize every download, bounded stream, restrictive caching. Sensitive content/snapshots encrypted per existing key policy. Never raw live token in template/revision/manifest, search index or logs; actual rendered bytes containing live token only existing restricted encrypted delivery/issuance or artifact boundary with minimum retention. Keep nonsecret digests/inputs after lawful purge; audit redaction/purge. Backup/restore must include DB, assets/artifacts and keys.

### TDS-12 — Queue and delivery

Separate bounded render/batch/print and actual delivery jobs, tenant/actor/action idempotency + canonical request fingerprint (identical retry same result; changed payload conflict), leases, backoff, cancellation, progress, safe failures and dead-letter recovery. No render/publish triggers send. Confirm actual audience/revision/locale and existing authority; worker rechecks applicable revocation/eligibility; changes invalidate review. Distinguish render, queue, provider acceptance, delivered/bounced/suppressed/uncertain. Existing reconciliation; no blind resend after ambiguous outcome. Test-send separate verified sandbox recipient, synthetic data, TEST marker and non-live link, audit/rate limit. Reuse SMTP/provider abstraction; multipart capability matrix and text fallback; render failure must not silently send legacy fallback or mutate booking/event. No test affects real recipients, RSVP or attendance.

## 8. TDS-13 — Logical schema and upgrade

Proposed logical aggregates, not DDL. Every tenant entity has organization_id, composite tenant FKs, explicit owner scope, RLS and restricted commands; no unchecked polymorphic IDs; existing actor/UUID conventions.

| Entity | Invariants |
|---|---|
| Existing notification_templates | Stable ID/code/purpose/status; extend validated scope or link common catalogue without duplicate email identity |
| Existing notification_template_revisions | Preserve historical locale/subject/body/revision/state and invitation/campaign FKs; add structured source/metadata/dependencies/review via compatible extension or sidecar |
| Common template definitions (if needed) | Stable owner/scope/purpose/mode/source locale; reference existing email lineage |
| Print document template revisions (if needed) | Independent non-email definition, locale/source/physical bounds, digest/approval and renderer version |
| Revision dependencies | Typed immutable component/asset/brand/contract refs, tenant integrity, no cycles |
| Template assignments | Explicit scope/purpose/channel/locale → active published revision; unique applicable selection, history/precondition |
| Review decisions | Append-only digest/reviewer/actor/grant/time/reason |
| Component revisions | Bounded reusable source, immutable publication/dependencies |
| Brand profiles/revisions | Approved property overrides, asset references, publication, resolved snapshot |
| Design assets/revisions | Quarantine/approved/revoked, digest/type/size/dimensions/license/alt, private object ref |
| Render jobs/artifacts | Tenant/actor/idempotency, manifest, lease/status/progress/error/expiry and protected blob |
| Existing invitation/campaign/delivery | Authoritative facts; add explicit revision/manifest references only as needed |

Validate mode/purpose/output, published digest/dependencies, unique locale variants, stale approvals, cross-tenant link denial, restricted deletion and write boundaries. Migration sequence: inventory existing purposes, variables, guards/readers; backward-compatible format metadata/read adapters; restricted authoring commands/library/brand/assets; opt-in structured multipart; explicit reviewed assignments; print aggregate/jobs. Test fresh DB and populated upgrades with issued, queued and historical legacy rows. Preserve old semantics and IDs. No forced AST interpretation. Forward-only upgrade; supported older readers or explicitly blocked incompatible downgrade, recovery documented.

## 9. TDS-14 — Illustrative API contract

Align exact routes/operation IDs/schema/error codes with OpenAPI v0.3 and existing conventions; no public generic template API. Staff auth/CSRF/origin, resource scope and operation/field permissions. Reject unknown executable fields, oversized trees; revision preconditions and idempotency as applicable. Safe non-enumerating problem responses.

| Family / proposed operations | Intent |
|---|---|
| GET/POST /templates | Scoped filtered paginated catalogue, create/clone draft |
| GET /templates/{id}/revisions/{revisionId}; PATCH /templates/{id}/drafts/{draftId} | Authorized source/dependencies, optimistic edit |
| POST draft validate/submit-review; revision review-decisions/publish/retire | Node diagnostics, digest review and immutable publication |
| GET /template-variable-catalogue | Typed permitted definitions and samples only |
| /template-components, /brand-profiles | Scoped draft/revision/preview/publish/retire |
| POST /design-assets/uploads; GET approved asset revision | Bounded quarantined upload; authorized metadata/content |
| POST /template-assignments | Published purpose/channel/locale selection and preconditions |
| POST /template-previews | Digest + synthetic fixture or authorized recipient; no issuance |
| POST /template-test-deliveries | Approved target ID, synthetic-only test, locale |
| POST/GET /document-render-jobs; POST job cancel | Scoped single/batch/print render/progress/results/cancel, no delivery |
| GET /render-artifacts/{id}/content | Current authorization, private no-store, controlled content disposition |
| Existing domain issue/approve/send operations | Choose approved assignment/revision/manifest; no bypass |

Validation response includes valid/errors/warnings (code,nodeId,path,messageKey), digest. Preview receipt includes id/status/resolvedLocale/sourceDigest/brandDigest/diagnostics/artifactId if appropriate. Job receipt includes id/status/total/processed/succeeded/failed/cancelled/createdAt/expiresAt. 202 async, 409 conflict, 422 or existing validation equivalent. No recipient ID in public URL or arbitrary context object. Maintain OpenAPI tests/auth matrix/representative fixtures.

## 10. TDS-15 — Security, privacy and accessibility

| Threat | Mandatory mitigation |
|---|---|
| XSS via paste/HTML/SVG/CSS/URL | Server allowlist AST, context escaping, reject active/event/script/javascript/obfuscated constructs, strict CSP, isolated preview without scripts/same-origin privileges |
| SSRF/exfiltration | Network-denied render worker, controlled asset resolver, no arbitrary remote fonts/images/URLs/files/paths/redirects/DNS/private-network requests; validate link scheme/policy without fetch |
| Template injection | Structured typed bindings and bounded predicates, no evaluation or arbitrary property access |
| Tenant disclosure | Composite FK/RLS and exact scope/field/operation checks, non-enumerating errors, tenant + permission cache context, current download authorization |
| Guest data/token leaks | Synthetic default, audited authorized real preview, scoped data, encrypted private outputs/minimized retention, no personal payload/raw tokens in logs/cache/metrics |
| Upload abuse | Type from bytes, quarantine, size/pixels/pages/depth limits, raster reencode, safe SVG sanitize/rasterize, reject active/executable/external refs/decompression bombs; font validation/license, malware screening per policy |
| Accidental/unauthorized send | Separate preview/render/publish vs issue/send, explicit recipient digest/confirmation, existing permissions, test marker/non-live links, rate limits and idempotency |
| QR misuse | Typed purpose, separate credentials, revocation/issue domain, final decode test, reject swapped/revoked credential |
| Resource exhaustion | Node/depth/asset budgets, bounded queues/time/CPU/memory, non-root worker, backpressure/cancel, monitoring |
| Historical mutation | Immutable revision/dependencies, exact hashes, explicit reissue, auditable purge |
| Supply chain | Pinned reviewed dependencies/security scans, process sandbox, no mandatory telemetry/network, documented updates |

Preview cannot access staff cookies/storage or arbitrary network. Email output safe independent of sandbox; no private data interpolation into image/CSS URLs. Public asset service (if enabled) only explicitly designated nonpersonal material. Preserve existing fragment-based public token handling; no raw tracking parameters/third-party redirect or open redirect. Renderer logs safe identifiers/counts/failure codes only.

Target WCAG 2.2 AA staff and guest web/email where applicable. Keyboard-only edit/reorder/resize/publish, semantic labels/headings, focus restoration, meaningful links, alternatives, contrast, visible diagnostics, responsive scaling, no color-only status. Print warnings/review where visual choices affect accessibility. Manual assistive technology and keyboard verification, not automated scans alone; disclose email/PDF support limitations.

## 11. TDS-16 — Operations, limits and proposed service targets

Initial suggested benchmark (not measured or approved production sizing): 4 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM, SSD, local DB. Suggested source ≤1 MiB/2,000 nodes/depth 24, component depth 8; raster ≤15 MiB/40 megapixels, stricter SVG/font spike limits. Warm bounded single preview p95 ≤3s, draft save p95 ≤500ms local network with debounced ~1s autosave. Initially ≤500 recipients/job, partition larger reviewed batches; stream outputs, bound CPU/memory/time and per-tenant/global concurrency. Preview expiry suggested 24h; sensitive output retention/legal hold/purge per approved policy. These are M0 benchmark inputs, not established SLOs. API responsive when renderer saturated/unavailable; visible queue/backpressure/errors.

Native/systemd and Compose same release fonts/renderer, non-root sandbox, persistent private storage, ownership, health/readiness, lease recovery, upgrade/recovery. DB/assets/artifact/key-consistent backup and restore digest tests. Local email capture, synthetic CI; external SMTP/host acceptance only with actual recorded evidence during planned Phase 9. Metrics queue age/depth, duration/failure/timeout/saturation/storage/cleanup/send reconciliation, no guest labels. Audited review/publish/assignment/real preview/export/send/test; draft save may summarize. Correlation IDs.
