# Eventor User Experience and Navigation
## Shared application experience contract v1.0

**Status:** Proposed for product-owner review; no implementation or repository integration authorized.  
**Date:** 2026-11-27. **Inspected main:** `0c5e7a2ddf0a676a89bb75faef1265438dc2ae45`.  
**Proposed destination:** `docs/implementation-design/v0.3/EVENTOR_USER_EXPERIENCE_AND_NAVIGATION_v1.0.md`.  
**Companions:** [OAC technical specification](ORGANIZATION_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [Organization Lifecycle Acceptance](ORGANIZATION_LIFECYCLE_ACCEPTANCE_SCENARIOS_v1.0.md). This document governs presentation and navigation; domain commands, privacy, permissions and lifecycle remain authoritative. All layouts, names, routes and role examples below are proposals, not implemented screenshots or real customer data.

## 1. Objective and design principles (UX-01)

Eventor should feel like one coherent application from initial provisioning through daily administration and the event day. Users should know where they are, what they may do, what requires attention and what will happen if they take an action. The interface MUST guide an authorized user to complete their job without requiring familiarity with the database, deployment internals or source code. It MUST not use a single unrestricted dashboard for every role.

Principles: explicit context; accessible and localized interactions; predictable visual hierarchy; meaningful empty and error states; permissions and readiness reflected but never enforced by the UI alone; safe review before consequential actions; honest freshness and status; independent venue-only operation; reuse owning domain workflows rather than duplicated forms. Avoid navigation overload, giant all-purpose screens, decorative widgets without a task, unbounded lists, modal chains, mandatory setup for irrelevant features or silent defaults. A user should be able to return to the previous task without losing valid draft work, subject to security/expiry and explicit context changes.

## 2. Reconciliation and source hierarchy

| Source | UX contract |
|---|---|
| [Blueprint v1.2](../../blueprint/v1.2/Event_Operations_Platform_Technical_Blueprint_v1.2.md) §§4,5,21,25–26,35,41,46 | Permission-scoped interface, operational cockpit, branding, guest-safe projections and accessibility |
| [ADR 0001](../../decisions/0001-modular-monolith.md), [0008](../../decisions/0008-modular-staff-frontend.md) | Thin root and modular Vue features, composables and shared primitives; incremental transition, no rewrite |
| [ADR 0003](../../decisions/0003-human-approved-allocation.md), [0004](../../decisions/0004-optional-event-operations-scope.md), [0005](../../decisions/0005-separate-invitations-rsvp-attendance.md), [0006](../../decisions/0006-cross-organization-collaboration.md) | Review/commit, optional profiles, separate credential facts and cross-party ownership |
| [ADR 0007](../../decisions/0007-internationalization.md) | bs-BA/en, stable domain identifiers, locale preference and explicit timezone |
| [ADR 0010](../../decisions/0010-organization-membership-access.md), [0015](../../decisions/0015-email-first-login-and-platform-administration.md), [0017](../../decisions/0017-host-staff-account-bootstrap.md), [0020](../../decisions/0020-host-existing-staff-membership.md) | Credential-first entry, safe membership switching and host provisioning boundaries |
| [ADR 0016](../../decisions/0016-event-rsvp-policy-settings.md), [0021](../../decisions/0021-booking-event-association-commands.md), [0022](../../decisions/0022-event-disruption-publication-and-acknowledgement.md), [0023](../../decisions/0023-permissioned-collaboration-grant-lifecycle.md), [0024](../../decisions/0024-shared-party-names-and-reviewed-grant-acceptance.md) | Versioned RSVP settings, explicit associations, separate notice acknowledgement, reviewed partner access |
| [PAC](PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [TDS](TEMPLATE_DESIGN_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [OAC](ORGANIZATION_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md) | Distinct management contexts, shared identity/brand/assets and editor, onboarding and organization home |
| [Operating Model](../../OPERATING_MODEL.md), [Roles](../../product/USER_ROLES_AND_PERMISSIONS_v0.1.md), [Roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md) | Provider/organizer/hybrid, role duties, existing milestones |

Current source `apps/staff-web/src/features/application-shell/StaffApplicationShell.vue` and `apps/api/src/staff-workspaces.ts` establish a bilingual header, credential-first login, membership switch and allowed tabs; `App.vue` selects Events when authorized, otherwise a permitted section. The proposed home, responsive shell, global search and setup wizard are additions, not claims of current implementation. Existing contract `/me/workspaces` hints and all server-side grants remain valid. PAC's proposed narrower managed access requires successor review; UX cannot imply owner visibility into restricted records. Do not modify accepted ADRs or v0.2 contract snapshots to achieve visual consistency.

## 3. Workspace taxonomy and context transitions (UX-02)

```text
Installation (PAC: explicitly privileged context)
  └── Organization selection → OAC home (active selected tenant)
       ├── Provider: booking / venue / resource / fulfilment work
       ├── Organizer: events / Registry / invitations / operational work
       ├── Shared: staff / settings / collaboration / reporting / TDS
       └── Authorized event → EOC (event context)
            ├── Planning, sessions, rosters, allocation, readiness
            └── Live: arrival, stations, tasks, alerts and corrections
Separate purpose-scoped entry points: customer, guest, vendor, station, display
```

Hierarchy is context, not authority inheritance. An event-scoped user can enter an allowed event without OAC administration or Registry permission. A provider may only manage venue-side tasks even in hybrid collaboration. External surfaces have distinct credentials/projections and do not expose the staff shell. PAC remains separate management context; normal organization users cannot see a PAC link or global navigation. Enter tenant from PAC only through approved scoped transition under actual actor, with visible grant/expiry banner if support; never impersonate. Return to PAC requires current privileged authority and appropriate authentication, not browser history replay. No implicit switch when following a foreign-tenant URL; ask to select an authorized membership, then resolve with current permission; deny without naming unauthorized tenant/resource.

## 4. Sign-in, first run and organization setup (UX-03)

### Entry decision table

| Condition | Landing behavior |
|---|---|
| Unauthenticated staff | Safe platform brand/login; locale selector; no tenant enumeration, no public organization list from email |
| Pending staff invite | Purpose-bound enrollment surface; verify recipient and identity, accept explicit organization membership; no password reset of existing user through invite |
| Valid credentials, one active membership | Direct selected tenant, subject to required MFA and current session policy |
| Valid credentials, multiple active memberships | Display authorized named choices only after verification; selection completes sign-in; no credentials in browser storage |
| Active account, no active membership | Safe access-unavailable/support guidance; no unauthorized names or registration-as-admin |
| New/partially configured tenant + setup authority | OAC home with guided resumable checklist and actionable missing prerequisites |
| Existing configured tenant + overview authority | Profile-aware organization dashboard; optional setup/reconfiguration accessible in Settings |
| Event/task-only or no overview grant | Most relevant permitted task/event, or safe list/Settings; no empty unauthorized dashboard |
| Authorized explicit deep link | Resolve after current auth/context; show target or safe denial; never bypass setup-dependent command checks |
| Platform-only identity | PAC only when its auth/context requirements met; not a fabricated tenant membership |

Proposed login, enrollment and MFA UX integrates PAC shared identity; keep host bootstrap fallback and ADR 0015 session expiry. Initial GHB administrator need not know UUIDs, tenant slugs or database commands. Sign-in failures non-enumerating; allow paste/password managers, keyboard and proper autocomplete, clear errors without secret echo. Do not enforce arbitrary client-side credential limits that conflict with actual accepted server contract. Never store password, session, MFA recovery code or invitation token in local storage/URL query/logs. Use existing fragment/capability handling where applicable, clear safe URL after redemption. Session expiry preserves no sensitive local draft; guide sign-in and authorized recovery. Onboarding invitation send is explicit; no automatic role based on email domain or existing name.

### Setup wizard wireflow

```text
Welcome → Organization profile → Capabilities → Identity/branding
        → Facilities/resources (if applicable) → Commercial policies (if applicable)
        → Communications/forms/templates → People/responsibilities
        → Review readiness → Explicit relevant service activation → OAC home
```

Steps adapt to profile and permissions, can be resumed or completed in domain screens. Show `Not applicable`, `Required`, `Optional`, `Needs attention`, `Ready` with reason; progress denominator = applicable steps, not a false universal completion score. Branding may inherit safe default; non-email workflows can continue without SMTP; missing seating never blocks booking/RSVP. Owner can proceed to available work while setup incomplete. Each step links to existing owning editor; no duplicate form/config models. Save/back/skip optional/exit, accessible progress and focus; concurrency conflict reload and compare. Readiness checks derived from current server facts; review shows dependencies, affected audience/public links and warnings; activation has explicit separate action. Don't silently publish public forms or create live credentials. Existing customer settings remain intact; no forced reset on upgrade. Setup screen never asks tenant admin for host secrets or platform credentials.

## 5. Canonical navigation (UX-04)

Desktop staff shell: compact header with approved organization brand, tenant name/switch (only multiple authorized memberships), current context, locale/theme, scoped search, notifications, account/support/sign out. Collapsible sidebar with stable grouped items, breadcrumb and page title/action toolbar. Tablet adapts to drawer/compact rail; phone uses accessible drawer and focused task views. Preserve visible organization/event/station name even when space limited. Event and tenant switch are distinct. Use accessible semantic nav/main/header landmarks. Do not render unavailable/unauthorized modules as misleading active links. If a permitted module is not configured, show setup reason and permitted link rather than hiding a legitimate task. Installed but not delivered features never look operational; show explicit unavailable only where useful to administrator. Order not rigid for personal favorites; stable canonical route IDs.

| Group / proposed route ID | Provider default | Organizer default | Hybrid | Owning feature / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `org.home` Overview | Yes | Yes | Yes | OAC authorized metrics/queue |
| `org.setup` Setup & readiness | Admin | Admin | Admin | OAC readiness |
| `org.calendar` Calendar | Yes | Yes | Yes | Authorized owned resources/assigned events, no source leak |
| `org.bookings` Bookings / inquiries / offers | Yes | Optional | Yes | Existing booking feature, commercial decisions |
| `org.venues` Venues & spaces | Yes | Optional owned venues | Yes | #105 source geometry and versions |
| `org.resources` Resources & services | Yes | Optional | Yes | Owned catalogues/fulfilment |
| `org.events` Events portfolio | Optional | Yes | Yes | #104 events/session/lifecycle |
| `org.registry` Guest Registry | Optional | Yes | Yes | Only organization-scoped Registry grants |
| `event.roster` Guest list | Optional per event | Optional | Optional | Event-specific; Registry separate |
| `event.invitations` Invitations & RSVP | Optional | Optional | Optional | #104/111 and invitation/RSVP grants |
| `event.allocation` Seating & plans | Optional | Optional | Optional | #106, map/approval |
| `event.operations` Operations cockpit | Optional | Optional | Optional | #107 and owning event grants |
| `org.partners` Collaboration & vendor tasks | As needed | As needed | As needed | #110/#112; explicit grant and projection |
| `org.studio` Design Studio & assets | As needed | As needed | As needed | TDS modes/purposes, no implicit send |
| `org.communications` Forms, delivery & campaigns | As needed | As needed | As needed | Existing owning workflows; SMTP under Settings or dedicated authorized subpage |
| `org.reports` Reports/exports | Authorized | Authorized | Authorized | Bounded read/export permissions |
| `org.admin` Administration | Authorized | Authorized | Authorized | Profile, modules, staff/access, policy, brand, governance, audit/support |

These defaults do not restrict cross-profile operation. Venue-only admin may enable event services if deployment supports and policy allows; organizer may manage an owned venue or approved partner projection. Both still require correct role/scope. A limited user sees only authorized navigation, with no unauthorized counts, links, names or disabled controls hinting at restricted records. Use task-focused shortcuts; no UI permission via profile. For OAC and EOC, use a consistent back-to-organization action and breadcrumb (organization → event → subtask). EOC may expose full event planning and live tabs subject to event capability and task role; don't require EOC to perform basic organizer work. Reception/gate operators may go straight to station workspace, with separate station identity and restricted context.

## 6. Role-based landing and task composition (UX-05)

| Example role | Default landing and priority actions | Do not show by default |
|---|---|---|
| GHB organization admin | OAC home, readiness, admin queues, member management, allowed operations | PAC, other tenants, restricted data without grant |
| Director/finance approver | Authorized KPIs, pending decisions with financial context and approved detail | Guest notes/Registry or unrelated account management |
| Booking manager | Inquiries needing review, today's availability, drafts/offers | Organizer confidential data and global policy |
| Venue coordinator | Calendar, venue readiness, reservations/service tasks | Guest list and pricing if ungranted |
| Event manager | Events portfolio / assigned event, programme and readiness | Unassigned events, Registry without explicit scope |
| Registry/guest coordinator | Authorized Registry or assigned event roster, imports and RSVP exceptions | Other tenant profiles, admission by RSVP alone |
| Communications operator | Approved campaigns, TDS if allowed, delivery queue | Forbidden recipient fields, send if only designer |
| Seating manager | Assigned event map, constraints and proposed changes | Unapproved plan publish or unrelated guest history |
| Reception/station | Camera scan/manual lookup, arrivals and safe feedback | Full guest list, bulk export, global dashboard |
| Vendor/task operator | Assigned tasks/deliverables and permitted context | Broad tenant navigation |
| Auditor | Scoped evidence and approved reports | Write actions |

Actual landing derived from current server hints, selected context, capability, role and optional last valid route; unknown or unauthorized route falls back safely. Never store a sensitive last record in shared browser preference. Empty granted scope = no assigned work, not a permission failure; denied = safe access explanation; unavailable = explicit system/configuration reason. Role-specific action toolbar uses allowed operation hints for discoverability only. Authority checked again on each API call and websocket subscription.

## 7. Dashboard and work-item design (UX-06)

Use focused summary cards and prioritized queues, not a wall of counts. OAC overview starts with the user's current organization, date/window/timezone, readiness/alerts, then authorized modules. Provider: open inquiries, awaiting decisions, today/next bookings, venue conflicts/closure, fulfilment. Organizer: upcoming events, sessions, RSVP/guest/plan/task status within authorized scope. Hybrid: both, clearly labeled, no mixing reservation counts and events. Management financial metrics explicit definition and currency; no false revenue from pending offers. Widgets provide current source/time and drill-down with filters. No exposed small sensitive cohorts or inferred forbidden counts. Zero only when actual known zero. Skeleton during load, stale observation badge after disconnect, not-applicable and unknown states distinct; partial widget failure does not make all home unavailable. No simulated counts on production screen. User preferences choose only permitted widgets; role and policy changes re-evaluate. Server provides bounded aggregates, not whole tenant data pulled into browser.

Work-item pattern: status/priority (business-defined), object/owner context, due time, reason, permitted next action, last update and link. Filters and pagination; keyboard and mobile readable. Acknowledgement/read status never constitutes business approval, sending, completion, notice resolution or acceptance of grant. Dashboard actions invoke owning workflow with current data/revision and confirmation when required. Dismiss a noncritical reminder only; do not silently resolve safety/booking conflicts. Task deadlines and alert thresholds approved by tenant/event policy, not guessed.

## 8. Common screen patterns and component system (UX-07)

| Pattern | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Page header | Context breadcrumb, title, short purpose, current status and primary permitted action; back navigation and safe help |
| List/table | Search, stable filters/sort, pagination/cursor, columns with units and scoped count; selection count, no implicit "all pages" bulk action |
| Detail | Overview, activity/history, related authorized references, actions; immutable snapshot marked and no direct edit |
| Form/editor | Labels/help/required indicator, field validation and summary, draft state, save/cancel, revision/conflict handling, unsaved changes |
| Wizard | Resumable step, actual readiness, dependencies, optional skip, review; no duplicate domain writes |
| Review/approval | Exact target, before/after, impact, revision/digest and policy; explicit choice/reason, actor authority, stale conflict requires rereview |
| Bulk action | Filter/selected IDs and count, affected scope/operation, preview invalid rows, atomic or documented per-item result, explicit confirmation, receipt |
| Import | Select file/worksheet/header, map fields, validation and duplicate review; commit reviewed set; row errors and protected report |
| Export | Scope/filters/columns/format, warnings, approval if required, job progress, safe private download, expiry and audit |
| Timeline/audit | Actual actor, timestamp/timezone, action/result and permitted history; separate notes vs audit; never editable history |
| Map/editor | Scaled zoom, legend/layers, accessible list/numeric alternative, lock/read-only/published indicators, exact revision, no guest source layers |
| Job/receipt | Pending/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled/uncertain distinguished; correlation ID, safe retry/reconcile, never fake success |

Shared tokens: semantic text/surface/border/action/focus/critical/warning/success, typographic scale, spacing, elevation and responsive breakpoints. Use TDS/PAC brand profile as source; no hardcoded GHB identity or logo. Shared controls include buttons, inputs, labels, field errors, dialog, drawer, table, badges, toast/live region, tabs, stepper and focus management. Reserve primary action for task, secondary for alternatives, destructive style for irreversible/high-impact actions. Do not rely on color alone. Keyboard accessible reorder and drag/resize alternatives for email/graphical/venue/seating editors. No requirement for a specific UI library until reviewed M0. Keep feature-level logic out of shared components; use composables and typed API client. No global root orchestration of every command.

## 9. Search, notification and personal workspace (UX-08)

Global search within selected context and effective scope; grouped by permitted resource kinds (booking, event, venue, guest if Registry grant or specifically permitted roster projection, task). Bounded terms/results, debounce and cancel stale request, safe pagination, no unauthorized autocomplete/suggestions/counts/highlights. Search index, if necessary, uses owning authorization at read time; no global unrestricted index or persistent client copy. Deep links carry stable resource reference, not secrets or confidential labels. Recents/favorites store safe route refs and revalidate; remove/deny inaccessible references on revoke/context switch. No cross-org search by default. Search of booking-only organization cannot reveal organizer guests.

Notifications: in-app inbox for scoped pending actions, assigned tasks, system/tenant notices and permitted alerts. Server-derived safe title/context, timestamp, read/ack state; no raw guest contact or sensitive content in toast/browser push. Open reauthorizes; expiry/revoke clears private data. Real-time updates if supported, poll/refresh fallback; read acknowledgement distinct from business decision. External communication from campaign/booking worker remains separate and explicit. No automatic email to all users from dashboard action. Preferences for locale, theme, density, saved view/favorites and optional notice channels are per actual actor/scope, do not alter brand/policy. Sensitive draft data only server-authorized encrypted storage where needed; never local storage of credentials or unrestricted exports.

## 10. Branding, themes and localization (UX-09)

Platform login default and PAC shell use approved platform identity; known public organization/event link may use explicitly approved public brand projection (no membership enumeration); authenticated OAC uses organization identity; EOC resolves event/authorized venue/organization/platform precedence. Mark event branding and owning party clearly, including partner venue not organizer. Guest/customer/display artifacts use pinned published brand and template, not operator's dark mode. User preference light/dark/system/high contrast separate from brand, accessible focus/contrast baseline cannot be overridden. Safe fallback if asset unavailable, invalid theme or storage degraded; never make login/security notice unreadable. Approved logo variants, semantic tokens, fonts/licensed fallback, localized names/contact/legal/footer; no arbitrary CSS/JS/remote asset fetch. TDS owns editing/rendering, PAC governs platform policies, OAC administers tenant properties. Preview/publish with actual revision. Do not invent GHB palette as requirement.

Use `bs-BA` and `en`, ADR 0007 precedence for staff preference → selected org default → deployment fallback en. Locale picker independent of timezone; user changes persisted by existing preference command; offer/RSVP/invitation uses explicit recipient/content locale and approved fallback, no automatic translation of authoritative legal/commercial text. Date/time explicit event/booking timezone, UTC storage, DST ambiguous time handled visibly; Bosnian `DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm` where appropriate per existing feedback; use Intl for number/currency/plural and correct diacritics ČĆŽŠĐ/čćžšđ. No translated strings as enum or key. Localize validation/status/empty states/help, plural, accessible labels, PDF/email where applicable. Missing translation fallback UI with tooling; missing mandatory authored variant blocks or clearly approved alternative. Test long labels and wrap, no clipped text. Future languages supported by architecture, no unverified RTL claim.

## 11. Consequential actions and truthful status (UX-10)

Review/confirmation matrix:

| Action | Preview evidence | Commit outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Publish form/brand/template | Resolved scope/version, locale/validation, public exposure and impacted new outputs | New published revision; never send or issue |
| Offer/confirm booking | Exact request, resource/time, pinned price/tax/policy, authority and conflict recheck | Owning booking receipt; no automatic event |
| Booking/event cancellation or postponement | Correct lifecycle, impact on reservations, commercial consequences, affected party and approved notice | Separate domain transition; no inferred refunds or other party event cancellation |
| Merge Registry | Source/destination, field conflicts, linked records and reviewed correction | Audited command, protected identity/history |
| Plan publish/solver commit | Input version, conflicts/hard rules, diff, approval and explicit human acceptance | New approved revision; no automatic application |
| Issue/send campaign | Exact audience, locale/template/policy versions, digest, recipient count and delivery channel | Explicit authorized issue/queue, acceptance/delivered not conflated |
| Revoke grant/session/credential | Exact scope, effect, reason, expiry and affected tasks | Owning revocation receipt, no unrelated change |
| Support/emergency | Actual actor, exact scope, purpose, expiry/approval and permitted intervention | Audited limited action; no impersonation |
| Suspend/archive/purge | Affected obligations, holds, history, access, drain/recovery and export | Reviewed domain/PAC lifecycle; no silent data loss |

Confirmations must state what changes and what does not; avoid generic "Are you sure?" for high impact. Approval/validation != execution; preview != publication; RSVP != attendance; offer != confirmed booking; notice != effective cancellation/acknowledgement != resolution; queue/provider acceptance != delivery; backup created != restore tested; readiness != authorization. Stale revisions and changed scope require fresh review; no automatic retries of ambiguous mutations. Disable double-click locally but use server idempotency. After timeout show uncertain state with receipt lookup/reconcile path. Separate reason and actual actor from target. Show safe problem code and correlation ID, not raw SQL/network secrets. Audit details accessible only if granted. No UI generic override.

## 12. Specialized public and operational surfaces (UX-11)

| Surface | User experience and boundary |
|---|---|
| Public booking | Branded published form, localized help/validation, submit receipt, scoped offer/cancellation link and status; no staff menu or internal notes, no account required by default |
| Guest invitation/RSVP | Verified purpose-bound access, own event details and response, approved policy/deadline and safe confirmation; no other guests/Registry; invitation not admission |
| Guest Portal | Own approved allocation/wayfinding, sanitized map, guest-safe programme/help, current published revision, access revoked/expired states; no internal layers |
| Gate/station | Explicit assigned station/event, QR camera permission/manual alternative, minimal guest details, large clear duplicate/revoked/accepted feedback, offline queue status; never RSVP as attendance |
| Vendor | Own task/deliverable/due date and approved evidence submission, limited contact/venue projection; no staff navigation or unrelated tasks |
| Display | Read-only sanitized published content, timestamp/revision and safe fallback; no guest directory or admin controls, no confidential layers |
| TDS | Shared library by owner/purpose, rich text/email/graphical editor, keyboard alternatives, preview/review/publish; synthetic default, never issue/send from preview |

Each uses separate credential and purpose validation; authorized links opaque, no secrets in URL query, referer, analytics or logs. Public pages have clear expiry/support path without disclosing forbidden record existence. Offline and reconnect show last synchronized state and pending/error count; no unsupported offline mutation promised. Gate conflicting scans reconciled visibly under domain rules. A public internet outage should not prevent supported LAN operations. EOC live views mark stale data and actual status. QR print/layout subject to TDS readability/security checks.

## 13. Responsive layout, accessibility and assistive technology (UX-12)

Target WCAG 2.2 AA for applicable web surfaces, verified with keyboard, screen reader and manual review plus automated checks. Logical DOM and focus order, skip link, visible focus, keyboard-operable controls, meaningful aria names, semantic headings/tables/landmarks, status announced without disruptive repeated live alerts. Error summary links to invalid fields, instructions not color-only, sufficient contrast, usable zoom/reflow, targets at least WCAG minimum with larger mobile task controls. Avoid hover-only actions, pointer-only drag, tiny scan buttons, animation without reduced-motion preference. Numeric/list controls provide equivalent create/move/reorder/resize/assign functions. Modal focus trap/return and escape, confirmation can be cancelled without side effect. Tables responsive by priority columns and accessible detail/card view, not hidden essential information; horizontal scroll only intrinsically large data/geometry with alternative. Mobile station and vendor tasks use focused screen, camera denial manual path; tablet and desktop full planning. Print styles and PDF accessible semantic content when supported; record limitations rather than claim PDF/UA. Representative viewport acceptance proposed 360, 768, 1280 and 1920 CSS px plus 200% zoom; no clipping/overlap for core workflow. Test Chromium/Firefox and actual supported mobile/device during final acceptance. No mandatory browser-specific API without fallback.

## 14. State, routing and API integration (UX-13)

Illustrative stable route pattern (not existing URLs): `/staff/org/:orgId/home`, `/staff/org/:orgId/bookings/:id`, `/staff/org/:orgId/events/:eventId/overview`, `/.../operations`, `/.../admin/access`, `/.../studio`; distinct private `/platform/...` and public purpose paths. Existing public capability paths and staff tabs remain supported until deliberate compatibility migration; no broken issued links. Route IDs independent of translated labels. Server validates path/selected membership and exact object scope; URL never grants authority. Unknown route safe not-found, foreign authorized membership prompts explicit switch, unauthorized existence not confirmed. Account/session/context changes cancel pending requests, close websocket, clear all tenant data/cache, reset selected event/dialog and refetch allowed navigation; actual session expiry preserved. Existing ADR 0015 page replacement is safe baseline. Never accept URL/open redirect or untrusted actionRef. Save durable drafts through owning authorized service, not local storage of PII. Unsaved state warning before route/context switch only where safe; revoke/expiry clears regardless. Back/forward history reauthorizes; no stale data flash.

| Proposed shared contract | Fields / behavior |
|---|---|
| Session context | Actor ID, selected organization/membership, locale, authorized workspaces, expiry, scope hints; PAC/elevation separately scoped and visible |
| Navigation manifest | Stable route/feature ID, labelKey, context type, available/ready/action hints, child IDs; generated from authorized capabilities; not permission token |
| Readiness | OAC derived per-capability status/reason, owning route ref, source revision and observed time |
| Overview / search | Authorized bounded projections, safe resourceRef and definition/time, no unauthorized count or arbitrary URL |
| Work items / alerts | Typed owning kind/ref, safe title, state/dueAt/time, actionHint and revision |
| Command receipt | Request/correlation ID, target/safe state, current revision, result/uncertainty and next allowed action; actual server outcome |
| Preferences | Actor-scoped locale/theme/density/saved route IDs, no restricted payload; existing saved views reused |

Extend `/me/workspaces` compatibly; API for OAC home/readiness/search/queues as OAC §9. Shared component state is derived from typed response; client cache keyed by actor/context and current authority, no shared global cache across organizations. Read authorization includes subscriptions and downloads, not only route visibility. Transport errors standardized, request ID surfaced for support, optional feature failure isolated. Keep `App.vue` thin; feature routes/composables and shared design system (ADR 0008). No independent UX domain database; persisted preferences/readiness facts only if OAC/PAC owning model requires. No runtime API/schema changes in documentation PR.

## 15. Incremental implementation and dependencies

| Package | Deliverable | Scheduled track |
|---|---|---|
| UX-M0 | Inventory current screen/route/capability mapping, shared design tokens, accessibility and interaction review; no rewrite | OAC-M0 / #104 when scheduled |
| UX-M1 | Incremental shell/context/home and readiness primitives, role landing, shared error/empty/list patterns, secure onboarding UX | #104, PAC shared identity |
| UX-M2 | Provider calendar/booking and venue/resource navigation, map accessibility patterns | Phase 1/#105/#112 |
| UX-M3 | Event portfolio/EOC, seating and guest/station/vendor/display role flows | #104/#106/#107/#110 |
| UX-M4 | Shared brand/locale/theme, TDS and forms, search/reports/preferences | #111/TDS/PAC |
| UX-M5 | Release integration, responsive/manual accessibility and full journeys | #108/Phase 9, OLA |

**Codex continuity:** #104/#112 current work then #105–107, unchanged. UX is a contract for new work and touched features, not a demand to refactor everything now or block existing domain PRs. Preserve existing links, grants, authentication and accepted ADRs. No implementation solely on merge of docs. No environment publication or early acceptance VM. Existing issue requirements remain; use cross-references instead of duplicate UX issues. Later ADR/engineering review selects UI library, routes and performance budgets.

## 16. Measurable UX acceptance criteria

Each test is proposed, not currently passed. Use synthetic fixtures and actual authorized contexts; run API/DB negative cases as well as browser behavior. Cross-reference OLA scenarios.

| ID | Observable outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| UX-AC-01 | Known/unrecognized credentials do not expose workspace names before verified sign-in; correct one/multi/no-membership outcomes | OLA-02; API/browser |
| UX-AC-02 | Switch tenant/context rotates session per ADR, preserves expiry/actor, clears prior state/streams; unauthorized deep links cannot flash data | OLA-06; browser/concurrency |
| UX-AC-03 | First-login setup resumable and profile-specific; optional skip and blocked prerequisite reason; no forced guest modules | OLA-03 |
| UX-AC-04 | Correct provider/organizer/hybrid navigation and role landing; PAC not visible/accessible to tenant | OLA-04/06 |
| UX-AC-05 | Authorized overview counts/time/filters match fixture; unknown/stale/empty distinguished, partial failure isolated | OLA-04/14 |
| UX-AC-06 | Search/favorites/notifications never expose unauthorized names/counts or old tenant refs after revoke | OLA-06/11 |
| UX-AC-07 | List filter, sort/page, selection and bulk preview accurately represent affected set; stale/invalid review rejected | OLA-07/09/13 |
| UX-AC-08 | Reviewed commands show exact version/impact/reason, actual outcome and safe uncertainty recovery; cancel no side effect | OLA-07–12 |
| UX-AC-09 | Platform/org/venue/event brand preview/publish/fallback works, personal theme independent; previous artifact unchanged | OLA-05 |
| UX-AC-10 | bs-BA/en labels, diacritics, timezone/DST and locale-formatted dates/amounts; mandatory authored translation policy | OLA-03/05/14 |
| UX-AC-11 | Public booking, guest, station, vendor, display limited to own projection; no staff navigation or data leak | OLA-07/09/10 |
| UX-AC-12 | QR camera denial/manual path, duplicate/revoked/queued/reconciled state explicit; RSVP never attendance | OLA-09 |
| UX-AC-13 | Keyboard-only core workflows, focus/error/contrast/labels and map/editor nondrag alternatives; manual assistive tech evidence | OLA-14 |
| UX-AC-14 | 360/768/1280/1920 viewport and 200% zoom representative journeys usable, no inaccessible essential actions | OLA-14 |
| UX-AC-15 | Expired/revoked access clears data and actions; safe error/support receipt, no secrets in browser storage/logs | OLA-06/11/14 |
| UX-AC-16 | Incremental migration preserves existing accepted public links/feature routes and user grants; exact-head regression tests pass | OLA-14/15 |

## 17. Open design decisions and integration

Proposed shell patterns and route names are not binding visual mockups. Validate user research, branding assets, mobile browser/scanner support, library license/accessibility, route compatibility, actual role presets and operational needs. No real GHB assets, venue geometry or data inferred. Navigation profiles are defaults not paywalls. Acceptance thresholds are proposed and must be measured, not claims. Integrate with OAC and OLA after approval via additive design index, architecture, operating model, roadmap, gap analysis and appropriate issue references; preserve Blueprint v1.2 historical snapshot and accepted ADRs. No repository modifications, runtime tests or feature implementation during preparation.

## Approved AGIS specialized station UX — 2026-11-27

[AGIS v1.0](ADMISSION_GUEST_INFORMATION_AND_STATION_MANAGEMENT_DESIGN_v1.0.md) refines UX-02/04/05/07/09/10/11/12/13. OAC exposes scoped station/profile/device administration; EOC exposes event station status/assignment and permitted interventions. The active station has one mode/context: large rapid gate scanner with explicit result and accessible manual path; self-service Info Pult with verified minimal personal view, approved map/text directions, no attendance mutation, privacy timeout and neutral reset; staffed help/seating with permitted lookup and separate reviewed corrections; printing with explicit document/reissue confirmation; passive public display with no personal lookup/action. Mode switching clears old context and data; do not use hidden UI controls as authorization. Distinguish pending, locally provisional, server-confirmed, stale, revoked and disconnected states without relying only on color; preserve bs-BA/en, accessible touch/keyboard and no browser history/cache leakage. Station Designer is constrained, revisioned and shares TDS brand/assets, not an unrestricted script/editor. Original UX-AC-01–16 remain required. This is an approved scope clarification, not a runtime implementation claim or instruction to interrupt the existing #104/#112 → #105–107 sequence. Preserve accepted ADRs, historical Blueprint v1.2, existing domain commands and issue criteria; final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

## Approved CID communication experience — 2026-11-27

[CID v1.0](COMMUNICATION_INVITATION_DISTRIBUTION_AND_MULTI_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESIGN_v1.0.md) refines permission-filtered OAC provider/sender/policy/campaign/schedule/history/budget navigation and domain-scoped EOC communication actions, plus assigned staff/vendor distribution tasks. Campaign Designer guides fixed audience, typed TDS content and locale, route strategy, consent/eligibility exclusions, costs and explicit review; changes invalidate approval, no silent reroute or recipient addition. Distinguish queued, accepted, verified delivered/read, failed, uncertain, suppressed, printed and operator-recorded handover; never infer RSVP, task acknowledgement or attendance from delivery. Accessible localized manual sharing/print/telephone alternatives, explicit test-send, redacted diagnostics and expiry/context clearing; no unrestricted inbox, guest directory, secrets, provider payloads or bearer links in ordinary history. This is an approved scope clarification, not a runtime or acceptance claim. Preserve all existing requirements, accepted ADRs, historical Blueprint v1.2, current #104/#112 → #105–107 sequence and established #110/#111/#108 roadmap; no immediate implementation or environment republication. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

## Approved adaptive experience and coordinated navigation — 2026-11-27

[AES v1.0](ADAPTIVE_EXPERIENCE_AND_SETUP_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [EPW v1.0](EVENT_PLANNING_PRODUCTION_AND_OPERATIONAL_WORKFLOWS_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [FRS v1.0](FORMS_REGISTRATION_AND_SUBMISSION_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [HPG v1.0](HOSPITALITY_PROTOCOL_AND_GUEST_SERVICES_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [RAI v1.0](REPORTING_ANALYTICS_AND_INTELLIGENCE_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) extend UX-01–13. AES owns presentation mode, resumable setup, safe defaults, dependency and readiness explanations, contextual quick actions and progressive disclosure; mode is independent of capability activation and effective permission. EPW checklist/timeline, FRS preset/visual form and submission inbox, HPG headcount/request/service and RAI standard/custom reports use shared accessible component and navigation contracts. Do not hide mandatory review or active blockers in simple mode. All consequential actions require owning domain checks; every mode supports locale, keyboard, error recovery, revision conflicts and safe context switches. Approved additive scope only; retain existing requirements, accepted ADRs, Blueprint v1.2, PROJECT_STATE and the #104/#112 → #105–107 → #110/#111/#108 development sequence. No immediate implementation, unrelated closure gates, environment republication or Blueprint v1.3 consolidation. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

# Eventor Organization Lifecycle Acceptance Scenarios
## End-to-end verification and release gates v1.0

**Status:** Proposed for product-owner review. All scenarios are **not run**; this document defines future evidence, not test results.  
**Date:** 2026-11-27. **Inspected main:** `0c5e7a2ddf0a676a89bb75faef1265438dc2ae45`.  
**Proposed destination:** `docs/implementation-design/v0.3/ORGANIZATION_LIFECYCLE_ACCEPTANCE_SCENARIOS_v1.0.md`.  
**Companions:** [OAC technical specification](ORGANIZATION_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md) and [UX and Navigation](EVENTOR_USER_EXPERIENCE_AND_NAVIGATION_v1.0.md). Read with [PAC](PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [TDS](TEMPLATE_DESIGN_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [Blueprint v1.2](../../blueprint/v1.2/Event_Operations_Platform_Technical_Blueprint_v1.2.md), [Roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md), [Operating Model](../../OPERATING_MODEL.md), [roles/permissions](../../product/USER_ROLES_AND_PERMISSIONS_v0.1.md), and existing issue acceptance requirements. This suite adds cross-module customer journeys; it never waives domain-specific tests or implies implementation completion.

## 1. Release objective and verification policy

A newly provisioned organization must become independently operational through supported application interfaces and secure enrollment. It must manage its own facilities, bookings, people, events, communications and permitted data without routine platform-owner intervention or manual SQL. A booking-only organization must not need guest records or operational events. An organizer must be able to use an explicitly authorized partner venue without accessing source records or requiring ownership of a venue. A hybrid organization may do both. Event-day staff, guests, customers and vendors must see only their intended scoped experience. Platform recovery remains a protected host task; the no-manual-SQL criterion applies to ordinary business/onboarding operations, not automated installer migrations, synthetic fixture setup or documented emergency recovery.

The final release requires evidence for all applicable blueprint, issue, PAC, TDS, OAC, UX and OLA gates. Every test records actual expected vs observed outcomes. Passing CI verifies that commit's covered behavior, not production readiness. Skipped external probes, mocked HTTP, schema presence, screenshots and editor concepts are not substitutes for real integrated behavior. Required but unsupported behavior is a release gap, not a pass. Approved non-applicability applies only to a specifically disabled optional module in a specific scenario; the overall release must still test the module in an appropriate scenario. Tests execute against disposable synthetic data; never use production guest records, real credentials, sensitive venue plans or real recipients. Do not execute actual production restore, destructive actions, bulk campaigns or external authority operations.

### 1.1 Evidence levels and schedule

| Level | Evidence | When |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | Unit/schema/contract checks; static design/validation | Each scheduled vertical slice |
| L2 | Real PostgreSQL runtime-role, RLS, API, worker, concurrency and migration tests | Each owning feature PR, exact head and post-merge |
| L3 | Browser/API/DB integrated scenarios; Chromium/Firefox, local SMTP capture, synthetic fixtures, actual editor/renderer/scanner test adapter | As owning feature becomes usable; no final VM needed |
| L4 | Cross-module journey, accessibility manual review, fault injection/load and isolated restore rehearsals | Once dependencies available; CI/local disposable environment |
| L5 | Final native Linux and Docker Compose clean install/upgrade/recovery and actual host/device/public HTTPS/SMTP evidence | Phase 9 only, after coherent release and both installers |

Use existing acceptance scripts/runbooks and suites where possible. Do not create competing fixtures/suites or recode already-passing tests. Tests that require missing features remain blocked in planning, not silently omitted. Exact acceptance commands, API operation IDs, schema names and role codes reconciled at implementation; steps below specify behavior, not invented existing endpoints.

## 2. Synthetic reference installation and fixture contract

| Fixture | Role and data |
|---|---|
| P | Platform Owner, explicit protected bootstrap; separate limited Superadmin and platform auditor for delegation tests |
| A (GHB-reference) | Hybrid organization; synthetic name/brand only, bs-BA, Europe/Sarajevo; administrator A-admin, booking manager, finance approver, venue coordinator, event manager, Registry manager, communications designer/operator, seating manager, gate operators A-g1/A-g2 and auditor |
| B (independent organizer) | en, synthetic distinct identity/brand; B-admin, event manager, Registry manager and task collaborator; no owned venue required |
| C (provider-only) | Synthetic separate organization, booking/resources only; C-admin/booking operator; all guest/event capabilities disabled by default |
| M | Existing named user with independent memberships in A and B, different role in each |
| N | Active member with no business grants |
| X | Unauthorized user or unrelated organization/account for negative tests |
| V | External vendor/task-scoped collaborator, no implicit membership |
| K | External booking requester/contact, no staff account |
| R1/R2 | Synthetic guest profiles with accented Bosnian names; R1 participates in two events; one restricted field/contact explicitly protected |
| Venue VA | Synthetic GHB-like facility with hall and prayer-row/count-zone template; dimensions/capacity fictional and validated within fixture |
| Venue VC | Provider C facility and resource; booking-only test |
| Events EA1/EA2, EB | Own A events, B independent event; distinct schedules/sessions, capacities, brand/policy snapshots |
| SMTP | Local capture service; isolated external sandbox in final phase only; never real guest addresses |

Use reserved domains such as `example.invalid` for fake addresses and configured local capture aliases. Define timestamps using a fixed fixture clock and IANA timezone, one DST edge case. IDs stable per isolated run, reset between scenario groups or declare dependencies; no real names/identifiers required. Assign actual supported role codes via reviewed setup, not assumed job title authority. Separate identities for approval/denial tests; single-owner technical recovery tested separately per PAC. Record explicit test policies: capacity, pricing/currency/tax, cancellation policy, approval thresholds, allowed modules, retention/hold, publication locale rules, MFA/recovery and permitted support scope. Fixture values synthetic, not GHB operational claims. Test both allowed and denied conditions with real runtime-role access; direct privileged fixture setup only in disposable environments and not part of normal user acceptance path.

## 3. Required run record

For each scenario and subassertion record: ID, owning requirement/issue, status (`not_run`, `blocked`, `pass`, `fail`, `not_applicable`), exact release/commit and deployment mode, build/migration checksums, browser/device/version, scenario fixture version, actor/scope, steps executed, expected and observed outcomes, safe timestamps/correlation IDs, evidence file/CI URL, deviations and reviewer. No secrets in screenshots/logs/receipts. Record setup prerequisites, actual assertions (DB state/count, response status, rendered output digest, queue state, audit actor, denial and no mutation), cleanup and any irreversible synthetic action. For negative tests prove prohibited result absent, not merely button hidden. For asynchronous actions prove final receipt or explicitly uncertain state; do not count 202 or provider connection success as delivered. Required test fail/blocked/not_run prevents full release sign-off. Document remediation under owning issue; avoid duplicate tracking issues. Do not mark this spec itself as implementation evidence.

### Example evidence record (blank template, not a result)

```yaml
scenario: OLA-07
assertion: booking-confirmation-conflict
status: not_run
commit: null
deployment: null
fixture_version: null
actor_scope: null
expected: exactly_one_confirmation_for_conflicting_resource
observed: null
correlation_ids: []
evidence: []
reviewer: null
notes: null
```

## 4. End-to-end scenarios

### OLA-01 — Installation owner provisions organization

**Tracks:** #104/#108; PAC-M1/M2; OAC-01/07, OAC-AC-01. **Level:** L2/L3 now when implemented, L5 final.

**Prerequisites:** installation bootstrap, management auth/roles, PAC provisioning service; synthetic blank tenant set. **Actors:** host custodian, P, ordinary tenant user X.

1. Using supported host bootstrap, establish explicit owner identity and required MFA/recovery; sign in to PAC. Attempt same privilege with ordinary account/first registration and verify denial.
2. In PAC wizard create A (hybrid), B (organizer) and C (provider), set locale/timezone, permitted capabilities and initial named administrator. Preview and explicitly approve each. Retry same idempotency request, attempt duplicate slug and invalid profile.
3. Record created tenant IDs and invitation/assignment receipts; simulate failed invitation delivery and retry/reissue without duplicate organization or identity. Existing user enrollment must not overwrite credential or imply verification.
4. Attempt tenant-admin access to PAC/global directory/host operations and global flag changes; verify safe denial at API/DB, not just missing menu.

**Pass:** exactly one organization per successful request; stable IDs; no partial authorized business records after failed transaction; authorized initial-admin onboarding path; no manual SQL for ordinary provisioning; global platform status/brand and other tenants not mutated. Host bootstrap and recovery protected; audit actual host/operator identity. **Evidence:** sanitized PAC wizard/receipts, DB count and RLS role checks, exact denial/no-mutation assertions, audit receipt.

### OLA-02 — Secure administrator enrollment and first sign-in

**Tracks:** #104/#108; PAC identity; OAC-AC-02/03; UX-AC-01. **Level:** L2/L3/L5.

1. Receive A-admin invitation through local capture or approved secure local onboarding; verify recipient identity, establish credentials/MFA under policy, accept membership and initial roles. No password sent or displayed in plaintext. Repeat with existing M identity for an additional tenant; require verified existing sign-in, no credential reset.
2. Redeem token twice concurrently; attempt expired, revoked, wrong purpose and wrong-account acceptance. Try invalid credentials for known and unknown email. Verify workspace names not disclosed until password verified.
3. Sign in with single membership (direct tenant), M (explicit authorized selection), N (member without grants) and active identity without memberships (safe support guidance). Test sign-out/expiry and approved recovery with no external SMTP.
4. Inspect browser storage, URL/referrer and logs for credential/token/other memberships; none present in prohibited locations. Verify actual actor and tenant session, no hidden access from membership alone.

**Pass:** one active intended membership/receipt on valid redemption; replay/wrong recipient denied; no new global account for existing identity; no premature verification assertion; ordinary member has only allowed workspaces; credential-first behavior and MFA policy observed. **Evidence:** auth API/DB and concurrent redemption results, captured synthetic mail metadata (redacted links), browser screenshots and audit/session records. ADR 0015/0017/0020 remain authoritative until reviewed successor.

### OLA-03 — First-login guided configuration and module readiness

**Tracks:** #104/#105/#111; OAC-02/04/06, OAC-AC-04/05/07/09; UX-AC-03/10. **Level:** L3/L4.

1. A-admin first login opens OAC setup. Set profile metadata and authorized defaults, choose modules, optionally inherit platform brand; save partial setup, sign out, resume another browser/device. Configure facilities, commercial policies, communications and people through owning features; return to wizard and observe recomputed readiness.
2. Change profile/timezone using valid revision; concurrently edit same profile from second session; stale write rejected. Verify already configured settings and historical facts not overwritten by wizard.
3. C-admin skips all organizer-only steps. Configure venue/booking form/catalogue/availability and required policy; SMTP unavailable but supported manual booking path remains. Publish only after review; invalid dependency/unsupported module rejected. B-admin with no owned venue can use approved partner projection when available.
4. Test non-admin landing and direct deep link to allowed existing work during incomplete setup. Toggle optional module with existing obligations; preview impact; deny unsafe disable or perform approved drain, verify history remains. Readiness cannot be forced by client state or used as permission.

**Pass:** actual saved state resumes and reflects owning facts; no global all-optional-modules gate; provider usable without event/guest, unauthorized setup denied; active reservations/issued artifacts unchanged; explicit publication/activation, no live email/credentials by wizard. **Evidence:** readiness snapshots/revisions, UI flows, API negative test, DB history and module dependency tests.

### OLA-04 — Organization home, daily navigation and scoped overview

**Tracks:** #104; OAC-AC-06/24; UX-AC-04/05. **Level:** L3/L4.

1. Seed known synthetic counts for inquiries, pending decisions, events and tasks. Open home as A-admin, C-admin, B event manager and finance approver; compare displayed metrics and drill-down filters against authorized fixture queries.
2. Test profile defaults and explicit enabled/disabled capability changes. A user with only an event grant lands on authorized event, not general Registry. User N cannot access business modules by direct route/API.
3. Simulate optional data service failure and stale observation. Check unknown/stale/empty/denied distinction, timestamp/timezone and independent widgets. Search allowed and forbidden terms; attempt favorites/notifications from prior context.

**Pass:** counts equal authorized dataset and definitions, no mixed-currency totals/forbidden cohort inference; route/action hints match current grants; only correct profile/task groups shown; no PAC visibility for tenant. Optional failure does not destroy unrelated work. **Evidence:** expected/actual count fixtures, browser routes, API projection tests and stale-state checks.

### OLA-05 — Independent branding, themes and template authoring

**Tracks:** #111; PAC-M3/TDS-M1–M4; OAC-AC-08/18; UX-AC-09/10. **Level:** L3/L4.

1. P publishes platform default brand. A-admin sets own logos, colors and bs-BA/en footer/identity; B uses distinct brand; preview inherited and allowed venue/event overrides. Draft, publish, edit and rollback as new revision; simulate invalid/missing asset and unsafe SVG/HTML/remote fetch.
2. Toggle personal theme/light/dark/high contrast and language. Verify login safe pre-tenant identity, selected shell brand, event brand, guest/public approved projection, no cross-tenant asset access or enumeration. Validate diacritics and contrast.
3. Authorized TDS designer creates localized rich-text invitation, responsive block email and A5 graphical card with typed fields; preview synthetic recipient and long name, batch PDF/print layout. Test designer without send privilege. Approved issuer sends explicit synthetic batch/test message with appropriate non-live marker for tests. Verify text/HTML multipart, rendered output and correct locale; synthetic preview has no live credential.
4. Publish new brand/template; compare exact digest/revision of previously issued artifact and new authorized output. Ensure old historical bytes preserved, no implicit resend.

**Pass:** distinct A/B brands, correct property precedence and immutable manifests; no rebuild for authorized brand revision; no unsafe asset execution/exfiltration, no extra recipient data from designer; preview/test not actual issuance; old artifact digest unchanged; accessibility and TDS acceptance criteria additionally required. **Evidence:** rendered HTML/text/PDF, manifest/hash, screenshot, SMTP capture, asset negative tests and no extra delivery/credential rows.

### OLA-06 — Tenant staff self-service, role scopes and workspace switching

**Tracks:** #104; ADR 0010/0015; OAC-AC-03/10–12/17/23/24; UX-AC-02/06/15. **Level:** L2/L3/L4.

1. A-admin invites booking, finance, guest and reception staff using graphical authorized workflow only; assign roles at organization/event/station scope within delegation ceiling. Add M existing identity, confirm no disclosure of B membership to A admin. Inspect effective permissions/source/expiry.
2. Sign in as each role. Exercise authorized action and direct API deny for unrelated guest, financial, export, role escalation, PAC and other event/tenant. Create/edit role preset beyond ceiling, grant to proxy account, try managed flag setter; all denied. Member N no business data. A event-scoped guest operator accesses EA1 roster only, not EA2 or Registry.
3. M switches A→B with active tabs, request/subscription and draft state. Verify session rotation, expiry preserved, actual actor, old data and requests cleared, stale links reauthorized. Concurrent revocation/operation records real result; cached reply rechecks authority. Test back/forward and unauthorized search/count.
4. A-admin suspends A membership of M; verify A sessions revoked, B unaffected; restore fresh login and preserved role grants. Attempt suspend last active organization admin or protected host-managed platform member; deny per ADR. Revoke role, expiry, download and stream access; current authorization prevents new actions.

**Pass:** all allowed workflows usable without platform ticket/manual SQL after handoff; no privilege escalation or cross-scope leak; last admin and managed membership protection; exact membership-scoped revocation and actual audit attribution. **Evidence:** runtime-role SQL and API negative matrix, parallel transactions, browser session traces (redacted), role/actor receipts. PAC authority changes tested separately only after reviewed successor migration.

### OLA-07 — Provider-only venue, catalogue and booking lifecycle

**Tracks:** Phase 1/#105/#112; OAC-AC-05/13–15/19; UX-AC-07/08/11. **Level:** L2/L3/L4/L5.

1. C-admin creates own facility/space, resources/services and calendar; validated capacity/availability, prices/taxes/approval/cancellation settings, localized public form. Use simple space without seating/guest setup. Configure setup/teardown buffers and out-of-service resource; preserve existing confirmed reservation on later catalogue change.
2. K submits public inquiry without account; submit invalid and repeat inputs, verify validation and scoped receipt, no booking confirmation/event. C booking manager reviews, drafts, alternatives, prices and offer; finance approval when policy requires; K accepts via scoped link. Attempt unsupported discount or self-approval, wrong-purpose or expired capability.
3. Authorized confirmer confirms; race competing reservation for same resource/time and verify exactly one eligible conflicting commit (or correct count-capacity invariant). Inspect pinned commercial/policy snapshot, calendar and fulfilment tasks. Change price/tax/form revision; previous records retain source facts.
4. Attempt guest Registry, invitation and event endpoints for provider-only without grants/modules; deny. Verify booking completed with zero operational event and guest/admission rows created by booking. Inspect customer projection omits internal notes and unrelated data.

**Pass:** complete provider journey from own configuration through confirmed booking using normal UI/API; atomic resource enforcement, approval and snapshot correctness, no event/guest dependency. **Evidence:** form/offer/approval/reservation IDs, DB counts/constraints, UI receipts, concurrency and negative tests. Existing Phase 1 acceptance and #105 scope remain intact.

### OLA-08 — Amend, cancel or disrupt without conflating business facts

**Tracks:** #112; OAC-AC-15; UX-AC-08. **Level:** L2/L3/L4.

1. Confirm synthetic booking with pinned cancellation policy; customer submits authorized request. Review and approve/reject or return; show consequences and allowed authority. Attempt unapproved execution or wrong actor. Execute approved cancellation once; retry idempotently and inspect release and follow-ups.
2. Test separate amendment/postponement path when supported; revalidate changed resource availability, preserve old offer and decision history; no implied money movement. Provider records disruption with approved public summary; notice alone does not cancel booking/event or automatically send.
3. Explicitly publish scoped notice to linked organizer; organizer acknowledges receipt, then separately reviews appropriate event decision. Verify no automatic event cancellation, guest notification or settlement completion. Deny access to private operational notes. Cross-party delivery/resolution must be genuinely implemented for full scenario; do not count existing record-only slice as done.

**Pass:** request/decision/effective cancellation/reservation release/notice/acknowledgement/resolution distinguishable; no bypass of commercial policy, old snapshots preserved, no unauthorized send or refund claim. **Evidence:** domain states before/after, append-only effects/audit, approved receipt, concurrency/retry tests and minimal projection. All original #112 criteria required.

### OLA-09 — Hybrid organization's own event through event-day operation

**Tracks:** #104/#105/#106/#107/#110/#111; OAC-AC-13/16–19/21; UX-AC-07/08/11/12. **Level:** L3/L4/L5.

1. A-admin or assigned staff configure synthetic hall and prayer-row/count zone, import reference plan and calibrate/draw/label with keyboard alternatives. Review/publish immutable venue revision. Create EA1/EA2 with sessions, timezone, optional modules/responsibilities; duplicate as new draft without credentials/approved facts. Use own venue or explicit booking association, not implicit conversion.
2. Registry manager imports synthetic CSV/XLSX with duplicates/invalid rows, maps headers, reviews matches, commits and tests supervised correction. R1 linked to EA1 and EA2 as one identity with distinct participation. Restricted note/contact only authorized role. Revoke event-only user Registry attempt; preserve historical names/references.
3. Publish authorized registration/invitation template and RSVP policy. Preview synthetic; explicit approved issue/send to test fixture; guest responds via purpose-bound link; staff records correction with audit; policy changes don't rewrite issued snapshot. Assert zero attendance from RSVP.
4. Assign guests manually with hard capacity/exclusions, lock assignments; generate CP-SAT advisory proposal, inspect conflicts/diff, reject infeasible and stale proposal; authorized explicit commit and publication. Guest Portal sees own allocation/map safe projection only, no source geometry/private annotations. Print personalized card/pass through TDS; validate QR and actual dimensions.
5. Issue separate admission credential; scan at two stations concurrently, duplicate/revoked/expired rejected; use manual lookup on camera denial, test bounded offline queue/reconnect/conflict and authorized attendance correction. Assert exactly one attendance subject fact unless explicit audited correction.
6. Event manager enters EOC from portfolio; verify current counts, map revision, tasks/alerts and stale/reconnect. Assign V vendor task, evidence and deadline; V cannot read other tasks/guests. External prerequisite/CDI coordinator records requirement/request/status/authorized completion only, no inspection or confidential data shown publicly. Display sanitized agenda/directions. Close/archive event through lifecycle and report authorized outcomes.

**Pass:** all transitions via owning commands and authorized UI, immutable published venue/plan/template/policy history, advisory solver only, separate credentials/attendance, least-privilege vendor and guest projections, live state truthful. No reliance on platform owner for routine tasks. **Evidence:** exact revision IDs and hashes, DB/API/browser/concurrent scan and worker receipts, PDF/QR decode, actual role negative matrix and cockpit count comparison. All #105–107/#110/TDS specific tests still required; each unsupported subflow blocks full integrated pass.

### OLA-10 — Cross-organization booking and organizer collaboration

**Tracks:** #104/#112/#110; ADR 0004/0006/0021–0024; OAC-AC-05/07/16/20/21; UX-AC-11. **Level:** L2/L3/L4.

1. A as venue provider confirms booking for B organizer. B creates EB; no B guest names in A booking. B requires no owned venue. A proposes exact allowed booking-link grant with empty projection where applicable; B reviews captured names, scope/actions/validity and fingerprint, accepts. Attempt accept by wrong party, stale digest and unauthorized action. No source data permission or global directory from grant.
2. B links eligible booking to EB under authorized event management and accepted scope; inspect permitted venue snapshot only. Verify A cannot view EB roster/RSVP/seat allocation/contact/notes and B cannot read A internal prices/booking data except explicit projection. A/B retain independent membership roles; no implicit cross-tenant context switch. Rename A after proposal: captured name unchanged.
3. Delegate bounded venue/setup task to A operator or V with explicit approval. Provider receives only assigned data. Record notice, explicit cross-party delivery, receipt acknowledgement and separate event resolution; deny unauthorized operations.
4. Revoke/expire grant with concurrent accept/link and retry; new access denied, past link/projection/history provenance retained as policy allows, no cancellation or data overwrite. End association separately under owning command. Try stale cached response.

**Pass:** reviewed exact scope, immutable captured names, separate party ownership, no broad guest/commercial data access; revocation/expiry enforced including retries and jobs; no automatic membership, cancellation, notice send or resolution. **Evidence:** actual grant digest/actor/time/scope, API/DB negative assertions, concurrency cases, browser partner review and association receipts. ADR 0023/0024 programmatic compatibility not silently changed.

### OLA-11 — Authorized support, security, reporting and audit

**Tracks:** PAC-M1/M4, #104/#111; OAC-AC-12/22–25; UX-AC-06/15. **Level:** L2/L3/L4.

1. A-admin requests help on exact synthetic booking/event problem; P inspect safe metadata only. Attempt restricted Registry/contact/export with no grant; deny under approved PAC successor policy. Obtain reviewed narrow support grant with actual actor, reason, expiry and required approval/step-up; organization banner and receipts visible. Perform supported owning correction (e.g. reviewed amendment, not generic status edit).
2. Attempt role self-escalation, unrelated event/other tenant, arbitrary SQL, bypass immutable snapshot, direct host operation or audit edit; deny. Expire/revoke scope while active request, stream, queued export and private download; reauthorize all future access. No invisible impersonation. Test single-owner technical recovery separately with local confirmation; no universal confidential-data self-approval.
3. Authorized A auditor/report operator creates scoped report/export, verify defined counts/columns, safe CSV formula handling, PDF pinned revision and manifest. Deny unauthorized field and download after revoke/expiry. Inject required audit failure and verify privileged mutation rollback. Inspect actual actor vs target and redacted logs.

**Pass:** exact authority and real attribution, no automatic sensitive content or escalation after successor reconciliation; immutable audit/history, safe private exports and fail-closed checks. If reviewed PAC successor not implemented, mark this scenario blocked, not a claim of existing leakage. **Evidence:** PAC and domain audit receipts, negative API/runtime-role tests, revoke race and artifact manifest. PAC-AC-03–07,31–35 remain mandatory.

### OLA-12 — Organization suspension, module drain and restoration

**Tracks:** PAC lifecycle/#104/#108; OAC-AC-09/26; UX-AC-08. **Level:** L2/L3/L4.

1. A requests temporary closure or PAC initiates suspension with known active bookings/events, public forms, partner grants, sessions, queued jobs. Preview exact impact and required approvals. Attempt unsafe suspension or module disable without approved drain; deny or require explicit approved safe policy.
2. Execute approved transition. Check new access/writes and eligible jobs stopped under policy, customer status only if expressly permitted, other tenant sessions of M unaffected by tenant-specific suspension. Verify no implicit booking cancellation, guest deletion, data purge, auto refund or email. Verify historical receipts retained and legal holds intact.
3. Restore via authorized lifecycle/PAC host recovery if necessary; review current memberships, readiness, policies and dependencies. Require explicit reactivation of services/public forms if appropriate, do not restore revoked grants/tokens or resend old deliveries.

**Pass:** reviewed lifecycle effects accurately enforced; no history loss, unrelated organization access intact; restoration validates current authority and explicit activation. **Evidence:** state/queue/session before/after, API denial tests, audit, retained hashes and recovery receipts.

### OLA-13 — Tenant portability, retention and offboarding

**Tracks:** OAC-18/22, PAC governance/#111/#108; OAC-AC-22/27; UX-AC-07. **Level:** L3/L4/L5.

1. Authorized A admin requests machine-readable scoped organization export before planned offboarding. Specify categories, filters and fields, review scope/approval, create bounded job; verify manifest schema/version/relationships/assets/omissions and exact counts vs allowed source. Download via current authorization; test forbidden cross-tenant fields, platform keys, raw capability tokens, other memberships and confidential audit access denied.
2. Submit synthetic privacy correction/anonymization/purge request under approved retention policy. Apply hold concurrently; purge blocked under lock. Review permitted redaction preserving required historical references; execute only approved scoped operation with per-item receipt and no unrelated cascade. No promised removal from all backups.
3. Offboarding request → PAC impact/review/drain/archive with explicit retention, revoke own tenant access and partner grants; retain global identity for B membership. Verify approved export handoff and time-bounded artifact expiry. Restore/reopen only if supported reviewed policy; no automatic reactivation.

**Pass:** export complete within declared scope, omitted items explicit, digest verified, no global/other tenant secrets; retention/holds and independent account preserved; no destructive unreviewed closure. **Evidence:** export manifest and parsed record comparisons, hold/purge concurrency, audit, access expiry. Portability is not physical backup.

### OLA-14 — Integrated reliability, accessibility and security regression

**Tracks:** all; OAC-AC-23/24/28; UX-AC-05/10/13–16; PAC/TDS nonfunctional. **Level:** L2/L3/L4, L5 device evidence.

1. Run fresh and populated upgrade migrations, exact-head OpenAPI/shared types/build/runtime-role/RLS/concurrency/security and secret scan; verify existing ordinary roles/IDs/issued public links/queued jobs/history retained and reviewed PAC permission changes affect only managed lineage. Re-run existing #104–112 tests.
2. Execute representative core workflows using keyboard-only and assistive technology, focus order/error/contrast/labels, drag alternative in TDS/venue/allocation; 360/768/1280/1920 viewport and 200% zoom in Chromium/Firefox, supported mobile/device at final acceptance. bs-BA/en diacritics, date/time/currency and DST; missing required authored translation visible and blocked/approved alternate, no clipping of critical controls.
3. Fault inject optional render/solver/SMTP/storage/realtime failure and interrupted worker/reconnect. Unrelated booking/manual guest work remains available where supported; stale dashboard not zero, retry/reconcile safe, no duplicate external side effect. Test timeout and cancellation receipts, session expiry/revocation and protected artifact download.
4. Measure representative synthetic load (initial proposal 4 vCPU/8 GiB/SSD; record actual hardware/dataset/concurrency), p95 home/readiness/search/commands and queue saturation under booking/check-in; verify agreed budgets and bounded resources, not invented SLO. Run threat model negative matrix (XSS/SSRF/CSRF/role/context/existence leak/credential/unsafe upload). Audit logs contain no credentials or protected values.

**Pass:** required regression suite passes exact tested commit; measured agreed performance and manual accessibility evidence with limitations; no cross-tenant leakage, stale privilege or unsafe retry; explicit partial degradation and recovery. No required missing test labelled pass. **Evidence:** CI runs, actual measurements, accessibility findings, browser captures, fault/concurrency/negative results and known limitations.

### OLA-15 — Final release acceptance on both installation modes

**Tracks:** #108 and Phase 9; OAC-AC-28; UX-AC-16; PAC-M5/M6. **Level:** L5 only.

**Prerequisites:** all required functional modules ready, both production installers delivered, exact release candidate and approved synthetic policies, supported host/device setup, actual test SMTP/TLS arrangements and recovery destination. Reserve the `eventor-acceptance` QEMU/KVM VM for this phase, as previously decided. No need to start it during documentation or ordinary feature development.

1. Clean native Linux install using supported installer, no manual routine DB setup, non-root identities, private PostgreSQL, secrets and TLS. Validate health, configuration, logs and bootstrap owner recovery. Record release/migration/config versions and actual host. Run OLA-01–14 applicable full journey on this mode with synthetic data, plus all original release acceptance gates.
2. Clean production Docker Compose install using same application build/schema/defaults and supported topology, persistent volumes, health/secret/backup paths; repeat journeys and compare equivalent results. No unrestricted Docker socket in API. Test idempotent installer and populated upgrade in both modes.
3. Actual intended public HTTPS/domain/proxy and external SMTP sandbox test with synthetic recipients; record real delivery/provider outcome and security headers, no live guest data. Missing domain/provider/port arrangement blocks those checks; do not invent successful evidence. Local email capture remains supported; no mandatory inbound SMTP server. Test LAN operation when public internet fails where supported.
4. Take encrypted verified backup with independent destination and matching protected keys/config/assets/release. Isolated restore with public ingress/external delivery disabled; validate data, hashes, encryption and RPO/RTO timings. Reconcile revoked memberships/sessions/holds/deleted records/queued deliveries before reopening. Simulate failed upgrade and supported rollback/forward-fix/recovery; never restore old code against incompatible schema. Maintenance/drain and explicit reopen audited. Host recovery works when web unavailable. Verify independent recovery receipt survives restore.
5. Record all required checks, approved limitations and actual evidence. Freeze release only when every mandatory gate passes; fail/blocked/not-run required gates keep release not ready. Compare native/Compose differences and resolve unsupported parity rather than silently waive. Sign-off by available responsible operator/product owner per policy; no fabricated independent reviewer.

**Pass:** clean install and upgrade/recovery both modes, ordinary organization becomes operational and completes required journeys, no security/tenant violations, measured restore/operational targets met and actual external evidence. **Evidence:** installer transcripts redacted, version/checksum manifest, per-mode scenario run records, actual public/SMTP tests, restore/integrity/recovery timing, final signed acceptance report. This test is future work; no VM, external service or environment change is requested now.
