Approval policy thresholds for sensitive purpose, audience size, budget, shared provider use or external notices may require distinct approver; proposer cannot self-approve where separation required. Queue/issue permission remains distinct from content authoring/approval. No preview/test/render may publish business decision or send real communication. Existing decision-bound notification campaigns retain their owner and scope; add common orchestration through domain-specific adapters, not weaken required event_decision FK.

Example synthetic campaign: 350 eligible event subjects; preview computes 180 email, 65 SMS, 45 Viber, 10 WhatsApp and 40 handover, 10 excluded (no eligible contact/permission). Counts and reasons are fictional; per-recipient route review required. Four guests may share one email address; personalized copies require explicit representative review, no blind collapse or disclosure. After review, one Viber consent withdrawn and one event participation cancelled: suppress those two before submission; do not move them automatically to another channel unless a separately eligible preapproved route and purpose policy allow. A new guest added after approval is not included; create additional reviewed campaign/intent. A schedule change invalidating pinned content stops unsent affected jobs and asks owner to review replacement notice. An RSVP response may stop reminders but does not delete original invitation or delivered message.

## 17. CID-15 — Scheduling, reminders, triggers and campaign lifecycle

Schedules: immediate explicit confirmation; one-off future send; versioned relative trigger (e.g. days before event/offer expiry/RSVP deadline); bounded recurring reminder rules for unanswered guests; business-event-triggered notices from existing committed outbox events. Use server absolute UTC `timestamptz`, store original intended local wall time, IANA timezone, DST ambiguity resolution and policy version. Explicitly reject nonexistent local time or ask for reviewed adjustment; choose offset for ambiguous time. Guest quiet hours evaluated from verified recipient timezone where available, fallback to approved event/org policy shown in review; no inferred timezone from IP. Required urgent notices may bypass quiet hours only if explicit policy, lawful/provider constraints and authorized reason/approval permit, not generic bypass. Set delivery expiry and maximum deferral; if quiet hours cross RSVP or offer deadline, block/route to operator rather than send stale/expired link. Schedule update recomputes relative rules with review/version; no silent audience expansion or duplicate reminder. End-of-event/booking withdrawal/module disable/suspension cancels or drains unsent items under owning lifecycle. Separate operational obligations from messages; if decision notice remains legally required, show unresolved obligation with permitted channel rather than silently discard.

Campaign states proposed: draft → preview_ready → reviewed/awaiting_approval → approved → scheduled or queued → running → completed/partial/failed/cancelled_remaining. Approval and schedule validity separate; pause stops new claims, in-flight cannot guarantee recall; resume revalidates scope/revisions/capability/estimate. Confirm/cancel/schedule/resume use expected revision and idempotency. Campaign terminal projection counts accepted, delivered, bounced, failed, uncertain, suppressed, expired, manual pending/complete separately; completed means work reached defined terminal outcomes, not all recipients reached/read. Cancellation of remaining after partial send shows already attempted/accepted/uncertain and unresolved obligations. Existing pre-send cancellation semantics preserved; new pause/cancel-remaining added only reviewed successor, no rewriting legacy `cancelled` meaning. No automatic delete of successful jobs. For scheduled jobs, distinguish policy authorization at approval from current actor/member/service authority at submission. Automated trigger authority must be explicitly granted purpose-bound system actor and rule revision approved; revoked creator role alone must not silently transfer their authority to a worker. Define scheduled authority policy with actual approver/owner, expiry, revocation and audit; require reapproval if necessary. Recheck at trigger, claim and final handoff. No background task can send as inactive/stale operator through cached authorization.

Reminders: query current authoritative unanswered status, deadline, prior communication history, max count/cooldown and consent. Fixed reviewed eligible cohort, shrink on response/revocation, no broaden on retry. One reminder occurrence ID per subject/purpose/rule version/window, stable idempotency independent of restart. Relative schedule uses current committed domain revision and explicit decision if change invalidates existing approved rule. No repeated reminders after accepted/declined response unless different approved reconfirmation purpose. Record system trigger causation and original reviewer. Critical disruption notice uses provider-owned approved audience and content; organizer chooses its own guest notification; cross-org receipt/acknowledgement separate. Do not automatically cancel/postpone event or transfer commercial responsibilities on message send/failure. Cross-party explicit notice workflow must remain available through #112 even before new provider adapters.

## 18. CID-16 — Routing, fallback, retry policy and failure semantics

Define channel choice algorithm as auditable deterministic plan, not provider SDK magic. Review each subject/purpose in tenant context: verify active domain state and audience; enumerate allowed channel/contact/provider routes, test eligibility, consent, current config/capability, sender, language, deadline, costs and quiet hours; rank preference and explicit event policy; snapshot choices and blocked reasons; reserve approved upper bound; issue/queue only on explicit authority. Support single selected channel, first eligible preferred route, ordered fallback chain, explicitly approved simultaneous multi-channel, individually reviewed manual assignment. Route is a specific channel + verified destination version + provider/account/config/sender + content revision + policy. Alternative provider for same channel is still a new route requiring explicit approval in plan; cannot circumvent suppression/region/template requirement. Do not silently switch sender/account or convert template. If no eligible route, create authorized follow-up obligation (not fake send). Manual or print/phone may be primary route, not just fallback.

| Observed condition | Automatic behavior (if reviewed policy allows) |
|---|---|
| Before submission, definite transient connection failure | Retry same immutable route with bounded backoff; only if evidence proves no external side effect. |
| Definite provider rejection without acceptance, retryable | Honor Retry-After/rate policy and expiry; retry same route or permitted alternative per reviewed plan. |
| Confirmed terminal non-delivery (e.g. verified bounce) | Suppress invalid contact as appropriate; consider preapproved alternate contact/channel only after rechecking policy/consent, cost and purpose. |
| Provider accepted, delivery unknown or read unknown | No automatic fallback merely due to absence of receipt/read. Reconcile or await bounded evidence; separately approved escalation can deliberately risk another communication and must disclose. |
| Timeout after submit, crash, partial response, unknown external effect | Mark uncertain; stable correlation, callback/poll/manual review. Do not blind retry or fallback. Exact provider-guaranteed idempotent replay only with same immutable request, valid key window and policy; otherwise explicit risk review. |
| Opt-out/suppression, revoked actor/credential/tenant grant | Block protected send; no alternate route to circumvent restriction. Another independently permissible contact route may be selected only under reviewed lawful purpose, not to evade channel/global opt-out. |
| Expired/stale domain revision, link revoked, provider template rejected | Block; require domain correction/new review, never mutate invitation via adapter. |
| Quota/budget exhausted or price changed | Stop new claims/reservations; review cost/replan. No unapproved charge. |
| Operator cancels before handoff | Record cancelled/suppressed remaining; release unused reservation; in-flight may still deliver. |

Retries: bounded attempt count (existing queues max five preserved until reviewed successor), exponential backoff + jitter with provider-specific retry-after and global/tenant limiter, not fixed aggressive polling. Dead-letter/manual review after expiry or exhaustion, do not infinite requeue. Classify permanent/transient/uncertain with adapter evidence and safe code. Store prior attempts immutable; a retry is new attempt of same approved intent, stable logical intent and provider idempotency scope as appropriate. A new manual resend requires reviewed reason, current authority, fresh cost reservation and separate logical intent to avoid confusion; may reuse valid domain capability, never revoke/replace implicitly. Fallback decision itself durable, idempotent (one active next route per intent), audited, parent attempt/evidence and rule revision, with compare-and-swap against late callback and cancellation. If verified late success appears after alternate route issued, preserve both facts, stop remaining chain, notify operator of potential duplicate; do not erase history. For multi-channel intentional delivery, counts reflect subjects vs sends and cost; require explicit approval. Keep operational exception queue scoped and redacted. Never use vendor fallback to bypass provider rate/abuse enforcement.

## 19. CID-17 — Cost, quotas and usage governance

Support free/local/manual and paid channels without embedding current provider prices in code or architecture. Rate-card revision per provider/account/sender/country/channel/category/segment/media unit, effective date, currency (ISO code), tax inclusion, quote source and validity; use decimal/integer minor units with explicit rounding, no floating point money. Costs may be per message, SMS segment, conversation/template category, media, monthly plan, usage tier or carrier surcharge; actual provider pricing evaluated at adapter review. Show estimate and max approved bound separately from actual reconciled charge, plus unknown charges. Physical print/postal cost manual estimate/actual separate; no automated payment or billing. Provider subscription or fixed fee allocation optional separate policy; do not pretend per-message estimate covers all charges. FX conversion only using pinned approved rate/revision/time with currency-specific budgets; no silent currency conversion. No price guarantee from estimate. Cost unknown: default block paid route or require explicitly approved finite conservative maximum and provider cap. Some providers can charge for failed/undelivered submissions; do not assume refund on failure/cancel. Reconcile actual account reports using exact provider references; unresolved discrepancy remains visible.

Preflight calculates per-recipient route estimates, segment length after final localized render, provider quote revision, approved fallback worst-case and any intentional multi-channel fanout, taxes/currency and quotas. Preview cost does not reserve funds; approval records max and validity. Before send, atomically reserve billable units/cost under tenant budget and optional shared service account cap using consistent lock order; check aggregate tenant and provider quota windows (hour/day/month or provider period), user/campaign/event limits and rate-limits. One reservation per logical chargeable attempt/route/idempotency scope, unique keys; no duplicate reservation on retry receipt. Unknown/uncertain attempt retains reservation until verified actual or explicit reconciled risk decision, cannot release early to overspend. Confirmed pre-submit failure releases unused reservation; accepted/charged settles actual (including fees), late charge append adjustment, history immutable. Cap reduction below outstanding reservations stops new sends, does not rewrite history; price increase beyond approved bound blocks until review; actual provider overage flagged, hard cap guarantee limited to controllable submissions, provider fees not fully under Eventor control. Admin can set hard and soft thresholds, approval levels, max daily/monthly and event budget, alert recipients; platform-managed service also tenant assignment quota and service-wide cap, fair-share/backpressure. No automatic credit purchase or invoice. Show usage by date, provider/channel/purpose/event and aggregate tenant with currency and attribution; PAC shared service aggregates only, no unauthorized contact content. Reports distinguish submitted, accepted, billable and actual cost; “0” only known zero, unavailable not zero.

## 20. CID-18 — Delivery evidence, reconciliation and history

Common projection must normalize without erasing channel-specific facts. Preserve existing statuses (e.g. `sent` = SMTP provider accepted, not delivered) and raw legacy meaning. Define append-only evidence event with typed source worker/provider/operator/system, actual actor/service, route/account scope, attempt ref, provider correlation ID, provider occurrence timestamp (if trustworthy), receive/record timestamp, safe normalized status, bounded error/receipt code, payload digest, signature verification metadata/version, optional restricted evidence reference, supersedes/corrects relation. Current status derived from valid evidence and channel capability, not from arbitrary operator edit. Do not persist full callback bodies containing addresses, content or tokens by default; quarantine encrypted limited TTL if necessary with restricted access. Human assertion never impersonates provider-verified result. Reject unknown future status safely, not success. Provider event timestamps can be delayed or out-of-order; monotonic facts (acceptance before delivery possible) with explicit contradiction handling rather than simple overwrite last callback. A later verified bounce can contradict prior delivery; preserve and flag, don't hide earlier event. Read status only when supported and actually verified, may be privacy-limited; never imply identity, legal notice receipt or RSVP.

| Common state / fact | Meaning |
|---|---|
| prepared / scheduled / queued | Local approved intent or task; not submitted. |
| claimed / submitting | Worker lease/handoff underway; not proof of acceptance. |
| accepted (legacy sent) | Provider accepted submission, not recipient delivery. |
| delivered | Verified provider/carrier/device delivery event with documented semantics; manual handover separate. |
| read / viewed | Verified channel-specific read evidence or in-app user read marker; no universal equivalence. |
| failed / bounced | Definite submission failure or confirmed delivery failure; preserve distinction and retryability. |
| suppressed / expired / cancelled_remaining | Intentionally blocked, expired or unsent cancelled item, never accepted by inference. |
| uncertain | External effect unknown, may have sent; requires reconciliation. |
| manual_prepared / dispatched / handover_claimed / contacted | Actor-recorded distribution task facts, not provider delivery. |
| reconciled | A review action with linked evidence, not itself a new delivery/read fact. |

Callback ingestion: endpoint routing ID high entropy but not authorization. Verify provider-specific signature on exact canonical raw body/request, timestamp/freshness/replay and expected account/webhook config; HTTPS, size/rate caps; validate schema allowlist and no PII logging. Account/service namespace plus exact immutable submission ref, provider message ID and tenant route; never trust tenant/contact ID from payload alone. Persist minimal verified evidence idempotently in narrow worker role transaction; unique account/endpoint/provider event ID (or documented stable digest), duplicate same payload no new fact; conflicting reused event ID quarantine. No cross-tenant routing ambiguity; provider callbacks may arrive before completion; stable reference prepared before submission allows correlation, otherwise hold bounded pending mapping without exposing data and reconcile. Callback cannot issue another send, mark RSVP, alter booking/event or grant. Return safe success/retry policy per provider without revealing subject. Separate signature/key rotation windows, old keys retained only for bounded valid in-flight events, verify replay. Polling where supported uses same evidence contract and authenticated account ref; no arbitrary callback URL or SSRF. No webhook network reachability required for local manual path; expose accepted-only limitations. Preserve Resend verified webhook functionality and stable SMTP reference semantics; do not broaden existing webhook mapping to other purposes without tests.

Operator reconciliation: show attempt history, exact reviewed route/recipient masked, timestamps, safe reason, external reference, last evidence and suggested next steps. Separate permission to reconcile, retry, change route, record manual evidence and see content. Operator records external confirmation/failure/unknown with reason and source/evidence ref; no ability to create fake provider receipt. If evidence proves no acceptance, authorize retry subject to cost/current policy. If uncertain persists, explicit review of duplicate risk and authorized new send (or no further action); original remains uncertain/resolved via actual evidence, not rewritten. Never auto-retry uncertain on lease expiry; if queue can prove no network side effect from durable pre-submit phase, safe retry only that phase. Dashboard: per purpose/event/booking/channel/provider, audience eligibility, delivered/accepted/failed/bounced/read/manual statuses, overdue follow-ups, uncertain, rate/cost quota, suppressions and callback health. No PII or tenant-specific labels in global telemetry. Drilldown to authorized source records, export masked by default, full export permission/retention and audit. Response/attendance/booking decision independent columns; no misleading universal delivered percentage.

## 21. CID-19 — Provider adapter and shared technical architecture

API-first modular monolith. Vue feature modules `features/communications` and existing domain views use shared components/composables per ADR 0008; Fastify transport-neutral orchestration and domain-specific command services; PostgreSQL forced RLS and narrow security-definer functions, restricted credential store, transactional outbox and tenant queue discovery; existing bounded worker processes plus transport adapters; isolated TDS renderer receives immutable sanitized inputs and no provider credentials or arbitrary network; callback ingestion verifies then normalizes under restricted worker identity. No new mandatory message broker, Redis, microservice, commercial control plane or background browser automation. Can scale workers independently using DB-backed lease and fair tenant claim policy. Provider integrations are reviewed installed code with versioned manifests, not user-uploadable plugin scripts. API and worker roles never have owner/superuser or cross-tenant raw credential table access. Host bootstrap/recovery protected and deployment-neutral.

Illustrative TypeScript contract (not code to merge):

```ts
interface DeliveryAdapter {
  readonly adapterId: string;
  readonly contractVersion: number;
  capabilities(profile: SafeProfile): Promise<CapabilityReport>;
  validateConfiguration(profile: SafeProfile, secret: ScopedSecretHandle): Promise<ValidationResult>;
  estimate(request: ImmutableDeliveryEnvelope): Promise<BoundedEstimate>;
  submit(request: ImmutableDeliveryEnvelope, grant: ShortLivedSubmissionGrant): Promise<SubmissionEvidence>;
  reconcile?(reference: ScopedProviderReference, grant: ShortLivedReadGrant): Promise<VerifiedEvidence[]>;
  verifyCallback?(raw: BoundedRawRequest, context: ScopedCallbackContext): Promise<VerifiedEvidence[]>;
}
```

Adapter cannot select another recipient, query Registry, issue invitation/token, change event/booking/task or call arbitrary API. Envelope includes opaque tenant/intent/attempt IDs, exact provider/account/sender/config revision, purpose, approved destination ciphertext handle resolved only at last boundary, subject/body/typed template or private artifact handle, locale, content digest, stable idempotency ref, expiry, route/cost authorization and minimal correlation. Grant binds worker lease/tenant/account/purpose/attempt/deadline; narrow secret service releases credentials only for exact approved profile and revalidated authority. Adapter return `definiteAccepted`, `definiteRejected` with retryability, `uncertain`, `preSubmissionBlocked` and normalized provider reference/evidence, not generic exception equals retry. Capability/test operation never issues real domain message; test is separately authorized synthetic intent. For providers lacking idempotency guarantee, application still deduplicates local intents and uses uncertain behavior; exactly-once external delivery is not promised. Batch submit only if per-recipient correlation, idempotency, partial outcomes and no recipient leakage are proven; otherwise one logical submission per recipient. Provider SDK retry defaults disabled/reviewed, pinned versions, sandbox no real secrets in CI. Any new adapter requires capability/limitation docs, threat model, tests, rate/cost policy, account setup/revocation, callback/polling evidence and operator recovery guide before exposure in UI.

Transactional path: owning command validates domain actor/role, selects revision and creates intent/outbox in same transaction (or records obligation for reviewed later communication). Scheduler computes due items under approved rule; worker discovers tenant IDs only through narrow queue, sets tenant context, claims ready attempt with lease/fence and reserves quota/cost atomically using consistent reviewed lock order (domain/permission/policy → campaign/intent → budget → lease as owning invariants require; audit actual lock ordering in M0). Decrypt minimal content and validate current authority, capability, suppression, expiry and current approved artifact; prepare stable external correlation and mark durable pre-handoff/submitting boundary before network. Recheck cancellation/revocation under existing send-authorization locks/fencing; don't hold broad DB transaction across unbounded network, review exact linearization point and bounded handoff; revocation before authorized handoff blocks, already-started external submission cannot be recalled. Completion validates lease fence and appends evidence/settles reservation, stale worker cannot overwrite newer outcome. Crash after boundary uncertain. A callback racing completion uses same immutable identity and append-only evidence, does not lose confirmed receipt. Transactional outbox retries never enqueue duplicate logical intent. Scope-specific realtime invalidation via authorized cursor, safe ref not content; clear on workspace switch/revocation. No delivery adapter can bypass underlying notification policy or own business transaction.

## 22. CID-20 — Logical data model and migration strategy

Logical entities below express required semantics, not DDL or mandatory separate tables. Prefer extending existing rows/sidecars, view/union projections and common service interfaces; do not flatten domain owners into generic untyped foreign keys or weaken checks. All tenant-owned entities carry organization ID with composite FK and forced RLS; exact event/booking/task/grant subject constraints; platform private global records accessible only through narrow broker projections. Actor kind member/system/provider/host with authentic attribution, no fake staff membership for worker. Immutable revisions and append-only evidence, current head pointers revision-checked, sensitive ciphertext bound to tenant/purpose/record/secret version, no raw capability or provider token in general rows.

| Logical aggregate | Fields / constraints / reuse |
|---|---|
| PurposeCatalogueRevision | stable purpose ID, owner family, allowed subject/contact/channel/template bindings, consent and approval/expiry policy, sensitivity; versioned allowlist, not arbitrary query. |
| ProviderProfile / ConfigRevision | tenant, profile ID, channel, adapter/version, account namespace, approved endpoint/sender refs, typed safe settings, credential ref/version, state, verified test evidence; extend 000033 config/head, support multi-profile without invalidating pinned legacy jobs. |
| CredentialVersion / OAuthGrant | owner scope/service assignment, kind, encrypted envelope/key version, allowed scopes/account, expiry/rotation/revocation epoch, refresh lock; private, no raw read API; reuse EDC1-compatible reviewed successor. |
| PlatformService / TenantServiceGrant | global service/account, purpose/channel caps, version/active state, explicit tenant assignment, sender policy, effective window, quota and audited revoke; global secret not tenant-visible. |
| SenderIdentity | organization/service assignment, kind/domain/number/bot, verification evidence, reply-to policy, status; account-specific unique scope, no spoof. |
| ProviderTemplateBinding | TDS template/revision/locale, adapter/account approved template ID/version/format/status, capability/purpose validation; no competing TDS template. |
| ContactChannelBinding / Verification | typed domain subject/contact/version, encrypted endpoint/chat/subscription, channel/account, verification evidence/expiry, opt-in; reuse Registry/booking/staff identities, no global contact dedup. |
| PreferenceRevision / ConsentEvidence / SuppressionEvent | subject/contact/purpose/channel policy and source/validity, affirmative evidence/withdrawal, representative and restricted evidence; append-only and current projection, no consent inference. |
| CommunicationIntent | domain owner typed reference and revision, purpose, subject, approved policy, template/brand/locale refs, explicit initiator/cause, optional campaign/occurrence, idempotency fingerprint; one logical intent, may have multiple reviewed routes. Existing invitation/offer/event command owns source. |
| CampaignRevision / Review / Approval | existing event decision campaign extension or owner-specific wrapper, audience filter/digest, fixed recipient refs/contact versions/exclusions, route/policy/schedule/cost snapshot, expected revision, expiry/actor/approval; never remove decision FK. |
| RecipientPlan / RoutePlan | intent/audience subject, immutable destination version, channel/profile/account/sender, ordered route/strategy, eligibility and quote, template artifact refs; one active fallback branch, shrink only on current checks. |
| ScheduleRule / Occurrence | purpose-bound owner/authorized system grant, relative/absolute time zone/cutoff/quiet hours, max reminders, current revision, occurrence unique subject/window; preserve event lifecycle. |
| DistributionJob / Attempt / Lease | link to existing domain delivery ID or new sidecar; route version, next time, expiry, idempotency digest, attempt count, fence, stable provider ref, pre-handoff marker, encrypted payload handle, state; narrow claims/complete. |
| DeliveryEvidence / CallbackMapping | scoped provider account/endpoint/attempt namespace, event ID/digest/status/source/times and safe refs, unique replay, append-only, quarantine for ambiguity; reuse 000037–39 and 000078 evidence. |
| ManualDistributionTask / Outcome | typed subject/domain intent, document revision, method, assignee/deadline, evidence and actual actor/timestamps, corrections; no provider receipt fabrication; AGIS/TDS job reference. |
| RateCardRevision / Budget / Reservation / UsageLedger | currency/units/quote validity, tenant/event/service limits, atomic reservation per attempt, settlement/release/adjustment immutable events and reconciliation ref; no payment execution. |
| CommunicationHistoryProjection | authorized union of domain intent/delivery/attempt/evidence/manual/response references, masked fields, counts, filters and safe state mapping; not source of truth, no global read model without RLS. |
| InAppReceipt / PushSubscription | scoped account or guest session/subject, encrypted endpoint/key, purpose/expiry/revoke, read marker separate from domain action; no kiosk subscription default. |
| ArtifactManifest / Audit | reuse TDS immutable revision and private storage digest, exact domain refs/expiry/retention; actual actor, reason, request correlation, no tokens/PII in logs. |

Migration plan M0 inspect actual table/permission/route/lease/lock order/crypto, all latest migrations (including legacy forward repairs) and current API consumers. M1 build shared adapter interface and authorized projections over three existing queues; existing schema remains source. Introduce nullable additive metadata/sidecar only where proven necessary; legacy status map `sent` accepted, `sending` active lease or uncertain per existing semantics, not delivered. Preserve historical values/IDs and known/unknown distinctions. Backfill only deterministic known facts (provider/channel/config refs present); unknown remains null, no invented delivery/consent/cost/recipient. Do not move plaintext capability or encrypted data without binding-compatible migration reviewed key rotation. M2 new multi-profile/head routing with compatibility for existing default SMTP config and API; pinned jobs stay on original exact revisions. M3 domain explicit no-email issuance and distribution task boundary with unchanged legacy issue-and-email endpoint; old email eligibility enforced on legacy endpoint, new channel-aware commands independently authorize. M4+ add reviewed new channel constraints/purpose-specific queues/sidecars; no generic recipient FK bypass. Add contract tests, populated migration rehearsal with historical active/revoked link, sending/uncertain/delivered attempts, queued pinned provider, disabled config, RLS and independent role, existing callbacks, legacy client paths; compare before/after counts, IDs, facts, digests and queue behavior. Dual-write/dual-read only with one authoritative submission owner and explicit migration cutover/drain; never parallel send during transition. Forward-only migration and supported version matrix, block incompatible downgrade, document recovery. No migration edits in this documentation turn.

## 23. CID-21 — API design and permission model

All routes below are proposed families, not existing OpenAPI operations or an implementation instruction. Existing endpoint paths, request schemas and state mappings remain compatible; audit live `api/openapi.v0.3.yaml` and route registration when scheduled. Use staff session + CSRF for browser commands, selected organization context determined by server, explicit event/booking/task scope, expected revision/ETag or reviewed fingerprint for material changes, idempotency key bound to canonical request and actor/scope/purpose. Auth before lookup; non-enumerating errors; replay must recheck current actor/grant/policy and return safe receipt rather than stale protected projection or secret. No raw bearer token in idempotency response. Cursor pagination and bounded lists, typed allowlisted sorting/filtering; no arbitrary query or external URL input. Scope rechecked on download, callback, worker claim/submit, scheduled occurrence and retry. Return safe error codes and request/correlation ID, not provider raw responses or credential data. 401 authentication, 403/404 non-disclosing scope denial as established contracts, 409 stale revision/idempotency conflict, 422 invalid plan/unsupported route, 429 local throttle with retry hints, 503 unavailable dependency where applicable; do not invent HTTP success on external uncertainty. 202 accepted means local job accepted, not recipient delivery.

| Proposed endpoint family | Authority and contract |
|---|---|
| `GET /communication/capabilities` | Selected tenant/purpose capability catalogue/readiness; no other tenant accounts, raw secrets or unsupported channel claims. |
| `GET/POST /organization/communication/providers` | Authorized org delivery manager; list redacted, create profile draft with typed adapter; never immediate send. |
| `GET /organization/communication/providers/{profileId}`; `POST .../revisions`, `.../test`, `.../activate`, `.../disable`, `.../retire` | Revision and config readiness, verified test target; review impact/pinned queue state; current auth and exact provider account. |
| `POST .../credentials/rotate`, `.../credentials/revoke` | Separate write-only secret authority, step-up where policy; return redacted revision receipt, never plaintext. |
| `POST .../oauth/start`, provider-specific callback, `POST .../oauth/disconnect` | Actor-bound one-use state, allowed provider origin/account/scopes and selected tenant, explicit consent and revocation; no workspace switch. |
| `GET/POST /organization/communication/senders`, `POST .../{id}/verify` | Verified sender ownership and provider account scope; no spoof or generic raw mail relay. |
| `GET /platform/communication/services`; `POST .../services`, `.../{id}/revisions`, `.../{id}/assignments`, `.../{id}/revoke` | PAC separate service-management capability, explicit assignment, no tenant content; narrow support paths only. |
| `GET/POST /organization/communication/policies`, `POST .../revisions`, `.../publish` | Tenant policy manager; purpose/route/quiet-hour/approval caps within deployment/provider constraints. No bypass of consent or provider rules. |
| Subject-scoped `GET/POST .../communication-preferences`, `.../consent-events`, `.../suppressions`, `.../corrections` | Existing Registry, booking-contact, account or task authorization plus sensitive field permissions; immutable evidence/current projection; never a global contact endpoint. |
| `POST /communication/campaigns` and `POST /communication/campaigns/{id}/preview` | Domain-specific source and scoped audience; no issuance or send. Response digest, revision, selected/excluded counts, route variants, diagnostics, estimate, expiry. |
| `POST .../{id}/approve`, `.../confirm`, `.../schedule` | Separate approval/queue authority; exact digest, expected revisions, approved limits and schedule. Domain command issues capability only when explicitly requested; transactional intent/outbox. |
| `POST .../{id}/pause`, `.../resume`, `.../cancel-remaining` | Reviewed impact with remaining/in-flight/accepted/uncertain counts; revalidate at resume; no external recall promise. |
| Domain-specific issue/distribute/resend endpoints | Preserve existing invitation issue-and-email and booking offer send contracts; new explicit channel-independent issue/distribution through owning domain. No generic endpoint mints capabilities. |
| `GET /communication/history`, `GET /communication/deliveries/{id}/attempts`, `.../evidence` | Authorized union projection filtered by exact scope, purpose and field rights; masked by default; pagination, no cross-tenant counts. |
| `POST /communication/deliveries/{id}/reconcile`, `.../retry`, `.../fallback-review` | Separate evidence, retry and cost authority; reviewed risk for uncertain, no fake provider event. |
| `POST /communication/distribution-tasks`, `.../{id}/claim`, `.../{id}/outcomes`, `.../corrections` | Exact subject, purpose, assignee, document/contact authority and manual evidence, no RSVP mutation. |
| `POST .../share/reveal`, `POST .../render-jobs`, artifact download endpoint | Explicit sensitive reveal/render/download, short-lived no-store, TDS manifests and existing domain capability; synthetic preview separate; no public export of token. |
| `GET /communication/usage`, `GET/POST .../budgets`, `.../quote`, `.../adjustments` | Scope/currency filters, approved limits and actual reconciliation; no payment. Platform aggregate only where authorized. |
| Provider-specific callback endpoint | No staff cookie trust; exact account endpoint + signature + replay check, normalized minimal evidence via restricted worker. No domain action. |
| Public verified preference/opt-out resolve + confirm | Distinct opaque purpose-limited capability, non-destructive resolve, explicit mutation and rate limits; no guest list. |
| Guest/staff `POST .../push-subscriptions`, `.../revoke`, scoped in-app read marker | Authenticated account or verified subject/session; strict endpoint validation, purpose and expiry, no domain approval. |

Example preview request (illustrative, synthetic):

```json
{
  "purpose": "invitation",
  "source": {"eventId": "synthetic-event", "scheduleRevision": 4, "rsvpPolicyRevision": 2},
  "audience": {"kind": "eligible_selected", "selectionRef": "reviewed-filter-ref"},
  "templateSetRevision": "template-rev-7",
  "routePolicyRevision": "policy-rev-3",
  "strategy": "preferred_with_approved_fallback",
  "schedule": {"localTime": "2027-02-15T10:00:00", "zone": "Europe/Sarajevo"},
  "budget": {"currency": "BAM", "maxMinor": 25000}
}
```

Example confirm response fields: `campaignId`, `reviewDigest`, `revision`, `status: scheduled`, counts `approvedSubjects`, `plannedRoutes`, `excluded`, `manualTasks`, estimate and approved cap in minor currency, `dueAt`, receipt ID. No plaintext addresses, secret, URL, credential or claim of provider acceptance. Examples are not actual GHB pricing or valid UUIDs. Preview is read-only with respect to issuance/submission; review snapshot may persist metadata under explicit create/preview command. A confirm of stale digest fails without side effects, including cached replay after authorization loss. Publish OpenAPI, shared TypeScript types, UI and DB commands together in owning slices.

### 23.1 Authorization matrix

Names below are capability families proposed for M0, not claims of existing permission codes. Preserve `organization.delivery.manage`, existing `event.notifications.*`, invitation/booking/guest/organization/collaboration and TDS permissions; map or narrow them through reviewed successor decisions. A broad organization role cannot automatically acquire all sensitive new capabilities. Scope can be org, event, session, exact booking, task, station, platform service assignment or guest capability; grant intersection with source authority and allowed action; no user-managed global provider configuration via tenant context.

| Actor / role | Allowed by explicit grant | Forbidden by default |
|---|---|---|
| Platform owner / delegated service manager | Platform service revision, assignment, quotas, redacted diagnostics and protected recovery | Tenant guest/contact/content, tenant sender use, staff impersonation, unrestricted secret export/host shell. |
| Organization admin | Organization policy/profile management and delegated roles within ceiling; separate content/send approval only with grants | Platform account/other tenant data, generic arbitrary send, automatic access to restricted Registry/booking. |
| Delivery configuration administrator | Manage approved provider/sender/config, test and activate; secret rotation if specifically authorized | Guest list, campaign send/approve, readable credentials. |
| Content designer | TDS draft and safe preview; publication if authorized | Live token issuance, actual send, audience export, provider secret. |
| Campaign preparer | Scoped purpose/audience/route preview and draft | Confirm/send unless separately granted, broaden approved audience, view hidden contacts. |
| Approver / finance reviewer | Review digest, cost cap and scope, approve if policy allows; financial view masked | Automatic send, access to unrelated commercial records/recipient content. |
| Invitation / booking / task issuer | Owning domain action + delivery permission and approved recipient route | Issue another domain credential, RSVP/attendance mutation by delivery, arbitrary recipient. |
| Distribution operator / Info Pult | Assigned task, minimum contact/document reveal if granted, record handover/phone result | Registry export, unrelated invitations, automated mass send, print replacement credential without specific issuance authority. |
| Delivery reconciler | Authorized attempt/evidence projection, record operator review, retry with separate grant/budget | Forge provider status, erase history, silent resend, change recipient. |
| Guest/customer | Own purpose-bound response, preference, verified subscription and permitted portal | Tenant directory, provider settings, other guests, admission mutation. |
| Worker / callback adapter | Exact leased intent/account and narrowly scoped secret/evidence operation | General Registry access, host owner or tenant switch, arbitrary send, business action mutation. |
| Auditor | Approved scoped metadata and evidence history; separate content access if necessary | Commands, unmask secrets, use audit to access other tenants. |

Authorization = supported adapter/channel ∩ platform service/tenant activation ∩ current organization/member/grant ∩ owning domain purpose/subject scope ∩ exact action/field authority ∩ reviewed plan and expiry ∩ current consent/suppression/credential/cost. Deny by default; navigation hints never authorization. Membership suspension/revocation and workspace switch follow ADR 0010/0015; service and OAuth revoke scoped independently. Platform support explicit reason, bounded scope/expiry, actual actor and audit under PAC; no silent bypass.

## 24. CID-22 — Security, privacy, abuse prevention and governance

Threat model includes tenant leakage, malicious sender or operator, compromised provider account, forged callbacks, arbitrary destination/SSRF, secret exposure, token forwarding, phishing content, duplicate submissions, consent abuse, runaway charges, cross-tenant service quota starvation, queue poisoning, stale scheduled authority and restore resurrection. Mitigate through bounded identity and purpose-specific constraints, strict typed payloads, review, separation of duty, encryption and least privilege, delivery and cost fences, verified evidence and audit. Apply existing project security architecture and accepted ADRs; no blanket weakening for easier onboarding.

- Transport: TLS with hostname/cert validation, no disable verification or plaintext credential downgrade. SMTP STARTTLS required or implicit TLS; approved internal relay still subject to deployment policy. Use network egress rules and per-adapter fixed allowlisted HTTPS hosts/endpoints; user-provided SMTP host/port only under policy allowlist/controlled relay verification. Resolve and validate IPs, prevent DNS rebinding/redirect to loopback, link-local, metadata, privileged admin/internal targets; explicit deployment allowlist for authorized local relay/capture, not broad private-network permit. OAuth/push/provider media/callback verification endpoints controlled. Disable redirect-follow on sensitive requests or revalidate destination and never forward secrets across origins. Provider SDK no arbitrary network or default retries; timeout, size and concurrency limits. Renderer network-denied as TDS. No external fetch of contact-provided URL/attachment. Do not allow arbitrary SMTP envelope, header injection, executable templates or user-selected unrestricted API target.
- Credentials: separate tenant/provider/service secret boundaries; encrypted authenticated context binding, per-kind key policy and rotation; no secret visible to ordinary API, tenant admin after saving, logs, metrics, SQL debug, CI, browser cache, backup manifest or support export. Limit decrypt to actual claim/account, no global secrets table access. Scoped OAuth, short-lived grants, revoke/rotate with verified sender account, new revision readiness and safe drain. Avoid sending secrets by email or test notification. Secret leak incident stops affected profile, rotates key, reconciles outstanding jobs and records actual operator; already escaped messages can't be recalled.
- Personal data: purpose-minimize contact fields, content and callback storage; keep live capability secret only narrow encrypted delivery/render boundary; subject/headers must not contain access secret, sensitive reason, medical/restricted info. Redact structured logs and safe failure taxonomy, no raw provider payload default. Provider processing agreements, region/retention/transfer and actual local applicable law reviewed before production; avoid generic compliance guarantees. Staff may reveal masked recipient only exact purpose/authority and audit. Avoid sending internal restricted map/Registry/contract data to public channel. TDS manifest and private attachment retention, size limits, allowlisted formats/safe render; malware checks for allowed uploads. Track legal hold and access review; purge content with documented authorization and retain minimum necessary non-identifying evidence. No unrestricted external provider history synchronization.
- Consent and anti-abuse: tenant purpose-specific consent/suppression and opt-out, approved sender, per-purpose audience caps, verified provider account and recipient eligibility, no arbitrary contact harvest, no credential forwarding links to unrelated domains, no generic external mail relay. Detect unusual queue volumes, repeated invalid destinations/bounces/complaints, sudden sender change and budget spikes with bounded alert/throttle; support disable and audited resolution, provider policy blocks not bypassable. Separate transactional necessity from promotional preference. No bypass through manual share/export permissions; physical/phone policy also applies. Quotas enforced before network, fair tenant claims, emergency mode reviewed with cost/consent controls; not a mass-send escape hatch.
- Browser/public: CSRF and selected tenant checks, CSP, safe paste/render, no third-party analytics/remote scripts on token pages, no-referrer and cache restrictions, fragment cleanup, no mutation on GET/preview/security scanner, rate limit and non-enumeration. OAuth state single-use, CSRF, PKCE and issuer/account check. Kiosk no token sharing or push enrollment unless expressly safe verified mode; shared device data clears per AGIS. Do not promise erase from user's clipboard/provider/inbox/printed page. Secure link forward risk explicit and revocable; high-risk purpose may require second verification.
- Evidence and audit: actor, tenant/scope, purpose, action, reviewed revision/digest, old/new policy, intended count, outcome safe code, reason, time, correlation and cost units; actual member/system/provider/host provenance. Append-only approval, attempt and evidence; corrections append. No fake provider status or human impersonation. Provider IDs namespace, replay and out-of-order reconciliation, conflicting payload quarantine. Incident drill verifies credential and contact isolation, no token in logs or artifacts not authorized. Operational metrics contain no guest name, phone, message content or live secret. Exports require current authorization and retention/expiry.

Retention decision must specify per-purpose content, address/recipient snapshot, provider metadata, rendered artifact, callback quarantine, consent proof, financial usage and audit windows and lawful hold, deletion actor and backup expiry; actual legal retention rules not inferred. Offboarding disables new sends/grants/subscriptions, reviews outstanding tasks/leases/unknown outcomes and authorizes portability within scope; secret revoke/erase according to policy, provider-side deletion where supported only reported when evidenced. No automatic business cancellation/refund or destruction of audit on offboarding.

## 25. CID-23 — User experience, deployment, operational resilience and observability

OAC Communication and Delivery Center tabs: Overview (authorized readiness, pending review, scheduled, failed/uncertain, usage); Providers and sender identities; Channel policies and preferences; Campaigns and schedules; Distribution tasks; Delivery history/reconciliation; Templates (link to TDS); Budgets and usage; authorized audit/support. Contextual EOC/booking/task actions open same feature views prefiltered to scope. PAC platform service screen separate. Booking-only tenant sees booking purposes without event/guest tabs. Limited operator sees assigned task only. Dashboard counts obey row/field permissions and current module state; no disabled controls exposing hidden records, stale count shown as stale. Shared UX tables, search/filter, saved views, pagination, accessibility and role landing; locale labels are display only, stable codes remain. No automatic send on view/open/change template. Mobile staff task/phone handover and guest preference pages usable with keyboard/screen reader. Provider readiness wizard with safe fields, account/sender proof, auth type, capabilities, test target, activation review and clear actionable safe error; no copy of token after save. Show expected content format and missing language/variables, actual eligibility/suppression and reason, audience/route cost review, explicit confirm and status feedback. Present accepted/delivered/read/manual/unknown differently with text, not only color. Print status uncertain remains review task. Show quiet-hour schedule/timezone and DST, per-channel limits, next retry and deadline, not fictitious exact delivery time. Expired/cancelled/unauthorized context clears data and caches. All UI concepts provisional, reuse existing feature modules and UX contract, no all-at-once rewrite.

Deployment profiles: local capture adapter with non-live synthetic tests and no external account; local trusted network with on-prem SMTP/relay or no electronic route; public hosted native Linux/systemd and production Compose, outbound approved network, optional inbound HTTPS callbacks and guest links through configured trusted reverse proxy; external provider accounts optional. Domain name, certificate, DNS sender verification, OAuth redirect URI, webhook URL and outbound allowlist configured per site; document firewall requirements and callback/poll limitations, no assumption of public port 25/80 or home ISP. Use same application/migrations/contracts and service identity/secret handling both install modes; no committed credentials or baked provider key. Dedicated workers bounded resources, no root, mounted private secrets/volumes, egress control, service health and queue readiness. Core login/booking/event/printing can operate when communication unavailable. Public links may be unusable if origin not reachable; manual/print/phone support and clear status, not promise offline RSVP submission. Internet loss with server reachable: internal task/print/in-app operations continue; external queue remains bounded with delayed/review-required statuses, deadlines and eligibility rechecked on reconnect. No offline client may originate confirmed provider send or persist live secrets. Station offline rules per AGIS unaffected.

Operations: per-tenant queue age/depth, rate-limit, lease expiries, worker liveness, retry/unknown count, callback verification failures, correlation lag, sender/auth expiry, suppression rate, budget utilization and quote discrepancies, renderer and storage health. Aggregate dashboards with privacy-safe labels; scoped detailed views only. Health/readiness distinguishes worker down from provider unavailable, configuration incomplete, depleted quota, callbacks disabled and no optional channel selected. Alerts deduplicated/rate-limited, avoid recursive notification storm when provider fails; local in-app operational alert independent of failed external channel. Runbooks: inspect correlation without PII, pause/drain/resume, rotate/re-authorize, reconcile provider acceptance uncertainty, handle callback replay/delay, restore queue safely, isolate tenant/provider and resolve quota discrepancy. No log raw message body. Config changes impact-preview and revision audit. Degraded mode does not mutate domain fact.

Backup and recovery: encrypted consistent DB, keys, private TDS assets/artifacts and config versions; restore in isolated network/capture mode, no automatic external sends or callbacks. Before reopening, reconcile active/expired/revoked capabilities, membership/grants, consent withdrawal/suppression, provider credential epoch, scheduled occurrences, queue leases and provider reference evidence after backup time; unresolved in-flight attempts uncertain; compare provider ledger to avoid replay and costs; operator explicitly opens approved channels after verification. No resurrection of withdrawn consent, disabled provider, revoked link or sent intent. Document supported rollback/forward repair; restore rehearsal on disposable data with both modes; no production destructive test. Existing OLA and PAC recovery acceptance remain.

### 25.1 Provisional quality targets and reference envelope

Targets are proposals for M0 measurement, not achieved performance or actual tenant size. Synthetic reference: two independent tenants and a shared service assignment; 10,000 authorized event subjects with 2,000 planned electronic routes and 200 manual tasks, two languages, several providers with low/high rate and uncertain outcomes; 20 concurrent staff operations and multiple workers. Validate against declared hardware/DB/provider simulation and measure rather than promise. Proposed p95 eligible paginated history response ≤ 750 ms on declared reference host; first audience preview job acknowledgement ≤ 2 s (background scan bounded, progress/expiry explicit); claim/suppression/budget transaction p95 ≤ 500 ms excluding external call; approved due jobs enter queue within 60 s under available capacity; callback ingestion p95 ≤ 1 s excluding upstream, live status visible within 5 s of persisted event with healthy stream; no cross-tenant starvation under enforced fair-share limits; provider/network timeouts bounded and no unbounded memory or retry. Actual provider delivery time outside Eventor guarantee. Measure 100 repeated concurrent confirmations/attempts and quota races, 100 duplicate/out-of-order callbacks, restore and network partition, Unicode rendering and browser/mobile accessibility. Adapt targets only with recorded evidence and owner approval. No claim of WCAG certification from automated checks alone; keyboard, labels, contrast, 200% zoom, screen reader and manual assistive tests, UX-AC-13/14. Localize bs-BA/en with preserved diacritics and language-specific provider template approvals. Preserve current acceptance profiles and supported browser evidence; actual device/provider compatibility validated at scheduled work.

## 27. Measurable acceptance criteria and evidence plan

Each criterion has reproducible pass/fail assertions on synthetic data, a current candidate commit and evidence layer. No case marked passed by documentation or existing CI. Test real PostgreSQL runtime role, independent connections, API contracts, browser and actual adapters with fake transport for deterministic failures; live sandbox on supported provider account after consent/test isolation. Do not send unsolicited real messages. No actual credentials/guest data in Git, reports, logs or artifacts. Two tenants A/B, A hybrid and B independent organizer, C provider-only, user M with independent memberships, revoked actor and platform service grant; synthetic contacts including no electronic address, shared phone/email, invalid/unverified, opted-out, guest no device, bs-BA/en, exact booking/task/grant; controlled clock, representative templates, signed callback fixtures and provider simulator with accepted, definite reject, timeout-after-send, delayed/duplicate/contradictory receipts, partial batch and cost mismatch. Use approved isolated test environment; GHB examples not actual policies or prices. Evidence record: ID, commit, environment/install mode, actor/scope, setup/fixture, exact steps, expected/observed counts/evidence, redacted artifacts and failure/owner; pass/fail/not run/approved N/A, no unsupported waiver. Actual provider account compatibility distinct from fake integration tests. Run focused slices incrementally, final VM once coherent product and both installers ready.

### Lifecycle journey and release gate extension

- OLA-01–03: owner provisions A/C; A admin chooses own email/OAuth + approved SMS/messaging profile and optional assigned platform service; C chooses no external channel and manual workflow. Verify readiness independent of unrelated modules, no routine owner intervention or secrets in browser. OLA-04/06: correct role dashboards, separate preparer/approver/send/config/reconcile, context switch and suspended member revoke; no unauthorized counts.
- OLA-05: TDS branded bs-BA/en text/HTML/card/short message, provider template mapping/approval, synthetic test and actual approved recipient preview, private artifact and printed QR; no preview issuance or send. OLA-07/08: C provider booking offer/decision/cancellation with manual or SMTP/HTTP route, B independent organizer gets scoped notice and decides separately, no event/guest records in C. Delivery failure creates explicit follow-up not business mutation.
- OLA-09: synthetic guests include no email, opt-out, invalid/shared contact, Viber/WhatsApp eligible and no device; approved campaign chooses preferred/print/phone routes, reviewed estimate/quotas and scheduled reminder. Concurrent confirm one intent; revoke/suppress after review, provider timeout uncertain without fallback; definite failure allowed alternative. Guest responds via distinct invitation capability or staff-recorded response; admission pass separate. Gate check-in, Info Pult, published seat-change notice and controlled reprint/replace follow AGIS. No delivery/print/lookup records attendance. Verify operator reconciliation and separate evidence/RSVP columns.
- OLA-10: explicit collaboration grant/partner task notice only allowed projection, recipient acknowledges/accepts through owner command, revocation blocks new protected delivery; no partner guest list or provider-owned internal notes. OLA-11/12/13: PAC scoped support, quotas and audit; tenant service grant suspension/offboarding, suppression and retention, lawful portability; preserve independent membership and history.
- OLA-14: adverse provider/auth/network/worker/callback/consent/price/race tests, browser accessibility, locale, performance and data isolation; OLA-15: both installer modes, actual approved external HTTPS/SMTP/provider sandbox evidence for advertised adapters, offline/manual/local capture and restore without replay. Existing G8 external HTTPS/SMTP gate retained, extended evidence for HTTP/SMS/messaging/push as supported; skips not passes. G1 exact-head/post-merge CI, G2 independent tenant operation, G3 isolation, G4 content/communication/print, G5 event journey, G6 reliability/localization, G7 deployment/recovery, G8 actual external evidence, G9 traceability and release defects. Optional Telegram disabled by explicit policy may be N/A; if advertised must be tested. Event-level opt-out of electronic channel does not erase planned product coverage. No legal, security, integrity or external-provider compatibility claims without actual evidence.

## 28. Open engineering decisions and integration procedure

At scheduled M0: validate purpose catalogue and exact authority, current runtime locks/permission names and migration compatibility; supported provider selection (one reference implementation per required adapter family), official account availability/region/registration, business template approvals, contract/DPA and recipient policy, authentication/scopes, callback signature/correlation/idempotency windows and polling, provider pricing/quotas/retention, SMTP local relay network exception, OAuth grants and encryption/secret rotation, shared-service account isolation and sender attribution, opt-in evidence/transactional lawful basis/quiet hours, budget reservation and accounting boundaries, batch semantics, performance fixture/targets, TDS channel template schemas/attachments and safe render, browser push support and data retention/legal hold. Owner/tenant must validate actual sender identities, communication policies, authorized approvers, budget, jurisdictions and provider accounts. Do not infer GHB operational facts or current prices. Do not commit real API keys, credentials or synthetic live capability. Do not change accepted ADR without reviewed successor. Provider APIs, policies and rates evolve; revalidate documentation and actual account at adapter implementation, not assume research guarantees access.

After owner approval, integrate full reviewed source verbatim to the proposed destination via separate documentation-only PR, approval record external to source to preserve byte checksum. Add additive cross-references to [design index](README.md), [architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md), [roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md), [gap analysis](../../BLUEPRINT_TO_REPOSITORY_GAP_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md), invitation design, PAC/OAC/UX/TDS, AGIS when merged, OLA and existing issues as mapped. Preserve original text and historical checksum references for previously reviewed specs. Coordinate AGIS PR #235 separately and check latest main before branch; do not merge AGIS as side effect of preparing CID. No code, migrations, OpenAPI, workflow, branches, issue or environment changes in this preparation. Preserve Blueprint v1.2/v0.2 snapshots, all accepted ADRs, PROJECT_STATE handoff and Codex's active branches/priorities. No new issues by default. Future consolidated Blueprint v1.3 separately reviewed. Verify full source checksum/blob and complete docs-only tree diff, relative links, append-only issue changes, all required exact-head CI before authorized squash merge, then post-merge CI; no feature implementation or environment republication. Final acceptance VM remains Phase 9.

## Appendix A — Official technical references (adapter feasibility only)

Inspected 2026-11-27. These are candidate integration references, not certification, prices, legal advice or commitments. Use current official documentation and account-specific provider rules when scheduled. Provider policies and versions may change.

- Google, [Gmail SMTP XOAUTH2](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/imap/xoauth2-protocol), [server-side Gmail API authorization](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/web-server): OAuth-supported transport/API, exact scopes and account policy reviewed.
- Microsoft, [OAuth for SMTP/IMAP/POP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/client-developer/legacy-protocols/how-to-authenticate-an-imap-pop-smtp-application-by-using-oauth/): authentication flow and mailbox authorization are provider-specific; do not depend on legacy password authentication.
- Resend, [HTTP email API idempotency](https://resend.com/changelog/idempotency-keys): provider-specific idempotency support, verify exact window/request behavior and supported webhook events before relying on it.
- Twilio, [outbound message status callbacks](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/guides/track-outbound-message-status): reference SMS adapter status capability, not universal delivery semantics or guaranteed pricing.
- Meta, [WhatsApp Business Platform](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/overview) and [template management](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/business-management-api/guides): official business send and managed templates; review actual account permissions, eligibility, opt-in, template policies and current pricing.
- Viber, [official documentation](https://developers.viber.com/docs/all/) and [REST Bot API](https://developers.viber.com/docs/api/rest-bot-api/): business phone-addressable service and subscribed bot are distinct paths.
- Telegram, [official bot introduction](https://core.telegram.org/bots/) and [bot features](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features): recipient starts conversation; deep-link enrollment can be purpose-bound, never arbitrary phone targeting.
- MDN, [Push API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Push_API), [PushManager.subscribe](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PushManager/subscribe), [PushSubscription](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PushSubscription): browser permission, service worker subscription, endpoint and encryption key material; verify browser/OS matrix and secure deployment requirements.

## Approved coordinated communication interoperability — 2026-11-27

[AES v1.0](ADAPTIVE_EXPERIENCE_AND_SETUP_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [EPW v1.0](EVENT_PLANNING_PRODUCTION_AND_OPERATIONAL_WORKFLOWS_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [FRS v1.0](FORMS_REGISTRATION_AND_SUBMISSION_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [HPG v1.0](HOSPITALITY_PROTOCOL_AND_GUEST_SERVICES_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [RAI v1.0](REPORTING_ANALYTICS_AND_INTELLIGENCE_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) use CID's reviewed intent, route, consent, cost and evidence contracts. AES quick actions and EPW reminders/escalations are explicit authorized communications, not bypasses; FRS receipts and registration decisions, HPG arrangements and RAI scheduled report delivery use purpose-limited recipients and approved TDS revisions. Private report/form/service artifacts require current download authority, expiry and reauthorization; no automatic attachment of a restricted export to a provider message. No delivery changes approval, registration, service fulfillment or attendance. Preserve consent, uncertainty reconciliation, no-email/manual alternatives, per-channel capability and tenant budget/grants. Approved additive scope only; retain existing requirements, accepted ADRs, Blueprint v1.2, PROJECT_STATE and the #104/#112 → #105–107 → #110/#111/#108 development sequence. No immediate implementation, unrelated closure gates, environment republication or Blueprint v1.3 consolidation. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

# Eventor Adaptive Experience and Setup (AES)
## Technical specification v1.0

**Status:** Proposed for product-owner approval; no integration or implementation authorized by this draft.  
**Date:** 2026-11-27. **Read-only repository baseline:** `e0fa44203f785284d597f69dae8510c91bada0d6` (main, CID PR #236). All five required CI checks on this baseline were observed completed successfully during preparation. CI is not product acceptance.  
**Proposed destination:** `docs/implementation-design/v0.3/ADAPTIVE_EXPERIENCE_AND_SETUP_DESIGN_v1.0.md`. Links are relative to that future location. The five proposed documents are companion drafts, not yet repository files.  
**Document control:** AES-01–15, AES-M0–M5, AES-AC-01–30. MUST denotes proposed product requirement, SHOULD preferred approach with justified exceptions, MAY optional. Endpoint names, entity names, permission codes and numerical envelopes are design proposals, not existing runtime contracts or certified targets. No acceptance tests executed.

## 1. Objective and boundaries

Make a small meeting as easy to configure as a calendar appointment while allowing the same event to become a complex institutional ceremony. Provide Quick Start, Guided Setup and Advanced Setup, a common setup/readiness contract, organization presets and progressively disclosed specialist tools. The minimum event is a draft containing the existing mandatory name, schedule/timezone and ownership fields; location and expected participants may be supplied or explicitly unresolved where the domain permits. No requirement to activate guests, RSVP, venue drawing, seating, admission, suppliers, hospitality or external delivery. A venue provider can create a booking inquiry/draft without any event. Never create a second simplified event table or duplicate auth, capacity, booking or policy state. Event templates are EPW-owned; AES presents and applies their reviewed configuration choices. No AI-generated irreversible decisions, arbitrary automation or bypass of approval/security. This is the cross-module experience contract; not a redesign of every existing page before further delivery.

## 2. Existing foundation and reconciliation

Blueprint §§2, 4–6, 7–13, 25, 34–35, 41–46 already allow optional event capabilities and typed layouts. Migration `000008_event_foundation.sql` defines events, event_schedule_revisions, event_sessions, event_capability_sets, event_capability_revisions and event_capability_overrides; 000121–127 provide organizer commands and lifecycle, 000189 RSVP settings. OAC-02 readiness, OAC-13 safe duplicate, UX-03 setup and UX-04/05 permission-scoped navigation are foundations. Current staff workspace implements event/session administration and optional roster capability, not a complete adaptive creation flow. Current handoff remains #104/#112. Do not assume that a feature listed in the design or database is operational.

Use [Blueprint v1.2](../../blueprint/v1.2/Event_Operations_Platform_Technical_Blueprint_v1.2.md), [architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md), [roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md), [project state](../../PROJECT_STATE.md), [gap analysis](../../BLUEPRINT_TO_REPOSITORY_GAP_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md), [operating model](../../OPERATING_MODEL.md), and [roles](../../product/USER_ROLES_AND_PERMISSIONS_v0.1.md). Read [RSVP design](RSVP_AND_INVITATION_DESIGN_v0.3.md), [collaboration design](CROSS_ORGANIZATION_COLLABORATION_DESIGN_v0.3.md) and [disruption design](CANCELLATION_AND_EVENT_DISRUPTION_DESIGN_v0.3.md) for owning commands. Existing accepted decisions prevail until reviewed successor: [modular monolith](../../decisions/0001-modular-monolith.md), [self-hosting](../../decisions/0002-self-hosted-deployment.md), [human-approved allocation](../../decisions/0003-human-approved-allocation.md), [optional scope](../../decisions/0004-optional-event-operations-scope.md), [invitation separation](../../decisions/0005-separate-invitations-rsvp-attendance.md), [collaboration](../../decisions/0006-cross-organization-collaboration.md), [localization](../../decisions/0007-internationalization.md), [incremental staff UI](../../decisions/0008-modular-staff-frontend.md), [membership protection](../../decisions/0010-organization-membership-access.md), [login/workspaces](../../decisions/0015-email-first-login-and-platform-administration.md), [scoped grants](../../decisions/0023-permissioned-collaboration-grant-lifecycle.md), [reviewed grant acceptance](../../decisions/0024-shared-party-names-and-reviewed-grant-acceptance.md).
