# Event invitations and RSVP — design addendum v0.3

**Status:** proposed domain/API design, ready for schema and contract review  
**Date:** 2026-11-10  
**Parent design:** Implementation Design v0.2  
**Related decisions:** ADR 0004 (optional, responsibility-scoped event operations); ADR 0005 (invitation, RSVP and attendance are separate lifecycles)  
**Related issue:** [#6 — Specify invitation and RSVP lifecycle](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/6)

This document extends the historical v0.2 design without rewriting it. It specifies the agreed invitation/RSVP behavior and incorporates the venue-provider/event-organizer operating model. It is not yet a production SQL migration or validated OpenAPI contract.

## 1. Product boundary: RSVP is an optional event capability

A venue booking does not require an operational event, a guest registry, invitations or RSVP.

The following records and behavior exist only when the applicable event/guest capabilities are enabled:
- Event and event-session records, where needed.
- Event guest participation records.
- Invitation records and invitation access links.
- RSVP policy and response history.
- Guest portal surfaces.

A venue-provider-only workflow remains complete with the booking/customer contacts and venue-side service requirements. It must not create attendee/guest records simply to represent a booking contact, nor require the venue provider to collect the renter's guest data.

For a hybrid event, the organizer may own guest operations while the venue provider handles venue-side tasks. Guest operations may be assigned to the venue provider only when it has explicitly accepted that contracted responsibility. The party responsible for guest data is the operating organization assigned to that module/task, not automatically the venue provider.

### 1.1 Capability dependencies

| Capability | Requires | Does not require |
|---|---|---|
| Venue booking | Booking customer/contact and venue/resource model | Event, event guests, invitations, RSVP, check-in |
| Event guest registry | Operational event with guest participation enabled | Invitations, RSVP, seating or check-in |
| Staff-recorded RSVP | Event guest and RSVP capability enabled | Guest email, invitation link, guest account, admission QR |
| Guest self-service RSVP | Event guest, RSVP capability, invitation link and guest-facing route | Guest account, seating, admission QR or check-in |
| Seating/allocation | Event participants or another explicit allocation subject set, plus spatial model | Invitation delivery or RSVP |
| Check-in | Admission/attendance subject and authorized scan/manual workflow | RSVP confirmation or seating |
| External prerequisite coordination | Event/task scope with an explicitly assigned responsible party | Guest Registry, invitations or RSVP |

Dependencies must be explicit and minimal. Enabling one capability must not silently activate every other event module.

## 2. Keep four independent state dimensions

The current v0.2 `event_guests.rsvp_status` combines different concepts (`pending`, `invited`, `confirmed`, `declined`, `waitlisted`, `not_required`). These must be separated in the successor schema.

### 2.1 Invitation lifecycle

Invitation issuance and delivery describe whether an invitation was prepared and communicated. They do not say whether the guest accepted.

Recommended concepts:
- Invitation record: draft/prepared, active, revoked, expired or cancelled.
- Delivery attempt: queued, sent, delivered, failed, bounced or suppressed.
- Access link: active, revoked, expired or replaced.

A guest may have an active invitation but no response. Delivery may fail while staff later record a phone confirmation. Resending an invitation must not erase an existing response.

### 2.2 RSVP response

RSVP describes the guest's stated intention, not the invitation's delivery state or actual arrival.

Initial semantic response codes:
- `accepted` — intends to attend.
- `declined` — will not attend.
- `tentative` — cannot yet confirm, when this response is enabled for the event.

The semantic choices and their display labels are event configuration. An organization may localize labels and enable/disable tentative response. A custom option must map to an explicit system meaning so that reporting and readiness logic remain deterministic; a free-form label must not silently acquire acceptance semantics.

No response is a state of `pending`; it is not an implicit decline. Whether RSVP is required, optional or not applicable is a separate policy, not an answer. A waitlist/admission decision is also separate and must not be represented as an RSVP response.

### 2.3 Participation / invitation eligibility

Whether a person is active in the event, cancelled, archived, invited, waitlisted or otherwise eligible is not the RSVP answer. Keep participation and admission eligibility as independent state dimensions.

### 2.4 Attendance

Attendance is a physical operational fact recorded by check-in or an authorized manual attendance workflow. An accepted RSVP does not mean the guest arrived; a declined or missing RSVP does not itself create a check-in. The current `guest_session_attendance` and append-only check-in records remain separate from RSVP history.

## 3. RSVP policy and timing

Each event that enables RSVP has a versioned policy snapshot. It should include:

- Whether RSVP is enabled.
- Whether a response is required, optional or not applicable by default.
- Enabled response options and their stable semantic codes / localized labels.
- Response deadline as an absolute `timestamptz`; display and entry use the event's configured IANA timezone.
- Whether a guest may change their response before the deadline.
- Whether staff may record a response after the deadline, and which role may authorize an override.
- Reminder schedule, maximum reminder count and quiet-hour rules.
- Permitted delivery channels and selected invitation template revision.
- Optional secondary verification policy for sensitive/high-profile events.
- Optional event-specific follow-up questions, independently versioned and validated.

The deadline is a response cutoff, not an automatic response. At cutoff, unanswered guests remain unanswered; dashboards may show them as overdue/unconfirmed. Do not convert them to declined automatically.

Policy changes after invitations have been sent must be versioned and auditable. The event must retain the policy revision used for each issued invitation/response. A policy update must not silently reinterpret previous answers. The effective deadline shown to each guest must be clear.

For normal self-service, guests may change an answer until the configured deadline when the policy permits it. After cutoff, guest self-service is closed. An authorized staff member may still record a late response or correction using an explicit override permission and reason; the original response and override remain in the history.

## 4. Guest self-service flow

### 4.1 Invitation issue

1. An authorized operator selects event guests and an approved contact point for each.
2. The application creates invitation records using the event's published invitation/template/policy revisions.
3. It creates or reuses the current valid invitation access link for each guest.
4. It queues a notification delivery attempt (email is the initial channel).
5. The delivery worker records provider reference, timestamps and safe delivery status/error information.
6. The guest list shows invitation and delivery state separately from RSVP response state.

Batching and reminders are operational conveniences. Each invitation, delivery attempt and response remains traceable to its event guest and the relevant configuration revisions.

### 4.2 Link security

The invitation URL contains a high-entropy, opaque bearer secret (at least 256 bits from a cryptographically secure random generator). The raw secret is never stored in the database, logs, analytics or audit payloads; only a one-way token hash is stored.

Invitation access is:
- Bound to exactly one invitation/event-guest record and one event.
- Purpose-limited to reading that guest's invitation context and submitting that guest's RSVP.
- Separate from admission QR credentials and check-in.
- Revocable and replaceable. Reissue revokes the previous link before a new link becomes active.
- Time-limited. Expiry is configured independently from the RSVP deadline; an expired link cannot submit a response.
- Rate-limited and protected against token enumeration.

The public endpoint must not mutate the invitation or response merely because a browser or email-security scanner performs a GET. Link resolution is a non-destructive POST exchange. The preferred web-link pattern places the secret in the URL fragment so it is not sent in the initial HTTP request; the first-party client then submits it over TLS to the resolve endpoint. No third-party analytics/assets should receive the secret. Use `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, avoid token-bearing redirect URLs and redact request bodies/headers in logs.

Resolving a link establishes a narrowly scoped guest session. The guest explicitly selects and confirms a response. The link must not be a one-click RSVP decision. Link resolution itself does not count as a response and should be idempotent so security scanners do not consume it.

A secondary verification step may be enabled for selected events, but a full guest account is not the default. The token is a bearer credential: the interface should warn guests not to forward it, and staff can revoke/reissue it.

### 4.3 Guest-visible information

The guest view may show only:
- The event name and approved guest-facing description/date/time/location.
- The invitation/RSVP prompt, deadline and allowed answers.
- The guest's own current response and confirmation.
- Optional event-specific response questions.
- Other personal event information only when separately enabled and approved, such as the guest's own seating locator.

It must not expose other guests, internal notes, restricted prerequisites, staff/organizer contacts not designated for public use, allocation rules, private floor-plan layers or venue internal operations data.

### 4.4 Response submission

1. The guest opens the invitation and resolves the link.
2. The application presents the currently valid policy and response choices.
3. The guest explicitly selects and submits an answer.
4. The server checks event/module state, link scope/revocation/expiry, response deadline and change policy.
5. It appends a response-history record and updates the event-guest current-response projection in one transaction.
6. It returns a confirmation and, if enabled, queues a confirmation notification.

The browser is never authoritative for the response status. Duplicate submissions must be idempotent; concurrent submissions must not silently overwrite one another. If the guest submits a new answer, preserve the previous answer as history.

## 5. Staff-recorded responses

Staff must be able to record a response received outside the portal, including:
- Telephone.
- In person.
- Email.
- Written communication.
- Assistant or representative.
- Import or another explicitly configured source.

The staff command records:
- The selected RSVP answer.
- Source/method.
- When the response was received (the reported/observed time).
- When the record was entered (server-generated timestamp).
- The authenticated operator who entered it.
- Optional respondent/representative detail where necessary.
- Optional brief note/reason, under appropriate classification and permissions.
- Whether it was late or an override was used, including the authorizing actor and reason.

The operator identity is mandatory for staff capture. Do not allow an API client to supply or impersonate the operator ID; derive it from the authenticated session. A staff-recorded response does not require an invitation link or guest email address.

Staff correction is append-only: add a new response-history record that supersedes the previous effective response, with reason and actor. Do not edit/delete the previous response. A staff override after the deadline must use a dedicated permission and be audited.

## 6. Proposed data model for the next schema revision

The following is a logical model, not final SQL. Exact keys, tenant foreign keys, indexes and constraints will be resolved in the schema-review issue.

### 6.1 `event_invitations`

One invitation instance for one event guest, with:
- Organization, event and event-guest foreign keys.
- Invitation purpose/type and lifecycle state.
- Selected contact-point reference and a minimal recipient snapshot needed to explain what was sent.
- Invitation/template revision and RSVP-policy revision snapshots.
- Created/issued/revoked/expired metadata.
- Actor responsible for issuing/revoking.
- Optional batch/campaign reference.

Do not copy every person contact field into a general-purpose event record. Store the minimum needed, classify it and enforce retention.

### 6.2 `event_invitation_links`

One row per invitation-link issuance/reissue:
- Invitation ID and organization/event scope.
- Token hash (unique; never raw token).
- Issued, expiry, revocation and replacement metadata.
- Status and optional last successful resolution timestamp.
- No response fields; link resolution is not a response.

A replacement creates a new row and marks the old one replaced/revoked. The previous hash remains only as needed to reject replay and prove lifecycle/audit history; remove according to retention policy.

### 6.3 `event_guest_rsvp_responses`

Append-only response history:
- Organization, event, event-guest and optional invitation IDs.
- Stable semantic response code and response-option revision/label snapshot.
- Source code (guest portal, telephone, in person, email, written, representative, import or other).
- Respondent kind (guest, assistant, representative or staff-recorded on behalf of guest).
- `response_received_at` — when the response was communicated, where known.
- `recorded_at` — server-generated timestamp when Eventor captured it.
- `recorded_by_user_id` — required for staff/import actions; null for guest self-service.
- Optional classified note/reason and request/idempotency identifier.
- Optional `supersedes_response_id` for corrections/changed answers.

Rows are never updated or deleted by ordinary application workflows. A correction appends a new row. The current response is either a validated projection on `event_guests` or a view derived from the latest effective history record; it must never be the only retained copy.

### 6.4 RSVP policy revisions

A published, versioned RSVP policy is bound to the event and invitations. It contains the enabled response semantics, deadline, change policy, reminder schedule, locale and guest-facing copy. A policy publication creates a new revision; previously issued invitations and response snapshots remain interpretable.

### 6.5 Existing schema reuse and changes

- `event_guests.rsvp_status` in v0.2 is a denormalized legacy field. In the successor revision, separate it from invitation status and admission/waitlist status. A compatibility mapping for existing values must be defined in the migration.
- `guest_credentials` currently mixes `admission_qr`, `guest_portal` and `staff_assist`. Do not use an admission QR as an invitation link. Decide in the successor schema whether `guest_portal` represents only an established short-lived portal session or is replaced by a distinct session/token construct.
- `notification_deliveries` already tracks channel, template revision, status and provider reference, but it needs a reliable invitation relation/message-purpose field or an equivalent normalized invitation-delivery table. A generic delivery row must not be the sole invitation record.
- `guest_session_attendance` and check-in records remain independent.
- `event_prerequisites` remain optional and responsibility-scoped; they are not a prerequisite for RSVP or guest participation unless a separately configured business rule explicitly establishes a dependency.

## 7. API contract proposal

These routes are proposed names/shapes to be normalized during OpenAPI v0.3 review. They are not yet added to the historical v0.2 OpenAPI file.

### Guest-facing routes

- `POST /public/invitations/resolve` — exchange the invitation secret for a short-lived, narrowly scoped guest session and safe invitation context. No response change occurs.
- `GET /guest-portal/me/invitation` — read the current guest-facing invitation and RSVP policy.
- `GET /guest-portal/me/rsvp` — read the guest's own current response.
- `POST /guest-portal/me/rsvp-responses` — explicitly submit/change an answer, with idempotency key and server-side deadline/policy enforcement.

Guest-facing responses must be purpose-built projections and must not contain event guest IDs or internal database identifiers unless strictly required by the client.

### Staff routes

- `POST /events/{eventId}/invitations` — issue invitations for selected event guests; accepts the published template/policy or explicit approved revisions.
- `POST /events/{eventId}/guests/{eventGuestId}/invitations/{invitationId}/resend` — queue a new delivery attempt without changing RSVP.
- `POST /events/{eventId}/guests/{eventGuestId}/invitations/{invitationId}/reissue-link` — revoke the old invitation link and create a new link.
- `POST /events/{eventId}/guests/{eventGuestId}/rsvp-responses` — staff-record a response from an outside channel.
- `GET /events/{eventId}/guests/{eventGuestId}/rsvp-responses` — permissioned response history.
- `POST /events/{eventId}/guests/{eventGuestId}/rsvp-responses/{responseId}/corrections` — append a correcting response with reason; never mutate the original row.

All staff routes require event-scoped permissions. Public routes are enabled only when the event has guest participation and guest self-service RSVP enabled.

## 8. Permissions and responsibility

Suggested permissions (exact naming is subject to the authorization catalogue):
- `event.guests.read`
- `event.invitations.issue`
- `event.invitations.resend`
- `event.invitations.revoke`
- `event.rsvp.read`
- `event.rsvp.record`
- `event.rsvp.override_deadline`
- `event.rsvp.export`
- `event.rsvp.policy.manage`

The module/task owner is explicit. The venue provider can see only its booking and venue-service fields unless it has been assigned the relevant guest-operation task and granted scoped access. An event organizer can operate RSVP for the event it owns. A third-party registration contractor may receive a restricted task-specific role. A booking relationship alone grants no guest-data access.

If the organizer operates invitations through its own system, the venue provider may retain a booking-only record and receive only the venue service information needed to perform its obligations. There is no requirement to synchronize the organizer's entire guest list into a venue-provider Eventor deployment.

## 9. Operational UI behavior

When guest participation or RSVP is disabled:
- Hide guest list, invitations, RSVP panels and guest portal routes from that event workspace.
- Do not show empty RSVP statistics as if an RSVP operation were expected.
- Do not require guest contact fields on the venue booking form.
- Keep booking contacts separate from event guests.

When RSVP is enabled:
- Event guest list shows independent columns for participation, invitation/delivery, RSVP response and attendance.
- Show invitation delivery failure separately from pending response.
- Provide filters for no response/overdue, accepted, declined, tentative (if enabled), no invitation and delivery failure.
- Show the effective deadline and timezone.
- Provide bulk issue/reminder/resend only with preview and scoped permission.
- Display response history and source/operator on the staff detail view.
- Use an explicit correction/late-override workflow, not inline edits that erase history.

## 10. Security, privacy and retention

- Token material is generated with a CSPRNG; only a one-way hash is retained.
- Token scope is one event guest and invitation purpose.
- Admission credentials and invitation credentials are distinct.
- No public guest directory/search endpoint exists.
- Guest responses are isolated by organization/event and are never exposed to the venue merely because it provided the space.
- Public event details and response options are an allow-listed projection.
- Rate-limit resolve and response endpoints; use generic failure messages to reduce token enumeration.
- Do not store bearer tokens, full invitation URLs or raw request bodies in logs, analytics, traces or audit events.
- Use TLS, secure cookies, CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated writes, strict response schemas and a no-referrer policy.
- Minimize IP/user-agent retention; any abuse/security metadata is separate, access-controlled and retention-limited.
- Guest export, access, correction and deletion/retention requests follow organization policy and applicable law. Eventor does not invent universal retention periods.

## 11. Acceptance scenarios

1. A venue-provider-only booking is created, quoted, confirmed and fulfilled without an operational event, event guest, invitation, RSVP or attendee contact list.
2. An organizer creates an operational event and enables guest participation but disables invitations/RSVP; staff may still manage event guests for seating or check-in.
3. An organizer enables RSVP and emails a personalized invite. The guest can resolve the link, read only their own approved context and submit an answer without creating an account.
4. A security scanner performs GET on the invitation URL; no response is recorded and the link remains usable.
5. The guest changes an answer before the configured deadline; both answers remain in history and the latest effective answer is shown.
6. The deadline passes; guest self-service changes are rejected according to policy while the previous answer remains intact.
7. An authorized staff member records a telephone/in-person/email/written/representative response without an invitation. The source, received time, recorded time, operator and note/reason are retained.
8. A correction appends a new response; the original response remains auditable.
9. A staff member without late-override permission cannot record a late response as an ordinary change.
10. Invitation delivery fails but a staff member later records a confirmation; delivery failure and RSVP confirmation remain separate.
11. A revoked, expired or replaced link cannot resolve or submit a response.
12. The invitation link cannot authenticate an admission QR scan or access another guest.
13. RSVP acceptance does not create attendance. Check-in is a separate authorized action and can differ from RSVP.
14. GHB acting only as venue provider sees booking/service data but no organizer guest list, invitation history, RSVP answers or organizer-only prerequisites.
15. In a hybrid operation, the venue team sees only the subset of guest/service data explicitly assigned to its task; the organizer retains control of its guest records.

## 12. Decisions still needed before implementation

The domain architecture is specified, but event owners must confirm operational defaults:
- Whether tentative response is enabled by default or disabled per event.
- Default response deadline and reminder cadence.
- Whether secondary verification is required for any class of events.
- Whether invitation delivery is email-only in MVP or allows additional channels.
- Whether guests may update RSVP after first submission until deadline (recommended default: yes).
- Whether RSVP can be recorded for a representative and which details are necessary.
- Event-specific response questions (for example meal requirements) and data retention for answers.

These are configuration/organization-policy choices where possible, not hardcoded global assumptions. Only questions that affect security, access control, schema semantics or contractual workflow need to block the technical design.

## Approved CID channel-independent distribution clarification — 2026-11-27

[CID v1.0](COMMUNICATION_INVITATION_DISTRIBUTION_AND_MULTI_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESIGN_v1.0.md) elaborates invitation issuance and distribution as independent explicit authorized operations. Retain existing email issue/send/reissue routes, invitation/RSVP state dimensions, current valid opaque scoped capability, revisioned RSVP policy, deadlines, non-destructive link resolution, history and separate admission credentials. Extend issuance to eligible guests without email or any electronic contact; authorized manual link/print/handover/postal/representative/telephone workflows, with separate delivery evidence and staff-recorded RSVP using existing response commands. Distribution through another approved channel does not silently reissue a credential, reset RSVP or count attendance. Never expose bearer links in ordinary history/export/logs; private controlled rendering/share only. Provider routing honors purpose, verified contact/relationship, eligibility, consent, budget, fixed review digest and revocation. Resend means another approved delivery attempt; replacement is a separate reviewed revocation/issuance. Provider acceptance/read/physical handover is not RSVP. Preserve existing email baseline and all acceptance criteria; future channel choices and engineering review follow CID-M0–M7. This is an approved scope clarification, not a runtime or acceptance claim. Preserve all existing requirements, accepted ADRs, historical Blueprint v1.2, current #104/#112 → #105–107 sequence and established #110/#111/#108 roadmap; no immediate implementation or environment republication. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

## Approved adaptive setup, intake and guest-service clarification — 2026-11-27

[AES v1.0](ADAPTIVE_EXPERIENCE_AND_SETUP_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [FRS v1.0](FORMS_REGISTRATION_AND_SUBMISSION_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [HPG v1.0](HOSPITALITY_PROTOCOL_AND_GUEST_SERVICES_DESIGN_v1.0.md) and [RAI v1.0](REPORTING_ANALYTICS_AND_INTELLIGENCE_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) preserve distinct submission, reviewed participation, invitation issuance/distribution, RSVP, service requests, admission and attendance lifecycles. Quick Start selects existing policies/templates and invokes existing authorized invitation commands; no implicit sends. FRS supports versioned RSVP questions and separate reviewed registration/intake, no auto-merge or RSVP on application alone. HPG uses minimal approved RSVP/demand projections and cannot mark attendance. RAI reports denominator, policy revision and snapshot/source freshness without treating application, acceptance or delivered invitation as arrival. Use CID for actual communications. Approved additive scope only; retain existing requirements, accepted ADRs, Blueprint v1.2, PROJECT_STATE and the #104/#112 → #105–107 → #110/#111/#108 development sequence. No immediate implementation, unrelated closure gates, environment republication or Blueprint v1.3 consolidation. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

# Implementation Design v0.3 — domain design addenda

**Status:** proposed detailed domain/API designs; successor migrations, API contract validation and implementation remain open.

This directory contains successor design addenda that refine the historical v0.2 design snapshot. They do not modify or replace the v0.2 SQL/OpenAPI artifacts.

## Contents

- [RSVP and Invitation Design v0.3](RSVP_AND_INVITATION_DESIGN_v0.3.md) — state separation, event policy, secure links, guest self-service, staff capture, proposed data model, API routes, access control, operating scope and acceptance scenarios.
- [Cross-Organization Collaboration Design v0.3](CROSS_ORGANIZATION_COLLABORATION_DESIGN_v0.3.md) — venue-provider/organizer ownership, booking-event links, scoped collaboration grants and immutable venue-plan snapshots.
- [OpenAPI v0.3 contract](../../api/openapi.v0.3.yaml) — concrete contract draft aligned to the API design and the v0.3 domain addenda.
- [Cancellation and Event Disruption Design v0.3](CANCELLATION_AND_EVENT_DISRUPTION_DESIGN_v0.3.md) — booking cancellation by customer or venue provider, event cancellation/postponement by organizer, notification audiences, cross-organization boundaries, audit and acceptance scenarios.

- [Template Design Studio v1.0](TEMPLATE_DESIGN_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) — approved Phase 7 scope for rich-text WYSIWYG, responsive block email and graphical invitation/card design; implementation/library decisions deferred to #111. No change to current coding priorities.

# Architecture overview

**Status:** proposed baseline, pending reconciliation with Implementation Design v0.2 and subsequent ADRs.

## Shape

Eventor is a modular monolith with independently deployable frontend entry points and background/optimization processes where operationally justified. Modules share one domain model and PostgreSQL database through explicit application boundaries; they are not independent microservices.

```
Staff Web ───────┐
Guest Portal ────┼── HTTPS ── Fastify API ── PostgreSQL
Check-in PWA ────┘                 │              │
                                  ├── Worker ─────┘
                                  ├── WebSocket / transactional outbox
                                  └── C++ OR-Tools optimization process
```

All database access is server-side. The API is authoritative for validation, workflow transitions, permissions and audit records.

## Operating scope and module activation

A deployment may be used by a venue provider, an event organizer, or a hybrid operator. Organization configuration establishes a default profile; an individual booking/event can override it. Profiles are defaults, not product tiers. A venue booking remains valid without an operational event record. Full event operations are explicitly activated only when needed.

Distinguish venue provider, booking customer/requester, contracting party, event organizer and operational operator. These roles may differ. Module/task responsibility is assigned explicitly to an accountable party and performing parties; scoped collaboration is granted deliberately and never inferred from a booking relationship. The venue provider retains its own facility/resource and contracted service responsibilities; Eventor does not transfer legal duties.

Modules such as guest participation, invitations/RSVP, seating, guest portal, check-in, external prerequisites and event-day cockpit are independently optional. Module dependencies are narrow and explicit. For example, venue booking does not depend on guest registry or RSVP. Public and staff projections collect and expose only information needed for the enabled scope.

See [Operating Model](OPERATING_MODEL.md) and [ADR 0004](decisions/0004-optional-event-operations-scope.md).

## Logical modules

- Identity, authentication, sessions and authorization.
- Organization, venue and event management.
- Configuration registry: forms, catalogues, services, equipment, prices, workflow and branding revisions.
- Booking inquiry, draft, offer, approval and confirmed booking (independent of operational-event conversion).
- Optional guest registry, event participation, invitations and RSVP.
- Venue/spatial inventory and venue-side floor plans/resources; optional event allocation and seating.
- Optional guest portal, QR credential issuance and check-in.
- Optional event prerequisites and external coordination.
- Optional event operations cockpit, notifications, audit and reporting.
- Import/export, document generation and background jobs.

## Frontends

- Staff web: administrative and operational workspaces.
- Guest portal: personalized, public-facing PWA with narrowly scoped data.
- Check-in PWA: staff-authorized scanning and attendance operations.

They may share UI and contract packages but must not share privileged data projections indiscriminately.

## Data and integration

- PostgreSQL is the source of truth.
- Migrations are forward-only and reviewed; destructive changes require explicit data migration strategy.
- WebSocket messages are published from a transactional outbox to avoid committing database state without corresponding event publication.
- Long-running imports, notifications, document rendering and optimization execute asynchronously.
- Email is an initial invitation delivery channel behind a provider abstraction. Do not bind the domain to a specific SaaS provider.
- Public access is limited to explicitly allowlisted portal/RSVP/booking endpoints through a reverse proxy. Admin interfaces and internal APIs remain private unless separately approved.

## Optimization boundary

The C++ OR-Tools CP-SAT process receives a validated, versioned allocation problem and returns a proposal, objective/diagnostics and assignment result. The API checks the result against current state and permissions. A human previews and explicitly commits the proposal. The solver cannot directly mutate authoritative booking or allocation records.

## Security boundaries

- Tenant/organization/venue/event scope is enforced server-side.
- RBAC is supplemented by field- and operation-level authorization.
- Public guest views are purpose-built projections; no general-purpose guest API is exposed publicly.
- Invitation and check-in tokens are different credentials with different scopes and revocation.
- Audit records cover privileged access, sensitive changes, manual RSVP entry, booking approval and check-in correction.
- Uploads are quarantined and validated before downstream processing.
- Real personal data and sensitive venue/security details are excluded from source control and test fixtures.

## Deployment

Target is self-hosted Linux. Deployment may use native packages/systemd and a reverse proxy. Containers may be used optionally, but no architectural requirement depends on Docker, Redis/Valkey or a cloud service. Exact deployment topology, backup/restore and observability standards require separate implementation decisions.

## Planned Template Design Studio (Phase 7)

See [Template Design Studio v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/TEMPLATE_DESIGN_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) and [#111](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/111). Three authoring modes share revisioned templates, brand/assets, locale variants, typed purpose-specific data bindings and audit. Extend existing notification template identities and delivery paths; do not create a competing email aggregate. Server-authoritative rendering uses a bounded isolated worker with private artifacts and no general network or database access. Preview, render and publication never issue credentials or trigger delivery; existing domain commands remain authoritative. Specific editor/renderer libraries and schema/API design require the M0 review and ADR. This is planned functionality, not current runtime or a change to implementation order.

## Planned Platform Administration Center

See [PAC v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md). Separate deployment-level management session/ingress, safe global metadata and explicit scoped tenant transitions under the real actor; reuse existing identity, memberships, domain services and TDS brand/asset revisions. Host-only bootstrap and recovery remain outside runtime. Typed approved host operation requests are not shell execution; no owner/migrator credentials, root or unrestricted Docker socket in the web app. Existing ADRs 0015/0017/0020 remain accepted; proposed managed-permission reconciliation requires a reviewed successor ADR, populated upgrade, independent-grant preservation and recovery tests before any implementation. This is planned scope, not a runtime claim or priority change.

## Organization Administration Center and shared experience (approved scope, 2026-11-27)

See [OAC v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/ORGANIZATION_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [UX v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/EVENTOR_USER_EXPERIENCE_AND_NAVIGATION_v1.0.md) and [organization lifecycle acceptance v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/ORGANIZATION_LIFECYCLE_ACCEPTANCE_SCENARIOS_v1.0.md). PAC, OAC and EOC are separate authorization/context boundaries in the same modular monolith, not independent products or a chain of inherited privileges. PAC provisions the organization and first administrator; OAC owns tenant self-service orchestration, readiness, permission-filtered overview and navigation; EOC owns the selected event operational experience. Reuse existing domain commands and data models, shared TDS brand/assets, notification and identity services; readiness is derived from server-validated configuration per capability, not an editable checklist. ADR 0008 requires incremental shell/composable/feature evolution; navigation hints never authorize actions. Preserve ADR 0015 and PAC's proposed successor authority review. Owner approved the three v1.0 scopes for documentation integration on 2026-11-27. The three reviewed source files are preserved verbatim, including their historical proposed-status text; this approval record governs their integration status, not approval of exact engineering decisions or immediate implementation. Existing accepted ADRs, historical Blueprint v1.2/v0.2 snapshots, issue obligations and current #104/#112 → #105–107 priorities remain unchanged. No runtime implementation or acceptance results are implied.

## Admission, guest information and station management — approved scope (2026-11-27)

[AGIS v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/ADMISSION_GUEST_INFORMATION_AND_STATION_MANAGEMENT_DESIGN_v1.0.md) establishes six purpose-bound station modes in the existing API-first modular monolith: entrance/gate, self-service and staffed Info Pult, seating assistance, printing and passive information display. PAC governs deployment policy and recovery; OAC owns tenant station/profile/device administration; EOC owns event/session assignments and live operations. Reuse migration 000014 admission credentials, check-in stations/attempts and attendance records, allocation revisions, guest portal, TDS brand/assets/rendering and transactional outbox. Audit current SQL and runtime boundaries before adding compatible extensions. No parallel attendance, identity, spatial or rendering engine. Staff, station/device, kiosk guest and public display contexts have independent server-enforced scope. A lookup, RSVP, preview or print never records attendance; only the authorized check-in command can do so. Separate online authority, encrypted bounded deferred capture and time-limited local-validation packages per Blueprint §13.4; offline validation is provisional until reconciled. Station Designer uses typed allowlisted components and actions, not arbitrary code. This is an approved scope clarification, not a runtime implementation claim or instruction to interrupt the existing #104/#112 → #105–107 sequence. Preserve accepted ADRs, historical Blueprint v1.2, existing domain commands and issue criteria; final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

## Communication, invitation distribution and multi-channel delivery — approved scope (2026-11-27)

[CID v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/COMMUNICATION_INVITATION_DISTRIBUTION_AND_MULTI_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESIGN_v1.0.md) extends the existing API-first modular monolith and transactional outbox. Domain intent, reviewed content/audience, channel/provider route, submission attempt, delivery evidence and recipient action are distinct. Wrap existing SMTP and preserve event notification, booking-offer email and invitation delivery identities, authorization, leases, idempotency, encryption and signed Resend reconciliation; converge through reviewed compatible interfaces, not a competing queue or identity/template aggregate. PAC optionally governs shared provider services, explicit tenant grants and budgets; OAC owns tenant provider accounts, sender identity, consent/preferences, campaigns and distribution tasks. TDS supplies immutable typed channel content/brand revisions; AGIS owns admission/lookup/print semantics. Support SMTP/HTTP email, OAuth, SMS, official WhatsApp/Viber, optional Telegram, opt-in push, scoped in-app and manual/print/physical/telephone distribution. Only owning domain commands change RSVP, bookings, grants, event decisions or attendance. A provider acceptance is not delivery; uncertain sends block blind retry/fallback. Fixed review digests, authorization rechecks, verified callbacks, reserved budgets/quotas and safe restore are mandatory. This is an approved scope clarification, not a runtime or acceptance claim. Preserve all existing requirements, accepted ADRs, historical Blueprint v1.2, current #104/#112 → #105–107 sequence and established #110/#111/#108 roadmap; no immediate implementation or environment republication. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

## Coordinated adaptive experience, planning, forms, hospitality and reporting — approved scope (2026-11-27)

[AES v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/ADAPTIVE_EXPERIENCE_AND_SETUP_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [EPW v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/EVENT_PLANNING_PRODUCTION_AND_OPERATIONAL_WORKFLOWS_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [FRS v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/FORMS_REGISTRATION_AND_SUBMISSION_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [HPG v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/HOSPITALITY_PROTOCOL_AND_GUEST_SERVICES_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [RAI v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/REPORTING_ANALYTICS_AND_INTELLIGENCE_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) extend the existing modular monolith, not five independent applications. AES orchestrates existing draft/setup commands and permission-aware projections, with one event identity across Quick Start, Guided and Advanced modes. EPW owns production plans, schedule/task/dependency/shift coordination and constrained approval instances, reusing existing event/session, resource reservation, task and approval authority. FRS owns typed form revisions and purpose-bound intake/review, reusing booking forms and invoking owning commands for reviewed registration/identity/RSVP/task/service actions. HPG owns event-specific service demand, request/arrangement/fulfillment history, delegation/protocol and minimal actionable projections; Registry, allocation, booking and attendance remain canonical. RAI owns approved typed datasets, versioned metric definitions, read projections, dashboard/report definitions and private artifacts; no arbitrary SQL, unrestricted joins, surveillance or autonomous decisions. TDS owns branded content/rendering, CID owns reviewed external delivery/evidence, AGIS owns credentials/stations/attendance, OAC/PAC own scoped configuration/governance, OLA owns evidence framework. Domain authority, RLS, tenant-aware references, immutable revisions, idempotency, review digests, outbox, revocation rechecks, private artifact storage and protected host operation remain shared. Approved additive scope only; retain existing requirements, accepted ADRs, Blueprint v1.2, PROJECT_STATE and the #104/#112 → #105–107 → #110/#111/#108 development sequence. No immediate implementation, unrelated closure gates, environment republication or Blueprint v1.3 consolidation. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

# Eventor operating model

This document describes how Eventor can support venue providers, event organizers and collaborative operations without making every deployment use every module.

See [ADR 0004](decisions/0004-optional-event-operations-scope.md) and [Issue #8](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/8).

## Three common operating profiles

### Venue provider

A venue provider rents spaces and supplies venue-side services. Its normal Eventor workflow is:

1. Receive a simple inquiry.
2. Review requested date, time, venue, expected attendance where needed, equipment/services and contact details.
3. Prepare a booking draft, offer or approval.
4. Confirm the booking and reserve venue/resources.
5. Prepare and deliver the agreed venue-side services.
6. Close/cancel/amend the booking as appropriate.

This workflow does **not** require creating a full operational event. It does not require the provider to manage the renter's guest registry, invitations, RSVP, seating, admission check-in or external organizer protocols.

A provider may ask for a small amount of operational information where it is needed for its own venue services, risk controls, contractual requirements or facility rules. That is not the same as taking responsibility for organizing the event.

### Event organizer

An organizer uses Eventor to coordinate the event itself. It can enable the capabilities that apply to the event, such as guest records, invitations/RSVP, seating, check-in, prerequisite tracking, live operations, staff tasks and reporting.

The organizer does not need to enable every capability for every event. A small lecture may need registration and attendance but no assigned seating; a private meeting may need a room booking only.

### Hybrid or collaborative event

A venue provider may operate the booking and venue-side tasks while an organizer operates guest and event workflows. In other cases, the venue may provide a paid service such as registration staff or seating assistance.

Eventor should allow each task/module to have an explicit owner and participants rather than assuming all operations belong to one organization.

## Keep party identities separate

These roles must not be collapsed into a single "organization" field:

| Role | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Venue provider | Supplies the physical space and venue-side services |
| Booking customer/requester | Initiates or manages the booking request |
| Contracting party | Enters the agreement and may be the payer |
| Event organizer | Actually organizes the event and its programme |
| Operational operator | Performs one or more specific tasks |

One organization may hold several roles, but the records must allow them to differ. For example, an event agency might submit an inquiry for a client, the client may sign/pay, and a third party may organize the programme.

## Module activation and dependencies

Organization profile establishes defaults. Each booking or event can override those defaults and enable only needed capabilities.

| Capability | Venue-provider default | Organizer use |
|---|---|---|
| Inquiry, quote and booking | On | Optional |
| Venue/resource calendar | On | Optional |
| Venue setup/service delivery | On as applicable | Optional |
| Guest registry and event participation | Off | Optional/on as needed |
| Invitations and RSVP | Off | Optional/on as needed |
| Seating and guest allocation | Off | Optional/on as needed |
| Guest portal / wayfinding | Off | Optional/on as needed |
| Admission QR and check-in | Off | Optional/on as needed |
| External prerequisites | Off | Optional/on as needed |
| Live event operations cockpit | Off | Optional/on as needed |
| Event reports and communications | Off | Optional/on as needed |

These are defaults, not locked restrictions. A venue provider may activate registration/check-in as a contracted service, and an organizer may have no need for seating.

Module dependencies should remain narrow:
- Guest RSVP requires event participation and a response channel, but not seating.
- Seating can work with event participants or a deliberately modeled allocation subject set; it does not require invitation delivery.
- Check-in requires an admission/attendance subject and credential or authorized manual lookup; it does not require seating or RSVP.
- External prerequisites can exist independently of guest management and must remain optional.
- A venue booking requires no operational-event conversion.

## Responsibility assignments

For every enabled task or module, the event workspace should be able to identify:
- Accountable party.
- Performing party/person/team.
- Approver, if required.
- Informed parties.
- Scope of information each party may see.
- Due date/readiness rule, if applicable.
- Whether it is not applicable or managed outside Eventor.

The venue provider remains responsible for its own facility, resource availability, house rules and contracted venue-side services. The organizer is responsible for the event tasks assigned to it. Eventor records this division; it does not decide legal liability or replace contractual/regulatory advice.

## Example: independent conference at GHB

GHB acts only as venue provider. A conference organizer books the large hall.

**GHB needs in its booking workspace:** organizer/customer name and booking contacts, date/time and duration, selected hall, expected attendance where relevant to venue policy, requested setup/equipment/services, rehearsal/setup/teardown needs, agreed price and booking status.

**Not required for GHB's booking workflow:** attendee names, guests' emails/phones, invitation tokens, RSVP results, guest-to-seat allocations, admission scans, organizer's police coordination documents or the full conference operations cockpit.

The conference organizer can manage those independently. If the organizer later chooses Eventor, it can use its own Eventor deployment or receive explicit scoped access to agreed modules/data. That access is never automatic.

## Product boundary

Eventor is both:
- A venue booking/resource management system when that is all the customer needs.
- A configurable event operations platform when the customer is organizing or operating the event.

This is a product configuration and responsibility model, not a paywall or separate codebase.

## Independent organization lifecycle (approved scope, 2026-11-27)

[OAC v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/ORGANIZATION_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md) and [UX v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/EVENTOR_USER_EXPERIENCE_AND_NAVIGATION_v1.0.md) define PAC provisioning → secure administrator enrollment → credential-first sign-in → resumable profile-specific setup → independently validated capability readiness → explicit publication/activation → independent staff, venue, booking, event, communication and governance workflows → controlled suspension/restoration/offboarding. Provider, organizer and hybrid are defaults, not commercial tiers; enable only supported permitted capabilities and minimal dependencies. Provider-only bookings do not require guest data or an operational event. Routine tenant administration must not require platform-owner intervention or SQL; protected host bootstrap/recovery remains available. Role and tenant ownership remain explicit, and collaboration requires reviewed grants. The [lifecycle acceptance scenarios](implementation-design/v0.3/ORGANIZATION_LIFECYCLE_ACCEPTANCE_SCENARIOS_v1.0.md) verify this journey with synthetic fixtures; actual GHB configuration is not presumed. Owner approved the three v1.0 scopes for documentation integration on 2026-11-27. The three reviewed source files are preserved verbatim, including their historical proposed-status text; this approval record governs their integration status, not approval of exact engineering decisions or immediate implementation. Existing accepted ADRs, historical Blueprint v1.2/v0.2 snapshots, issue obligations and current #104/#112 → #105–107 priorities remain unchanged. No runtime implementation or acceptance results are implied.

## Approved coordinated capability and responsibility clarification — 2026-11-27

[AES v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/ADAPTIVE_EXPERIENCE_AND_SETUP_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [EPW v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/EVENT_PLANNING_PRODUCTION_AND_OPERATIONAL_WORKFLOWS_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [FRS v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/FORMS_REGISTRATION_AND_SUBMISSION_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [HPG v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/HOSPITALITY_PROTOCOL_AND_GUEST_SERVICES_DESIGN_v1.0.md), [RAI v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/REPORTING_ANALYTICS_AND_INTELLIGENCE_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) apply progressive complexity independently of provider/organizer/hybrid operating profile. A venue provider may use basic bookings, preparation tasks, forms and permitted reports without guest records; the organizer owns its event participation, registration, hospitality, allocation and admission. Explicit collaboration grants and accepted assignments expose only the task/service projection, never inferred authority from a booking or event link. Quick Start is a UX choice, not a role or subscription tier; activation/readiness does not confer access. EPW tasks/approval steps, FRS submissions, HPG service arrangements and RAI metrics cannot mutate owning domain facts except via independently authorized commands. Approved additive scope only; retain existing requirements, accepted ADRs, Blueprint v1.2, PROJECT_STATE and the #104/#112 → #105–107 → #110/#111/#108 development sequence. No immediate implementation, unrelated closure gates, environment republication or Blueprint v1.3 consolidation. Final integrated acceptance remains Phase 9.

# Eventor delivery roadmap

**Baseline date:** 2026-11-16  
**Product/design baseline:** Technical Blueprint v1.2 and accepted v0.3 domain/architecture decisions.  
**Implementation baseline:** `main` at `06d47b255c7107b94201c191da562ea2612e57c1` (PR #201). See [current state](PROJECT_STATE.md) for verification receipts.
**Detailed audit:** [Blueprint-to-repository gap analysis v1.0](BLUEPRINT_TO_REPOSITORY_GAP_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md).

## Current integration note — 2026-11-23

- Event administration, session lifecycle, persistent Guest Registry and event participation are usable from the bilingual staff workspace.
- Staff can review mapped CSV/XLSX imports, resolve matches by name or exact source reference, review proposed profile updates, and download filtered exports and import reports.
- Access administration includes organization profile settings, member search, scoped event roles and suspension/restoration. Provider disruption notices can be recorded and reviewed; cross-party delivery and acknowledgement remain open.
- The current product implementation track is #104, followed by venue geometry, allocation and admission under #105–#107. Issue #112 covers the remaining disruption coordination.
- Native and Docker production installation paths remain under #108. Current development Compose runs PostgreSQL only. Final acceptance remains scheduled for the integrated release candidate on the acceptance VM.

## Delivery principle

Build a coherent, usable Eventor product before final environment acceptance. Continue automated tests throughout development. Do not spend the next phase repeating already-completed external acceptance preparation while core user workflows remain absent.

The product remains an API-first modular monolith:
- Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite for staff and guest-facing interfaces.
- Fastify + TypeScript for the API and background workers.
- PostgreSQL as authoritative storage.
- SVG-based spatial model and editor.
- Transactional outbox and real-time publication.
- OR-Tools CP-SAT for advisory allocation proposals; a human must review and explicitly commit solver output.

## Phase 0 — Establish the current baseline

- [x] Merge the integrated PostgreSQL migration and feature stack (PR #85).
- [x] Merge worker and staff-session browser acceptance coverage (PR #99).
- [x] Merge guest invitation browser acceptance coverage (PR #101; mocked HTTP boundary).
- [x] Align invitation OpenAPI paths with runtime behavior (PR #102).
- [x] Audit Technical Blueprint v1.2 against actual runtime/API/UI/migrations/tests (PR #103).
- [x] Keep project-state, roadmap and issue tracker synchronized with the current implementation.
- [ ] Reconcile stale historical issues and PRs; do not mistake historical checklists for current status.

## Phase 1 — Complete a coherent venue-booking vertical

**Existing foundation:** public booking inquiries and forms, staff inquiry review, booking drafts/revisions, commercial offer and approval foundations, pricing/tax/cancellation configuration, resource reservations, notification campaigns and delivery worker.

- [ ] Audit each booking lifecycle transition against the v0.3 domain design and identify any remaining runtime/UI gaps.
- [ ] Complete direct/manual booking creation where not already covered.
- [ ] Complete offer revision, customer acceptance/rejection, approval and confirmation as one demonstrable workflow.
- [ ] Complete cancellation, amendment and postponement workflows with resource release and immutable commercial snapshots.
- [ ] Complete venue-side fulfilment/task assignment and responsibility history.
- [ ] Complete customer-facing booking communications and delivery reconciliation.
- [ ] Add operator-facing liveness/readiness and useful diagnostics.
- [ ] Define and automate end-to-end booking acceptance scenarios using synthetic fixtures.

## Phase 2 — Event organizer and Guest Registry foundation

- [x] Ship organizer event create/edit/archive, approval, publication, start and close, and session list/create/edit/schedule/start/complete.
- [x] Ship persistent Registry profile search, edit/archive, history, encrypted contacts, source references and organization-level relationships with scoped grants.
- [x] Link Registry profiles to independently managed event participations with pinned event identity.
- [x] Ship event categories, internal and restricted tags, groups and roles, guest relationships and encrypted custom fields.
- [x] Ship mapped CSV/XLSX name imports with review, protected exact reference matching, and downloadable diagnostics and exports.
- [x] Ship supervised and reversible merges for unlinked profiles and non-overlapping closed-event history.
- [x] Ship personal roster views and atomic bulk category, status and internal tag edits.
- [ ] Finish organization, user, membership and role administration, event settings and session disruption workflows.
- [x] Extend reference imports to create profiles for authorized staff reviewing unmatched references.
- [ ] Add reviewed merge resolution for contacts, identifiers, active relationships and open or overlapping events.
- [x] Extend roster filtering and bulk management and add group allocation preferences and group-to-group relationships.
- [x] Verify signed-in provider isolation and event-scoped guest access, including grant revocation and Registry restrictions.
- [ ] Complete organizer/venue collaboration acceptance across booking, disruption and operational workflows.

**Planned platform administration refinement:** [PAC v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION_CENTER_DESIGN_v1.0.md) defines PAC-M0–M2 for reviewed authority, organization/global account administration and a dedicated control-plane workspace, reusing #104. No immediate authentication rewrite; ADR 0015/0017/0020 remain in force until a reviewed successor decision and migration. Existing #104/#112 → #105–107 priorities remain unchanged.

## Phase 3 — Venue model and spatial editor

- [ ] Implement reusable venue/building/level/room/space hierarchy and versioned venue templates.
- [ ] Support halls, rooms, mosque/prayer spaces and other configured layouts without hardcoding one venue.
- [ ] Implement source-plan onboarding for PDF/image/SVG and workbook references, preserving originals and requiring human review.
- [ ] Build the SVG spatial editor with scale calibration, layers, geometry, labels and reusable objects.
- [ ] Model tables, rows, prayer rows, individual positions, capacity zones and non-allocatable features distinctly.
- [ ] Support color-coded tableless zones and mixed precise/count-based capacity.
- [ ] Add map revisions, approval, publication, history and printable output.
- [ ] Ensure accessibility and keyboard alternatives to drag-and-drop editing.

## Phase 4 — Guest seating and allocation

- [ ] Implement manual assignment and movement first.
- [ ] Implement category/group-based allocation and capacity validation.
- [ ] Implement together/avoid, preferences, exclusions, distance/session and other hard/soft constraints.
- [ ] Implement locks, diagnostics, conflicts and targeted reflow.
- [ ] Add OR-Tools CP-SAT worker behind a versioned, validated input/output contract.
- [ ] Present solver output as a proposal with explanation and before/after diff.
- [ ] Require explicit authorized human commit; never silently apply optimization.
- [ ] Publish immutable allocation-plan revisions and provide live staff and printable plan views.
- [ ] Render sanitized guest-facing map/wayfinding views.

## Phase 5 — Guest portal, invitations and admission

**Existing foundation:** capability-protected invitation links, RSVP, staff-recorded response/correction and invitation management UI.

- [ ] Complete batch invitations, reminders, delivery controls and full guest communication history.
- [ ] Build branded guest portal/PWA with event information and personal permitted data.
- [ ] Show the guest's own allocation and safe map/wayfinding, including accessibility information.
- [ ] Design and implement a separate admission credential lifecycle; invitation links are not admission passes.
- [ ] Generate revocable opaque QR credentials and printable guest cards.
- [ ] Implement gate scanning UI/PWA, station/operator management, manual lookup and correction.
- [ ] Prevent duplicate admission and preserve audit history across multiple gates.
- [ ] Add real-time synchronization and bounded offline tolerance with explicit reconciliation.
- [ ] Keep invitation, RSVP, eligibility and physical attendance as separate facts.

## Phase 6 — Event-day operations and collaboration

- [ ] Build the Live Event Operations Cockpit with role-scoped live metrics, map layers, alerts, timeline and interventions.
- [ ] Add role-specific reception, gate, seating, venue, floor/zone and management workspaces.
- [ ] Implement staff/vendor assignments, deliverables, deadlines, evidence and scoped collaboration.
- [ ] Implement external prerequisite/CDI tracking as a readiness checklist (request, responsible party, schedule, status, completion and restricted references).
- [ ] Add transactional-outbox-backed realtime updates and reconnect/resynchronization.
- [ ] Add read-only information display panels for welcome, session, venue, seating, directions and announcements.
- [ ] Add operational reports, exports, printable plans, guest cards and signage.

## Phase 7 — Communications, branding and configuration

- [ ] Deliver the [Template Design Studio v1.0](implementation-design/v0.3/TEMPLATE_DESIGN_STUDIO_DESIGN_v1.0.md) under #111: shared library, rich-text WYSIWYG, visual responsive drag-and-drop email design and precision graphical invitation/card design.
- [ ] Implement typed purpose-specific variables, reusable components/assets, versioned branding/locale variants, reviewed publication, secure server rendering and individual/bulk PDF/print layouts (TDS-M0–M6; AC-01–25). Admission/seating/map outputs depend on their owning workflows; basic invitation authoring does not.

**Scope clarification (2026-11-27):** this adds requirements to Phase 7, not a change of current priorities. Continue #104/#112, then #105–#107 as planned. Do not start Studio implementation merely because this documentation is merged. Preserve all existing Phase 7 acceptance requirements.

- [ ] Support plain text and HTML, variables, validation, preview, test-send, localization and revision history.
- [ ] Support approved bulk send, reminders, audience selection, retries and ambiguous-outcome reconciliation.
- [ ] Implement organization → venue → event branding inheritance and pinned asset/template revisions.
- [ ] Complete reusable forms and data/request submission workflows for guest registration and vendor/staff operations where required.
- [ ] Complete localization and accessibility across all user-facing modules.
- [ ] Add configurable reporting and document templates.

**PAC coordination:** PAC-M3/M4 add owner-controlled platform-default identity/theming, typed policy/module controls, data governance, scoped support and communications, sharing TDS brand/assets and existing domain commands under #111. Specialized interventions wait for owning workflows. No separate brand or delivery subsystem.

## Phase 8 — Installation, upgrade and operations

One release artifact must support two equivalent installation modes.

### Native Linux
- [ ] Dependency and supported-distribution detection.
- [ ] Dedicated service identities, filesystem permissions and secure secret provisioning.
- [ ] PostgreSQL setup/connection, migration and least-privilege role provisioning.
- [ ] API, worker and frontend deployment with systemd services.
- [ ] Reverse-proxy/HTTPS integration and trusted-proxy configuration.
- [ ] Initial administrator/bootstrap flow and configuration validation.
- [ ] Upgrade, rollback, backup/restore and service health commands.

### Docker Compose
- [ ] Production-oriented Compose topology for API, worker, frontend/reverse proxy and PostgreSQL as appropriate.
- [ ] Persistent volumes, non-root containers, health checks and dependency readiness.
- [ ] Secret/environment handling without committing credentials or baking them into images.
- [ ] Migration and initial-admin bootstrap workflow.
- [ ] Upgrade, rollback, backup/restore and log/health procedures.
- [ ] Document external reverse-proxy use and optional bundled proxy topology.

### Shared release requirements
- [ ] Both modes use the same application build, migrations, configuration schema and security defaults.
- [ ] Installer offers a clear native-versus-Docker choice and validates prerequisites before changing the host.
- [ ] Idempotent install/upgrade behavior and safe failure recovery.
- [ ] Document supported Linux versions, resource sizing, networking, SMTP and DNS/TLS options.
- [ ] Local email capture (for example, Mailpit) supported for development/testing; external SMTP is configurable, not mandatory for local development.

**PAC operations integration:** PAC-M5 under #108 covers measured health, backup manifests/restore drills, typed host-operation requests, local host maintenance/release recovery, same secure native and Compose procedures. PAC-M6 contributes AC-01–40 to Phase 9; no earlier VM requirement. The application must never receive arbitrary host privileges.

## Phase 9 — Integrated release candidate and final acceptance

**The `eventor-acceptance` QEMU/KVM VM is deliberately reserved for this final phase.** It is not the environment for early feature discovery.

- [ ] Freeze a coherent release candidate after Phases 1–8 are functionally complete.
- [ ] Run a clean native installation on the acceptance VM.
- [ ] Run a clean Docker Compose installation on the acceptance VM.
- [ ] Exercise upgrade and rollback paths for both deployment modes.
- [ ] Execute complete venue booking and organizer event workflows.
- [ ] Execute guest import, invitations, RSVP, seating, QR admission and multi-gate check-in.
- [ ] Exercise cockpit, vendor/staff coordination, CDI readiness and information displays.
- [ ] Test email capture and at least one external SMTP sandbox/provider.
- [ ] Validate public HTTPS with the intended reverse proxy/tunnel and domain.
- [ ] Rehearse representative database upgrade, off-host backup/restore, PITR and encryption-key recovery.
- [ ] Run security, tenant isolation, accessibility, browser/device, load and failure-recovery checks.
- [ ] Record evidence and unresolved limitations; do not claim production readiness without passing gates.

## Scope and product-owner dependencies

- The platform remains reusable and self-hosted; GHB is the first reference organization, not a hardcoded product boundary.
- Booking-only venue-provider use must remain possible without activating organizer guest/event capabilities.
- Venue facts, capacities, prices, approval authorities, cancellation terms and operational policies require owner confirmation before being enforced as GHB-specific configuration.
- The application records external coordination and assigned responsibilities; it does not implement law-enforcement or inspection activity.
- No real guest information, credentials, invitation tokens, private venue drawings or operationally sensitive source material may be committed.

## Current priority

Proceed with **Phase 1 audit/closure and Phase 2 event/Guest Registry foundation**. Do not start the acceptance VM stage until the application and both installers form a coherent release candidate.

# Blueprint-to-repository gap analysis — v1.0

**Audit baseline:** `main` at `a0a346268016079d58756bd95e7af2b87ccc4fec` (2026-11-18).

**Blueprint:** Technical Blueprint v1.2  
**Purpose:** establish what exists in the repository, what is only a design/schema foundation, what is partially usable, and what remains to be built before Eventor is a ready-to-use event operations product.

This is a static repository audit of the source tree, API route registrations, Vue application composition, migrations, tests and deployment files. It is not a claim that every existing workflow has been manually exercised. CI evidence and the separate external-acceptance record remain authoritative for what has actually been tested.

## 1. Executive assessment

Eventor is **not yet a complete event operations application**. The current implementation is materially weighted toward the venue-booking/commercial vertical. It has a substantial PostgreSQL/security foundation, working staff authentication, a Vue staff shell, public booking inquiry forms, booking inquiry/draft/offer workflows, commercial configuration, notification campaigns/delivery, a meaningful invitation/RSVP slice, and an integrated booking-cancellation request/review/approved-execution workflow with a public customer request/status journey.

The organizer workspace now supports event and session lifecycle, persistent guest profiles, event rosters, mapped imports, exports, supervised merge and roster organization. The spatial editor, guest allocation, admission, check-in, operations cockpit, branding and external prerequisites still need product workflows.

A usable slice connects the role-scoped API and staff or guest interface. The matrix records the remaining work within each slice.

### Status vocabulary

- **Implemented (usable slice):** runtime API and user-facing workflow exist; scope may still have limitations.
- **Partial:** a meaningful runtime slice exists, but important workflow stages or product requirements are missing.
- **Foundation only:** schema, security primitives, design or tests exist, but there is no complete runtime/user workflow.
- **Missing:** no meaningful implementation was found in the audited repository tree.
- **Not assessed:** requires venue-owner input, real deployment or runtime exercise beyond static GitHub inspection.

## 2. Product-area gap matrix

| Blueprint domain | Current repository evidence | Status | Main gap to close |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform, tenancy, authentication and authorization | PostgreSQL migrations 000001–000015 and later hardening; RLS/least-privilege roles; Fastify staff sessions, CSRF/origin checks; staff login UI; audit commands and tests | **Partial / strong foundation** | Complete organization/user/membership administration, role assignment UX, event-scoped permission coverage, operational health/readiness and full admin workspace. |
| Venue booking and public inquiry | Public booking form projection/submission, spam/rate protections, inquiry inbox/detail, assignment/status/notes/history, draft conversion and revisions, allocation availability preview | **Implemented slice** | Finish and acceptance-test the end-to-end commercial booking lifecycle, fulfilment tasks and operational communications; distinguish requested, approved and delivered service. |
| Commercial offers, approval, pricing and tax | Offer lifecycle, approval policies, price lists, tax profiles/calculation, cancellation policies, public offer acceptance/rejection and booking reservation commands; staff views | **Implemented slice / needs end-to-end acceptance** | Close remaining workflow edges, customer-facing presentation, manual booking path, resource fulfilment and cancellation/change lifecycle acceptance. 
| Booking cancellation and disruption | Migrations 000115–000120; staff request queue/detail, approve/reject/return-for-changes, policy-pinned preview, approved execution with atomic reservation release, public single-use request capability and reusable read-only status capability | **Partial / implemented cancellation slice** | Complete venue/event disruption notices and follow-up projection, amendment/postponement lifecycle, and a dedicated public cancellation browser E2E journey. A customer request is not effective cancellation and does not move money. |
| Event administration and sessions | The bilingual Events workspace supports list/create/edit/archive, approval and publication, and event start and close. Sessions support list/create/edit, scheduling, start and completion.
