## 3. Concrete evidence and boundaries

### 3.1 Current staff application

The current staff navigation includes:
- Email delivery configuration.
- Campaign review and delivery operations.
- Guest invitation management (including staff RSVP capture/correction).
- Booking inquiry workspace.
- Booking approval policies.
- Booking forms.
- Price lists.
- Cancellation policies.
- Booking cancellation request/review workspace.
- Tax profiles.
- Organization locale settings.
- Organizer event and session administration.
- Guest Registry, event roster and import/export.

This is a real staff application, not a blank shell. However, it is not yet the blueprint's event operations cockpit or the complete navigation/workspace map.

### 3.2 Runtime API boundary

The current API route families include booking forms/inquiries/drafts/offers, price/tax/approval/cancellation policies, booking reservation commands, staff booking-cancellation review/detail/decision/preview/execution, external booking-action capability issue/revoke/resolve, public cancellation request/status, organizer event administration, event invitation projections, guest invitation issue/revoke, guest RSVP and delivery configuration/campaign operations.

Guest Registry profiles, imports, restricted roster operations and permission-filtered exports have runtime API and staff UI paths. Venue/floor-plan editing, event guest allocation, admission QR, check-in stations, cockpit/realtime, external prerequisites, branding and vendor workspaces need runtime slices.

The current API has separate API and notification-worker entry points. The worker handles notification delivery; it is not the planned allocation solver or event-operations job platform.

### 3.3 Database maturity

Migrations 000124–000127 provide session administration and organizer lifecycle commands. Migrations 000128–000163 extend the existing person, participation and roster tables with tenant-scoped commands, protected fields and reviewed imports. CI covers PostgreSQL migrations, RLS, concurrency, populated upgrade and logical backup/restore.

### 3.4 Email and forms

There is already an email delivery configuration and test-send screen, campaign review/approval/queueing and delivery history. The campaign view displays the subject and body template for review, but no visual/template authoring interface was found. Likewise, public booking request forms are implemented; that does not mean guest registration forms, vendor forms or generic event submission forms are complete.

### 3.6 Booking cancellation and disruption boundary

The cancellation slice is now integrated rather than being only a schema foundation:
- Staff can review a tenant-scoped request queue, inspect authorized request history, approve/reject/return requests for changes, preview the pinned cancellation policy and exact reservation effects, and execute an approved cancellation.
- Approved execution is serialized on the booking and releases the exact booking reservations in the same transaction; the confirmed commercial snapshot and pinned policy revision remain auditable.
- A customer can submit a purpose-bound single-use request and receive a separate reusable, contact-scoped, read-only status capability. Only token hashes are persisted; the raw status token is returned by the API.
- Public tokens are carried in URL fragments, removed from browser history, omitted from cookies and redacted from request logs. The status link preserves the selected locale.

This is not the whole disruption domain. Venue/event cancellation notices, customer-facing follow-up, amendment/postponement workflows and a dedicated browser E2E test for the public cancellation journey remain outstanding. A customer request does not itself cancel a booking; no refund, fee, credit or other money movement is inferred or initiated.

### 3.5 QR and check-in distinction

Guest invitation links are capability-protected links for invitation/RSVP. They are not admission QR passes. Admission credentials need a separate lifecycle, scope, revocation model and scanning/check-in workflow. The current repository does not contain the gate-scanning product slice.

## 4. Recommended implementation sequence

The following order prioritizes a coherent, usable product and avoids building acceptance infrastructure around unfinished workflows.

### Track A — Complete the venue-booking product vertical

1. Reconcile current booking implementation against the accepted Release 1 scope.
2. Finish remaining booking lifecycle edges: manual booking, offer revision/approval/acceptance, confirmation, amendment/postponement and venue/event disruption notices. The staff/public cancellation request and approved-execution slice is integrated; it still needs dedicated browser E2E and full disruption follow-up acceptance.
3. Complete venue-side fulfilment tasks and assigned responsibility workflows.
4. Complete booking communication/template authoring and operational history.
5. Add health/readiness and operator-facing diagnostics.

### Track B — Build the event organizer foundation

6. Complete organization/user/membership and role administration, event settings and session disruption handling.
7. Extend the delivered Guest Registry and import workflows with reviewed resolution of linked records and more import fields.
8. Extend roster configuration, group allocation preferences, bulk controls and permission-scoped acceptance.
9. Extend invitations/RSVP to batches, reminders and the full guest portal journey.

### Track C — Venue geometry, allocation and plans

10. Implement reusable venue/building/level/room hierarchy and versioned templates.
11. Implement source-plan artifact onboarding (PDF/image/XLSX) and human-reviewed native geometry conversion.
12. Build the SVG spatial editor with zones, rows, tables, seats, floor positions, capacity pools and non-allocatable features.
13. Implement manual and category-based guest allocation first.
14. Add hard/soft constraints, locked assignments, solver proposal/diagnostics and targeted reflow; integrate OR-Tools only behind a stable validated boundary.
15. Add plan revision comparison, approval, publication, print packages and staff viewers.

### Track D — Event-day operations

16. Implement separate admission QR credential issuance, revocation and branded guest cards.
17. Implement the responsive check-in PWA, station/operator management, camera scan, manual fallback, duplicate detection, corrections and offline strategy.
18. Build role-specific staff workspaces and the Live Operations Cockpit.
19. Add realtime updates, operational alerts, task ownership, reports and information-display/signage modes.
20. Implement external prerequisite tracking, including CDI request/schedule/completion coordination.

### Track E — Product-wide completion and release

21. Add organization/venue/event branding inheritance and template authoring across all generated outputs.
22. Complete localization, accessibility, privacy, retention and audit requirements.
23. Complete application-level integration, browser and workflow test coverage continuously during development.
24. Deliver and validate both installation methods.
25. Only after the product is functionally complete, deploy the release candidate to the `eventor-acceptance` VM and run the final end-to-end acceptance suite.
26. Conduct external HTTPS/provider/recovery/production-host acceptance after the VM acceptance baseline is clean.

Tracks can overlap where dependencies permit, but the order above reflects the principal dependencies. The Guest Registry and event participation model should precede full guest seating/check-in; venue geometry should precede allocation; admission credentials should precede gate scanning; the Cockpit should consume stable event, allocation, attendance and task projections.

## 5. Installation deliverable: native Linux and Docker

The installer is a product deliverable and must support two explicit deployment modes. Both modes must run the same release artifacts, use the same PostgreSQL schema/migrations and pass the same application acceptance suite.

### 5.1 Native Linux mode

- Supported Linux distribution/version matrix and prerequisite checks.
- Install/pin supported Node.js runtime and PostgreSQL compatibility requirements.
- Create dedicated unprivileged API/worker accounts and protected directories.
- Configure PostgreSQL roles and database, run checksum-verified migrations.
- Generate independent secrets and create root-managed, least-privilege environment files.
- Build/install versioned API and frontend release artifacts.
- Install and enable API/worker systemd units.
- Configure or integrate a supported reverse proxy and HTTPS; do not assume inbound port 80 is available (DNS-01 certificate validation must be supported).
- Create the initial organization and administrator through a secure first-run/bootstrap flow.
- Provide upgrade, rollback compatibility checks, backup, restore, service restart and health verification.

### 5.2 Docker mode

- Provide a maintained `compose.yaml` and versioned application images/build definitions.
- Include API, worker, web/reverse-proxy and PostgreSQL services with explicit health checks and dependency conditions.
- Persist PostgreSQL and required application data in named volumes or operator-selected bind mounts.
- Keep secrets out of images, source control, command history and container environment inspection where practical; document secret-file handling.
- Use non-root application containers, read-only filesystems where practical, dropped capabilities and explicit resource limits.
- Run migrations as a controlled one-shot deployment step, not as an uncontrolled race on every replica startup.
- Provide TLS/reverse-proxy integration, backup/restore, upgrade and recovery procedures.
- Support external PostgreSQL as an alternative where appropriate, without making it mandatory for the single-host deployment.

### 5.3 Shared installer requirements

- Interactive and non-interactive modes suitable for automation.
- Preflight checks, configuration validation and clear failure/rollback behavior.
- No destructive database reset during upgrade.
- Explicit database backup gate before schema migration.
- Versioned releases and compatibility checks between app and schema.
- Secure first-admin bootstrap; no hard-coded default password.
- SMTP is optional at install time; support local development/test capture (for example Mailpit) and later SMTP configuration such as Gmail SMTP or a transactional provider.
- Installation mode must not alter application features or security guarantees.

Native deployment has systemd unit templates, role bootstrap, migration and backup/restore checks. The native installer and operator runbook still need prerequisite detection, secure first-admin bootstrap, release staging, health/readiness and tested upgrade and recovery. The development Compose file starts PostgreSQL 18.6 on loopback. The release Docker topology and application images remain outstanding.

## 6. Immediate engineering priorities

1. Finish the organizer workflows in issue #104, starting with supervised merge cases involving active records and event controls.
2. Use issues #105–#107 for venue geometry, guest allocation and admission/check-in, in that dependency order.
3. Complete the booking lifecycle edges and disruption coordination tracked in issue #112.
4. Prepare the two production installation paths under issue #108 with controlled migrations, health verification, secure configuration and recovery.
5. Keep CI/unit/PostgreSQL/browser tests running on every feature PR. Reserve the dedicated `eventor-acceptance` VM for the final integrated release candidate.

## 7. Known limitations of this audit

- The matrix summarizes source inspection and references repository verification. Product-wide end-to-end acceptance, deployed-host testing and the final VM run remain outstanding.
- A route/schema/test fixture is not proof of a complete user workflow; classifications intentionally require both runtime and UI evidence for a usable feature.
- The GHB reference venue workbook, venue capacities, physical hierarchy, branding assets and operational policies still require validation with authorized venue representatives.
- No independent human reviewer was available for this audit. It is an implementation inventory and planning artifact, not an independent security or product certification.
- The audit baseline is the exact `main` commit stated at the top. Re-run/reconcile it as features merge.

# Eventor project state

Updated 2026-11-25. This page is the current development handoff. Detailed historical entries and older CI receipts are preserved in the [state archive](PROJECT_STATE_HISTORY_2026-11-23.md).

## Verified integration baseline

`main` was verified at `f6039be2d630b7834fe19856660a051a17db2ec9`, after [Settings Partner access #229](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/pull/229). Post-merge [contracts/PostgreSQL](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/actions/runs/45671121922) and [secret history](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/actions/runs/45671121975) passed. This includes collaboration lifecycle APIs (#228), attributed link ending (#227), the disruption inbox (#226/#225), booking selection/association (#224/#223) and prior verified foundations. Detailed receipts are in the linked archive.

## Latest implementation slice

The current #104/#112 API slice proposes narrow booking-link access without direct database manipulation. The caller needs both collaboration management and organization/exact-booking management. Recipient, purpose and validity are explicit; only `booking.event.link` with an empty data projection can be proposed. The existing grant/revision/audit/name capture are reused. Proposal is unaccepted and changes no booking/event facts; recipient review/acceptance remains separate.

Migration 201/ADR 0023 validate finite validity and preserve explicit nullable expiry. Canonical IDs, purpose and equivalent times normalize for idempotency. Cached creation returns the original receipt after rechecking both source authorities; current lifecycle is read separately. Full application/fresh PostgreSQL upgrade/migration/RLS/concurrency/auth-role tests and real concurrent API proposal→review→accept→link/revocation checks passed locally. Exact-head CI is required before integration.

The accepted partner selector (#230/migration 200) merged at `807378fc9e82fc1abe5a9590ea1b0218bc708ee5`, identical to checked head `bef6da065a76b086724999eba6504069ed550cd7` after all five checks/CLEAN. Post-merge verification is pending. Its full/fresh SQL/API/Chromium/Firefox and inspected desktop/mobile checks passed locally. It requires exact event management and reads only accepted/effective linking scopes, excluding all existing associations before pagination. No provider records, directory, commercial or guest data is read.

Remaining work includes staff proposal controls/recipient discovery and cross-organization notice delivery. Email, relationship correction and disruption resolution remain open; acknowledgement is receipt only.

The interactive preview was stopped at the owner’s request. Its disposable `--rm` database container was removed on stop: source, fixtures and build remain, but exploratory database edits were not retained. Recreate the next interactive preview with a persistent named volume and a local backup before shutdown.

Preview feedback already includes persistent language selection, permission-aware tabs/error isolation, `DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm` Bosnian dates, optional generated codes, preferred-name help, SMTP under Settings and persistent Registry label badges such as VIP.

## Implemented workflows

- **Bookings:** public configurable inquiries, staff inquiry-to-draft review, allocation availability/alternatives, versioned offers, customer decisions, approval, confirmation, pinned pricing/tax/policy snapshots, communications and delivery worker. Cancellation includes staff review/execution, eligible reservation release, and separate customer request/status capabilities. Requests, booking cancellation and event cancellation remain separate decisions. Commercial settlement remains manual.
- **Provider disruptions:** permitted-booking search and append-only notice recording/history with public summaries and optional affected UTC times. Projections omit operational summaries. Recording does not send notifications or change booking/event status. Explicit local event-inbox publication and receipt acknowledgement are available; partner/email delivery and event resolution remain open under #112.
- **Organizer events:** bilingual creation, revision-checked editing, archival, planning, approval, publication, start and close. Sessions support listing, creation, timing/title edits, scheduling, start, completion and confirmed cancellation. Scoped managers can publish versioned RSVP settings while preserving issued invitation policies. Event guest capabilities are optional.
- **Registry:** persistent profile search/edit/archive, classification-filtered search/export, permission-filtered participation history, encrypted contacts and source references, contact verification, relationships and internal configurable labels. Supervised reversible merges cover unlinked profiles, non-overlapping closed-event history and explicitly reviewed non-conflicting contact, supported source-reference and non-overlapping classification transfers and non-conflicting active relationship transfers. IDs, encrypted values, consent, primary status, verification evidence and reference encryption identity are preserved. Restoration can return unchanged transferred records or explicitly reviewed current records while keeping unselected records at the destination and removed references deleted. Stale reviews require a fresh review. Initial contact conflicts, overlapping/edited classification correction, changed relationship correction and other linked/overlapping cases remain open; see ADR 0013/0018/0019.
- **Guest lists:** Registry links with pinned event identity and guest references; participant status, categories, internal/restricted tags, group hierarchy, roles, placement preferences/rules, relationships, encrypted custom fields and staff notes. Personal saved views and transactional bulk category/status/tag/group changes and recorded-name restoration are available. Bulk group changes preserve existing roles and unrelated memberships; retired groups remain removable. Name/status/category/tag/group filters apply to exports; CSV/XLSX exports include guest references.
- **Imports:** mapped CSV/XLSX review with worksheet/header selection, encrypted staging, separate profiles, matched reuse/update and exact source-reference matching. Authorized staff can review unmatched references before creating profiles; diagnostics and exports are permission-filtered.
- **Access administration:** member name search, scoped-grant/permission inspection, reusable event role presets, grant/revocation and member suspension/restoration. Suspension revokes the affected member's sessions. Organization name, operating profile and default time zone use revision checks; new events use the organization time zone. Email-first sign-in, membership switching and explicit host-managed platform administration are implemented; host-only initial-account and existing-account membership commands are available; broader tenant onboarding and a complete global account-management console remain open.
- **Invitation/RSVP foundation:** opaque scoped invitation capabilities, guest response flow, staff-recorded responses/corrections/history and delivery processing. RSVP remains separate from physical attendance.

Authenticated browser tests verify that a venue-provider session cannot read organizer guests. An event-scoped member grant exposes only that roster and does not grant Registry access. Revocation removes roster access while leaving the member session active.

Canonical UUID validation accepts identifiers already stored in PostgreSQL, including legacy version/variant bits. Tenant authorization and authenticated encryption retain their boundaries; see [ADR 0011](decisions/0011-database-uuid-compatibility.md).

## Next work, in roadmap order

1. Continue [#104](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/104): broader organization/user/member administration and event settings; initial-merge conflict resolution for contacts and unsupported identifiers, relationship conflict/correction and open/overlapping event history; remaining configurable roster/bulk controls. Audit existing commands before adding aggregates.
2. Complete collaboration/disruption work under [#112](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/112): provider-to-organizer delivery, acknowledgement, linked-event resolution and booking amendment/postponement acceptance. Provider notice recording alone does not complete this issue.
3. Implement venue geometry/editor [#105](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/105), advisory allocation [#106](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/106), then admission/check-in and operations cockpit [#107](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/107).
4. Complete both secure native Linux and production Docker Compose installers under [#108](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/108), including bootstrap, configuration, health, upgrade and recovery.
5. Run final integrated acceptance on the acceptance VM after the release candidate and both installers are complete. Production readiness and deployed-host acceptance remain unverified.

The [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) and [blueprint gap analysis](BLUEPRINT_TO_REPOSITORY_GAP_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md) retain the broader backlog. Public customer-cancellation browser acceptance covers submission, idempotent retry, cookie omission, fragment cleanup, reusable scoped status, unchanged booking confirmation and bilingual revoked-link errors. Both cancellation routes skip staff-session restoration, preserving the link locale even when staff cookies are present. Full organizer/venue collaboration acceptance remains a follow-up.

## Development and verification

Read this page, [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), the relevant [design](implementation-design/v0.3/) and [decisions](decisions/) before editing. The [local guide](development/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md) describes setup, focused checks and logs. Use the existing checkout and inspect local changes before switching or pulling.

```bash
./scripts/dev/doctor.sh                 # read-only workstation checks
./scripts/dev/check.sh quick            # contracts, API types, staff tests/types
./scripts/dev/check.sh api 'test name'  # focused API regression
./scripts/dev/check.sh web              # staff tests and build
./scripts/dev/check.sh full             # full application checks before PR
```

Full application checks are distinct from CI. Exact-head CI also runs dependency audits, PostgreSQL 18.6 migration/upgrade/RLS/concurrency and browser integration, systemd verification and reachable-history secret scanning. Live HTTPS/SMTP probes are optional and skipped without configured targets; a skip is not a pass. Check the exact PR SHA and required checks before merging, then inspect post-merge workflows.

Docker is optional for development PostgreSQL; the native regression runner can use installed PostgreSQL 18 binaries. [Development Compose](../compose.dev.yaml), role bootstrap/migration scripts and [systemd templates](../deploy/systemd/README.md) exist. These are foundations for the two release installers, not evidence that installation or recovery acceptance is complete.

## Product boundaries

Keep the API-first modular monolith, tenant/field-level permissions, immutable commercial/event history and optional event capabilities. Venue providers do not gain organizer guest access through booking ownership. Solver proposals require human review/commit. Configurable policies, venue measurements and reference-deployment operational/legal facts require evidence rather than assumptions. The [blueprint](blueprint/v1.2/Event_Operations_Platform_Technical_Blueprint_v1.2.md), [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) and accepted ADRs own the detailed rules.

# OpenAPI successor contract design — v0.3

**Status:** proposed API surface and security design; aligned with the canonical OpenAPI v0.3 draft in `docs/api/openapi.v0.3.yaml`  
**Date:** 2026-11-10  
**Depends on:** ADR 0004–0006; accepted MVP/role model; RSVP and Invitation Design v0.3; Cancellation and Event Disruption Design v0.3; Successor PostgreSQL Schema Design v0.3  
**Historical source:** `docs/implementation-design/v0.2/eogp_openapi_v0.2.yaml` (read-only snapshot)  
**Concrete contract draft:** [`docs/api/openapi.v0.3.yaml`](openapi.v0.3.yaml)

## 1. Contract goals

- Preserve the API-first modular-monolith boundary: the API is authoritative for state transitions, permissions, validation, audit and concurrency.
- Keep booking-only venue operations usable without operational event or guest capabilities.
- Represent venue provider, booking customer/requester, contracting party, payer, event organizer and operational task owner independently.
- Make cross-organization access explicit through grant IDs and event-owned snapshot IDs; a booking ID alone never authorizes event or guest access.
- Keep staff session, guest invitation capability, external booking action capability and unauthenticated public intake as separate security contexts.
- Make every state-changing operation idempotent where clients/workers may retry, and concurrency-aware through expected revision / `If-Match`.
- Use purpose-specific request/response schemas. Public/guest projections must never reuse unrestricted staff entities.
- Keep v0.2 OpenAPI unchanged.

## 2. Security schemes and principal types

| Security context | Intended routes | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Staff session cookie | Staff administration and operational commands | Authenticated user + active organization membership + permission/scope check |
| Guest invitation capability | Guest's own invitation and RSVP actions | One invitation, one guest/event, limited purpose and expiry |
| External booking action capability | External booking requester cancellation/status actions | One booking and allowed external action; no tenant membership |
| Public / no credential | Published booking form and inquiry intake only | Anti-abuse controls; no internal workflow visibility |

Security requirements:
- Public operations explicitly set `security: []`; do not rely on accidental inheritance.
- Guest routes require only the guest capability, never a staff cookie as substitute.
- External booking actions require only the purpose-bound booking capability, never a guest token.
- Staff routes require a staff session plus server-side membership, permission and scope checks.
- Never accept `actorUserId`, `organizationId` or grant identity from a caller as proof of authority. The server resolves actor context; target owner IDs are checked against the authorized aggregate/grant.
- Public capability tokens are opaque, high entropy, stored only as hashes, rate-limited, revocable, purpose-bound and redacted from logs. GET/preview must not mutate or consume a capability.
- Apply CSRF/origin protections to cookie-authenticated mutations; define secure cookie attributes, CORS allow-list, content-type enforcement and request-size limits.
- Return generic not-found/unauthorized outcomes where revealing existence would enable enumeration.

## 3. Common command and response conventions

### 3.1 Headers

- `Idempotency-Key`: required for public submissions and retryable state-changing commands (format and retention window specified in shared header schema).
- `If-Match`: required when mutating a versioned draft, booking, event, grant or configuration revision.
- `ETag`: returned for versioned aggregate representations.
- `X-Request-Id`: generated by server and returned for support/audit correlation; clients cannot use it to impersonate an actor.

### 3.2 Common error model

Use one RFC 9457-style problem response with stable application `code`, safe `detail`, `instance`/request ID and optional field errors. Standard outcomes:
- `400` malformed request; `401` missing/invalid credential; `403` authenticated but not authorized; `404` unavailable/not found; `409` state or reservation conflict; `410` expired/revoked purpose token; `412` stale `If-Match`; `422` domain validation/policy failure; `429` rate limit; `500` generic server failure.
- Conflict responses may include a safe conflict code and current aggregate revision, but never leak another tenant's resource details.
- Disabled optional capability returns a stable `CAPABILITY_DISABLED` response (normally 409 or 404 according to route-discovery policy); do not return success with silently omitted data.

### 3.3 Asynchronous work

Long-running imports, campaign delivery, document rendering and solver runs return `202` plus a scoped job reference. Job status endpoints return only jobs visible to the requesting principal. Outbox/provider delivery is not synchronous with authoritative domain transitions.

## 4. Proposed route inventory

Routes below define the intended contract surface. The canonical OpenAPI v0.3 YAML is the concrete route baseline; route additions or semantic differences against this broader inventory must be recorded and resolved before Issue #17 closes.

### 4.1 Identity, organizations and authorization

| Method / path | Operation ID | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST `/auth/session` | `createStaffSession` | Staff login |
| DELETE `/auth/session` | `deleteStaffSession` | Logout/revoke session |
| GET `/me` | `getCurrentPrincipal` | Current user, memberships and safe permission summaries |
| GET `/organizations/{organizationId}/memberships` | `listOrganizationMemberships` | Authorized membership management |
| POST `/organizations/{organizationId}/memberships` | `createOrganizationMembership` | Add member |
| PATCH `/memberships/{membershipId}` | `updateOrganizationMembership` | Change membership state/roles |
| GET `/organizations/{organizationId}/roles` | `listOrganizationRoles` | Permission bundles |
| GET `/organizations/{organizationId}/permissions` | `listPermissionCatalogue` | Stable permission catalogue |

### 4.2 Public booking intake and booking administration

| Method / path | Operation ID | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/public/organizations/{organizationSlug}/booking-forms/{formCode}` | `getPublishedPublicBookingForm` | Public published form projection |
| POST `/public/organizations/{organizationSlug}/booking-inquiries` | `submitPublicBookingInquiry` | Rate-limited public inquiry |
| GET `/organizations/{organizationId}/booking-inquiries` | `listBookingInquiries` | Staff inbox |
| GET `/booking-inquiries/{inquiryId}` | `getBookingInquiry` | Immutable original submission |
| POST `/booking-inquiries/{inquiryId}/create-draft` | `createBookingDraftFromInquiry` | Separate editable draft |
| POST `/organizations/{organizationId}/booking-drafts` | `createBookingDraft` | Staff-created draft without inquiry |
| GET `/booking-drafts/{draftId}` | `getBookingDraft` | Draft and current revision |
| POST `/booking-drafts/{draftId}/revisions` | `createBookingDraftRevision` | New immutable revision |
| POST `/booking-draft-revisions/{revisionId}/offers` | `createBookingOffer` | Issue immutable offer |
| GET `/booking-offers/{offerId}` | `getBookingOffer` | Offer projection |
| POST `/booking-offers/{offerId}/accept` | `acceptBookingOffer` | External scoped acceptance if enabled |
| POST `/booking-draft-revisions/{revisionId}/confirm` | `confirmBooking` | Approval + atomic resource reservation |
| GET `/organizations/{organizationId}/bookings` | `listBookings` | Booking calendar/list |
| GET `/bookings/{bookingId}` | `getBooking` | Permission-filtered booking |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/amendments` | `requestBookingAmendment` | Date/space/service amendment with replacement availability check |
| GET `/bookings/{bookingId}/history` | `getBookingHistory` | Status and decision history |

A public inquiry receipt must not reveal internal status, staff notes or booking calendar. Offer acceptance and cancellation actions use purpose-bound external capabilities with limited projections. A customer contact is not automatically the contracting party; explicit authorized contacts are captured on confirmation.

### 4.3 Venue inventory and resource availability

| Method / path | Operation ID | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET/POST `/organizations/{organizationId}/venues` | `listVenues` / `createVenue` | Venue registry |
| GET/PATCH `/venues/{venueId}` | `getVenue` / `updateVenue` | Venue administration |
| GET/POST `/venues/{venueId}/spaces` | `listVenueSpaces` / `createVenueSpace` | Space hierarchy |
| GET/POST `/venues/{venueId}/resources` | `listVenueResources` / `createVenueResource` | Resource inventory |
| POST `/availability/space` | `checkSpaceAvailability` | Availability preview |
| POST `/availability/resources` | `checkResourceAvailability` | Unit/pool availability |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/holds` | `createBookingHold` | Temporary hold |
| POST `/holds/{holdId}/extend` | `extendBookingHold` | Extend subject to policy/availability |
| POST `/holds/{holdId}/release` | `releaseBookingHold` | Release hold |
| GET `/bookings/{bookingId}/reservations` | `listBookingReservations` | Space/resource time blocks |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/reservations/release` | `releaseBookingReservations` | Controlled release after authority/state check |

Availability is advisory until a hold/confirmation transaction commits. The database remains the final concurrency authority. Confirmation and amendment revalidate under lock and either commit every required reservation or none.

### 4.4 Booking cancellation and venue disruption

| Method / path | Operation ID | Security |
|---|---|---|
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/external-action-capabilities` | `issueExternalBookingActionCapability` | Staff session; issues a purpose-bound capability to an explicitly authorised booking contact |
| POST `/external/booking-actions/resolve` | `resolveExternalBookingAction` | Public capability exchange; token supplied in request body/header, never query string |
| GET `/external/booking-actions/me` | `getExternalBookingActionContext` | External booking capability; minimal booking/contact/action projection |
| POST `/external/booking-actions/cancellation-requests` | `submitExternalBookingCancellationRequest` | External booking capability |
| GET `/external/booking-actions/cancellation-requests/{requestId}` | `getExternalBookingCancellationRequest` | Same capability, bound to the same booking |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/external-action-capabilities/{capabilityId}/revoke` | `revokeExternalBookingActionCapability` | Staff session |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/cancellation-requests` | `submitBookingCancellationRequest` | Staff session |
| GET `/bookings/{bookingId}/cancellation-requests` | `listBookingCancellationRequests` | Staff session |
| POST `/booking-cancellation-requests/{requestId}/approve` | `approveBookingCancellationRequest` | Staff session + approval permission |
| POST `/booking-cancellation-requests/{requestId}/reject` | `rejectBookingCancellationRequest` | Staff session + review permission |
| POST `/booking-cancellation-requests/{requestId}/withdraw` | `withdrawBookingCancellationRequest` | Requesting party/capability or authorized staff |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/venue-cancellation` | `initiateVenueBookingCancellation` | Staff session + venue cancellation permission |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/cancellation-preview` | `previewBookingCancellationEffects` | Staff session or limited external projection |
| POST `/bookings/{bookingId}/cancellation-execution` | `executeBookingCancellation` | Staff session + execute permission |
| GET `/bookings/{bookingId}/cancellation-history` | `getBookingCancellationHistory` | Staff session |
| GET `/bookings/{bookingId}/disruption-notices` | `listBookingDisruptionNotices` | Staff session / scoped event collaborator |
| GET `/organizations/{organizationId}/cancellation-policies` | `listCancellationPolicies` | Staff session + configuration read |
| POST `/organizations/{organizationId}/cancellation-policies` | `createCancellationPolicy` | Staff session + configuration manage |
| POST `/cancellation-policies/{policyId}/revisions` | `createCancellationPolicyRevision` | Staff session + configuration manage |
| POST `/cancellation-policy-revisions/{revisionId}/publish` | `publishCancellationPolicyRevision` | Staff session + configuration publish |

Do not expose an unscoped public route with a caller-supplied booking ID. The resolution exchange binds the external capability to one booking and action set. Approval, effective cancellation, resource release and commercial effects are distinct steps. Revocation invalidates the capability immediately. A booking cancellation never automatically cancels the linked event.

### 4.5 Events, optional capabilities and responsibility

| Method / path | Operation ID | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST `/organizations/{organizationId}/events` | `createEvent` | Explicit organizer-owned event |
| GET/PATCH `/events/{eventId}` | `getEvent` / `updateEvent` | Event projection/update |
| GET/POST `/events/{eventId}/capabilities` | `getEventCapabilities` / `publishEventCapabilities` | Versioned optional module activation |
| GET/POST `/events/{eventId}/responsibility-assignments` | `listEventResponsibilities` / `createEventResponsibilityAssignment` | Accountability and task ownership |
| PATCH `/event-responsibility-assignments/{assignmentId}` | `updateEventResponsibilityAssignment` | Scoped assignment change |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/booking-links` | `linkBookingToEvent` | Explicit cross-owner association and grant check |
| GET `/events/{eventId}/disruption-notices` | `listEventDisruptionNotices` | Minimum necessary venue disruption facts |
| POST `/event-disruption-notices/{noticeId}/acknowledge` | `acknowledgeEventDisruption` | Organizer acknowledgement |
| POST `/event-disruption-notices/{noticeId}/resolve` | `resolveEventDisruption` | Relocate/amend/postpone/cancel/unresolved |

Event creation does not occur as a side effect of booking confirmation. Disabled capabilities have no guest records or public routes enabled by default.

### 4.6 Collaboration and event-owned venue snapshots

| Method / path | Operation ID | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST `/organizations/{organizationId}/collaboration-grants` | `proposeCollaborationGrant` | Grantor proposes scoped collaboration |
| POST `/collaboration-grants/{grantId}/accept` | `acceptCollaborationGrant` | Grantee acceptance |
| GET `/organizations/{organizationId}/collaboration-grants` | `listCollaborationGrants` | Own grants |
| POST `/collaboration-grants/{grantId}/revoke` | `revokeCollaborationGrant` | Immediate future-access revocation |
| POST `/venues/{venueId}/snapshot-shares` | `createVenueSnapshotShare` | Provider approves revision/layers/resources |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/venue-snapshots` | `createEventVenueSnapshot` | Copy approved share into event-owned immutable snapshot |
| GET `/event-venue-snapshots/{snapshotId}` | `getEventVenueSnapshot` | Provenance and permitted content |
| GET `/event-venue-snapshots/{snapshotId}/layers` | `listEventVenueSnapshotLayers` | Snapshot-owned layer projection |

Grant acceptance does not grant every member broad access; the actor's membership and role in the grantee organization must also permit the operation. Snapshot routes never mutate provider master geometry.

For `createVenueSnapshotShare`, `approvedLayerIds` must identify spatial layers belonging to the exact `venueSpaceRevisionId`. `approvedResourceIds` may identify resource pools or discrete units belonging to that revision's venue. The database rejects duplicate/foreign identifiers. When the organizer copies the share, each snapshot layer must refer to an approved source layer, every source object must belong to one of those approved layers, and every copied resource must be in the approved resource list. The source revision, its approved layer/object rows and approved resource rows are visible through narrowly filtered RLS only while the share and `venue.snapshot.use` grant remain active. Revocation hides provider master rows from the recipient and blocks new bindings/copies, while the organizer's already-copied event-owned snapshot remains historical data.

### 4.7 Guest registry, invitations, RSVP and attendance

| Method / path | Operation ID | Security |
|---|---|---|
| GET/POST `/organizations/{organizationId}/persons` | `listPersons` / `createPerson` | Staff |
| GET/PATCH `/persons/{personId}` | `getPerson` / `updatePerson` | Staff |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/participations` | `createEventParticipation` | Staff |
| GET `/events/{eventId}/participations` | `listEventParticipations` | Staff |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/invitations` | `issueInvitations` | Staff + invite permission |
| POST `/invitations/{invitationId}/resend` | `resendInvitation` | Staff |
| POST `/invitations/{invitationId}/revoke` | `revokeInvitation` | Staff |
| POST `/invitations/{invitationId}/reissue` | `reissueInvitation` | Staff |
| POST `/guest/invitation/resolve` | `resolveGuestInvitation` | Guest invitation capability; non-consuming |
| GET `/guest/invitation/me` | `getMyInvitation` | Guest invitation capability |
| POST `/guest/invitation/me/rsvp` | `submitMyRsvp` | Guest invitation capability |
| GET `/guest/invitation/me/rsvp-history` | `getMyRsvpHistory` | Guest invitation capability |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/participations/{participationId}/rsvp-records` | `recordStaffRsvp` | Staff + RSVP record permission |
| POST `/rsvp-responses/{responseId}/corrections` | `correctRsvpResponse` | Staff + correction permission/reason |
| GET `/participations/{participationId}/rsvp-history` | `getParticipationRsvpHistory` | Staff |
| POST `/check-in/scan` | `scanAdmissionCredential` | Staff/check-in device capability |

Guest operations return the caller's own safe projection only. When an event is cancelled or an invitation is superseded, opening the prior valid link returns a safe cancellation/schedule-change notice (for example, 410 with a guest-safe body) and cannot accept a new RSVP. The invitation link is not an admission QR. Staff-recorded responses capture source/channel, guest-reported time, server-recorded time and authenticated operator. Corrections append a new response/correction record.

### 4.8 Event cancellation, postponement and guest communications

| Method / path | Operation ID | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST `/events/{eventId}/cancellation-preview` | `previewEventCancellation` | Impact, linked bookings, sessions, tasks and candidate audience counts |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/change-requests` | `createEventChangeRequest` | Create cancellation, postponement or reschedule request with expected event revision |
| POST `/event-change-requests/{requestId}/approve` | `approveEventChangeRequest` | Approval under event-owner policy |
| POST `/event-change-requests/{requestId}/reject` | `rejectEventChangeRequest` | Reject/return with reason; event state is unchanged |
| POST `/event-change-requests/{requestId}/execute` | `executeEventChangeRequest` | Commit effective decision, schedule/capability suppression and outbox effects |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/schedule-revisions` | `createEventScheduleRevision` | Publish replacement schedule only through the authorized change process |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/notification-campaign-previews` | `previewEventNotificationCampaign` | Resolve cancellation/postponement/schedule-update/reconfirmation audience and counts |
| POST `/events/{eventId}/notification-campaigns` | `createEventNotificationCampaign` | Confirm fixed recipient snapshot |
| GET `/event-notification-campaigns/{campaignId}` | `getEventNotificationCampaign` | Campaign projection and aggregate delivery counts |
| GET `/event-notification-campaigns/{campaignId}/recipients` | `listEventNotificationCampaignRecipients` | Restricted recipient-level view |
| POST `/event-notification-campaigns/{campaignId}/retry-failures` | `retryFailedEventNotificationDeliveries` | Retry eligible failed attempts idempotently |

A campaign has an explicit purpose: event cancellation, postponement, schedule update or RSVP reconfirmation. Audience choices are accepted/tentative, all active invitees, all previously invited recipients or permitted custom selection. The default may be all active invitees, but the server must return an explicit preview explaining who qualifies. Recipient membership and a minimum necessary encrypted contact snapshot are frozen when the campaign is confirmed; retries never recalculate it. Event cancellation/postponement commits independently of provider delivery.

### 4.9 Spatial allocation, prerequisites, cockpit and jobs

Keep v0.2 operations where their semantics remain valid, but re-scope them to event-owned snapshots and capability permissions. Add event snapshot provenance to allocation inputs/results. Keep solver output advisory until an authorized human commits it. Check-in routes require the check-in capability. Prerequisite/task routes use explicit responsibility assignment. Cockpit output is permission-projected.

Job operations:
- `GET /jobs/{jobId}` — scoped job status.
- `GET /events/{eventId}/notifications` — permission-filtered notification status.
- `GET /events/{eventId}/audit` — authorized audit projection; never expose token values or unrestricted provider payloads.

## 5. Cancellation and rescheduling command semantics

### Booking cancellation

1. External customer submits a cancellation request using a booking-action capability, or authorized venue staff initiate a venue-side cancellation.
2. Server resolves pinned booking policy and authorized booking contacts.
3. Preview reports policy revision, approval requirement, resource effects and safe commercial consequence summary.
4. Approver decision is a distinct command; rejection/withdrawal leaves confirmed booking and reservations intact.
5. Effective execution locks booking and reservation rows, checks expected revision, applies cancellation once, releases future blocks, retains completed work, records commercial follow-up and writes audit/outbox.
6. Notify booking contacts asynchronously. Linked event receives only a scoped disruption notice.

### Event cancellation

1. Organizer operator requests impact preview and selects reason/internal/public text.
2. Server returns session/guest/invitation/task/booking counts and candidate audience counts without leaking unnecessary guest data.
3. Authorized initiator/approver executes under event revision precondition.
4. Transaction marks event/sessions cancelled, prevents new RSVP/invitation/check-in/credential operations, suppresses pending ordinary messages, preserves history and records campaign/outbox intent.
5. Campaign recipient snapshot is resolved and committed according to selected audience and permissions; actual provider delivery is asynchronous.
6. Linked booking remains unchanged until separately amended/cancelled.

### Postponement

Publish a new schedule revision; never rewrite the old one. A material date/time/venue change may require accepted/tentative guests to reconfirm. Previous responses remain historical answers to the previous schedule. A linked venue booking amendment is a separate request/approval and must secure replacement reservations before releasing the old blocks where feasible.

## 6. Capability and scope behavior

- A venue-only organization can use all Release-1 booking routes without event/guest routes or event rows.
- Event routes require an event-owned record and relevant capability enabled.
- Cross-org routes require both active grant and actor's own organization membership/role.
- Revoked/expired grants prevent new actions immediately; audit and historic snapshots remain.
- External booking contact actions reveal only booking-specific fields and never guest lists.
- Venue provider receives aggregate attendance/capacity only when needed and permitted; no guest identity/RSVP data by default.
- Guest routes reveal only personal invitation/response details and sanitized public event information.

## 7. Contract validation and generation

The final OpenAPI 3.1.1 YAML must include explicit security schemes: `staffSessionCookie` for staff; `guestInvitationCapability` for a guest's own invitation; and `externalBookingActionCapability` for a booking contact's limited action session. Raw bearer secrets are exchanged through a non-mutating POST resolve operation, never placed in query strings, and are redacted from logs. The route inventory must map each command above to concrete operations. The final YAML must:
1. Use globally unique operation IDs and explicit response schemas for every operation.
2. Resolve all local references and path parameters.
3. Define security requirements per route; test the public allow-list.
4. Include examples for success, validation, authorization, stale revision, conflict, expiry and capability-disabled responses.
5. Validate representative payloads with JSON Schema 2020-12/OpenAPI 3.1 semantics.
6. Generate TypeScript types/client artifacts reproducibly from a pinned generator, or use a pinned runtime schema generator; do not hand-maintain duplicate contracts.
7. Add contract tests for booking-only operation, external booking cancellation, venue disruption isolation, RSVP, event cancellation audiences, grant revocation and reservation conflicts.
8. Keep v0.2 YAML unchanged as historical reference.

The contract is subject to the pinned full validator and Redocly lint in CI. Route implementation and request/response contract tests remain separate work; Issue #3 must remain open until those tests are added and pass.

# Database integrity and resource reservation design — v0.3

**Status:** accepted integrity design baseline for successor DDL; exact schema and runtime validation remain open  
**Date:** 2026-11-10  
**Parent reference:** v0.2 schema starter  
**Related:** [Issue #13](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/13), [Issue #2](https://github.com/TeraflopsBH/eventor/issues/2), [ADR 0004](../decisions/0004-optional-event-operations-scope.md), [ADR 0006](../decisions/0006-cross-organization-collaboration.md)

This proposal does not modify the historical v0.2 SQL snapshot. Its purpose is to define the integrity patterns that a reviewed successor schema must implement and test.

## 1. Design principles

1. Use database constraints for invariants that can be represented relationally.
2. Every tenant-owned row has one explicit owner organization. A same-tenant relationship uses a composite organization-scoped foreign key.
3. A cross-organization relationship is a separate, explicit domain relationship with its own owner identifiers and scoped grant; it is never represented by weakening an existing tenant FK to a bare UUID.
4. Avoid polymorphic `scope_type + scope_id` references where the target is a known table and can be represented by typed foreign keys.
5. Resolve availability and capacity conflicts within the same transaction that commits a hold/reservation.
6. A venue-only booking does not depend on event, guest, RSVP, check-in or other organizer modules.
7. Event module/task ownership is explicit. A global user identity alone does not prove the user is authorized to act for a given organization.

## 2. Tenant-scoped self-references

The v0.2 tables `persons` and `guest_credentials` already have `UNIQUE (organization_id, id)`, but self-references use only the UUID.

Successor constraints:
- Replace `persons.merged_into_person_id REFERENCES persons(id)` with a composite FK `(organization_id, merged_into_person_id) -> persons(organization_id, id)`.
- Replace `guest_credentials.replaced_by_credential_id REFERENCES guest_credentials(id)` with `(organization_id, replaced_by_credential_id) -> guest_credentials(organization_id, id)`.
- Keep nullable targets nullable; a null target means no merge/replacement. Ensure state checks require a target only where the lifecycle semantics require one.
- Add tests proving a person/credential in organization A cannot point to a row in organization B.

The same pattern applies to any future tenant-owned parent/child or supersedes/replaces reference.

## 3. Venue hierarchy consistency

The current `venue_spaces` row separately points to `venue_id`, optional `building_id` and optional `level_id`. Existing FKs prove each object belongs to the organization, but not that the building belongs to the selected venue or the level belongs to the selected building.

### 3.1 Required candidate keys

Add composite candidate keys:
- `venue_buildings(organization_id, venue_id, id)`.
- `venue_levels(organization_id, building_id, id)`.

Then use:
- Existing `(organization_id, venue_id) -> venues`.
- `(organization_id, venue_id, building_id) -> venue_buildings(organization_id, venue_id, id)`.
- `(organization_id, building_id, level_id) -> venue_levels(organization_id, building_id, id)`.

The final FK requires nullable hierarchy to be internally consistent. Use a CHECK so `level_id IS NOT NULL` implies `building_id IS NOT NULL`. A space without a building/level remains valid if that is a supported venue layout. If a space has a building but no level, that can be allowed where the model requires it.

Tests must reject:
- Building from another venue in the same organization.
- Level from another building in the same organization.
- Building/level from another organization.
- Level without a building.

## 4. Catalogue option revision consistency

Current v0.2 structure:
- `config_catalogue_options` belongs to one catalogue.
- `config_catalogue_option_revisions` belongs to one stable option.
- `config_catalogue_revision_options` references catalogue revision, stable option and option revision independently.

This permits a catalogue revision to pair option A with option B's revision, or to pair an option from a different catalogue, because independent FKs do not prove the identities match.

### 4.1 Relational design

Add `catalogue_id` to `config_catalogue_option_revisions` as a controlled redundant key and enforce it with:
- `UNIQUE (organization_id, catalogue_id, option_id, id)`.
- Composite FK `(organization_id, catalogue_id, option_id) -> config_catalogue_options(organization_id, catalogue_id, id)`.

Ensure `config_catalogue_revisions` has `UNIQUE (organization_id, catalogue_id, id)`.

Add `catalogue_id` to `config_catalogue_revision_options`; enforce:
- `(organization_id, catalogue_id, catalogue_revision_id) -> config_catalogue_revisions(organization_id, catalogue_id, id)`.
- `(organization_id, catalogue_id, option_id, option_revision_id) -> config_catalogue_option_revisions(organization_id, catalogue_id, option_id, id)`.

The stable option identity, selected option revision and containing catalogue revision then have to match. A trigger is not needed for this identity check. The migration must backfill `catalogue_id` from the existing option relationship and fail if historic rows are inconsistent.

## 5. Polymorphic scope references

The v0.2 pattern `scope_type + scope_id` appears in several places. A CHECK validates the type string but cannot prove that `scope_id` points to a row in the correct table or belongs to the same organization.

### 5.1 Keep a type when it is only a capability category

`roles.scope_type` describes the kinds of scopes where a role can be granted. It does not point to a particular event/venue/space row. A constrained enum/check is appropriate.

### 5.2 Replace polymorphic target IDs with typed nullable FKs

For records that point to a specific known entity, prefer explicit columns and checks:
- `user_role_grants`: `scope_event_id`, `scope_venue_id`, `scope_space_id`, `scope_station_id`, plus a scope-type CHECK requiring exactly the matching target and nulling the others. Organization scope has no target ID.
- `brand_profiles`: `scope_venue_id` or `scope_event_id`; organization scope uses neither.
- `document_templates`: same explicit organization/venue/event scope pattern.
- `config_catalogues`: organization/venue/space/event typed references according to the actual supported domain.
- `booking_form_definitions`: organization/venue/space typed references.
- `booking_price_lists`: organization/venue/space typed references.

Every typed FK includes `organization_id`. If the referenced scope belongs to a different organization, it is not valid through that owner's local scope FK; the cross-organization design uses a grant and event-owned snapshot instead.

This is intentionally more columns/checks than a generic UUID, but the integrity is visible, migration-testable and enforced by PostgreSQL. Consider reusable typed scope tables only if they can retain actual FK enforcement without adding an untestable polymorphic escape hatch.

## 6. Actor identity and organization membership

The v0.2 schema uses global `users(id)` in many `created_by`, `updated_by`, `approved_by` and other actor fields. A user is a login identity and can be a member of several organizations; `users(id)` alone does not prove membership in the organization that owns the record.

### 6.1 Membership-scoped actor reference

For ordinary actions on tenant-owned records:
- Use `organization_memberships` as the acting context.
- Add/use a unique key `(organization_id, id)` and `UNIQUE (organization_id, user_id)`.
- Store `actor_membership_id` (or a normalized actor reference) on tenant-owned audit/business action rows and composite-FK it to `organization_memberships(organization_id, id)`.
- Where the user ID is also stored for immutable display/audit, enforce `(organization_id, actor_user_id) -> organization_memberships(organization_id, user_id)`.

The authorization service must still check role/permission and scope at command time. Membership FKs prove organization membership, not permission to perform the action.

### 6.2 Cross-organization delegated action

A collaborator acting on another organization's task is not a member of the data owner's organization. Do not fake membership or weaken the FK.

Instead, record:
- Target/data-owner organization.
- Actor user and actor membership in the grantee organization.
- Active collaboration grant/task assignment authorizing the operation.
- The operation, resource, time and request ID.

The service verifies both the actor's grantee membership and the active grant. Audit records must retain the acting organization separately from the target data owner.

Background/system actions should use explicit service principals or job identities, not a fabricated human user.

## 7. Space holds and confirmed reservations

### 7.1 Problem

v0.2 has `booking_holds` and `booking_space_reservations` as separate tables. A normal B-tree index can help find overlaps but cannot prevent two concurrent transactions from reserving the same space/time, especially when one row is a hold and the other is a confirmed reservation.

### 7.2 Recommended unified occupancy relation

Use one authoritative relation, candidate name `venue_space_time_blocks`, for every interval that makes a space unavailable. It may cover:
- Temporary hold.
- Confirmed booking block (setup, rehearsal, event, teardown or buffer).
- Maintenance/closure/unavailability block (where facility operations require it).

Columns include:
- Owner organization and venue-space FK.
- Exactly one relevant source reference (inquiry/draft/booking/maintenance as applicable).
- Reservation kind and lifecycle status.
- `starts_at`, `ends_at` as `timestamptz`.
- `expires_at` for temporary holds.
- Actor/audit metadata and idempotency key.
- Optional source draft/booking revision.

Use half-open intervals `[starts_at, ends_at)`, so a booking ending at 12:00 does not conflict with another starting at 12:00. Enforce `ends_at > starts_at`.

### 7.3 Database overlap constraint

Use PostgreSQL range/GiST exclusion to prevent overlapping active blocks for the same venue space:
- Install `btree_gist` through an approved migration.
- Exclusion keys: `organization_id WITH =`, `venue_space_id WITH =`, and `tstzrange(starts_at, ends_at, '[)') WITH &&`.
- Apply the exclusion to active statuses such as held/confirmed/maintenance/blocked. Released, cancelled, consumed or expired blocks do not exclude time.
- Make the constraint deferrable only if a controlled multi-row reschedule needs to swap time blocks within one transaction; default immediate checking is simpler.

An index predicate cannot depend on volatile `now()`. An expired hold must be transitioned to `expired` by a worker and also during every reservation operation for the affected space, before conflict checking. All hold, confirm, extend, release and reschedule commands lock the space row in a consistent order and update the unified relation in one transaction. The exclusion constraint is the final race-condition guard.

If the extension cannot be installed in the target PostgreSQL environment, an alternative must be explicitly designed and tested; do not silently fall back to a normal B-tree overlap index.

### 7.4 Booking confirmation transaction

1. Lock all affected venue-space rows in stable sorted ID order.
2. Mark expired holds for those spaces as expired.
3. Verify current draft/offer/policy revisions and authorization.
4. Insert/transition all required space-time blocks.
5. Let the exclusion constraint detect any overlapping active hold/reservation.
6. Commit booking status, confirmed snapshot and reservation blocks atomically.
7. On any conflict, roll back everything and return a clear conflict response.

Do not create a confirmed booking if only some of its required spaces/time blocks were reserved.


### 7.5 Typed reservation origin references

The unified occupancy row must not reintroduce an unchecked polymorphic `source_type + source_id` pair. Use typed nullable origin columns (for example, `booking_draft_revision_id`, `booking_id` and `maintenance_window_id`) with organization-scoped foreign keys and a CHECK that exactly one supported origin is selected. If the implementation instead introduces a reservation-subject supertype, that supertype must itself contain typed FK targets and enforce the same exactly-one invariant.

Keep the original draft/offer provenance separately where needed; the current occupancy owner is not a substitute for the immutable booking revision or approval snapshot. The chosen origin model must support a hold transitioning to a confirmed booking without creating a gap in occupancy protection.

## 8. Equipment/personnel and count-based resources

The current `booking_resource_lines` correctly captures requested, approved and delivered quantities/values, but a commercial line is not itself a schedule reservation.

Keep commercial/service lines separate from physical resource reservations.

### 8.1 Discrete units

Model bookable assets/personnel units in a normalized resource inventory. A unit reservation contains owner organization, unit ID, booking, interval, quantity (normally one), status and source line. Apply the same half-open GiST exclusion approach per unit to prevent overlapping active reservations.

Examples: a particular projector, wireless microphone set, interpreter booth, vehicle or named staff assignment.

### 8.2 Pooled capacity

For fungible pools (for example 10 identical microphones, 4 technicians, 80 chairs), reserve a quantity against a resource pool and interval.

A simple exclusion constraint cannot enforce a sum of overlapping quantities. Use a single parent resource/pool row as the serialization point:
- Every reserve/change/release operation locks the pool row with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (or a transactionally equivalent lock).
- Expire stale holds.
- Calculate overlapping committed quantity under the agreed conflict policy.
- Reject if `existing + requested > capacity`.
- Insert/update the reservation in the same transaction.
- Use a stable lock order when reserving multiple pools.

Test with concurrent transactions, not only sequential fixtures. For highly contended pools, consider serializable isolation after measuring its retry behavior.

### 8.3 Personnel scheduling

Personnel can be represented as discrete units or skill/capacity pools depending on the operation. Availability, working-hour limits, role qualifications and breaks are separate constraints; they must not be inferred from the presence of a commercial personnel line.


### 8.4 Correct pooled-capacity overlap calculation

The capacity check must evaluate the maximum simultaneous quantity over the requested interval, not simply sum every reservation whose interval intersects it. Two existing reservations may each intersect a long requested interval while not overlapping one another; summing both for the entire interval can falsely reject a valid request.

After locking the pool row, collect the interval boundaries of the requested reservation and all active overlapping reservations, partition the requested interval into adjacent half-open segments, and verify that the sum of active quantities plus the requested quantity never exceeds pool capacity in any segment. Define how zero-duration boundaries are handled consistently with the half-open `[starts_at, ends_at)` convention. Execute the capacity read and insert/update in the same transaction after acquiring the serialization lock; use a stable pool lock order for multi-pool commands.

## 9. Event module defaults and configuration

The v0.2 `events.checkin_enabled` defaults to `true`, contradicting ADR 0004.

Successor design:
- Remove per-feature boolean proliferation where practical.
- Represent module activation through published, versioned event capability settings.
- Event creation begins with only core event identity/session capabilities; guest registry, invitations/RSVP, seating, check-in, guest portal, prerequisites and cockpit are off until explicitly enabled or inherited by an approved event preset.
- Organization operating profile supplies defaults; each event can override.
- A venue booking does not need any event module.
- Module dependencies are explicit (for example, invitation-based RSVP requires guest participation plus guest-facing route; check-in does not require RSVP).
- Configuration changes after activation are revisioned and audited.

If a transitional boolean remains in the migration, it must default false and have one source of truth. Do not keep both `checkin_enabled` and an event-module registry with independent mutable values.

## 10. Event task responsibility

ADR 0004 and ADR 0006 require explicit responsibility. `event_prerequisites` currently has an internal coordinator and an external-party name, but not accountable/performed party assignments.

Add a normalized `event_responsibility_assignments` (candidate name) for module or task:
- Event owner organization.
- Capability/task code and optional task instance reference.
- Accountable party kind: organization, external party or event-owning organization.
- Accountable organization ID or external-party ID (exactly one where applicable).
- Performing organization/person/team, potentially distinct from the accountable party.
- Approver and informed party references as needed.
- Collaboration grant reference where a different Eventor organization is involved.
- Scope of data projection/capabilities for the assigned party.
- Due time, status, evidence/reference and readiness rule as appropriate.

An event prerequisite is one task category using this common responsibility model. A venue setup request may also use it. A third-party operator without an Eventor tenant can remain a named external party; an external login is not required.

The accountable organization is a business assignment recorded by Eventor, not a legal liability decision. The platform must not infer or certify statutory responsibility.

## 11. Integrity validation matrix

| Scenario | Expected database/application result |
|---|---|
| Person A references merged target owned by B | FK rejection |
| Credential A references replacement credential B in another tenant | FK rejection |
| Space references building from another venue | FK rejection |
| Space references level from a different building | FK rejection |
| Level provided without building | CHECK rejection |
| Catalogue revision contains option A paired to option B's revision | FK rejection |
| Event role grant references a venue/space in another tenant without approved grant | FK/application rejection |
| Actor user has no membership in target organization | FK/application rejection |
| User is member but lacks permission | API authorization rejection |
| Concurrent active space holds overlap | One transaction rejected |
| Active hold overlaps a confirmed reservation | One transaction rejected |
| Two concurrent pooled resource reservations exceed capacity | One transaction rejected or retried then rejected |
| Event check-in not enabled | Check-in APIs/UI unavailable |
| Venue-only booking | No operational event/guest/module rows required |
| External event collaborator performs an assigned task after grant revocation | Authorization rejection; historical audit preserved |

## 12. Migration and rollout sequence

1. Select the PostgreSQL major version and ensure required extensions (including `btree_gist`) are available.
2. Resolve cross-organization ownership using the accepted ADR 0006 model and event-owned venue snapshots.
3. Build new typed scope references, tenant-safe self-FKs, venue hierarchy FKs and catalogue composite keys.
4. Add membership-scoped actors and scoped collaboration attribution.
5. Replace separate space holds/reservations with the unified occupancy relation; design data migration for active, historical, cancelled and expired blocks.
6. Add discrete and pooled equipment/personnel reservation structures.
7. Add event module capability revisions and responsibility assignments.
8. Reconcile with invitation/RSVP v0.3 design and Issue #10.
9. Apply migrations to an empty disposable PostgreSQL database and run all positive/negative integrity scenarios.
10. Run concurrency tests using independent database connections and the actual non-owner runtime role.
11. Test upgrade from the prior schema, recovery/backup and grant revocation behavior.
12. Only then close Issues #2 and #13.

## 13. Open implementation choices

The architecture above is recommended. The exact DDL still needs review for:
- PostgreSQL version and extension availability.
- Which space-time block kinds share one exclusion relation.
- Whether equipment/personnel use the same generic resource model or distinct tables over a common reservation abstraction.
- Capacity-pool transaction isolation and retry policy.
- How service principals/jobs are represented consistently in audit.
- Whether typed scope columns should be generated through migration templates or repeated explicitly.

These are engineering choices; they must preserve the invariants and acceptance scenarios above.
